Den vita kupolen är Avicii Arena, som ti: The white dome is Avicii Arena, formerly known as the Globe. It opened in 1989 and is the largest spherical building in the world. On the outside, the SkyView glass gondolas will carry you right up to the top.
Det entomologiska kvinnorovet: The sculpture The Entomological Rape of Women
Det finns en vägkrog i Aspnässkolans his: Aspnäs School has a roadside tavern in its past. When Järfälla parish opened its very first school in 1846, it bought a manor house at the Aspnäs crossroads that had once been a tavern. That house was demolished in 1959, but the school still has buildings from 1901 and 1945. And the old schoolhouse? It now does duty as a wind shelter at the Ängsjö outdoor centre.
Det gamla huset på Hornsgatan 82 kallas: The old house at Hornsgatan 82 is known as Bysis. From 1782 to 1872 it was Stockholm's debtors' prison. Next door was the Rixi cinema, which became a recording studio in 1971. Parts of ABBA's Ring Ring and Carola's debut album Främling were recorded there. Today it's called Ingrid studio, and artists such as Lykke Li and Peter Bjorn and John have recorded here.
Det gamla torpet Islinge gård har gett n: The old croft of Islinge gård gave its name to the whole of Islinge, in north-western Lidingö. On Lilla Värtan, south of Islingeviken bay, stands Torsvik lighthouse, also known as the Islinge lighthouse. It was built in 1950 and switched off in 1980, but it still marks the finish line of the Lidingö Runt sailing race. Islinge is also home to Nyckelviksskolan, an art school with courses in art, crafts, architecture and design.
Det gamla torpet Tussmötet har gett namn: The old croft of Tussmötet has given its name to Tussmötevägen, a city block and Tussmöteparken park. Even the local cinema was called Tusse-Bio when it opened in March 1938 on the corner of Bandhagsvägen and Tussmötevägen. It later changed its name to Corso and closed for good in December 1969.
Det gula tornet byggde AGA 1943 för att: AGA built the yellow tower in 1943 to test and manufacture equipment such as periscopes for Swedish submarines, and production carried on inside the rock behind it until 1987. Today the area is called Dalénum, after the inventor Gustaf Dalén, who worked here from 1912 until his death in 1937. The ice rink next door became familiar to a wide audience through the TV series HCZ.
Det gula tornet en bit härifrån har ett: The yellow tower just up the road has an exciting past. AGA's optics tower was built in 1943, and in the factory carved into the rock behind it, AGA tested and made, among other things, periscopes for Swedish submarines. Production carried on in various forms until 1987, and the tower was renovated in 2022.
Det går inte att missa Karlatornet: med: You can't miss Karlatornet. At 246 metres and 73 storeys, it's the tallest building in Sweden and the Nordic countries, and its exterior was completed in 2024. Around the tower, the new Karlastaden district is taking shape with some 2,000 homes. The area has a long industrial past: the shipbuilding and engineering group Götaverken was based here on Lundbyvassen from 1841, and the last part of the shipyard closed in 2015.
Det här var en gång gurkland. Axel Svens: This used to be cucumber country. Axel Svensson's market garden ran from 1907 until the 1970s, and cucumbers were its speciality. Where its greenhouses once stood is now the garden suburb of Hildedal. Svensson's two-storey house from 1919 is still there at Växthusvägen 60 – fittingly, on Greenhouse Road – a reminder of the days when market gardens were a common sight here.
Det här är ett hörn fullt av unika saker: This corner is full of one-offs. Sätra's indoor athletics hall from 1998 is the only one in the municipality designed for youth athletics competitions. The Sätra pistol range is the only one of its kind in Söderort, Stockholm's southern suburbs. And Pingstkyrkan Bredäng is the only Pentecostal church in Stockholm's south-western suburbs. A little further on is the Church of Saint Maroun, which used to be called Sätra Church.
Det höga betongtornet i närheten hör til: The tall concrete tower nearby belongs to Kista fire station, built in 1980. It's a training tower for firefighters and a familiar local landmark. At Kista gård, the old farm, stands Kistastenen, the Kista runestone – proof that people lived on Järvafältet long before Kista became a hub for the IT industry.
Det höga huset på berget är Fyrtornet Da: The tall building on the hill is Fyrtornet Dalénum, the Lighthouse Tower, designed by Wingårdh and completed in 2020. At 68 metres above sea level, it's the highest building on Lidingö. Down by the shore is the Larsberg bridge-keeper's cottage from around 1803, built for the bridge that, that same year, linked Larsberg with Kaknäs on the Stockholm side. The whole area was once home to the AGA factories, where Gustaf Dalén worked.
Det höga huset som syns på långt håll he: The tall building you can see from miles away is Tyresö View. It's 82 metres high with 23 storeys, and in 2016 it was the fourth-tallest residential building in Stockholm County. Under the glass roof of the shopping centre are some 70 shops, the municipal offices and a library with its own exhibition hall.
Det lugna radhusområdet Kälvesta bär på: The quiet terraced streets of Kälvesta hold a sad chapter in Swedish aviation history. On 15 January 1977, a Skyline aircraft operating Linjeflyg Flight 618 crashed into this residential area. All 22 people on board were killed, and the tragedy is remembered today as the Kälvesta air disaster.
Det lustiga namnet Pungpinan kommer från: The odd name Pungpinan comes from a tavern that stood here from the 17th century until the 19th. The Pungpinan croft, built in 1763 on the Skarpnäck estate, was named after the tavern, and in 1933 it became a meeting place for young people from the newly built cottage area. Later the youth organisation Unga Örnar met here too, and since 2000 the croft has been privately owned.
Det långa, slingrande skivhuset Ormen Lå: A short walk away is Ormen Långe, 'the Long Serpent', a long, winding block of flats. Together with six tower blocks on Botkyrkavägen, it had the honour of being the first modern suburban housing in these parts. Right next to it is Fittjanäset, a headland between Lake Mälaren and Lake Albysjön. Fittja bridge spans the narrow strait over to Fittja – and right up until the late 1950s, this was exactly where the main road traffic heading south out of Stockholm crossed.
Det stora kontorshuset alldeles i närhet: The big office building nearby is Bankhus 90, now called Ursvik Entré. It was built between 1989 and 1992 for Skandinaviska Enskilda Banken, following an architecture competition. A short way off stands something much older: the Stora Stampan windmill, probably one of the oldest surviving windmills in Greater Stockholm.
Det tornprydda huset vid farleden kallas: The house with the tower by the shipping lane is known as Smugglarvillan, the Smugglers' Villa. Built in 1912, the Bremer Villa tells of fortunes made from herring fishing around the turn of the century and from bootlegging in the 1920s. On the island's highest point, 31 metres above sea level, stands the sea mark Valen, the Whale. Beneath it, a compass rose is carved into the rock along with the year 1684.
Det var bolaget Lidingö villastad, under: From 1906, the company Lidingö villastad, led by Hjalmar Arwin, turned Lidingö from farmland and a summer retreat for well-off Stockholmers into a modern suburb. Its very first purchase, and its first office, was Vattängen farm on Stockholmsvägen. In the middle of the villa town you'll also find Centralpalatset, built in 1912–1913, and Vasaborgen, which was planned as early as 1913 but not built until 1923.
Det är inte varje dag man ser en soffgru: It's not every day you see a three-piece suite on a rooftop – but you will here. The furniture store founded by Skinngruppen in 1975 has become a local landmark thanks to the giant sofa perched on top. Krokslätt used to be an industrial area, home to the Krokslätt factories, and it's also where the very first self-built family homes in the Gothenburg area went up.
Dieselverkstaden hette ursprungligen Sam: Dieselverkstaden, the Diesel Workshop, was originally known as the Assembly Hall, and Atlas Diesel built diesel engines here right up until 1951. Since 2002 the old factory hall has been full of culture instead, with an arts centre, a library, a climbing centre and a five-screen cinema. And deep beneath the shopping streets of Sickla Köpkvarter is a test mine where rock drills and mining machines are put through their paces.
Djupt inne i berget under bostadsområdet: Deep in the rock beneath the Eriksberg housing area, the red line's metro trains sleep. Norsborg depot lies 18 to 37 metres down inside Aspberget and the Eriksbergsåsen ridge, connected to the metro at Norsborg. Norsborg station itself, a couple of minutes from here, opened in 1975 and is the westernmost station on the whole network.
Djupt inne i ett bergrum i Edsberg finns: Deep inside a rock cavern in Edsberg lies Elefanten, 'the Elephant' – a command centre built in 1972–77 to withstand a nuclear bomb, with room for 200 people. It was meant to protect the leaders of Stockholm and Sollentuna municipalities in the event of war. After standing empty for 19 years, it was bought in 2017 by the Swedish Armed Forces, who modernised it and put it back into service. Above ground, life is more peaceful, with Edsberg church, a red wooden church.
Djupt under campus forskade man en gång: Deep under the campus, scientists once carried out research in accelerator physics. Since 2019 the old laboratory has been the Accelerator art gallery, opened by the artist Tino Sehgal. The lab is named after Manne Siegbahn, winner of the 1924 Nobel Prize in Physics. Ralph Erskine designed the Law Building as a semicircle wrapped around an old oak – and the same idea of sparing the oaks shaped Aula Magna too.
Djupt under fötterna, 27 till 36 meter n: Deep below your feet, 27 to 36 metres down in the bedrock, is the metro station, opened in 1975. Above it is one of the biggest shopping centres in the Stockholm region, with more than 95 shops and 22 restaurants. Across Centralvägen is Eric Grate's Park, named after the sculptor, who spent the last fifteen years of his life in Solna. Two of his bronzes stand there: Oberon and Sparvguden, the Sparrow God.
Djursholm är villornas rike, och i närhe: Djursholm is a world of grand villas, and nearby is Villa Snellman, one of the early works of the architect Gunnar Asplund. Djursholm's own Strandvägen, along the waters of Lilla and Stora Värtan, is often counted among the most exclusive addresses in Sweden. The Djursholm railway, Djursholmsbanan, used to run past here, and for many years there was a little kiosk selling sweets and newspapers on the narrow platform at the Bragevägen stop.
Djursholms slott ägdes av ätten Banér i: Djursholm Castle belonged to the Banér family for over 300 years, from 1508 to 1813, and parts of it date from the late Middle Ages. Today it's the municipal hall – and you can hire its banqueting rooms for a wedding. On the hill next door is the water tower from 1890. It was built beside a little Dutch-style windmill, which was pulled down shortly afterwards. And Djursholm's co-educational school, founded in 1891, stood just nearby.
Domkyrkan, ofta öppen dagtid: Gothenburg Cathedral, usually open during the day
Donsö är en levande skärgårdsö med Donsö: Donsö is a lively archipelago island with its own church and more than 1,500 year-round residents. A little to the south is tiny Kårholmen, which has a lovely story. On 7 May 1933, twenty people hired a motorboat, founded a club called Arbetarna till havet – “Workers to the Sea” – and were allowed to take over the island. They were all poor working people, and today the island is almost entirely covered with just over 80 summer cottages.
Drottningtorget ligger mitt framför Cent: Drottningtorget is the square right in front of the Central Station, which opened in 1858 and is one of the oldest station buildings in Sweden still in use. Much of the Nordic region's largest tram network sets off from here. Gothenburg got horse-drawn trams in 1879 and electric ones in 1902, and while many other Swedish cities scrapped their trams, Gothenburg chose to keep them.
Du är nu i Majorna, strax väster om Mast: You're now in Majorna, just west of Masthugget, where ships' masts were once hewn. Up on the hill stands Masthuggskyrkan, the Masthugget church from 1914 and one of the city's best-known landmarks. By the square are the Maritime Museum and Aquarium and Sjömanstornet, the Sailors' Tower, topped by the statue of a sailor's wife gazing out over the river for ships that never came home.
Du är nu i Masthugget, där fartygens mas: You're now in Masthugget, where ships' masts were once hewn. Up on the hill stands Masthuggskyrkan, the Masthugget church from 1914 and one of the city's best-known landmarks. By the square you'll find the Maritime Museum and Aquarium and Sjömanstornet, the Sailors' Tower, topped by the statue of a sailor's wife gazing out over the river for ships that never came home.
Duggregnet 5 vid Björkhagsplan ritades a: Duggregnet 5 at Björkhagsplan was designed by the architect Georg Varhelyi, and anyone who knows Le Corbusier's famous Unité d'Habitation in Marseille will spot the family likeness straight away. When it went up in 1957 it was Stockholm's tallest residential building, and today the City Museum has marked it blue, its highest grade. Down in the metro station are artworks by Lenka Jonesson, unveiled in 1991.
Duvnäs nämns i skrift redan 1436, men vi: Duvnäs is mentioned in records as early as 1436, but the villas didn't arrive until the Saltsjöbanan railway opened its station here in 1893. In Ringparken stands Herrgårdsvillan, the Manor Villa, built in 1910–11 as a show home to tempt buyers to the new building plots. The park is also home to Ringparksstugan, a cottage where neighbours get together for their yearly celebrations. A little further on, Kvarngården – the miller's house from the mid-1700s – is a reminder of the old watermill that once stood by Duvnäsviken bay.
Där Alviks gamla industriområde en gång: Alvik's old industrial area by Lake Mälaren is now mostly offices and a handful of restaurants. Gamla Tryckeriet, the Old Printworks, is an events venue nearby where the TV competition show Floor Filler was recorded. The Tvärbanan light rail plunges into the rock through the Alvik tunnel, about 250 metres long, and then crosses the Oxhålssundet strait on the 400-metre Alvik bridge, completed in 2000.
Där Husby står i dag övade militären änd: Where Husby stands today, soldiers were still training right up until 1965, as Järvafältet was a military training ground. The district was built in 1971 and was first called Husby gård. Today it has Husbybadet, a swimming centre with an adventure pool, a 25-metre pool and a diving tower with 1- and 3-metre boards.
Där Obs! Stormarknad slog upp portarna 1: Where the Obs! Stormarknad hypermarket opened its doors in 1963, there was once Haga gård, an outlying farm of the Vårby estate that was pulled down in the early 20th century. The store building is still here, but Obs! closed in 1998 and furniture shops moved in. Right next door is Fittjanäset, and across the narrow strait to Fittja ran Fittja bro, the Fittja bridge – the main road south out of Stockholm until the end of the 1950s.
Där Skärholmens centrum ligger i dag fan: Where Skärholmen centrum stands today there was once a farm, Smista gård, dating back to at least the 800s, and people were living nearby as early as the 200s, in the Roman Iron Age. In the 1700s and 1800s Smista was an outlying farm belonging to Vårby gård. Today you'll find, among other things, the Red Cross folk high school, some of whose courses even travel abroad, and Skärisbiografen, a cinema that opened in 2017.
Där Stockholmsmässan står i dag låg en g: Where Stockholmsmässan, the Stockholm exhibition centre, stands today, there used to be a lake. Brännkyrkasjön, also called Kyrksjön, lay just south of Brännkyrka Church and was drained bit by bit, from the 1870s right through to the 1950s. Since 1971 the exhibition halls and car parks have occupied the western side of the old lake bed, while the eastern side is still mostly open land.
Där Ulriksdals Golfklubb ligger i dag gi: Where Ulriksdal Golf Club is today, the pace used to be much faster – this was once the site of the Ulriksdal racecourse. The commuter rail station is 7.1 kilometres from Stockholm Central, on the line towards Märsta, and took on its present look in 1990, with the ticket hall on the platform and the entrance through a pedestrian tunnel.
Där bostadsområdet Minneberg ligger låg: The Minneberg housing area stands on the site of the old Stockholm Bonemeal Factory, which turned out glue, bone oil, chicken feed and even a washing powder called Pärlglans. The smelly business moved away in 1968, and Minneberg was built in the 1980s. Next door is Tranebergs gård, a farm that goes back to a ferryman's croft from the 1670s. The croft was named Traneberg after its owner, Bengt Trana.
Där bostadsområdet Rissne ligger i dag h: The Rissne housing estate stands on old military ground. The Svea Artillery Regiment had its barracks here until 1963, and the Ordnance Administration School took over the site until 1977. The blocks of flats only went up between 1982 and 1988. Fittingly, the square was called Dragonplan, Dragoon Square, before it was renamed Rissne torg.
When the sun shines on Hisingen, there's electricity to be harvested. The Nya Solevi solar park, in Säve north-west of Gothenburg, is designed to produce around 5.5 gigawatt hours a year. It went up in record time: the first spade went into the ground in September 2018 and it opened in December the same year. While it was being planned, it was called Säve Solcellspark.
Där villorna står i dag låg förr åkrar s: The villas you see today stand on what were once fields belonging to Viksjö gård, a farm that goes back to prehistoric times. In 1921 the farm was sold to Viksjö AB, which went on farming the land, but in 1963 a group of builders began developing the area. The result is a mix of villas and terraced houses from the 1960s, 70s and 80s, with patches of nature in between.
Edsbacka krog vid Edsviken blev den förs: Edsbacka krog, by the Edsviken bay, became the first restaurant in Sweden to hold two Michelin stars, under the restaurateur Christer Lingström. The stars went when it changed hands in 2010, but since spring 2021 the restaurant has once again been called Edsbacka krog. Back in the 17th century, a fallen runestone lay just north of the restaurant; its base now stands just south of the avenue up to Edsberg Palace.
Edsbergs centrum invigdes 1964 och fick: Edsbergs centrum opened in 1964 and was given a makeover around 2004, including a new multi-storey car park. Here you'll find a library, a pharmacy, an Ica supermarket and two grill restaurants, Oscar and Ló Mero Kök och Bar. Right next door is Edsbergskyrkan, a red wooden church belonging to Sollentuna parish. The district is also home to Edsberg Palace, Rudbecksskolan school and the Edsbacka krog restaurant.
Edsbergs centrum invigdes 1964 och har b: Edsbergs centrum opened in 1964 and has a library, shops and a couple of grill bars. Right beside it stands Edsbergskyrkan, a red wooden church. And somewhere in the rock not far away lies Elefanten, 'the Elephant' – a command centre built in the 1970s to withstand a nuclear bomb, and now back in use by the Swedish Armed Forces.
Edsbergs slott stod färdigt 1760 vid Eds: Edsberg Palace, on the northern shore of Edsviken bay, was completed in 1760 at the initiative of Thure Gustaf Rudbeck, and the Rudbeck family owned it for almost 200 years. Today part of the Royal College of Music's chamber music programme is based here, and the palace has its own wedding room. Close by is Edsbacka krog, the first restaurant in Sweden to win two Michelin stars.
Edsängens gravfält, ett par hundra meter: A couple of hundred metres away is the Edsängen burial ground, with around 125 Viking Age mounds – one of the largest in Sollentuna. Not far from there is something completely different: Elefanten, the Elephant, a command centre blasted into the rock and built to withstand a nuclear bomb. Closest of all is Rudbecksskolan, one of Sweden's biggest sixth-form schools, with around 2,400 students and a national athletics programme.
Efter badet: The sculpture Efter badet, 'After the Swim'
Ekebyhovskyrkan, en bit härifrån, är mer: Ekebyhovskyrkan, Ekebyhov Church, a little way from here, is more than just a church. It's part of a church centre that houses the parish office for every parish in the Ekerö pastorate, and it even has its own full-time preschool. A little further on is Tappström, a narrow strait about one and a half kilometres long and only just over three metres deep, which separates the islands of Lovön and Ekerön.
Ekensberg har fått sitt namn efter värds: Ekensberg takes its name from the Ekensberg inn, built in the early 1700s and still standing at Gröndalsvägen 184. Between 1926 and 1934, Ekensberg was the name for most of what's now called Gröndal. The headland lies between Mörtviken bay and the Essingesundet channel.
Ekerö centrum, en bit härifrån vid Tapps: Ekerö centrum, a little way from here at Tappström, is easy to spot thanks to its navigation marker, more than twenty metres tall. The area was designed by Ralph Erskine, who lived on the island of Lovön himself, and his vision was to create a little town on Lake Mälaren. Of all his projects, Erskine was proudest of this one, saying it worked as a complete community. From Tappström, commuter boat 89 runs all the way to Stadshuskajen, the City Hall quay in Stockholm.
Ekerö är främst en bostadsort, och den s: Ekerö is mainly a place to live, and most commuters head into Stockholm. Until 1990, the village of Träkvista, not far from here, was the centre of the municipality. That year Ekerö centrum, designed by the architect Ralph Erskine, opened and took over the role. Träkvista torg still has a supermarket, a pizzeria and a restaurant, though.
Ekerö, inte att förväxla med åländska Ec: Ekerö – not to be confused with Eckerö in Åland – lies on the island of Ekerön in eastern Lake Mälaren and is the main town of Ekerö municipality. Ekerö centrum was designed by the renowned architect Ralph Erskine and opened in 1990; before that, Träkvista was the heart of the town. The biggest employer here is the municipality itself.

Ekerö – not to be confused with Eckerö in Åland – is the main town of Ekerö municipality. It's mainly a place to live, and most people commute into Stockholm. Ekerö centrum at Tappström was designed by Ralph Erskine, and its hallmark is a dot more than twenty metres up, standing over the shops like a navigation marker. In the past, though, the heart of the town was Träkvista.
Eklanda är en ung stadsdel med gamla röt: Eklanda is a young district with old roots. For a long time there was just a small cluster of older buildings here, but from 1993 houses began springing up, and now there are about 700. The Änggårdsbergen nature reserve is right next door, making the area a playground for the many families with children who live here.
Eklanda är stadsdelen där barnfamiljerna: Eklanda is a district that families with children have made their own. Since building started in 1993, around 700 homes have sprung up, with about 3,100 residents, right next to the Änggårdsbergen nature reserve. A short way from here, in Åby, is Åbytravet, Sweden's second-largest trotting track.
Elektraparken har fått sitt namn efter E: Elektraparken takes its name from Elektraverken, which made electrical measuring instruments nearby from 1917. Between 1915 and 1944 the site was home to Södra folkparken, a 'people's park' for open-air entertainment. In 1939 the building magnate Olle Engkvist built a lavish villa for himself and his wife Signhild on Västberga allé, but Villa Engkvist was knocked down as early as 1967–68 to make room for an industrial building.
Elementens kamp: Elementens kamp – “The Battle of the Elements”
En biograf blev början på en hel butiksk: A cinema was the start of an entire chain of shops. Saga, on Sofiagatan, showed films from 1942 to 1964. When Bengt Johansson bought the closed cinema, he opened a grocery there – Saga hemköp, the first of the Sagabutikerna shops. Right next door was Härlanda prison, in use from 1907 to 1997. Its walls are still standing as a listed building, and since 2011 the area has been called Härlanda park.
En bit bort breder Ryssbergen ut sig, en: A little way off are the Ryssbergen hills, around 30 hectares of pine forest on bare rock, rising to 60 metres above sea level. Down below, in Ryssviken, is Marinstaden, a neighbourhood in an old harbour where people live right on the water. In the other direction is Birka, one of Nacka's oldest residential areas, where the first houses were built for factory workers in the 1880s.
En bit bort går Kongahällavägen, Hisinge: Not far off runs Kongahällavägen, the oldest country road on Hisingen, stretching about 23 kilometres from Torslanda to Eriksdal, south of Kungälv's fortress. Until 1970 it was called Kungälvsvägen. The new name uses the old spelling of the royal estate of Kungahälla, which lay roughly where Ragnhildsholmen is, by the Nordre älv river.
En bit bort ligger Angereds Centrum, knu: Not far away is Angereds Centrum, the local hub, with around sixty shops and restaurants and the end of the line for three tram routes. The decision to build it was taken unanimously by the municipal executive board in 1975. On Angereds torg stands Blå Stället, an arts centre with a library, cinema, theatre and restaurant, and by the terminus is Angered Local Hospital, opened in 2015.
En bit bort ligger Glose, sydväst om Kär: Not far away is Glose, south-west of Kärna in Kungälv municipality. The shore meadows along the Ryskärsfjorden inlet are so rich in birds and plants that Swedish Radio has broadcast its nature programme Naturmorgon live from there. The area is both a nature reserve and a protected Natura 2000 site, and the county authorities rank it among the most valuable natural areas in the region.
En bit bort ligger Kästadalsparken, en l: A little further on is Kästadalsparken, a playground in the Kästa villa area where everything is inspired by fairy tales. Flemingsberg Church was built in 1975–1976 to designs by Gunnar Cedervall and consecrated by Bishop Ingmar Ström in August 1976. Nearby also stood Hagstaeken, the Hagsta oak – Huddinge's largest oak and a protected natural monument – until it was felled in December 2025.
En bit bort ligger Preemraff Göteborg, e: A little way off is Preemraff Göteborg, a refinery that can process around six million tonnes of crude oil a year. Most of the oil comes from the North Sea and is stored in huge caverns in the rock. Even ULCC-class ships, the biggest tankers in the world at 333 metres long and 60 metres wide, have docked at the crude oil harbour on Hjärtholmen.
En bit bort ligger pingstkyrkan Aspnäsky: A little further on is Aspnäskyrkan, a Pentecostal church whose motto is “Discover faith, share hope, grow deeper in love”. In the same area is Aspnässkolan, which in 1846 became the first school in Järfälla parish to have its own building. It started out in an old roadside inn, and the original schoolhouse is now used as a shelter at the Ängsjö outdoor centre.
En bit bort svävar Angeredsbron, cirka 5: A little further on, Angeredsbron soars about 50 metres above the ground. This 930-metre bridge spans the E6 motorway, the Göta älv river, the E45 and the railway. Ships have 47 metres of clearance beneath it, and the spans between its piers are around 130 metres long. At one end the road runs straight into the Gårdsten tunnel, built in 1978 – 235 metres long, with three traffic lanes and a path for walkers and cyclists.
En bit bort, på Göta älvs östra strand,: Not far off, on the eastern bank of the Göta älv river, lies Agnesberg. Travellers have been stopping there for centuries – it was a coaching inn long before the railway station arrived in 1880. After that, industry moved in, including a paint maker and a flour-milling company. Across the river is Kärra, which goes by Hisings Kärra in postal addresses.
En bit härifrån breder Gunnestorps mosse: Not far from here lies Gunnestorps mosse, a bog where bulrushes, water lilies, cranberries and sundews grow. East of the bog, down towards Tuvevägen, runs a strip of meadow and broadleaf woodland. And on the northern edge of the bog are the ruins of Mosstorpet, now part of the Fruktträdgården playground.
En bit härifrån breder Kvibergs kyrkogår: Not far from here is Kviberg cemetery. At 130 hectares, it's the largest cemetery in Sweden and the second largest in northern Europe by area. It has over 24,000 graves, with room for 30,000 coffins and 50,000 urns. Gamlestadsvägen, which runs right past, has had its name since 1883.
En bit härifrån breder Trångsundsskogens: Not far from here, the Trångsundsskogen nature reserve stretches along the western shore of Lake Drevviken, from the swimming spot at Mörtviken to just north of Trångsund manor. The reserve was created in 2006 and covers 53 hectares, ten of them water – though the manor and its immediate grounds aren't part of it. Mörtviks gård, a farm, also stands at Mörtviken.
En bit härifrån breder naturreservatet V: Nearby lies the Välen nature reserve, a wetland at the far end of Askimsviken bay. Shaggy Highland cattle have grazed its shore meadows since 1992, and the reserve contains two ancient sites from the Bronze Age. In the other direction is Opaltorget, the end of the line for the Tynnered tram.
En bit härifrån breder villaområdet Nora: Not far from here lies the villa neighbourhood of Nora, about ten kilometres north of Stockholm. This used to be farmland, but in 1926 the fields of Nora gård began to be divided up into villa plots. In the same area is the lake Nora träsk, which drains into the Åkerström-Norrström coastal catchment.
En bit härifrån byggs tunnelbanestatione: Not far from here, the new Barkarbystaden metro station is under construction, right in the middle of the urban development of the same name. In the other direction is Järfälla Church, where in 1728 Olof Celsius wrote about a runestone outside the porch door. He described it as lost and worn away – and sure enough, nobody has seen it since. Further off is Kyrkbyn, the church village, which used to be called Järfälla gård.
En bit härifrån börjar Eklanda, en stads: A short way from here is Eklanda, a district in western Mölndal on the edge of the Änggårdsbergen nature reserve. Apart from a small core of older buildings, it wasn't developed until 1993, and today around 3,100 people live here, many of them families with children. The plan is for new housing on the farmland to the east to join Eklanda up with the village of Fässberg.
En bit härifrån börjar Görvälns naturres: A little way from here is the start of the Görväln nature reserve, which runs for almost eight kilometres along the unspoilt shore of Lake Mälaren, from Hässelby to Kallhäll. Inside it is Baset, an old croft that has been privately owned since 2021. But a legal right of way means the path down to the swimming spot has to stay open to everyone – so a dip in Mälaren is still free for all.
En bit härifrån börjar Pixbo, ett bostad: A short way from here begins Pixbo, a residential area on the southern side of Lake Rådasjön. Pixbo is very hilly, because it's built on and around a height called Björnåsen. It lies in Härryda municipality – apart from a handful of properties that belong to Mölndal – and has its own postal town.
En bit härifrån börjar Rågsveds friområd: Not far from here begins the Rågsved open space, also known as Kräppladalen: just over 100 hectares of countryside with some dramatic terrain – hills, valleys and steep slopes. In the middle of it lies the Snösätra storage area, which since 2014 has become a hub for graffiti and street art, with façades and walls painted with the owners' blessing. Nature and spray cans, side by side.
En bit härifrån börjar naturreservatet J: Not far from here the Jonsereds strömmar nature reserve begins, following the Säveån river valley from the bridge at Kåhög to Lake Aspen. It's mixed broadleaf woodland with a rich variety of fungi, including the red-listed smoky finger fungus. Keep an eye out for grey wagtails, kingfishers and dippers – birds that love running water.
En bit härifrån börjar naturreservatet Ä: Just along from here begins the Älta mosse–Strålsjön nature reserve, set up in 1995 and covering 52 hectares. Together with the Strålsjön–Erstavik reserve it forms a large green area for walks and outdoor life, with little Lake Strålsjön at its heart. The lake's water is dark because it drains in from Älta mosse, a peaty bog, and it's home to pike, perch and roach.
En bit härifrån finns ett unikt minne fr: Not far from here is a unique relic of the Second World War. Käppalaställningen is an anti-aircraft position with several foxholes and three gun emplacements. It was restored and reopened in 1994 as a protected monument to Stockholm's air defences – the only one of its kind in Sweden.
En bit härifrån gick förr den numera ned: The now-closed Djursholm railway ran a short way from here, and from 1924 Valevägen had its own stop, Bragevägen, with a kiosk selling sweets and newspapers on its narrow platform. It closed in 1976. Until the 1920s, the train ran through open fields here. Not far away, at Hildingavägen 26, is the Laurin Villa, designed in 1910 by the architect Karl Güettler.
En bit härifrån går Bullegummans gata, m: Not far from here runs Bullegummans gata, the Bun Lady's Street, and it comes with a sweet story. In the 1930s, a Mrs Liljegren lived here who baked such good buns that the children on their way to Påvelundsskolan school just couldn't resist them. So she cut a hatch in the wall of her house and sold buns through it, and the locals came to know her as Bullegumman, the Bun Lady. The house still stands in its original state, and the hatch was still there as recently as 2011.
En bit härifrån går Marieholmsbron, en b: Not far from here is Marieholmsbron, a bridge carrying trains, pedestrians and cyclists from Gamlestaden over the Säveån and Göta älv rivers to Tingstad on Hisingen. The section over the Göta älv is a swing bridge that pivots to let boats through. It's part of the Bohusbanan railway and links Gothenburg's harbour railway to the rest of the rail network.
En bit härifrån gömmer sig något unikt:: A short way from here is something unique: Hammarkullen, the only fully underground tram stop in Sweden. It lies 25 metres below ground and was modelled on Stockholm's metro stations, because in the 1970s there were plans to run a metro out to Angered. The platforms are built for 120-metre trains, but only 70 metres of them are used today.
En bit härifrån höll Sollentunamässan ti: Not far from here stood Sollentunamässan, the Sollentuna exhibition centre, which opened in 1973. With just over 17,000 square metres of exhibition space, it was Sweden's third-largest trade fair venue until it closed in 2008 and Kistamässan took over. Demolition began on 24 May 2017, and homes are now going up where the exhibition halls once stood.
En bit härifrån korsar Gamlestadsbron Sä: Not far from here, Gamlestadsbron, the Gamlestaden bridge, crosses the Säveån river – and there's been a bridge on this spot for more than 500 years. When Nya Lödöse was founded in 1473, traffic was heavy, as the main road to Norway passed this way. In the summer of 1723 the city architect Johan Eberhard Carlberg was given permission to build a brand-new wooden bridge, but by January 1724 it had been swept away by a fierce flood carrying timber.
En bit härifrån ligger Akalla, en stadsd: Not far from here is Akalla, a district on the Järvafältet plain, built between 1972 and 1977 at the same time as its neighbours Husby and Kista. Running through it is Sibeliusgången, a 900-metre walkway named after the Finnish composer Jean Sibelius. Along the way you'll pass bubbling fountains by the artist Bertil Johnson, put up in 1976 – among them the Akalla fountain in a little square.
En bit härifrån ligger Angereds sporthal: A short way from here, by Angered Centrum, is the Angered sports hall, with room for 400 people. It's the home ground of the handball club GIK Wasaiterna – and of the roller derby team Dock City Rollers, whose players race round the track on roller skates. Next door are Angered Arena and the Angeredsvallen sports ground.
En bit härifrån ligger Arendalsbanan, sp: A short way from here is Arendalsbanan, the speedway track that was home to the Kaparna team. Its attendance record of 5,940 spectators was set in September 2002, when Kaparna took on Rospiggarna. The track record, 60.1 seconds, was set in September 2004 by none other than Tony Rickardsson, then riding for Masarna.
En bit härifrån ligger Arken kombitermin: Not far from here is the Arken combi terminal, where semi-trailers are lifted between ships and trains. It was built because the old terminal at Gullbergs vass and Central Station had to move to make way for the Västlänken rail tunnel. Construction began in 2018, and it opened in 2019. Arendal itself was once home to a large shipyard, Arendalsvarvet, which operated from 1963 to 1989.
En bit härifrån ligger Askims norra kyrk: Not far from here is Askim's northern churchyard, and just north of it is an Iron Age burial ground with around eighty burial mounds. In the early Middle Ages the parish church was built on this spot, but it burned down in 1876. A memorial stone in the churchyard marks where the old church once stood.
En bit härifrån ligger Bandhagens tunnel: A short way from here is Bandhagen metro station, designed by Magnus Ahlgren and opened on 22 November 1954. From there it's six and a half kilometres to Slussen. Rising beside Bandhagen's centre is the Murbruket block, an eleven-storey slab block from 1955 that the Stockholm City Museum has classed as culturally valuable.
En bit härifrån ligger Bastusjön, en lit: Not far from here is Bastusjön, a small lake in Skuru that's lovely for a swim. It's almost six metres deep, and home to perch, roach and two kinds of freshwater mussel. A little further on is Solsunda, which was called Skuru gård until 1922. In the 16th century King Gustav Vasa gave the estate to Danvik's Hospital, and since the early 20th century the main house has served as a rest and treatment home.
En bit härifrån ligger Beckomberga, där: A little way from here is Beckomberga, where the Beckomberga psychiatric hospital stood from the 1930s until it closed in 1995. The hospital was built in 1930–32, and in the mid-2000s work began on turning the old buildings into flats. Bromma sjukhus, Bromma Hospital, in Beckomberga has been a care home since 2020.
En bit härifrån ligger Benareby, inklämt: Not far from here is Benareby, squeezed between the lakes Nordsjön, Yxsjön, Finnsjön and Gravsjön. The village was once known for its wooden barrels, made mainly for the fish-processing industry, and the coopering tradition has survived right up to the present day. Closest to the stop is the little lake Abborrtjärnen.
En bit härifrån ligger Benareby, mellan: A little way from here is Benareby, nestled between the lakes Nordsjön, Yxsjön, Finnsjön and Gravsjön. Benareby was once known for its wooden barrels, which mostly went to the fish-processing industry, and the barrel-making tradition is still alive today. There are also lots of old summer cottages here that people now live in all year round.
En bit härifrån ligger Biskopsgårdens ky: Not far from here is Biskopsgården Church, consecrated in 1961 by Bishop Bo Giertz. At the consecration he burned the cross into the church door himself – you can see it on the door facing Vårvädersgatan. At first only a small chapel was planned, but when the parish was formed it became the parish church. It was originally called Södra Biskopsgården Church, but changed its name when Norra Biskopsgården Church was deconsecrated in 2004.
En bit härifrån ligger Björlanda, den ga: Not far from here is Björlanda, the old church village of Björlanda parish on Hisingen. It has struggled to make up its mind: first a town of its own, then part of Torslanda, then on its own again from 2018, and since 2023 it has counted as part of the Gothenburg urban area. The houses cluster around the church, and most of them were built in the 1990s.
En bit härifrån ligger Bäckebols gård, e: Not far from here is Bäckebols gård, a manor house whose stone building was begun in 1764 and is now listed. It comes with a curious extra: Friedländerska kyrkogården, a privately owned cemetery with just over twenty graves – the smallest cemetery in Gothenburg.
En bit härifrån ligger Dammträsket, i fo: Not far from here is Dammträsket, known locally as Dammkärr, a small lake that has recently been turned into a stormwater pond. On its shore is Mellanberg, an old croft and smallholding where you can still see traces of laundering and farming in the surroundings. A little further on is Kvarntorp, which began as a watermill and appears on maps as early as 1638.
En bit härifrån ligger Danderyds gymnasi: Not far from here is Danderyds gymnasium, a sixth-form school that opened in 1982 and is one of the largest in Stockholm County, with 1,390 students in 2024. The area around it is called Rinkeby – but this is a farm and housing area in Danderyd, not to be confused with the district of the same name in northern Stockholm.
En bit härifrån ligger Djupedal, med mån: Not far from here is Djupedal, with lots of stables and two hill forts above the village. Just a few kilometres north, on Ragnhildsholmen in the Nordre älv river, stood the castle of the Norwegian king Håkon the Old. Closer to hand is Klareberg, where bus drivers take their breaks and riders and dog owners do their training.
En bit härifrån ligger Drottning Silvias: Not far from here is Queen Silvia Children's Hospital, the biggest children's hospital in Sweden, with about 1,900 staff and around 45,000 patient visits a year. Since 1997 it has been based in the old Östra sjukhuset hospital. Children come here from all over the Gothenburg area – and for the most specialised care, from all over the country.
En bit härifrån ligger Fredrikshamns ska: Not far from here is the Fredrikshamn redoubt, a small fort that recalls the year 1645. In the closing stages of the Hannibal Controversy, a war between Sweden and Denmark-Norway, Hannibal Sehested tried to attack Gothenburg, and Norwegian troops threw a temporary bridge across the river to the Swedish east bank. The redoubt was built to guard the bridgehead here on Hisingen.
En bit härifrån ligger Fridhems kyrkogår: Not far from here is Fridhem Cemetery, a vast 87-hectare burial ground consecrated in 1968. It includes one of the Church of Sweden's three Islamic burial grounds in Gothenburg. For the first fourteen years a travelling church stood in as a temporary chapel, until the present chapel was consecrated in 1982. Closer to the stop, the Bäckebol Center retail park spreads out around you.
En bit härifrån ligger Frölunda torg, ri: Not far from here is Frölunda torg. Designed by the architects Hjalmar Klemming, Lars Grönlund and Erik Thelaus, it took seven years and 80 million kronor to build. When Olof Palme opened it in 1966, it was the largest shopping centre under one roof in the Nordic countries. Gothenburgers, by the way, are famous for their puns, and they have a long tradition of giving buildings witty nicknames.
En bit härifrån ligger Gaisgården, Gais: Not far from here is Gaisgården, the training ground of the football club Gais, and it has had a dramatic history. One June morning in 1996 it was hit by fire, but it was rebuilt. Before the 2009 derby against IFK Göteborg, someone painted one of its gable walls in IFK's blue and white, and the Gais chairman reported it to the police. A bit further on is Lake Stora Delsjön, up to 22.5 metres deep.
En bit härifrån ligger Gothia Arena, hem: Not far from here is Gothia Arena, home of the Högsbo Basket club. The hall has three courts; it's the only club-owned sports hall in Gothenburg and one of the biggest club-owned basketball halls in Sweden. The fixed stand seats around 500, and with retractable seating and extra chairs it can hold 1,000 spectators on match days.
En bit härifrån ligger Gunnestorps mosse: Not far from here is Gunnestorps mosse, a bog that's part of S.A. Hedlund's park and Hisingsparken. North of the bog are the ruins of an old croft called Mosstorpet. They're now part of the Fruktträdgården adventure playground, so children play today where a crofter's family once lived.
En bit härifrån ligger Hammarkulletorget: A little way from here is Hammarkulletorget, a square built in 1971. When it was revamped in 1997 it got new colours and a new shape. To get there you take the tram and get off at what's known as Gothenburg's only underground station. Closer to this stop is Eriksbo, part of the Hjällbo district.
En bit härifrån ligger Hässelby slott, u: A short way from here is Hässelby slott, Hässelby Palace. Built in the 1650s, possibly to designs by Simon de la Vallée, it's one of the oldest surviving secular buildings in Stockholm. This former noble estate only started being called a palace when the Hässelby gård district was created, to avoid mixing the two up. By the entrance a runestone stands on a Viking Age burial mound. It was moved there in the 1860s from Skesta backe, about three kilometres away.
En bit härifrån ligger Högsbo pegmatitbr: Not far from here is the Högsbo pegmatite quarry – two old quarries about 200 metres apart. Feldspar, quartz, mica and beryl were mined here from 1945 until the late 1950s, and rare minerals such as monazite, columbite and bismuthinite turned up too. Since 2016 the area has been part of the Änggårdsbergen nature reserve.
En bit härifrån ligger Imam Ali-moskén,: Not far from here is the Imam Ali Mosque, considered the largest Shia Muslim congregation in all the Nordic countries, with activities in several languages. All around you is Jakobsberg, Järfälla's commercial and administrative centre, just over 15 kilometres north of central Stockholm.
En bit härifrån ligger Isolda, en tremas: A short way from here lies Isolda, a three-masted schooner built at the Lödöse shipyard in 1902. She was the last Swedish merchant sailing ship in ocean trade, sailing to the West Indies, Mexico, South America and West Africa. The same skipper, Carl Julius Ahlgren, commanded her for just over fifty years, from 1909 to 1960, and she didn't get a diesel engine to help her along until 1928.
En bit härifrån ligger Järnbrottsmotet,: Not far from here is Järnbrottsmotet, an unusual double-trumpet interchange. It works just like a proper motorway junction, even though none of the roads is actually signposted as a motorway. It was built in the 1990s on the site of the Europa roundabout – an unusually large roundabout that the Söderleden road cut straight across, controlled by traffic lights.
En bit härifrån ligger Klare mosse, en l: A short way from here is Klare mosse, a small pond that's one of the best spots on Hisingen for frogs and newts. Among them is the rare great crested newt, which thrives in all the little pools and hollows. The pond was overgrown for many years, but thanks to the Osbäck project it's in much better shape today.
En bit härifrån ligger Komettorget, där: Not far from here is Komettorget, where the tram turns round and two bus routes connect. Around the square is a centre with shops and a restaurant, along with some well-tended allotments. A footpath with steps climbs to a hilltop and the large housing areas on Kosmosgatan and Universumsgatan.
En bit härifrån ligger Kornhall, en hamn: A little way from here is Kornhall, a harbour and small village on the Nordre älv river, just inside the river's estuary. There's a small shipyard and a marina, but Kornhall is best known for Kornhallsleden, a ferry crossing with a long history that cuts the journey to Gothenburg considerably. The name refers to the spot where grain – korn – was loaded and unloaded.
En bit härifrån ligger Kungshamn, en ham: Not far from here is Kungshamn, a harbour already in use in the Middle Ages and mentioned in the 13th century in Bjärköarätten, an early town law. This is where the king of the Svear assembled his ledung – the fleet raised from the people – before it set sail for foreign shores or to meet the enemy. Just offshore lies Sveriges holme, 'Sweden's Islet', with Danmarks holme, 'Denmark's Islet', further out. Sveriges holme was given to the state in 1937 and is now a protected nature reserve.
En bit härifrån ligger Kvastekulla grift: Not far from here is Kvastekulla griftegård, a cemetery designed by the Finnish architects Bengt Lundsten and Per-Mauritz Ålander, who won a Nordic architecture competition for it. Their aim was to keep the beautiful landscape intact, disturbing nature as little as possible. The cemetery opened in 1959, followed four years later by the chapel, with its walls of bare concrete and its copper roof.
En bit härifrån ligger Kvastekulla kapel: Not far from here is Kvastekulla chapel, a building that really stands out. Its walls are bare concrete, its roofs are clad in copper, and a tower-like lantern rises above the chancel. The chapel was consecrated four years after the cemetery, which was completed in 1959 and designed to blend in with the landscape.
En bit härifrån ligger Kåhög, ett litet: Not far from here is Kåhög, a small community of villas by the Säveån river north of the E20, close to both Gothenburg and Lake Aspen. A little further on is Lexby, where the actor and director Sissela Kyle grew up. She writes about her childhood there in her autobiography, CV. Livets gång.
En bit härifrån ligger Lilla Varholmen,: Not far from here is Lilla Varholmen, an island next to Hjuvik that's linked to Hisingen by a bridge. Car ferries leave from there for the islands of Öckerö municipality, and buses run all the way into the Nils Ericson terminal in central Gothenburg. The island has a long history of lighthouses, and the leading lights that stand there today date from 1927.
En bit härifrån ligger Lillhagsparkens s: Not far from here is Lillhagsparkens sjukhus, originally Lillhagen, a hospital for the mentally ill. Gothenburgers just called it Lillhagen, Hagen or LS. There's no care there any more; the forensic psychiatry unit moved out in 2013. Closer to the stop was Hökälla säteri, an old manor estate in Skogome.
En bit härifrån ligger Lundadepån, en av: Not far from here is Lundadepån, one of SL's bus depots, in use since 2009. It has room for 75 buses plus workshops, and since August 2024 its routes have been run by Keolis. A little closer is something much older: Kälvesta kvarn, a 17th-century windmill that was moved here from Observatoriegatan in central Stockholm.
En bit härifrån ligger Långsjön, en grun: A short way from here is Långsjön, a shallow lake just three metres deep that marks the border between Stockholm and Huddinge, between the villa suburbs of Herrängen and Segeltorp. Along its northern shore is Långsjö gård, which dates back to the 17th century, when it was a croft belonging to the Långbro estate. The farm has given its name to the whole Långsjö district.
En bit härifrån ligger Lövsta sopstation: A little way from here is the Lövsta waste station. For much of the 20th century it was the main site for dealing with Stockholm's household rubbish, and it later became a pioneer in using waste to produce district heating. And here's a curious fact: Hässelby existed as a district administration only in 1997 and 1998, before it was merged with Vällingby.
En bit härifrån ligger Malmvik, en herrg: Not far from here is Malmvik, a manor going back to the 14th century. On a wooded knoll south of Ekerövägen lies the Wallenberg family burial ground, known as the Wallenberg Mausoleum. Lindö, incidentally, was once an island in its own right, but as the land has slowly risen since the Ice Age, it has joined up with Lovön through a 200-metre-wide isthmus at Lindöbro.
En bit härifrån ligger Novum Forskningsp: A short way from here is Novum Research Park. Its white concrete buildings, with window frames in different colours, are meant to bridge the gap between the hospital's concrete and the tower blocks of Flemingsberg. The idea is that companies will take researchers' discoveries further. All around is Campus Flemingsberg, with some 17,000 students from five universities and colleges.
En bit härifrån ligger Partille Arena, i: Not far from here is Partille Arena, which opened in September 2016. Swedish Radio has held its P3 Guldgalan music awards there several years running, and in April 2018 Bryan Adams set the attendance record, playing to 5,503 people. The arena is also home to the women's and men's teams of the handball club IK Sävehof.
En bit härifrån ligger Pinntorp, en lite: A little way from here is Pinntorp, a small village in Landvetter parish, close to Tahult. Beside it is a forest called Pinntorpaberg, which – as the name suggests – grows mostly on a hill, or berg. The village has a famous former resident, too: the road racing motorcyclist Kent Andersson once lived in Pinntorp. Since 2023 it has officially been part of the Landvetter urban area.
En bit härifrån ligger Rissne torg, som: Just up the road is Rissne torg, the square once known as Dragonplan, where an eight-sided building has become the local landmark. Deep below it, 25 to 40 metres down in the bedrock, is Rissne metro station. Its artwork is a lettered timeline of world history, running from 3000 BC to 1985 – the year the station opened. The work is by Madeleine Dranger and Rolf H Reimers.
En bit härifrån ligger Rågsveds tunnelba: Not far from here is Rågsved metro station. It opened on 14 November 1959 and was the end of the line until 1960, when the tracks were extended to Hagsätra. The platform is outdoors, and on it stands Fågel Grön, 'Green Bird', a bronze sculpture by the artist Björn Selder. The metro cuts the district neatly in two, with the iconic horseshoe-shaped centre on one side.
En bit härifrån ligger Råtjärnen, en rik: Not far from here is Råtjärnen, a true miniature lake of just 0.012 square kilometres, 75 metres above sea level. A bit further on, by Lake Finnsjön, is the little village of Lahall, which for a long time had just two farms. Holiday cottages were later built on their land, and many of them have since become year-round homes.
En bit härifrån ligger Selma Lagerlöfs t: A little way from here is Selma Lagerlöfs torg, the square where Bäckebol's church hall once stood. It belonged to Bäckebol parish, which merged with Backa parish in 2010. But the name Bäckebol lives on as a district of its own in northern Gothenburg, on Hisingen. The square was built in 1971 and is named after the Nobel Prize-winning author Selma Lagerlöf.
En bit härifrån ligger Skarpnäcksfältet,: Not far from here is Skarpnäcksfältet, once an airfield. For many years it hosted the Skarpnäcksloppet motor race, and the last air show took place in August 1980. Since then a residential area has grown up on the field. Closer by is the Gubbängen business area, also known as the Norra Sköndal industrial area – one of the smallest in the city.
En bit härifrån ligger Skintebo, ett kus: A little way from here is Skintebo, a residential area by the coast that even has a copy of Kina slott, the Chinese Pavilion. In the other direction is Stora Svindal, about a kilometre north-east of Billdal. Until 2015 it counted as a little village of its own, but it has since grown together with Billdal.
En bit härifrån ligger Skrubbatriangeln,: A short way from here is Skrubbatriangeln, an industrial estate in the Skrubba district that opened in 1987. The name isn't hard to work out – the area is shaped like a triangle. Skrubba is bordered by lake Drevviken to the west and south, and by Trollbäcken in Tyresö to the east. Further off, on the shore of Drevviken, is the Strandkyrkogården cemetery.
En bit härifrån ligger Sollentuna sjukhu: Not far from here is Sollentuna Hospital, which opened on 15 November 1978. The building has an unusual shape: an eight-storey slab ringed by nine lower, single-storey wings. It was completely renovated between 2015 and 2020, and at the same time it took over the urgent care centre from Löwenströmska Hospital.
En bit härifrån ligger Sophie Elkans gat: Not far from here is Sophie Elkans gata, named in 1992 after the Gothenburg-born writer Sophie Elkan, best remembered as Selma Lagerlöf's close friend. Also nearby is Gothia Park Academy, BK Häcken's clubhouse and training ground, with three full-size football pitches.
En bit härifrån ligger Storkällans kapel: A short way from here is Storkällan Chapel, in Storkällan Cemetery in Nacka. The name has a lovely story behind it: it comes from an open spring – storkällan means 'the big spring' – that still provides the forest animals with fresh water today. A peaceful spot where the wildlife has its very own drinking fountain.
En bit härifrån ligger Strålsjön, en lit: Not far from here is Strålsjön, a small, nutrient-poor forest lake tucked away in the nature reserves east of Älta. Its water is dark because it drains in from the peaty Älta bog. Small as it is, the lake has pike, perch and roach, and in the south-west bog myrtle is among the plants growing along the shore.
En bit härifrån ligger Tyresös centrum,: Not far from here is the centre of Tyresö, where the Tyresö View tower soars 82 metres and 23 storeys – in 2016 it was the fourth-tallest residential building in Stockholm County. Beside it is the Tyresö Centrum shopping mall under its glass roof, with 74 shops, the municipal offices and a library with its own exhibition hall, and Bollmoradalen Church, the parish church for the whole municipality.
En bit härifrån ligger Vidja, vid östra: A short way from here is Vidja, on the eastern shore of Lake Orlången. The village is something of a dead end: the only road in comes from the north, through Ågesta, and since 2018 the two have formed the district of Vidja-Ågesta. In the forests around Lissma lies Kvarnsjön, a long, narrow, shallow lake protected as a Natura 2000 site.
En bit härifrån ligger Villa Finedal, up: A short way from here is Villa Finedal, built in 1886 as a summer home for the fireworks maker Adolf Rickard Törner. The villa is of great cultural and historical value and has been listed since 1979. Closer by is the old folk high school. Missionsskolan, the mission school, moved here in 1908 from Högbergsgatan on Södermalm, and people trained here in mission work, development aid and music, among other things.
En bit härifrån ligger Wendelsbergs folk: Not far from here is Wendelsbergs folkhögskola, which opened in 1908 and is Sweden's oldest folk high school – a kind of adult education college – run by one of the popular movements. The wooden buildings were put up at the end of the 19th century by Bruno Wendel, who wanted a place where he and his wife could spend their old age. Instead it became a school, when the temperance movement bought the house in 1907.
En bit härifrån ligger byn Skändla, vars: Not far from here is the village of Skändla, whose name comes from Skinhälla – “the sunlit rock”. Like many of the wooded hills on northern Hisingen, Skändla was once an island in an archipelago. As the land slowly rose and the sea drew back, it became fertile ground that is still used for grazing and farming today. Closer to the stop, look out for the little lake of Holmdammen glinting in the light.
En bit härifrån ligger ett område som he: Not far from here is an area called Ingenting – which means “Nothing”. It takes its name from Ingenting farm, which belonged to Karlberg Palace. The sculptor Johan Tobias Sergel spent several summers there, and the poet and songwriter Carl Michael Bellman is said to have stayed too. Legend has it that either Bellman or King Gustav III dreamed up the odd name as a joke, but its true origin is still debated. The farm was demolished in the early 1980s.
En bit härifrån ligger rondellen vid Skr: A short way from here is the roundabout at Skra Bro – an invisible border in the road network. Here, responsibility for Kongahällavägen passes from the state-run Swedish Transport Administration to the north to Gothenburg's municipal Traffic Office to the south. Skra bro itself, an old bridge over the Osbäcken stream, has given its name to the whole area.
En bit härifrån ligger ruinen av Ytterby: Not far from here are the ruins of Ytterby's old church, built in the Romanesque style in the 12th century, on what was then Norwegian land. Legend has it that Saint Olaf himself had it built. The church was rebuilt in 1699 and served as the parish church right up until 1870. The countryside around Ytterby has been lived in since the Iron Age and is full of ancient remains.
En bit härifrån ligger villagatan Anunds: Not far from here is Anundsvägen, a residential street best known for a royal visit: Queen Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom came here in the 1950s. Closer by is Snabba hus Råcksta, with 247 flats, one of the ten finalists for Stockholm's Building of the Year in 2020.
En bit härifrån ligger Åkermyntans centr: A short way from here is Åkermyntan Centre, which opened in November 1977. It gets a mention in a sketch by the comedy group Killinggänget, in which the character Fred Asp – famous for partying with his ferret, Göran – lives nearby. The whole of Hässelby is named after Hässelby Palace, whose lands once covered much of today's three Hässelby districts, and Hässelby Villastad is Stockholm's westernmost district.
En bit härifrån ligger Öringesjön, en my: Not far from here is Lake Öringesjön, very shallow and rich in nutrients, with an average depth of only about two metres. Even so, it's one of the best lakes in the Södertörn area for aquatic plants, with 29 species – several so rare they're on the national red list. The Alby nature reserve also has Kolardammarna, ponds dug in 1997 and 1998 to clean stormwater before it reaches the lakes.
En bit härifrån låg Filmstaden i Råsunda: A short way from here was Filmstaden in Råsunda, the studios where nearly 400 Swedish feature films were shot between 1920 and 1973 – a place closely linked with Ingmar Bergman. Closer still was the tramway's Råsunda depot from around 1910, with housing for its staff in the Boken and Björken blocks. And here's a fun fact: Näckrosen is the only metro station with exits in two different municipalities.
En bit härifrån låg Hundhamra, en gård s: Not far from here stood Hundhamra, a farm mentioned as far back as Erikskrönikan, the medieval Chronicle of Eric. The farm is long gone, but a hillfort and a burial ground remain. A runestone is also said to have stood here, raised for a man who died on Ingvar the Far-Travelled's doomed Viking expedition to the east. During the Second World War, the Norsborg anti-aircraft position was built in the area – one of the strongest in Stockholm's defences – to guard the city and the Norsborg waterworks against air raids.
En bit härifrån låg LM Ericssons central: A short way from here was LM Ericsson's central warehouse, built between 1965 and 1975. Its goods handling was so automated that the warehouse became a sight in its own right. In the other direction you can see Grantorp, where the colourful early-1970s tower blocks of the Million Programme, Sweden's great housing drive, have become a familiar part of the skyline. The municipality now classes them as a particularly valuable heritage environment.
En bit härifrån låg Stockholm-Barkarby f: Not far from here was Stockholm-Barkarby airport, also known as Hägerstalund airfield, where planes took off and landed from 1913 right up until 2010. In the Norra Igelbäcken nature reserve, one of the old runways still crosses the stream. Igelbäcken itself winds about 10.5 kilometres from Lake Säbysjön all the way to the Edsviken bay by Ulriksdal Palace. And closer by is Hästa klack, a nature reserve since 2026.
En bit härifrån låg Täby Galopp, Skandin: Not far from here was Täby Galopp, the largest gallop racecourse in Scandinavia. King Gustaf VI Adolf opened it on 28 August 1960, and the last race day was held on 18 May 2016, when racing moved to Bro Park. Right next to it is the Grindtorp housing area, between Näsbydal, the old racecourse and Täby centrum.
En bit härifrån låg torpet Parken, anlag: Not far from here stood the croft of Parken, founded in 1839 and pulled down in the mid-1950s – just as Bagarmossen was growing into a suburb. Today the district is a beautifully preserved 1950s suburb, known for its many footpaths and pedestrian underpasses that keep people and cars apart, and for its low-rise flats, small houses and terraces that sit nicely in the landscape.
En bit härifrån reser sig Hummelmoraberg: A little way from here, Hummelmoraberget rises in the Görväln nature reserve, sloping down towards Lake Mälaren. On its side you can see traces of the time just after the Ice Age: ridges of gravel and stone once washed up by the waves – which means the sea once reached all the way up here. South of the hill are Hummelmora hage, an old wooded pasture, and Hummelmora torp, a croft.
En bit härifrån rinner Forsån, en bara 1: Not far from here runs Forsån, a stream just 1.4 kilometres long that links Lake Magelungen with Lake Drevviken and forms the border between Stockholm and Huddinge. It drops only 0.7 metres in total, most of that in the first hundred metres. Forsen farm stood beside the stream from the 18th century; today all that's left is its foundation, about 25 metres from the bridge.
En bit härifrån rinner Forsån, knappt en: Not far from here is Forsån, a stream just under one and a half kilometres long that links Lake Magelungen with Lake Drevviken and marks the boundary between Stockholm and Huddinge. Almost its entire drop – all of 0.7 metres – comes in the first hundred metres; after that it flows along calmly. Forsens gård, an 18th-century farm, once stood beside the stream. Today only its foundations are left, about 25 metres from the bridge.
En bit härifrån rinner Glose å, sex kilo: A little way from here, the Glose å stream, six kilometres long, flows out into Ryskärsfjorden. The inlet has shallow waters and grazed shore meadows teeming with plants and birds, and the whole area is part of the Nordre älv estuary, a large nature reserve ranked among the most valuable natural areas in the county.
En bit härifrån rinner Vendelsån, en lit: Not far from here runs Vendelsån, a small river fed by three lakes with lovely names: Svartsjön, Ramsjön and Lycksjön – the Black Lake, the Wild Garlic Lake and the Lucky Lake. It winds through Gudö and Vendelsö and flows into Lake Drevviken near the spot where the Gudöån river begins. To the east, the Vendelsö-Gudö district borders the deep forests of Tyresta National Park.
En bit härifrån slingrar sig Osbäcken, e: Not far from here winds Osbäcken, a small stream with a big claim to fame: it's the only stream on the whole of Hisingen with sea trout. It flows from the Klare mosse bog, alongside Björlandavägen, and out into the sea at Björlanda kile. To improve the water quality, some of its flow has been diverted in an EU-funded project, which also created a pond.
En bit härifrån slingrar sig Söderån, et: Close by winds Söderån, a stream just over a kilometre long that links Lake Orlången with Lake Ågestasjön. It starts in Orlången's northern bay, which goes by the lovely name of Fräkenbotten, and then flows through a wetland called Pumphusängen – all part of the Orlången nature reserve. A little further away is Ågestaverket, Sweden's first nuclear power station to deliver energy to consumers.
En bit härifrån sticker Tyresö View upp: Not far from here, Tyresö View pokes up above the rooftops – an 82-metre, 23-storey apartment block that in 2016 was the fourth-tallest in Stockholm County. At its foot is Tyresö centrum, a shopping centre under a glass roof with 74 shops, the municipal offices and a library that's always putting on new exhibitions.

A short way from here, Tyresö View pokes up above the rooftops: an 82-metre residential tower with 23 storeys, designed by Archus arkitektur. In 2016 it was the fourth-tallest residential building in Stockholm County, behind Kista Torn and Skatteskrapan among others. All around is Bollmora – a town in its own right from 1965 to 1974 – where Tyresö's municipal offices are based.
En bit härifrån sticker halvön Männö udd: A short way from here the Männö udd peninsula juts out into Lake Bornsjön. It has something of a split personality: the northern half belongs to Botkyrka and the southern half to Salem, but the whole headland is part of the Bornsjön nature reserve. It's also home to the Söderby burial ground, one of the best preserved in the Lake Mälaren valley, with around 150 visible graves from the early Iron Age.
En bit härifrån stod Hagstaeken, en grov: Not far from here stood Hagstaeken, a mighty oak with the largest trunk of the ten oaks protected as natural monuments in Huddinge. Despite protests, it was felled for safety reasons on the night of 3 December 2025, following a government decision. The area is also home to Flemingsberg manor, whose history goes back to the 15th century and which gave the whole district its name.
En bit härifrån står Bjurslättskyrkan, s: Not far from here is Bjurslätt church, which has switched traditions: it used to be a church in what is now Lundby parish, but since 1998 it has belonged to the Greek Orthodox Church. Further on, at Vågmästareplatsen, is Kville saluhall, a food hall that opened in 2013, with meat, fish and seafood, a bakery, a café and a wide choice of restaurants.
En bit härifrån står Högenskolan, som nä: A short way from here stands Högenskolan, hailed as a ‘country school palace’ when it was built in 1930. The old Högenskolan burned down – perhaps because the children were allowed to light the stove themselves before the schoolmaster arrived in the morning. The new school was designed by Ivar Burman in the Nordic Classicism of the 1920s.
En bit härifrån står Högenskolan, uppför: Not far from here is Högenskolan, built in 1930 for the children of Högen, Fiskebäck, Önnered and Tynnered. When it was new it was called a 'country school palace'. The old school had burned down – possibly because the children were in charge of lighting the stove before the schoolmaster arrived in the morning – so perhaps it's no surprise the new one was given a slate roof.
En bit härifrån står Nasirmoskén, som in: Not far from here is the Nasir Mosque, which opened in 1976 as the first building in Sweden built specifically as a mosque. It belongs to the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community. The hilltop estate of Högsbohöjd has a charming touch: several of its courtyards are named after women, such as Elin, Gerda and Fredrika. The Högsboleden road was built in 1966, at the same time as the estate.
En bit härifrån står Villa Korndal, uppf: Not far from here is Villa Korndal, built in 1870 for David Otto Francke, the entrepreneur who made Korndal paper mill the biggest in Sweden. The villa later passed to the Wallenberg family and after that became the home of the managing director of the Papyrus company. Paper mills, a financial dynasty and company bosses – all under one roof.
En bit härifrån står en gammal lada som: Not far from here, an old barn has been turned into a theatre. Teaterhuset Mölndal has 150 seats and is home to six amateur dramatic societies. Since 1998 it has staged revues and comedies, mostly performed by young people – and there's even an English-language theatre group in the building.
En bit härifrån står en lada som bytt hö: A little way from here is a barn that has swapped hay bales for spotlights. Teaterhuset Mölndal is an old barn turned into a 150-seat theatre, where several amateur drama groups perform – mostly revues and comedies put on by young people. There's even an English-language theatre group based here.
En bit härifrån tar Partille kommun vid,: A little way from here, Partille municipality begins, and the nearest part of it is Sävedalen. The name says exactly what it is: the valley of the Säveån river. Sävedalen borders Gothenburg and counts as one of its inner suburbs – in fact it's officially part of the Gothenburg urban area, even though it belongs to a different municipality.
En bit härifrån tar naturreservatet Älta: Not far from here begins the Älta mosse – Strålsjön nature reserve, 52 hectares of wild country protected since 1995. Together with the neighbouring Strålsjön – Erstavik reserve, it forms one large, unbroken stretch of countryside, with the little lake Strålsjön at its heart. Perfect if you fancy swapping tarmac for bog and forest lake.
En bit härifrån tränar BK Häcken. Gothia: Not far from here is where BK Häcken train. Gothia Park Academy is the football club's base on Hisingen, with a 1,300-square-metre clubhouse and three full-size pitches, two of them artificial and floodlit. On top of that there's a grass pitch as well, so there's rarely any shortage of turf to kick a ball around on.
En bit härifrån, i Biskopsgården, ligger: A little way from here, in Biskopsgården, stands Biskopsgården Church. When Bishop Bo Giertz consecrated it in 1961, he also branded the cross that you can still see on the church door facing Vårvädersgatan. At first, only a small church had been planned. Down by the Älvsborgsfjorden inlet is the Rödjan district – mostly industry, but also home to the Rya forest.
En bit härifrån, i Hansta naturreservat: Not far from here, in the Hansta nature reserve at the very northern tip of Stockholm municipality, is Astrid Lindgrens berg, Astrid Lindgren's Hill. It was named in 1989 as a thank-you to the author for her work to protect Hansta's natural and cultural heritage. The reserve was created in 1999, covers about 270 hectares and borders the Järvafältet nature reserve.
En bit härifrån, i Hässelbygårdsskolan,: Not far from here, inside Hässelbygårdsskolan, was the Prisma cinema, which opened in 1960 and showed films to the public until 1984. The very first film was Let's Make Love, starring Marilyn Monroe, and the auditorium had 375 blue armchairs. In neighbouring Vinsta, which the City of Stockholm bought from Spånga in 1949, you'll find terraced houses and villas in the north and the hill of Johannelundstoppen in the south-west.
En bit härifrån, i Orlångens naturreserv: Not far from here, in the Orlången nature reserve, lies the forest lake Mörtsjön. On its shore is the croft of Charlottendal, where Prince Eugen painted his picture Spring. The lake is unusually rich in nutrients for a forest lake, so crucian carp and rudd do well here – and someone has added common carp, too. In the other direction is Sjötorp, an old croft by the Flemingsbergsviken bay.
En bit härifrån, i Sjöängen, låg en gång: Not far from here, in Sjöängen, there was once a lake called Brännkyrkasjön, also known as Kyrksjön, the Church Lake. It was drained bit by bit, but it might be making a small comeback: in 2009 the Älvsjö district council decided in principle to turn Sjöängen into a park with an artificial lake, bringing back a little of the lake that disappeared.
En bit härifrån, i Skälby, står runstene: A little way from here, in Skälby, stands the runestone U 89, a finely carved slab of coarse-grained granite 132 centimetres tall. It has certainly sparked people's imaginations: in his work Atlantica, Olof Rudbeck the Elder offered a rather fanciful reading of its inscription. The piece that's missing from the stone was already gone in the earliest drawings of it, from the 1600s.
En bit härifrån, i Tyresö strand, ligger: Not far from here, in Tyresö strand, is Karptjärnen, a little pond barely two metres deep. It has a curious story to tell: both medicinal leeches and horse leeches live in it, probably released back when Stockholm's pharmacies bred and caught leeches to treat all sorts of ailments. In spring the pond is teeming with tadpoles, too.
En bit härifrån, i Vinsta industriområde: Not far from here, in the Vinsta industrial area, is Vällingby fire station, in service since December 1964. Its firefighters have an unusual speciality: they're specially trained in breaking through roofs and in rope access – working at great heights. Their patch stretches all the way from Abrahamsberg in the south to Lövsta in the north.
En bit härifrån, i hörnet Telefonvägen o: Just down the road, on the corner of Telefonvägen and Mikrofonvägen, there were once plans for the Tellus Towers – two residential skyscrapers of 82 and 62 storeys. The project was unveiled in 2013, but in 2020 it came out that the city planning office was no longer behind it. The name came from the Tellusborg area. Telefonplan is also home to Midsommargården, one of Stockholm's six community centres, which has been putting on cultural activities since 1946.
En bit härifrån, i området Gunnared, lig: Not far from here, in the Gunnared area, is a pond called Titteridamm, and there's a charming story behind the name. On Saturday evenings, so the tale goes, the local girls would come down to the pond to check their reflections in the still water and smarten themselves up before the dance. In other words, they “peeked in the pond” – tittade i dammen. The area is also home to Gunnared cemetery, opened in June 2003 and covering a full 80 hectares.
En bit härifrån, i slutet av Kumla allé: Not far from here, at the end of Kumla allé on a peninsula in Lake Drevviken, is Kumla herrgård, Kumla Manor. Its roots go back to the Middle Ages, and much of western Tyresö was originally carved out of its lands. In fact, it was Kumla that changed its name to Trollbäcken in 1947. Since 2013 the manor has been serving food, and it hosts conferences too.
En bit härifrån, inne i Alby naturreserv: Not far from here, inside Alby nature reserve, are the Kolardammarna ponds, a water treatment project built in 1997 and 1998 on the old Kolarängarna meadows. They're fed by the wonderfully named Fnyskbäcken – roughly 'Snort Brook' – which mostly carries stormwater from Bollmora. First an oil separator catches the worst of the pollution, then the particles are left to settle on the bottom before the water flows on to the lakes along the Tyresån river.
En bit härifrån, mellan Övre och Nedre R: Not far from here, between the lakes Övre and Nedre Rudasjön, is Rudans gård, an old 17th-century croft that's now the heart of the Rudan nature reserve and recreation area. In the other direction, outside Haninge Culture House on Poseidons torg, stands runestone Sö 269. It originally stood on Söderbymalm, and it gave its name to Runstensvägen, Runestone Road, in the middle of Handen.
En bit härifrån, nära gränsen till Tyres: Not far from here, close to the boundary with Tyresö, is Storkällan, a cold-water spring on the edge of Storkällan's chapel and cemetery. It was the spring that gave both the chapel and the burial ground their name, and it still provides fresh water for the animals of the forest.
En bit härifrån, på Elektronvägen, finns: Not far from here on Elektronvägen are the Labour Movement Archives and Library, Arbetarrörelsens arkiv och bibliotek. Founded in 1902, it's the oldest institution of its kind in the world, holding records from most of the parties and organisations in the labour movement, along with more than 600 personal archives.
