It used to be on Upplandsgatan in central Stockholm, close to Folkets hus and the headquarters of the LO trade union confederation, before moving here in 2012.
En bit härifrån, på Järfällasidan, ligge: Not far from here, on the Järfälla side, is Hummelmoraberget in the Görväln nature reserve. It bears traces of the time after the Ice Age: beach ridges of gravel and stone, thrown up by the waves, show that the sea once reached all the way up here. And a bit of trivia: the Hässelby district administration only existed in 1997 and 1998.
En bit härifrån, på Kalvsund, står Breme: Not far from here, on the island of Kalvsund, stands Bremerska villan, better known as the Smugglers' Villa. Built in 1912, it's a monument to fortunes made from herring fishing – and from bootlegging in the 1920s. With its towers, it's a landmark for ships passing along the channel. At the island's highest point stands Valen, a pole beacon, and beneath it a compass rose dated 1684 is carved into the rock.
En bit härifrån, på Klockargårdens skola: A short distance from here, in the playground of Klockargården school, Carl Milles' elephants are having fun: the sculpture group Playing Elephants has stood there since 1947. Dating back to 1843, it's the oldest school in the municipality still in use. Along Stockholmsvägen in Näset you'll also find Näsets krog, a preserved 18th-century roadside inn, and Villa Nynäs, where Lidingö's first general store opened in the late 19th century.
En bit härifrån, på Kofferdalsvägen 37,: Not far from here, at Kofferdalsvägen 37, is Villa Dalfrid. It's a private home, but not just any home: on 24 September 1979 it was listed under the Swedish Cultural Environment Act. The area belongs to Askim parish, whose roots go all the way back to the Middle Ages.
En bit härifrån, på andra sidan Göta älv: A short way from here, across the Göta älv river, is Villa Ellesbo. Gothenburg's city architect Carl Wilhelm Carlberg designed the manor and its garden in 1795 in an Italian-inspired style, with terraces stepping down to the river. The garden is full of rare trees and huge old oaks. Just south of the manor is Rösbo, home to one of the biggest beech woods in the Gothenburg area.
En bit härifrån, på en kulle i Glöskär,: Not far from here, on a hill in Glöskär, stands Burås mill. The three-storey windmill was built in 1892–93 by the master builder Emanuel Andréasson, but wind power goes back a long way here – there have been windmills on this spot since the 1700s. The mill became a listed building in 2004.
En bit härifrån, på en udde söder om Bor: Not far from here, on a headland south of Lake Bornsjön, Salem Church nestles among great oaks, limes, alders and birches, with the old Södertäljevägen road running past. The area is full of ancient remains. And here's a curious detail: for a few years in the 1970s and 80s, Salem parish was part of Botkyrka municipality, and since 1983 it has made up most of Salem municipality.
En bit härifrån, strax öster om E18 i hö: A short way from here, just east of the E18 at Kallhäll, is Lake Översjön. It's a rift-valley lake, 4.1 metres deep and 22.1 metres above sea level, shared between Järfälla and Sollentuna. Around it stretches an open farming landscape, mixed with conifer forest and bare rock.
En bit härifrån, ungefär nio kilometer n: Not far from here, about nine kilometres north-east of central Gothenburg, is Lärjeholm manor. It was listed in 1973, and the main house stands just 150 metres from the Göta älv river. Around the buildings are traces of the old garden, and to the south the Lärjeån stream marks the edge of the grounds.
En bit härifrån, vid Askims norra kyrkog: Not far from here, at Askim's northern cemetery, history lies in several layers. Just north of the cemetery is an Iron Age burial ground with around eighty grave mounds, and Askim's medieval parish church stood here until it burned down in 1876. Most intriguing of all is the privateer's grave, where a privateer captain who sailed for Lars Gathenhielm is said to be buried.
En bit härifrån, vid Drevvikens västra s: Not far from here, on the western shore of Lake Drevviken, is Trångsunds gård, traditionally known as “the pearl of Drevviken”. The manor dates back to the mid-1700s, and its main house was designed by none other than Carl Fredrik Adelcrantz, the head of the royal building office. The name Trångsund means “narrow strait”, after the tightest point on Drevviken, the largest lake in the Tyresån river system.
En bit härifrån, vid Elisedal i nuvarand: Not far from here, at Elisedal in what is now Kallebäck, matches were once made. In 1907 Eric Holmberg moved his production here from Södertälje, and right up until 1917 the factory was called Södertelje Tändsticksfabrik, the Södertälje Match Factory – even though it was in Gothenburg. After that it became Göteborgs Tändsticksfabrik, and most of its matches were exported.
En bit härifrån, vid Göta älv, låg Sverr: A little way from here, by the Göta älv river, was Sverres Varv, which began life as a factory making ship models. The company was founded in 1915 and built models for Gothenburg's shipyards and the maritime museum, including one of the East Indiaman Finland. For the Jubilee Exhibition of 1923, it produced a whole series of models of ships, shipyards and harbours. When demand dried up, it switched to making toys.
En bit härifrån, vid Idrottsvägen i Åbyo: Not far from here, on Idrottsvägen in the Åby area, is Åbybadet, a swimming centre that opened its doors on 16 June 2023. It cost a cool 500 million kronor to build, so every splash is rather an exclusive experience. A bit further on, hooves thunder round Åbytravet, Sweden's second-biggest trotting track.
En bit härifrån, vid Nordsjön, ligger by: A short way from here, on Lake Nordsjön, is the village of Bolås, five kilometres south-east of Mölnlycke. It has switched parishes over the years: historically it belonged to Landvetter, but in 1949 it was moved to Råda parish. Closer to the stop is the little forest lake Slättebacketjärnen.
En bit härifrån, vid Rådasjön, ligger Rå: A little way from here, beside Lake Rådasjön, is Råda säteri, a manor with a main house, wings and farm buildings. It was listed on 3 June 1969. Rådasjön is 23 metres deep and supplies Mölndal with its drinking water. The Mölndalsån river flows through the lake, and further downstream it changes its name to Gullbergsån.
En bit härifrån, vid Stubbåkersgatan, li: A short way from here, on Stubbåkersgatan, is Fässberg Cemetery – 116,000 square metres in all, including natural woodland, with 4,800 graves. Fässberg Chapel and an old mortuary have stood here since 1936, and in 1982 a memorial grove opened at the heart of the cemetery. In the other direction is the new Åbybadet swimming centre, opened in 2023.
En bit härifrån, vid fritidsbåtshamnen i: Not far from here, at the marina in Hovås, is one of the Swedish Sea Rescue Society's stations. It was set up in 1983 and today has 25 volunteer crew. One of its first boats, Pernilla, turned out to be too slow, so it was refitted with a new engine and propeller.
En bit härifrån, öster om E4:an och väst: Not far from here, east of the E4 and west of Edsviken bay, is Silverdal, which was once a croft. When plans to build here got under way in 1989, the project was first called Margreteborg, before the name was changed to Silverdal. In the other direction is Sörentorp, a part of Solna that stretches down towards the grounds of Ulriksdal Palace.
En bit härifrån, öster om sjön Trehörnin: Not far from here, east of Lake Trehörningen, lies Solbacken, a neighbourhood made up almost entirely of small houses. It's part of the Högmora district, created in 2018. For a long time the area was mostly holiday cottages, but these are now being turned into year-round homes. The whole area lies within Kynäsberget, a stretch of forest and hills that covers most of central Huddinge.
En bit ut i skärgården ligger Grötö, där: A little way out in the archipelago lies Grötö, home to just 84 people all year round. At the northern end of the island is a nature reserve with one of Bohuslän's rare sandy beaches, and along the west coast runs an esker, a ridge of rounded boulders left by the ice. The passenger ferry leaves from Björkö, and in the main harbour there's a guest harbour and a kiosk that's open in summer.
En gångväg knyter ihop hållplatsen med Å: A footpath links the stop with Årstidstorget, the Seasons Square, northern Kortedala's local square with a café and bakery, a pizzeria and a health centre. A little further on, a time machine awaits: Kortedala museum, a flat of about 50 square metres showing what a working-class home might have looked like in the 1950s, furnished with original fittings from other flats in the area.
En kort bit bort ligger Svensbydösen, äv: A short way from here is Svensbydösen, also known as Queen Hacka's Grave. It's the only known long dolmen – a Stone Age burial chamber – in Gothenburg, and the oldest structure in the municipality. Legend has it that a gold ring forged by a giant lies inside, and treasure hunters have done the tomb serious damage looking for it. When the Norrleden road was being planned in 1978, archaeologists excavated the site and confirmed that it really was a dolmen.
En kort bit bort står Centrumkyrkan, en: A short distance away is Centrumkyrkan, a church that changed hands in an unusual way. The Methodists had used it since 1996, but when their congregation grew too small, they handed the building over to the Church of Sweden in 2023. In November 2025 it was consecrated as the new church for Kållered parish in the Mölndal pastorate.
En kort promenad bort fanns Hallinge, en: A short walk away was Hallinge, a small locality that Statistics Sweden designated in 1990, made up of temporary housing just south-west of the Smedstorp croft. It borrowed its name from Hallinge gård, a farm a kilometre and a half away. Today only the Smedstorp croft is left, so Hallinge turned out to be a brief footnote in the statistics.
En kort promenad bort korsar Linnarhults: A short walk away, Linnarhultsbron, the Linnarhult Bridge, crosses the Lärjeån river. It was built in the early 1970s to replace an old stone arch bridge – but the old bridge was never pulled down and still stands right next to the new one. Two bridges side by side: one from the age of the car, the other from a slower time.
En kort promenad bort ligger Ahlby säter: A short walk away is Ahlby säteri, a stone manor house from the 1620s and the oldest surviving building in Lilla Alby. One of its owners was Clas Fredrik Horn af Åminne, who was convicted of complicity in the murder of King Gustav III. Landsvägen, the Country Road, has kept its rural-sounding name because it was once part of the main road out of Stockholm. It's also where you'll find Swedbank's head office, built in the shape of a double V.
En kort promenad bort ligger Annelunds g: A short walk away is Annelund farm, where Per Henrik Ling, ‘the father of gymnastics’, lived from 1822 to 1839. The main house and the gymnastics wing are both listed. According to an old tall tale, Gustav III gave the farm to his favourite, Elis Schröderheim – but it isn't true. Schröderheim lived on another farm that has since vanished.
En kort promenad bort ligger Kärra kyrka: A short walk away is Kärra Church, which was a chapel until 2001 and has belonged to Tuve-Säve parish since 2010. Across the Göta älv river is Agnesberg, where travellers have found food and a bed for several hundred years – it was a coaching stop long before the railway arrived in 1880.
En kort promenad bort ligger Lundby Kolo: A short walk away are the Lundby allotments, Lundby Koloniträdgårdar, originally known as Lundby kolonien – though in 1972 the association had to give up roughly half its land for a football pitch and a car park. Nearby runs Hjalmar Brantingsgatan, one of the city's longest streets at almost 4,400 metres. And down at Frihamnen, along this same street, is the lowest point in Gothenburg, two metres below mean sea level.
En kort promenad bort ligger Park Studio: A short walk away is Park Studios, where artists such as Ace of Base, Stina Nordenstam and Dan Hylander recorded in the 1990s. From 2004 to 2016 the studio was owned by the band Kent and their producer. Park-Bio, the cinema in Örby's Folkets hus community centre, opened in 1928 and showed films until 1968 – and since 2021 the projector has been rolling again. As for Örby Palace, it's now rented by the Embassy of Vietnam.
En kort promenad bort ligger Skändla rös: A short walk away is Skändla rös, a Bronze Age burial cairn 18 metres across and just over two metres high. It sits on the boundary between Bohuslän and Västergötland – which, until the Treaty of Roskilde in 1658, was the border between Sweden and Norway. Every year there's a haymaking day in the meadows next to it, when the grass is cut by hand, scythes and all.
En kort promenad bort ligger Sköndalssko: A short walk away is Sköndalsskolan school, designed by Cyrillus Johansson and opened in 1953. The Swedish National Heritage Board describes its design as unusual for its time, with many interesting architectural details. In the other direction is the Gubbängen business area, also known as the Norra Sköndal industrial area – one of the very smallest in the city.
En kort promenad bort ligger Vällingby c: A short walk away is Vällingby centre, the model for the 1950s suburban dream known as the 'ABC town'. Here you'll find Trappan, a civic centre from 1956 designed by Sven Backström and Leif Reinius, built in terraces between a lower and an upper square and home to theatre, music and a library. Right next door is the brick church of St Thomas, S:t Tomas kyrka, by Peter Celsing, consecrated in 1960, with a wooden crucifix by the artist Bror Hjorth.
En kort promenad bort ligger Västra Fröl: A short walk away is Västra Frölunda churchyard, which dates back to the Middle Ages. The old Västra Frölunda church stood here until it was pulled down in the 1860s. Look out for the iron rings in the churchyard wall – they were for tying up horses. The oldest gravestones date from 1680 and 1729.
En kort promenad bort ligger herrgården: A short walk away is the manor of Stora Frösunda, built in 1783 and given its palatial look in the 1890s. Today it's owned by SAS Institute, and next to it stands the runestone U 121. Nearby rises Hagahuset, built between 1954 and 1957 to house the entire administration of Stockholm County Council.
En kort promenad bort ligger kulturhuset: A short walk away is Cyklopen, a self-run, non-profit cultural centre with music, art and adult education. The first building was burned down by arsonists in 2008, but it was rebuilt. Just below Högdalen centre is Högdalen skatepark: with about 5,500 square metres of concrete, it's the largest in Stockholm and almost as big as Stapelbäddsparken in Malmö.
En kort promenad bort ligger tjärnen Kla: A short walk away is Klare mosse, a pond that's one of the best spots on Hisingen for frogs and newts. Among them is the rare great crested newt, which thrives among all the little pools and hollows. The pond had become overgrown, but it was given a new lease of life by the Osbäck project, and from here the Osbäcken stream flows down towards Björlanda kile.
En kort promenad bort står De tre vingar: A short walk away stands De tre vingarna, The Three Wings, a monumental steel sculpture by the American artist Alexander Calder. The city bought it in the early 1960s, but Angered was running late, so from 1967 the sculpture stood on Götaplatsen as a stopgap. It didn't move out to Angered until 1979. Nearby is Angered Arena, with an ice rink and a swimming pool that puts special emphasis on teaching children to swim.
En kort promenad bort, längs Solvädersby: A short walk away, along Solvädersbyn, are 124 houses with a properly sporting past. They were first built for the 1994 Winter Olympics in Lillehammer, used again for the 1995 World Athletics Championships, and finally settled here in 1996. That's why the streets there have athletics names instead of weather names. On the same site, in 1954, what was then the longest building in Europe went up; it was demolished in 1995.
En kort promenad härifrån ligger Bräcke: A short walk from here is Bräcke soldattorp, a soldier's croft built in the 1830s and a local heritage museum since 1965. From 1889 it was home to the soldier Sven Olof Emanuelsson Björk. The croft hasn't always stood here – it used to be north of Bräcke village. Inside there's only room for a single room, a kitchen and a hallway.
En kort promenad härifrån ligger Dvärgah: A short walk from here is Dvärgahuset, the Dwarf House, a stone cist grave from the late Neolithic. People once believed it was a home for dwarfs – hence the name. Three huge blocks form a roof over the burial chamber, and one of the end slabs has a round hole ground into it whose purpose nobody knows.
En kort promenad härifrån står Torslanda: A short walk from here is Torslanda church, said to be one of the most popular wedding churches in the Diocese of Gothenburg. It's the parish church of Torslanda, which until 1967 lay outside the City of Gothenburg, in the old Västra Hising district of the province of Bohuslän. Since 2010 it has been part of Torslanda-Björlanda parish.
En kort promenad härifrån, bredvid Bromm: A short walk from here, beside Bromma Church, is Stockholm's smallest and oldest school, Bromma kyrkskola, dating from 1864. In the mid-1890s the teacher here was also the parish clerk, the organist and the local vaccinator. Before the school was built, children learned their letters in a small room in Gamla Klockargården, the old parish clerk's house next door – teaching had been the parish clerk's job since the mid-1600s.
En kyrka som slutat vara kyrka finns en: A short walk from here is a church that's no longer a church. Lövgärdet Church was deconsecrated on 19 June 2016 – formally taken out of religious use. Before that it even switched parishes, belonging to Gunnared parish from 1973 and to Angered in its final years. Lövgärdet itself is a neighbourhood in the Gårdsten district of north-eastern Gothenburg.
En promenad bort ligger Slätta damm, som: A short walk away is Slätta damm, a pond that formed around 1860 in S.A. Hedlunds park. There's a barbecue spot and a waffle café by the water, and in cold winters people go skating on the ice. The birds you'll see swimming here are mostly ducks and goldeneyes. The park is part of Hisingsparken, the largest park in Gothenburg.
En riktig kuriosa: på J. Sigfrid Edström: Here's a real oddity: on J. Sigfrid Edströms gata, traffic drives on the left – even though the rest of Sweden drives on the right. It's down to the way the tracks in and out of the Rantorget tram depot are laid out. The street is named after the first director of Gothenburg's tramways. In Gårdahallen next door, the tram society Spårvägssällskapet Ringlinien looks after the city's vintage trams and buses.
En väderkvarn som har flyttat två gånger: Here's a windmill that has moved house twice! Kälvesta kvarn, also called Lilla Stampan, was built in the 1600s and first stood on a hill by Observatoriegatan in central Stockholm. In 1884 it was moved to Lunda, and in 1892 it arrived at its current spot on Skestavägen in Solhem, a short walk from here.
Enebyberg är ett villasamhälle med cirka: Enebyberg is a residential community of about 5,000 people, full of houses from the first half of the 20th century. It belongs to Danderyd municipality but borders both Täby and Sollentuna. A couple of blocks away is Eneby Church on Eneby torg, which the Church of Sweden and the Uniting Church in Sweden share.
Enligt legenden växte helgonet Sankt Bot: Legend has it that Saint Botvid grew up at Hammarby gård, a short way from here by Prästviken bay on Lake Aspen – and Botkyrka is named after him. In the Middle Ages the farm became a rectory, and the present main house from 1804 was the church's rectory right up until 1997. The farm is even mentioned in the runic inscription on the famous Botkyrka monument by the church.
Eriksberg var ett av Göteborgs stora var: Eriksberg was one of Gothenburg's great shipyards. The huge gantry crane that still towers over the site is a reminder of those days, and it has become a landmark for the whole riverside.
Essingeleden svävar förbi här på Blommen: The Essingeleden motorway sweeps past on the Blommensberg viaduct, spanning the Vinterviken valley and almost skimming the roofs of Blommensberg school. The bridge opened on 21 August 1966. Just a stone's throw away is Stora Fågelsången, an 18th-century farm by the little lake Trekanten, whose garden is now allotments – without the usual cabins. A bit further on stands Sankt Sigfrid's church, a red wooden church moved here from Vasastaden in 1904.
Ett hotell man bor i på riktigt! Hässelb: Here's a hotel people actually live in! When Hässelby familjehotell, the family hotel, opened in 1955, it was the builder Olle Engkvist's largest co-housing block. The staffed services were dropped in 1976, but residents still keep some of them going as volunteers. Its neighbour, Hässelby ungdomshotell, the youth hotel, originally had flats for young people and for pensioners, as well as artists' studios and a day nursery.
Ett litet namnskämt: tunnelbanestationen: Here's a little naming quirk: Abrahamsberg metro station isn't actually in Abrahamsberg at all, but in Riksby. Before the metro came, trams on the Ängby line ran past here from 1944, and the station's abstract murals in glazed tiles, made by Rigmor Roxner in 1999, are a nod to the tiled stations of the tram era. Close by is the white-rendered Abrahamsberg church, consecrated on All Saints' Day 1955.
Ett lokstall som heter Sundbyberg fast d: An engine shed called Sundbyberg – even though it's in Solna! The old steam locomotive shed and water tower building were put up in 1904 by the Stockholm–Västerås–Bergslagen Railway, and SJ named them Sundbyberg because they were near that station. The buildings are well preserved and considered of very high cultural and historical value. The nearby Huvudstaleden road was planned as part of an urban motorway, but only part of it was ever built.
Ett par hundra meter bort ligger Kvarnto: A couple of hundred metres away is Kvarntorpshällen, a rune-carved rock slab discovered in 1943 by the author Jan Fridegård. Its inscription includes the word 'stepsons', which is rare in runic texts. Nearby is the egg-shaped Näsbydal housing estate, with 900 flats ranging from a single room to seven rooms over two floors. Next door, the Grindtorp area sits beside what used to be Täby's racecourse.
Ett par hundra meter bort ligger Tacksäg: A couple of hundred metres away is Tacksägelsekyrkan, the Church of Thanksgiving, also known as Trångsund Church. It was designed by the architect Sture Frölén and consecrated in 1957, as Trångsund was growing into a town. It served as the parish church until 1987, when Mariakyrkan in Skogås took over. Beside the church there's a memorial grove and a small burial ground.
Ett par hundra meter bort står Tibble ky: A couple of hundred metres away is Tibble Church, sometimes called the cathedral of Roslagen, which serves as both a church and the administrative centre of Täby parish. The Tibble district is also home to Täby centrum, and its library holds two fragments of Viking Age runestones found at Lissby in 1930. One of them measures just 47 by 46 centimetres.
Ett par hundra meter härifrån ligger Hög: A couple of hundred metres from here is the Högsbo pegmatite quarry, where feldspar, quartz, mica and beryl were mined from 1945 until the late 1950s. The rock also held rare minerals such as monazite and columbite. Today the quarries are part of the Änggårdsbergen nature reserve, which is also home to the small lake Axlemossen.
Ett par hundra meter härifrån låg Hörnin: A couple of hundred metres from here, by what is now Parkhemsvägen, stood Hörningsnäs gård, a manor and large estate in Huddinge parish. The farm buildings burned down in the 1950s, but the name lives on in the Hörningsnäs housing area. A little further on is Lake Trehörningen, where you may spot bats and protected frogs and toads.
Ett par hundra meter härifrån stod Hagst: A couple of hundred metres from here stood Hagstaeken, a mighty oak in Glömsta. Measured round the trunk, it was the biggest of the ten oaks protected as natural monuments in Huddinge. On the night of 3 December 2025 it was cut down for safety reasons, following a government decision and despite protests. A little further on, the valley of Glömstadalen opens up, an area the municipality values for its cultural heritage.
Ett par hundra meter härifrån står Stens: A couple of hundred metres from here is Stensjökyrkan, one of the two churches in Stensjön parish. A little further on, at the very top of the steep hill on Kvarnbygatan known as Mölndals kråka, the Mölndal Crow, is Mölndal's city museum. Its café serves lunch on weekdays and coffee and cakes at weekends – a well-earned reward after that climb.
Ett par kvarter bort ligger Atlantisområ: A couple of blocks away is Atlantis, a 1950s terraced-house village that drew international attention – Olof Palme lived here with his family from 1968 to 1983. Further off, in Beckomberga, stood Beckomberga sjukhus, a psychiatric hospital built in 1930–1932 that stayed open until 1995. Since the mid-2000s its old buildings have been turned into homes.
Ett par minuter bort ligger Filmstaden H: A couple of minutes away is Filmstaden Heron City, Sweden's biggest cinema, with eighteen screens and 4,166 seats in all. It's part of Kungens kurva, which together with Skärholmen Centre draws 30 million visitors a year. Long before the popcorn arrived, this was the site of Sadelmakartorp, the saddler's croft, which dates back to the late 17th century and became a schoolhouse after 1860.
Ett par minuter bort ligger Högdalens sk: A couple of minutes away is Högdalen skatepark, also known as Highvalley Skateworld – a whole concrete world for skaters, with a freestyle area, a children's area, the Mega Ditch and a bowl. At around 5,500 square metres, it's the biggest in Stockholm. Next door is Cyklopen, a cultural centre run entirely by volunteers, and a little further on is Högdalen's town centre, which was modelled on the centre in Vällingby.
Ett par minuter bort ligger Skärisbiogra: A couple of minutes away is Skärisbiografen, a non-profit municipal cinema that opened in 2017 and is run by Kulturhuset Stadsteatern, Stockholm's culture house and city theatre. Its neighbours are the Red Cross folk high school, offering courses with an international and humanitarian focus, and the old Skärholmen upper secondary school from 1974. Underneath it all lie traces of Smista gård, a farm that goes back to the 800s, in the Viking Age.
Ett par minuter bort snurrar Vridande mo: A couple of minutes away, Vridande moment, ‘Torque’, slowly turns. Also known as Skruven, the Screw, Aston Forsberg's steel sculpture has become the emblem of Skärholmen centrum. It won first prize in an ideas competition in 1968. Skärholmen centrum had 15 million visitors in 2013, and together with nearby Kungens kurva, home to the world's second-largest IKEA store, it forms the biggest out-of-town shopping area in the Nordic countries.
Ett par minuter härifrån börjar Ulriksda: A couple of minutes from here, the Ulriksdal nature reserve begins – about 32 hectares between the Brunnsviken and Edsviken bays, protected since 1988. It also includes the ancient graves of the Mellanjärva burial ground. In the palace park stands Villa Beylon, a pink-rendered brick villa from 1803, next to Ulriksdal Palace Theatre, which has been a state-listed building since 1935.
Ett par minuter härifrån ligger Björkäng: A couple of minutes from here is the Björkängen sports ground, with a football pitch and two ice rinks where Huddinge IK play their home hockey games. One of the rinks used to be called Nickehallen, after the club stalwart Bengt 'Nicke' Nilsson. Until 2018 the area belonged to the Stuvsta-Snättringe municipal district, which was then split in two, so that Stuvsta and Snättringe each became a district of their own.
Ett par minuter härifrån står runstenarn: A couple of minutes from here are the Häradsvägen runestones, a pair from the Viking Age. One of them has had quite an adventure: in the 1800s it served as a doorstep in Lindal, then went missing for a while before turning up again in 1938, lying on a burial mound at Skälby gård. The other was given a rather fanciful interpretation by Olof Rudbeck the Elder in his work Atlantica.
Ett par minuter härifrån, längs Hallunda: A couple of minutes away, on the Hallunda heritage trail opposite Slagsta motel, is a rock carving that wasn't discovered until 1971. Nearby is Slagsta gård, a historic manor, and down by Lake Mälaren is Slagstabadet, an EU-designated bathing spot with excellent water quality. One of Slagsta's two brickworks once stood there, and in the woods you can still make out terraces and old house foundations.
Ett par minuters promenad bort ligger Lå: A couple of minutes' walk away is Långsjö farm, on the northern shore of Lake Långsjön. It has two identical main houses, and the reason is a touching one: the businessman Robert Ditzinger built them in 1882, one for each of his two sons. The farm goes back to the 17th century and gave its name to the whole district of Långsjö.
Ett par minuters promenad bort ligger Ty: A couple of minutes' walk away is Tyresövallen, formerly known as Bollmoravallen. It's the home ground of Tyresö FF and the Tyresö Royal Crowns, with room for about 2,700 spectators. Tyresö's ice rink is in the same area, and a little further on is the glass-roofed Tyresö centrum, with the municipal offices and library.
Ett par stenkast bort, i Sundby, ligger: Just a short way off, in Sundby, two rune-carved rock slabs lie side by side: U 80, large and richly decorated, and U 81, which was never finished. Sundby is counted as part of Old Spånga. The name has been known since 1312, although the district itself wasn't created until 1953, on land the City of Stockholm had bought from Spånga in 1949.
Ett stenkast bort ligger Hagsätra centru: A stone's throw away is Hagsätra centrum, the local town centre, which opened in 1960 – the same year the metro arrived. Look out for Barnet med käpphästen, the Child with the Hobby Horse, a copper sculpture by Marie Stenqvist that has become the centre's emblem. A little further on there's an outdoor pool with a funny name: Älvsjöbadet. Despite what it says, it isn't in Älvsjö at all, but right here in Hagsätra. It was built in 1937–1938.
Ett stenkast bort ligger Älta kyrka, int: A stone's throw away is Älta Church, beside Ältavägen. The road was built in 1934 and winds for just over eight kilometres through the open countryside between Älta and Nackanäs. The neighbouring area of Stensö carries a memory of the water: the peninsula was once an island in Lake Ältasjön, and at its tip the Stensö beach invites you in for a swim.
Ett stenkast bort står Vårby gårds kyrka: Close by is Vårby gård church, colourful and full of imagination, and considered one of the first postmodern buildings in Sweden. It was consecrated on 25 May 1975 and sits on a slope looking out over Lake Mälaren, next to a Viking Age burial ground. And just south-west of the church, at Duvberget, the Vårby hoard – a cache of silver treasure – was discovered in 1871.
Ett stenkast härifrån breder Rålambshovs: Just nearby is Rålambshovsparken – Rålis to the locals – named after the old Rålambshov estate. The park was laid out in the 1930s, at around the same time as Västerbron, the Western Bridge, and Lilla Västerbron, the Little Western Bridge, runs straight across it. By the square you'll also find Riksarkivet, the National Archives. Its main building was completed in 1968, when the archives moved here from Gamla Riksarkivet, the Old National Archives, on Riddarholmen.
Ett stenkast härifrån ligger Albykistan,: A stone's throw from here is Albykistan, a reconstructed stone cist – a type of late Stone Age grave that is very rare around Lake Mälaren. Only seven are known in the whole of Stockholm County, and this one has been dated to around 1800 BC. From the Stone Age to the big top: Alby is also home to Subtopia, the base of the contemporary circus company Cirkus Cirkör.
Ett stenkast härifrån ligger Bullegumman: Close by is Bullegummans gata, the Bun Lady's Street, named after Mrs Liljegren, who in the 1930s sold home-baked buns through a hatch in the wall of her house to children on their way to Påvelundsskolan. The house was later used for a while as a reception centre for refugees. It still stands in its original state, and the hatch was still there in 2011.
Ett stenkast härifrån ligger Kristineber: A stone's throw away is Kristineberg Castle, a manor that looks like a castle. It was once a malmgård – a country house on the edge of the city – and still has much of its 18th-century character. The main house has been a private home since the 1930s, while the wings are used by Kristinebergsskolan school. Over by Fredhällsparken park was the Tranan cinema, which showed films from 1933 to 1961.
Ett stenkast härifrån ligger en teater s: A stone's throw from here is a theatre that used to be a barn. Teaterhuset Mölndal has 150 seats and is home to six amateur theatre societies, all under one shared umbrella organisation. These days it's mostly revues and comedies created by young people, and the building even has an English-language theatre group.
Ett stenkast härifrån ligger Ågestaverke: Just a stone's throw away is Ågestaverket, the Ågesta plant – also known as R3 or Adam – which was Sweden's first nuclear power station to supply energy to consumers. Most of its output was district heating for Farsta, which earned it the name ‘the nuclear heating plant’. The reactor ran on heavy water and natural uranium. It closed in 1974, but most of it is still standing and has found a new role as a training ground for Stockholm's fire service.
Ett stenkast härifrån låg Råsunda fotbol: A stone's throw from here stood Råsunda football stadium. The 1958 World Cup final was played there on 29 June, when Brazil beat Sweden 5–2 in front of almost 50,000 spectators. The stadium closed in 2012, once the new national arena in Arenastaden was finished, and the site has since been turned into homes and offices.
Ett stenkast härifrån står Ängbystenen,: A stone's throw from here, on a small knoll in the middle of the houses, stands Ängbystenen, runestone U 60. It gave its name to Runstensvägen, Runestone Road, and the streets around it also have names linked to runes and the Viking Age. A little further on is Björklunds hage, Bromma's best-preserved burial ground from the early Viking Age, and the Stora Ängby manor, whose main house dates from the very end of the 1600s.
Ett stycke härifrån slingrar sig Bällsta: Not far from here winds the Bällstaån stream, also called Spångaån in its upper reaches. It rises on a hill in Viksjö and goes on quite an adventure: under Spånga it runs through a tunnel about 1.4 kilometres long, and further on it crosses the Solvalla trotting track end to end, right through the green infield.
Fagersjö började som en del av Södertörn: Fagersjö started life as part of Södertörns villastad, a planned garden suburb. Nearby is Villa Edvardshäll, the very first villa in the Fagersjö area, built in 1903 just north of what was then the brand-new Nynäs railway. Its builder, the machinist Axel Edvard Samuelsson, named the house after himself – and naming your villa after yourself became something of a tradition among Fagersjö's pioneers.
Fagersjö ligger utmed sjön Magelungens n: Fagersjö stretches along the northern shore of Lake Magelungen, and it's home to Högdalstoppen – two of Stockholm's highest points, with sweeping views over the south of the city. The street has its own little story too: Villa Lundin, nicknamed ‘the Castle’, was once at Vildandsvägen 14. In the 1930s the Lundin family are said to have owned one of the only two cars in Fagersjö.
Faggens krog är en nästan musealt bevara: Faggens krog is an 18th-century townhouse preserved almost like a museum. Carl Michael Bellman sang about it, and over the years it has been both a tavern and a cloth factory. Just below the music pavilion on Vita bergen stood Ceders Café, where the Ceder family served summer fika – coffee and cake – from the 1910s onwards. The building was later used by the youth club Vitabergsklubben, led by the author Per Anders Fogelström, until arsonists destroyed it in 1969 and 1970.
Falutorget fick 1883 sitt namn efter Fal: Falutorget was named in 1883 after Falun, the town at the far end of the Bergslagsbanan railway, and until the 1860s this ground was reed bed on the edge of the Göta älv river. For many years the square was overshadowed by Gasklockan, the gasholder – an 86-metre-tall round structure you could see from much of Gothenburg. It was taken out of use in 1993 and finally demolished in 2017, after delays caused in part by nesting peregrine falcons.
Falutorget fick sitt namn 1883 efter Fal: Falutorget was named in 1883 after Falun, the far end of the Bergslagsbanan railway, whose station building stood nearby. Until the 1860s this was all reed beds, part of the Göta älv river, until dredging created new land. For many years the Gasklockan gasholder towered over the area: 86 metres tall and visible from much of the city. It was taken out of use in 1993, and when it was finally demolished in 2017, the work was held up by – among other things – nesting peregrine falcons.
Farsta centrum invigdes den 23 oktober 1: Farsta Centre opened on 23 October 1960 and was big for its day, escalators and all. Its car park, with space for 4,000 cars, was one of the largest in Europe, and moving walkways were installed to carry shoppers from their cars to the shops. Farsta was hailed as the southern suburbs' answer to Vällingby.
Farsta gård: Farsta gård, the old Farsta manor farm
Farsta gård och Farstastenen: Farsta gård and the Farsta runestone
Farsta gård vid Magelungen har rötter än: Farsta gård, on the shores of Lake Magelungen, has roots that go all the way back to the 14th century. Today the farm is run by the Farsta association council, an umbrella group of around 70 local clubs and societies. Here you'll also find Farstastenen, the only surviving runestone in Söderort, Stockholm's southern suburbs. It was put back up in 1875 and stands beside the footpath from the farm down to Farstabadet.
Farsta torg, ett par minuter härifrån, a: A couple of minutes from here is Farsta torg, laid out like an Italian piazza and opened on 23 October 1960. The long square measures 180 by 100 metres, and its gently curving shape may have been inspired by Piazza delle Erbe in Verona. Most days there's a market selling fruit and flowers. Next door is the former Farsta gymnasium, a secondary school that's now home to the Adolf Fredrik music classes.
Farstaviken sträcker sig från Baggensfjä: Farstaviken bay reaches in from Baggensfjärden towards Gustavsberg, the main town of Värmdö municipality, about 20 kilometres east of Stockholm. Here nature itself has redrawn the map: as the land has slowly risen since the Ice Age, the islands of Farstalandet and Ormingelandet have joined together. Meanwhile, places like Mörtnäs, Hemmesta and Torsby have merged with Gustavsberg.
Feskekôrka, räkmacka vid vattnet: Feskekôrka fish market – and a prawn sandwich by the water
Filmhuset: Filmhuset, home of the Swedish Film Institute
Filmstaden i Råsunda: Filmstaden in Råsunda, the old film studios
Finansmannen Ernest Thiel lät Ferdinand: The financier Ernest Thiel commissioned Ferdinand Boberg to design him a villa in the Viennese Art Nouveau style, and since 1924 it has been an art museum, Thielska galleriet – the Thiel Gallery. On its walls you'll find Bruno Liljefors, Ernst Josephson, Carl Larsson, August Strindberg and Anders Zorn, alongside Edvard Munch, Paul Gauguin and Toulouse-Lautrec. Just next to it, on a south-facing slope at Blockhusudden, is Gravitational Ripples by Lea Porsager, the memorial to the victims of the 2004 tsunami.
Finnboda varv anlades 1874 som filial ti: The Finnboda shipyard was founded in 1874 as an offshoot of the Bergsund yard. Since then the old shipyard has become a mixed neighbourhood. Its old workshops – the joinery, the steam engine shop and the canteen – now house flats, offices and shops. The shipyard workers used to live on the surrounding hills, Finnbodaberget, Skatberget and Finnberget among them.
Fiskebäck är stadsdelen där Göteborg möt: Fiskebäck is where Gothenburg meets the sea, by the southern archipelago. The district covers 561 hectares and borders Hinsholmen and Långedrag to the north and Önnered to the south. Its name – 'fish brook' – gives away what once mattered most here, and life by the water still shapes the area today.
Fisksätra, inklämt mellan Lännerstasunde: Fisksätra, squeezed in between the Lännerstasundet strait and the Nacka forests, is Sweden's most densely populated urban area, with 7,724 people per square kilometre. Lännerstasundet is an arm of the Baltic on the border between the Boo and Nacka districts. Fisksätra is also home to the Toy and Collectors' Museum, a museum devoted entirely to toys and play.
Flatenbadet är stadens största friluftsb: Flatenbadet is the city's biggest outdoor swimming spot, and Stockholm Vatten, the water company, reckons Lake Flaten is the cleanest lake in Stockholm. The buildings were designed by the architect Paul Hedqvist, and the bathing place opened on 23 June 1934. All around it is the Flaten nature reserve, the largest in Stockholm, which even has a racetrack for radio-controlled model cars.
Flemingsbergs industriområde anlades på: Flemingsberg's industrial area was laid out in the 1960s, and Billman-Regulator's factory from the early part of that decade is still standing; the street name Regulatorvägen remembers the electronics firm. Serious culture may be on its way, too: the municipality is planning space for the activities the Royal Swedish Opera and Dramaten, the Royal Dramatic Theatre, currently have in Nacka. This is also home to the Labour Movement Archives and Library, the oldest of its kind in the world.
Flera gator i trakten har fått sina namn: Several streets in this area are named after a sawmill. Sörensens gata honours the sawmill owner Nils Georg Sörensen, whose company, Säfveåns AB, also lent its name to Hyvelsågsgatan, Klyvsågsgatan and Stabbetorget. On a hill by Stabbetorget stands Björkekärr Church. And a little further on is Queen Silvia Children's Hospital, the biggest children's hospital in Sweden.
Flysta är i huvudsak en villastadsdel, m: Flysta is mostly villas, but it has a small mystery of its own. A Viking Age runestone, known as Uppland runic inscription 70, once stood here. People have searched for it several times without success, and it's probably lost for good. Neighbouring Sundby counts as part of Old Spånga, and its name goes all the way back to 1312.
Fontänen Elementens kamp: The Elementens kamp fountain, 'the Struggle of the Elements'
Fontänen Tors fiske: Tors fiske, Thor's Fishing, the fountain
Forsån, en bit härifrån, är en liten å m: Not far from here runs Forsån, a small river with a big job. In just 1.4 kilometres it links Lake Magelungen with Lake Drevviken as part of the Tyresån lake system. It flows mostly at a gentle pace and marks the boundary between the City of Stockholm and Huddinge municipality. North of Drevviken is Orhem, a district made up mostly of countryside in the Flaten nature reserve.
Fotbollsplanen ligger på mark som förr h: The football pitch stands on land once known as Söderlingska ängen, Söderling's Meadow, after the organ builder Johan Nikolaus Söderling – the first person to suggest turning Slottsskogen into a park. Majvallen was built as a public relief-work project from 1946 and opened on 5 June 1949, at a cost of just over 327,000 kronor. Today it's where Göteborgs FF, among others, play their home games.
Fotbollsstadion Råsunda fick en smygprem: Råsunda football stadium had a low-key opening in April 1937 with a match between AIK and Malmö FF, and at the time it was Sweden's largest sports venue. King Gustaf V performed the official opening that May, at a match between Sweden and England. Råsunda was the home of the men's national team and AIK's home ground up to and including 2012. Nearby Råsunda IP sports ground had already opened back in 1910, and AIK played some of its matches there too.
Fotö är en liten ö i Göteborgs norra skä: Fotö is a small island in Gothenburg's northern archipelago – just 0.70 square kilometres, yet home to just over six hundred year-round residents. Yew grows here; the islanders call it barlind. There's a swimming spot on the east side and a sheltered harbour on the south side. Climb up to the higher ground on a clear day and you can see all the way to Vinga.
Fotö är en riktig miniatyrvärld: 621 bof: Fotö is a whole world in miniature: 621 permanent residents share just 0.70 square kilometres. On the south side there's a sheltered harbour, and on the east side, a tempting place for a swim. The island is also known for its yew trees – called barlind in the local dialect – and on a clear day you can see all the way to Vinga, the lighthouse island, from the higher rocks.
Framför biblioteket en bit härifrån står: In front of the library nearby stand nine granite animals. This is Fredens rike, the Peaceable Kingdom, a play sculpture by Pye Engström, who lived in the area for a whole month to get to know it. The title comes from the Book of Isaiah and its vision of a kingdom of peace where former enemies live side by side. The animals are carved from black, red and grey granite, and the whole group is made for children to play on.
Fredens rike: Fredens rike, the Kingdom of Peace
Frescati hage vid Brunnsviken hette tidi: Frescati hage, the meadow by Brunnsviken bay, used to be called Norrbrunnshagen, after the Norra Brunn tavern. In 1897 the State Entomological Institute was built here to study insect pests on farms. Down on the shore paddles Brunnsviken Canoe Club, founded in 1909. And a little further away is Södra huset, the university's building complex, sometimes called the Blue Houses because of its sky-blue facade.
Fridhems kyrkogård, alldeles intill, rym: Fridhem Cemetery, right next to us, has around 5,627 Christian grave plots. It's also home to one of the Church of Sweden's three Muslim burial grounds in Gothenburg. The cemetery opened in 1968, and until 1982 a mobile church had to serve as its chapel. A little further away is the manor house Bäckebols gård.
Fridhems kyrkogård, en bit härifrån, inv: Fridhem cemetery, a short way from here, opened on 20 November 1968. For fourteen whole years a portable church had to serve as a temporary chapel, until the present chapel was consecrated by Bishop Bertil Gärtner in 1982. The cemetery covers no less than 87 hectares and holds around 5,627 grave plots.
Fridhemsplan är en av Kungsholmens stora: Fridhemsplan is one of Kungsholmen's big hubs, with the metro, buses and shops. In the 16th century, Kungsholmen was known as Munklägret, 'the Monks' Camp', after the monks who owned land here.
Frihamnen var förr en hamn där varor kun: Frihamnen, the Free Port, was once a harbour where goods could be stored without paying customs duty. Now a whole new district is taking shape here. In a moment we'll cross the Göta älv on Hisingsbron, a lift bridge that opened in 2021, replacing the old Götaälvbron.
Frihetens port: Frihetens port, the Gate of Freedom
Frimurarhemmet, ritat av arkitekten Ludw: Frimurarhemmet, the Freemasons' Home, designed by the architect Ludwig Peterson, is made up of eleven buildings, the first of which was ready in 1912. Elderly Freemasons and their families from all over Sweden could apply to live here, and since 2007 the buildings have belonged to a housing cooperative. Neighbouring Gångsätra, like so much of Lidingö, started out as a farm and is mentioned in writing as early as 1379.
Fritidshusområdet Kungshättan på östra d: Kungshättan, a holiday-home area on the eastern part of the island of Kungshatt, had no fewer than 87 holiday homes on 30 hectares in 2010. The island has a long history: in 1531 the Crown acquired an outlying plot here, probably then called Serszöön, from the village of Norrby on Lovön. The neighbouring island of Fågelön also lies in the eastern part of Lake Mälaren.
Fruängen blev egen stadsdel den 1 februa: Fruängen became a district in its own right on 1 February 1948, when it was split off from Västberga. Fruängen School was built between 1956 and 1960 to designs by the architect Ture Ryberg, and the City Museum has given it a green listing for its heritage value. Much earlier, around 1650, the croft of Istorp – also known as Komöte – appeared here. It's long since gone.
Fruängens station är den högst belägna i: Fruängen is the highest station on the entire metro network, at 46.8 metres above sea level. The local church, Vårfrukyrkan – the Church of Our Lady – has an unusual story. The church centre opened in 1963, but the actual sanctuary included in the original plans wasn't started until 2004, and it was finally consecrated on Advent Sunday 2005. A block away is Triangelhuset, the Triangle House, from 1955, named after its unique three-sided floor plan.
Fräntorp bebyggdes under 1930-talet med: Fräntorp was built up in the 1930s with small prefabricated houses that the future owners put up together. Stone was quarried on the rocky hills of Valåsen and Källeberget from the mid-1800s to the early 1900s, and on the high ground above the motorway there are traces of ancient settlement. Folkets hus, the community hall, stands where the main house of the Fräntorp estate once was.
Från 1895 till 1994 marscherade soldater: From 1895 to 1994, soldiers marched across this barracks yard. Today the buildings are listed and house a restaurant, a market and museums. The Sports Museum, Idrottsmuseet, has more than 15,000 objects, and since 2005 it has also held the boxer Ingemar Johansson's collection of trophies. The old horse hospital has been home to a military history museum.
Från Burö färjeläge på Hälsö går Nordöle: From Burö ferry terminal on Hälsö, the Nordöleden ferry route runs out to Knippla, Hyppeln and Rörö, the outermost islands in the Kattegat. The ferries Nordö III, Ulrika and Linda serve it, and it's the only Swedish Transport Administration ferry route that calls at more than two terminals. Hälsö itself is a small island of just 1.28 square kilometres.
Från Kärrtorp når man ända bort till Nac: Kärrtorp stretches all the way to Nackareservatet, the Nacka nature reserve, in Nacka municipality, so you're never far from the forest. Closer by is the Reflexen cinema, showing films since 1961, and Kärrtorpshallen, the sports hall from the early 1960s designed by Kjell Ödeen and given a green listing for its heritage value by the City Museum. Kärrtorp Park only got its current name in 2009, but in its southern part stands the old croft that gave the district its name.
Från Ropsten går Lidingöbanan över Lidin: From Ropsten, the Lidingöbanan line runs across the Lidingö Bridge out to Lidingö. The bridge opened in 1925, and for many years it was the only road link to the island.
Från Tappström går pendelbåten linje 89: From Tappström, commuter boat 89 runs all the way into Stockholm, to Stadshuskajen by the City Hall, with boats such as M/S Lux. Tappström, the channel that marks the boundary between the islands of Lovön and Ekerön, also has a guest harbour for visiting boats. A little further off stood the Tappsund brickworks, which opened in the late 1800s and closed down in 1959.
Från slutet av 1800-talet och under 1900: From the late 19th century and right through the 20th, Albano was an industrial area. Today it's dominated by Campus Albano, shared by Stockholm University and KTH Royal Institute of Technology, which opened in September 2023 with around 1,000 student flats. Albano is also home to Nordita, the Nordic Institute for Theoretical Physics. It was founded in 1957, with Niels Bohr among its instigators, and moved here from Copenhagen in 2006.
Från toppen av Väsjöbacken, en bit bort,: From the top of Väsjöbacken, a short way off, on a clear day you can see central Stockholm and the Globe arena to the south – and, far to the north, the control tower at Arlanda. The ski slope has four runs and a vertical drop of 82 metres. A little further on, in the Rösjö nature reserve, Jarlabanke's stone from the late 11th century stands beside an ancient path towards Täby.
Frölunda Torg öppnade 1966 och var ett a: Frölunda Torg opened in 1966 and was one of Sweden's first big suburban shopping centres. All around is Västra Frölunda, and a few kilometres to the west the sea and the archipelago begin.
Frölundaborg invigdes 12 september 1967: Frölundaborg opened on 12 September 1967 with a sensation: Västra Frölunda IF beat the Swedish national ice hockey team 4–3. The arena holds just over 6,000 spectators and is still home to Frölunda HC. Next to it runs Friidrottens väg, the Athletics Way. It used to be called Viljo Nousiainens Gångväg, after the coach who led Patrik Sjöberg, Stefan Holm and Christian Olsson to great things at Slottsskogsvallen stadium.
Fullersta gård, några minuter härifrån,: A few minutes from here is Fullersta gård, a former manor that since 2009 has been an art gallery, with a permanent exhibition that includes works by Peter Dahl and Ewert Karlsson – and a café. Even closer is Fullersta bio, where an old cinema and former Konsum co-op shops have been turned into an art gallery and theatre.
Furulundskyrkan är lite ovanlig: den är: Furulundskyrkan is a bit out of the ordinary: it's shared between EFS, a revival movement within the Church of Sweden, and the parish of Furulund-Öjersjö. Tucked away not far from here is Prästtjärnen, a little lake that, small as it is, is a full 14 metres deep. It sits just over 108 metres above sea level and drains into the Göta älv river basin.
Furåsens kyrka ligger alldeles intill, m: Furåsen Church is right next door, and not far from here is a street with a sweet story behind it. In the 1930s, a Mrs Liljegren lived around here and baked buns that the children walking to Påvelundsskolan school just couldn't resist. She opened a hatch in the wall of her house and sold them through it, and so she became Bullegumman, the Bun Lady. Today the street carries her nickname.
Fynda på Bellevue marknad: Hunt for bargains at Bellevue market
Fynda på Kvibergs marknad: Bargain-hunting at Kvibergs marknad, the Kviberg market
Fyra vägar möts vid Bellevue i Gamlestad: Four roads meet at Bellevue in Gamlestaden: Generalgatan, Artillerigatan, Kvibergsvägen and Kortedalavägen. Around the junction you'll find kiosks, hairdressers and restaurants, and at Bellevue market people hunt for bargains among the second-hand stalls. From 1910 to 1914 the ball-bearing giant SKF had its offices at Mariedal, a landeri – one of Gothenburg's old country estates – nearby.
Färingsö är runstenarnas land. En bit hä: Färingsö is runestone country. Not far from here, in Eneby, stands a Viking Age runestone whose carver, experts say, wasn't much of a rune artist. Still, its pattern resembles another stone, so perhaps the same man carved both. In Törnby there's a runic inscription on a reddish granite boulder set in the ground. A man named Saxe had it carved in memory of his mother – sadly, her name has been lost.
Färja till Brännö eller Styrsö: Take the ferry to Brännö or Styrsö
Färja tillbaka över älven: Take the ferry back across the river
Färjan Älvsnabben över älven: The Älvsnabben ferry across the river
Fässbergs kyrka ligger strax intill, och: Fässberg Church is right beside us – and between 1922 and 1976 it was actually called Mölndal Church. Fässberg has the largest population of any parish district in both the province and the county. Close by is Fässbergs Bio, a 400-seat cinema in the old secondary school's assembly hall, now converted into an events venue.
Få byggnader har bytt skepnad som Hammar: Few buildings have changed roles quite like Hammarkullen church. It was a parish church in Angered parish until it was deconsecrated in 2011 and became a preschool. Then the building was transformed once again, and today it's Hammarkullen mosque.
Fåfängan, kafé med utsikt: Fåfängan, a café with a view
Författaren Gösta Langenfelt kallade nam: In 1944 the writer Gösta Langenfelt called the name Alléparken, 'the Avenue Park', a monstrosity – there was neither a park nor an avenue here. It later turned out, though, that an avenue really had led to the croft of Asplund, and a few of its trees are still standing. Next door are the 'English terraced houses', 43 of them, built in 1919–1920. And up on Alviksberget, Elfvinggården went up in 1939–1940: a collective housing block for single, educated women.
Förr reste sig Tyskbagarbergen på platse: This is where the Tyskbagarbergen hills once rose, named after Martin Kammecker, a baker from Mecklenburg who built windmills on his land in the 1600s. One of them stood at the far end of Jungfrugatan. The hills were in the way of traffic, so a passage, Karl XV:s port, was blasted through to let Nybrogatan continue up to Valhallavägen. That's where you'll now find the monumental red-brick home of the Swedish Patent and Registration Office, designed by Ragnar Östberg.
Förr slingrade sig Ekerövägen genom skar: Ekerövägen used to snake through tight, narrow bends right here, between Tillflykten and Lindö lada. In 1994 they blasted straight through the rock instead, creating the 178-metre Lindö tunnel. The result? Fewer accidents and shorter rush-hour queues.
Gallhålans naturreservat bildades 1988 o: The Gallhålan nature reserve was created in 1988 and enlarged in 2013 to 96 hectares. As well as oak woodland, it has alder swamps, pine forest on bare rock and a hay meadow, with hazel, guelder rose and alder buckthorn among the shrubs. The reserve lies on the eastern slope of the Tahult drumlin, a long glacial ridge that drops steeply to the little lake Agntjärnen, and it's rich in birdlife.
Gamla Boråsvägen en bit härifrån var en: Gamla Boråsvägen, the old Borås road just along from here, was once Gothenburg's main route in and out of the city, part of national road 5 from 1945 into the 1950s. Its narrow, steep and winding stretch, known as Kallebäcks lider, was dreaded by motorists and carters alike. Just south of the road, Örgryte IS trains at ÖIS-gården, where one of the pitches has been called Hammarviken Arena since 2013.
Gamla Danderyds socken var en gång rätt: The old parish of Danderyd was once fairly sparsely populated. In 1905 it had 3,605 inhabitants, spread over an area that now takes in Djursholm, Stocksund, Enebyberg, Mörby and Nora. The parish church, Danderyd Church, is a little way from here beside the E18. And in nearby Rinkeby there was once a fragment of a runestone, U 132, which went missing in the latter half of the 1800s.
Gamla Filmstaden: Gamla Filmstaden, the old film studios
Gamla Huddingevägen var en gång en del a: Gamla Huddingevägen was once part of the main Huddinge road. But so much through traffic was cutting right through the villa suburb of Örby that in 1971 the road was diverted north of the district. Not far from here is Stockholmsmässan, Sweden's largest exhibition and congress centre, along with the Scandic Talk Hotel, seen as the exhibition centre's signature building.
Gamla Kungälv i trä omger hållplatsen. R: All around the stop is old wooden Kungälv. The town hall on Gamla torget, the Old Square, has become a symbol of the old town, and some of its oldest houses line Västra gatan. Zetterlöfska huset dates from 1762, while Strandska huset, with its gateways, double staircase and cobbled courtyard, was built by the merchant David Werming. Thorildska huset has served as both a school and a telegraph station.
Gamla Kvibergs regemente har fått nya li: The old Kviberg regiment has found new lives. The former horse stables now house Kvibergs marknad, a market with 160 stalls full of antiques, curiosities, books and toys. And just north of the barracks rises Prioritet Serneke Arena, the biggest multi-sport complex in the Nordic region, with an indoor ski slope and a 1.2-kilometre ski track.
Gamla Stockholmsvägen, alldeles i närhet: Gamla Stockholmsvägen, the old Stockholm road nearby, links Snättringe and Glömsta. Further along the same road is Nytorp, a former croft from the mid-1600s that now serves coffee – an old crofter's cottage turned café.
Gamla flygfältet kallas det också, Torsl: A short way from here, on the west side of Hisingen and about 15 kilometres from central Gothenburg, is Torslanda airfield, also known as the old airfield. It was laid out in 1923 and served as the city's airport for more than fifty years, until Landvetter took over in 1977. Today Torslanda is best known for Volvo's car plant, the Torslanda Works.
Gamla stans gränder: The narrow lanes of Gamla stan, the Old Town
Gamlestaden är just det, den gamla stade: Gamlestaden means just what it says: the old town. Nya Lödöse was founded here in 1473, long before present-day Gothenburg was laid out in 1621. The area later became industrial, and it's where the ball-bearing company SKF grew up.
Gamlestadens fabriker, mat och design: Gamlestadens fabriker – food and design in the old factories
Gamlestadsvägen, en bit härifrån, är en: Gamlestadsvägen, a little way from here, is a major road running alongside the E45 through Bagaregården, Gamlestaden and Olskroken. It was named in 1883, after the Gamlestaden district. It crosses the Säveån river on the Gamlestaden bridge, passes Nylöse Church and carries on towards the Lärje junction. The Fredrikshamn redoubt, a fortification from 1645, is nearby too.
Gamlestadsvägen, som löper alldeles inti: Gamlestadsvägen, the road running right beside us, was named back in 1883 after the district of Gamlestaden. A little further on is Hospitalskyrkogården, also called Nylöse hospitalskyrkogård, which served as the graveyard for the hospital parish from the late 1500s. Hardly any of the gravestones are left, but a Franciscan friary once stood on the same spot.
Gatan fick sitt namn 1888 efter Albert L: The street was named in 1888 after Albert Lindhagen, the man behind Stockholm's grand street plans. Nearby was Gamla Stadshagen, sometimes called Guldgrävarlägret, the Gold Diggers' Camp, where some 350 emergency homes housed working-class families from 1917 to 1965. And Thorildsplan is named after the writer Thomas Thorild, who wrote in his letters about seeking out the parks of Kungsholmen to take in the view.
Gatan har fått sitt namn efter Johannisd: This street is named after Johannisdalsgården, a croft first recorded in the 1770s and pulled down in the 1940s. Much of today's Mälarhöjden grew up on the farm's land, and the Johannisgården block is another reminder of the old property. Just up the road is Fruängen's town centre, which opened in 1962 and has a green listing from the City Museum.
Gatan har fått sitt namn efter markland,: This street is named after the markland, an old unit used to value land. Right next door is the Frölundaborg ice rink, which opened in 1967 with a friendly in which Västra Frölunda IF beat the Swedish national ice hockey team 4–3. And winding past Slottsskogsvallen, the athletics stadium where high jumpers like Patrik Sjöberg and Stefan Holm trained, is Friidrottens väg – the Athletics Way.
Gatan minns adelsätten Eketrä, som från: This street remembers the noble Eketrä family, who from the 18th century until 1875 owned the Västra Pilegården estate, right where the tarmac is today. It's also where the Bräcke tram line branched off to the south. The line closed in 1968 and was taken up in the 1980s, but its embankment is still here, almost untouched – a trace of another age.
Gatan är en bit av en riktig kungsväg. G: This street is part of a genuine royal road. On 19 August 1787 Gustav III opened his own road to Drottningholm Palace, running from the Royal Palace across Bromma, roughly along today's Gustav III:s väg. The surroundings, though, are pure 20th century: Abrahamsberg is one of Stockholm's larger areas of narrow slab blocks, sometimes called 'the yellow town' because of all the yellow brick.
Gatorna här har väder i blodet. Väderils: The streets round here have weather in their blood. Väderilsgatan, just up the road, was named in 1958 as part of a group of street names on the theme of weather and meteorology – and it's where tram line 2 turns round in a loop. Near the stop is Länsmanstorget, an indoor square built in 1966. Länsmansgården Church held its last service in April 2024 and is set to become an activity centre open to everyone.
Gatorna på Södra Guldheden är uppkallade: The streets of Södra Guldheden are named after doctors. Doktor Liborius gata honours Johan August Liborius, chief surgeon at Sahlgrenska Hospital from 1845 to 1870, who is seen as the hospital's first modern surgeon. Doktor Bex gata is named after Abraham Bex, Gothenburg's town physician around 1685. At the very top of that street are some unusual shop buildings from 1951, where the Konsum co-op was the first tenant.
Gatunamnen här doftar häst, och det är i: The street names around here smell of horses – and that's no coincidence. A few hundred metres away is Åbytravet, Sweden's second-largest trotting track, run by the Åby Travsällskap association. Its neighbour, the Åbybadet swimming centre, opened in 2023, so both people and horses can get their hearts racing here.
Gatunamnen här doftar sågspån. Sågmästar: The street names around here smell of fresh sawdust. Nils Georg Sörensen ran the Säfveåns AB sawmill, and it inspired several of Björkekärr's street names, all taken from sawmill terms: Hyvelsågsgatan, Klyvsågsgatan and Stabbetorget, this square. Sörensen even got a street named after him. On a hill by the square stands Björkekärr Church, and the area borders the Delsjö nature reserve.
Gatunamnen här är ingen slump, Biskopsgå: The street names round here are no accident – Biskopsgården is full of names with a weather theme. A short walk away, on Vårväderstorget, 'Spring Weather Square', is Biskopsgården library. It opened in 1964 and is now one of the most popular libraries in the city, with 700 to 800 visitors on an ordinary day. In 2020 the Swedish Arts Council named it a Romani reading embassy.
Gatunamnet ljuger inte: ett par hundra m: The street name tells no lies: a couple of hundred metres away, Kållered Church stands on a rise in the village. As well as being the parish church of Kållered, it's the oldest building in the whole of Mölndal municipality. Kållered was farming country for centuries, until the superstores moved into the western part of town.
Gatunamnet passar bra, för en kort prome: The street name is well chosen: a short walk away is Skansberget, one of eight ancient hillforts in Huddinge municipality. Closer still, the Smista bridge spans the E4/E20 motorway. This steel bridge for pedestrians and cyclists opened in 2008 and crosses in a single span between Segeltorp and Sätra, making it easier to get from one to the other.
Gatunamnet passar perfekt. På Tullinge g: The street name couldn't be more fitting. At Tullinge gymnasium, the upper secondary school a couple of hundred metres away, there's a tradition of a Nobel laureate visiting every year – usually a scientist. In 2014 the chemistry laureates Eric Betzig and William Moerner came, and in 2017 Michael W. Young. Not many schools can boast guest speakers like that.
Gatunamnet påminner om Svenska Ostindisk: The street name recalls the Swedish East India Company, based in Gothenburg from 1731 to 1813. Its ships sailed to China and came home laden with tea, porcelain and silk.
Gatunamnet är ingen slump. Strax intill: The street name is no coincidence. Right next to us is Stora Sköndal, which started life as a Lutheran deacons' institution. It was founded in Gävle in 1898 to train deacons, and moved here in 1905, when the Stora Sköndal estate was bought. Fittingly enough, Terrasshuset, the Terrace House, designed by Axel Kandell and marked in blue by the City Museum, stands on a steep south-facing plot in a block called Predikanten – the Preacher.
Gatunamnet är inte taget ur luften. Inge: The street name didn't come out of nowhere. In 1885 the engineer Gerhard Arehn opened a factory here on Kungsholmen making matchboxes – and the machines that made matchboxes. The business eventually became part of Svenska Tändsticksaktiebolaget, the Swedish Match Company. Nearby you'd also have found Tullmuseum, the Customs Museum, which from 1927 displayed objects collected by Swedish Customs, and the old Jewish cemetery, Aronsberg.
Genom Henriksdalsberget går Saltsjöbanan: The Saltsjöbanan railway runs through the Henriksdal hill in a 337-metre tunnel, and trains have rumbled through it since 1893. The area around Henriksborg used to be industrial, and from 1882 until the late 1950s the Rylander and Rudolph factory made, among other things, batteries for crank telephones and carbon rods for arc lamps. In 1987 the Danvikcenter office building won a European award for its steelwork.
Gibraltargatan en bit härifrån fick sitt: Gibraltargatan, a short way from here, was named in 1886 after the Gibraltar estate. In 1923 the street-naming committee wanted to change it to Gibraltarsgatan, but the city council turned the idea down. From 1922 the street was home to the Gibraltarvallen sports ground, until Mossen took over in 1959 and the old ground became mostly a car park. The footpath Syster Bojans backe, Sister Bojan's Hill, is named after Ingeborg Kastman.
Gillar du bröllop? Tuve kyrka, några min: Fond of weddings? Tuve Church, a few minutes away, is one of the most popular churches for weddings in the Diocese of Gothenburg. It's the parish church of Tuve, a parish that belonged to the Östra Hising hundred in Västergötland until it became part of the City of Gothenburg in 1967. Since 2010 the church has been part of Tuve-Säve parish.
Glose gränsar till Ryskärsfjorden, där g: Glose looks out over Ryskärsfjorden, where shallow water and grazed shore meadows attract a wealth of plants and birds. The meadows are part of the Nordre älv estuary, a nature reserve and Natura 2000 site ranked among the most valuable natural areas in the county. Sveriges Radio's nature programme Naturmorgon has even broadcast live from here. And a little further on stands Burås kvarn, a mill from the 1890s.
Golfhistoria i grannskapet! Lidingö golf: There's golf history in the neighbourhood! Lidingö Golf Club's parkland and woodland course at Sticklinge opened in 1927, and at the time it was the first 18-hole course in Sweden. If you'd rather go for a swim, there's Sticklingebadet, also called Sandviksbadet, a small beach on Stora Värtan bay. And the trail of Lidingöloppet, the famous cross-country race, passes through Sticklinge too.
Gothia Arena, Högsbo Baskets hemmahall,: Gothia Arena, home court of the Högsbo Basket club, is just a couple of hundred metres away. The whole area was part of the old parish of Västra Frölunda, which had about 13,500 inhabitants in 1944 and became part of the City of Gothenburg the following year. Its parish church, Västra Frölunda Church, now stands in the district of Järnbrott.
Granne med Frölunda torg, som Olof Palme: Frölunda torg, right next to us, was opened by Olof Palme in 1966 as the biggest shopping centre under one roof in the Nordic countries – and it's a good place to talk about Gothenburg humour. Kal and Ada, or 'Kal å Ada', are the stars of the classic Gothenburg jokes, and tradition has it that Aron Jonason, court photographer to King Oscar II, was one of the founding fathers of the Gothenburg pun. Beside the square is Frölunda kulturhus, the culture centre, with a library, a theatre and a swimming pool.
Granne med gymnasieskolan ligger Svandam: Next to the upper secondary school is Svandammen, a park and swimming spot popular with teenagers and families alike. A little further on is Spånga station on the Mälaren Line, 11.3 kilometres from Stockholm Central Station. On an ordinary winter weekday, around 7,900 people board trains there.
Granne med tenniscentret växer Råstapark: Next to the tennis centre, Råstapark is taking shape – AIK's future training ground and clubhouse for the men's team. It's due to be finished in autumn 2028 and will replace Karlberg, where the team has trained since 1999. A short walk away is Lake Råstasjön, Solna's only lake if you don't count Mälaren.
Granne med värdshuset gömmer sig en rikt: Tucked away next to the inn is a real gem: Confidencen, the Ulriksdal Palace theatre and Sweden's oldest rococo theatre. It was fitted out in 1753 by the architect Carl Fredrik Adelcrantz and restored in stages in the 1990s and 2000s. The inn itself is younger, built in 1868 on the initiative of King Karl XV.
Grannkommundelen Viksjö i Järfälla har e: The neighbouring district of Viksjö in Järfälla has a name with a long history. It comes from Viksjö farm and is a corruption of the original Vikhusa, which already appears on an 11th-century runestone. The farm was sold in 1921, development began in 1963, and today the area is mostly detached houses.
Grevegårdens kyrka ligger några hundra m: Grevegården Church is just a few hundred metres away, but a little further on, in Älvsborg, is one of the area's sweetest stories. In the 1930s a Mrs Liljegren baked buns and sold them through a hatch in the wall of her house to children on their way to Påvelundsskolan school. She became known as Bullegumman, the Bun Lady, and in 1965 the street was named after her.
Groens malmgård: Groens malmgård, an old country house
Groens malmgård är en riktig överlevare:: Groens malmgård is a true survivor. Its Carolean-style main building is the last of its kind in Stockholm, and its garden has been tended without a break for more than 300 years. A malmgård is an old country house on what was once the edge of the city. The street outside has had several names, among them Stadsträdgårdsgatan and Wintertullsgatan. From 1885 it was Vermdögatan, but that was thought misleading, so in 1939 it became Malmgårdsvägen. Back in the 1600s a windmill turned here too – Bengt Bagares kvarn, Bengt the Baker's mill.
Grynkvarnsparken har fått sitt namn efte: Grynkvarnsparken is named after a groats mill that once ground grain here; the farm beside it was demolished in the 1940s. In the southern part of the park, at what is now Bolidenvägen 2, stood the croft of Linde, which served travellers as both a coaching station and a tavern. The park was designed in the 1950s by city gardener Holger Blom and Erik Glemme, and today Talltunneln, one of the slip roads onto the Södra länken ring road, runs right under the lawns.
Grädde och ost, det passar ju ihop. Alld: Cream and cheese – a natural pairing, wouldn't you say? Right beside Gräddgatan, Cream Street, rises Ostkupan, the Cheese Dome. That's the nickname for a 14-storey block from 1964, home mostly to students living in corridor rooms with shared kitchens. The name Kallebäck is even older: it means the stream with the kettle and is mentioned as early as 1496.
Gräsbacken Sjöbacken, som i folkmun kall: The grassy slope of Sjöbacken, which locals call Tippen, 'the Tip', was once a shallow bay of the sea. When Frölunda torg was built, the earth dug out for it was dumped here – and the result is a much-loved spot for picnics and kite flying, with ice skating in cold winters. Down in Fiskebäck harbour there's also a fishing museum with a café, opened in 1999.
Gröna Lund öppnade 1883 och är Sveriges: Gröna Lund opened in 1883 and is Sweden's oldest amusement park. In summer you can hear the screams from its roller coasters far out across the water. Opposite is Liljevalchs, the art gallery.
Gröndal växte fram som en tidig arbetar-: Gröndal grew up as one of the early working-class and factory suburbs once the Western Main Line was built past Liljeholmen in the 1860s. The famous Gröndal terraced block, designed by Sven Backström and Leif Reinius, housed the Galjonen cinema from 1952 to 1962. The Riggen apartment building at Fågelsångsvägen 13 is a lot younger – it was nominated for Stockholm Building of the Year in 2016.
Gröndal är känt för stjärnhusen, och här: Gröndal is famous for its star-shaped apartment blocks – the first of their kind in Sweden were built right here. They were designed by the architects Sven Backström and Leif Reinius, with the master builder Olle Engkvist driving the project, and they've since become known around the world. From 1926 to 1934 the district was called Ekensberg; its present name comes from the Gröndal estate.
Gubbängens IP hette ursprungligen Bandha: Gubbängens IP, the Gubbängen sports ground, was originally called Bandhagen sports ground, and it has a colourful past. In summer, the speedway bikes of Hammarby Speedway and Getingarna roared round the track, and back in the day it was even known for car speedway. Today it's used for bandy and field hockey – and since 2020, when Stockholm's first indoor bandy hall was finished, it's also home to IK Tellus.
Guldrummet i Historiska museet: The Gold Room at the Swedish History Museum
Gullmarsplan har fått sitt namn efter Gu: Gullmarsplan is named after Gullmarn, the fjord at Lysekil on the Bohuslän coast. The square was built in the 1940s along with the surrounding district, and the metro station opened on 1 October 1950 – before that, trams stopped here. Today it's one of Stockholm's biggest interchanges, where the metro, the Tvärbanan light rail and buses all meet.
Gunnareds kyrka ligger bara några minute: Gunnared church is only a few minutes away and has been part of Angered parish since 2014. A little further on is Titteridamm pond, surrounded by roads such as Titteridammsvägen and Titteridammsstigen. Legend has it that the name comes from the girls who would gaze at their reflections in the pond's shiny surface before the Saturday dance – ‘titta’ means to look.
Gunnareds kyrkogård, en kort promenad bo: Gunnared Cemetery, a short walk away, took a long time to happen. Plans for a new cemetery in north-eastern Gothenburg began back in the 1980s, the land was acquired in a land swap with the city, and in the late 1990s an architecture competition was held. The cemetery finally opened in 2003 and covers 80 hectares. Gunnared Church stands beside it.
Gustaf Adolfs torg och Stora Hamnkanalen: Gustaf Adolfs torg square and the Stora Hamnkanalen canal
Gustav III ritade i stor utsträckning sj: Gustav III designed much of his English-style park at Drottningholm himself, but he didn't live to see it finished. A memorial temple to the king was planned for Monumentholmen, but only the foundations were ever laid. Next to it is Svanholmen, Swan Island, where a swan house that looks like a Chinese pagoda gave the park's wing-clipped mute swans shelter in winter. And the Gothic Tower, begun in 1792, was never fully finished inside.
Gustav Vasa skänkte en gång Skuru gård t: King Gustav Vasa once gave Skuru gård, the Skuru estate, to Danvik's Hospital, so that the rent could help cover the hospital's costs. The estate, a short walk from here, was bought in 1922 by its manager, Mathilda Sundelin, who renamed it Solsunda. The manor-like main house has been a convalescent and treatment home since the early 1900s. Perch and roach swim in little Bastusjön, the lake beside it.
