Gustavi domkyrka har brunnit två gånger,: Gothenburg Cathedral, Gustavi domkyrka, has burned down twice, in 1721 and 1802, and the building you see today was completed in 1815. The streets around it follow the grid of the city's earliest years, and Kungsgatan, one of the longest pedestrian streets in Sweden, is just a block away.
Gymnasieeleverna en bit härifrån har lek: The sixth-formers a short way from here have their lessons in an old weaving mill. Krokslättsgymnasiet started out in 1992 as an upper secondary school for healthcare and rents space in the Krokslätt factories, a textile mill built in the 1890s. The buildings were listed in 1991 and are protected in the local plan today, even though their interiors have been rebuilt.
Gymnasieeleverna en bit härifrån pluggar: The students at the upper secondary school just nearby have their lessons in a genuine piece of industrial history. Hulebäcksgymnasiet opened in 1995 in the converted and extended Hulebäck factory, built in 1878 as a branch of Mölnlycke fabriker. The railway has moved too. Mölnlycke station opened in 1894 about 350 metres east of where it stands today, and it was moved here in 2003. Now the Västtågen regional trains between Gothenburg and Borås stop here.
Gäddviken var förr namnet på hela Svinde: Gäddviken was once the name of the whole of Svindersviken bay, and the shore has had industry ever since the mid-1600s – including a superphosphate factory from the 1870s. The old coffee roastery is now a store for the Royal Opera and Dramaten, the Royal Dramatic Theatre, so there may well be stage sets and costumes behind those walls. A little further on is the manager's house of Beckbruket, the old pitch works. It dates from the 1830s and is the oldest surviving building in Finnboda.
Gärdesgården, byggd 1940 till 1941, pres: When Gärdesgården was built in 1940–41, the newspaper Svenska Dagbladet described it as a modern residential hotel, with a shared restaurant, a sun terrace and even a Finnish sauna for the residents. In Tessinparken next door is the 1973 sculpture Husmorssemester, ‘Housewife's Holiday’: a granite woman in a summer dress, carrying a suitcase. It recalls the state grant that let housewives take a holiday between 1946 and 1979.

Gå ner i tunnelbanan och det känns som a: Head down into the metro and it's like stepping into a child's drawing. The artists Elis Eriksson and Gösta Wallmark decorated the station with pictures that look as if children drew them, inspired by memories of their own childhood. The station opened on 31 August 1975, along with the first stretch of the blue line, between T-Centralen and Hjulsta.

Gården Stora Fågelsången är från 1700-ta: Stora Fågelsången is an 18th-century farm on the western shore of Trekanten, a small lake. The City of Stockholm has owned it since 1963, and the old garden is now given over to allotments – though without the usual little allotment cottages. The City Museum has marked the farm blue, meaning it's considered of exceptional cultural and historical value. A little further on, the Essingeleden motorway roars past on the Blommensberg viaduct, almost skimming the roofs of Blommensbergsskolan school.
Gården och värdshuset Sandsborg har gett: Sandsborg, an old farm and inn, has lent its name to both a cemetery and a metro station here in Gamla Enskede. A little further on is the Museum of the Visually Impaired, in premises that once belonged to De blindas tekniska fabrik, a workshop for blind people. Its collections trace the history of blind and partially sighted people in Sweden back to the late 1700s. And inside Skogskyrkogården, the Woodland Cemetery, is Almhöjden, a hill crowned with weeping elms that looks like something out of a Caspar David Friedrich painting.
Gårdsten har vänt en trend. När det komm: Gårdsten is a neighbourhood that turned itself around. When the municipal housing company Gårdstensbostäder was set up in 1997, more than 800 of its roughly 2,200 flats were standing empty. The company put its office right in the middle of the area so it could work closely with tenants. The renovation of eastern Gårdsten won the Stora Samhällsbyggarpriset, one of Sweden's top urban development awards, in 2006, and in 2019 Gårdsten became the first neighbourhood to be taken off the police list of 'particularly vulnerable areas'.
Görvälns griftegård ritades av landskaps: Görväln cemetery was designed by the landscape architect Per Friberg and laid out between 1966 and 1977 on old farmland and a wooded hill. A 300-metre watercourse with eleven waterfalls runs down to a large reflecting pool. In 2017 a Muslim section with 220 coffin graves opened. Nearby is Görväln school, in use from 1896 to 1939 – the school building is still standing.
Göteborgs botaniska trädgård öppnade 192: Gothenburg Botanical Garden opened in 1923 and is one of the larger botanical gardens in Europe. It has a rock garden, a Japanese valley and greenhouses full of thousands of plants. Across the road is Slottsskogen, the city's big park.
Göteborgs stad tackade 1874 nej till att: In 1874 the City of Gothenburg turned down the chance to buy the Tingstadsvassen reed beds at ten öre per square foot – yet two years later it decided to buy the area for 300,000 kronor. Nearby are two veteran vessels: the sailing ship Isolda from 1902, the last Swedish merchant sailing ship in ocean trade, and the tug Sven from 1897, built as an icebreaking steam tug.
Göteborgs stadsmuseum i Ostindiska huset: Gothenburg City Museum in the East India House
Göteborgsoperan står ungefär där länscel: The Gothenburg Opera stands roughly where the county jail used to be, a prison that opened in 1857. From Lilla Bommen harbour, cargo and passenger boats once sailed all the way to Stockholm and Norrköping, by way of the Göta älv river, the Göta Canal and the lakes. Outside the opera house, water trickles down Källan, the Spring, a stone sculpture by Bård Breivik from 1994.
Haga Nygata och jättekanelbullar: Haga Nygata and giant cinnamon buns
Haga parkmuseum i Koppartälten: Haga Park Museum in the Copper Tents
Hagakyrkan invigdes 1859 och ligger vid: Hagakyrkan, the Haga Church, was consecrated in 1859 and stands at the edge of Haga, one of Gothenburg's oldest districts. Haga Nygata, Haga's main street, is lined with little shops and cafés – and this is where you'll find the famous giant cinnamon buns, as big as a side plate.
Hagaparken börjar nästan här. Gustav III: Hagaparken park starts almost right here. Gustav III had Övre Haga built as an inn in 1788–1789, with two kitchens and three dining rooms. Haga Trädgård is known from Bellman's song 'Fjäriln vingad syns på Haga' – 'The winged butterfly is seen at Haga' – and fittingly, the Butterfly House moved into one of its greenhouses in 1989. For a view, climb Frösundatoppen, about 72 metres above sea level.
Hagsätra centrum invigdes 1960 efter bar: Hagsätra's shopping centre opened in 1960 after just a year of building work – the same year the metro arrived – and cost 25 million kronor in the money of the day. Its best-known feature is “Barnet med käpphästen”, The Child with the Hobby Horse, a copper sculpture by Marie Stenqvist. And if you need some greenery, Hagsätraskogen is close by – a forest that in 2021 became Stockholm's eleventh nature reserve.
Hallunda var en levande jordbruksbygd än: Hallunda was a thriving farming area right up until the early 1970s, when the Million Programme – Sweden's huge state housing drive – arrived and Botkyrkastaden was built on the farmland. Hallunda manor, an 18th-century manor house nearby, was left out of the town plan, though, and it's still privately owned – one of the few old manor estates in the Stockholm area that is. Next to it lies a large Iron Age burial ground.
Hammargården ligger på sydöstra Färingsö: Hammargården lies in south-eastern Färingsö, and its small houses were once staff homes for the youth reform school that stood here. Just to the south, Lullehovsbron bridge crosses Lullehovssundet, a strait in Lake Mälaren just over 200 metres wide and about seven metres deep in the middle. At its southern end lies the little island of Kaninholmen, Rabbit Island. The bridge and the strait both take their name from the hamlet of Lullehov on Lindö.
Hammarkullen är känt för sin karneval, s: Hammarkullen is known for its carnival, which fills the district with music, dancing and colourful costumes every year. The stop is deep inside the rock, and you reach it by a long escalator.
Handelshögskolan grundades 1909 som Sver: Handelshögskolan, the Stockholm School of Economics, was founded in 1909 as Sweden's first business school, and its main building on Sveavägen was designed by Ivar Tengbom in 1925. Its researchers have helped shape what economists call the Stockholm School. Around the corner is Betlehemskyrkan, Bethlehem Church. Its predecessor from 1840, near Hötorget, was Sweden's first free-church building. That church was demolished in 1953, and the new one was consecrated here in 1956.
Haninge kulturpark: Haninge kulturpark, the Haninge culture park
Harestads kyrka ligger ett stenkast häri: Harestad Church is a stone's throw from here, in the church village of Kyrkeby. The village was classed as a small locality in 1995, but it has since had fewer than 50 residents and lost that status. So the village may be too small for the statistics, but the church still stands, in Harestad parish – part of Kungälv municipality since 1971.
Harestads socken ligger vid kusten sydvä: Harestad parish lies on the coast south-west of Kungälv and takes in small villages such as Flateby, Toreby and Kornhall. In 2000 it had 951 residents. Its parish church, Harestad Church, stands in the church village of Kyrkeby, a little way off. The parish used to belong to the old hundred, or district, of Inlands Södre, and it has been part of Kungälv municipality since 1971.
Havsguden Poseidon av Carl Milles har va: Carl Milles's sea god Poseidon has watched over the square since 1931 and is one of Gothenburg's best-loved landmarks. Gathered around him are the Gothenburg Museum of Art, the Concert Hall, the City Theatre and the City Library, the city's most visited cultural venue. In Götapalatset, the Göta cinema opened in 1936, closed in 1997 and was given a new lease of life in 2015. And don't miss Peter Linde's bronze statue of the writer Karin Boye.
Hela Bergshamra ligger i Nationalstadspa: The whole of Bergshamra lies within the Royal National City Park. The land for the Kungshamra student housing was donated by King Gustaf VI Adolf – hence the name, ‘King's Hamra’. The 1951 water tower by Edsviken bay is a landmark visible from far around, and on Pipers väg stands Övre Karlsro, also known as Carl Malmsten's house.
Hela kommundelen har fått sitt namn efte: The whole district is named after Breviks gård, a manor whose roots go back to the 14th century. Its last main building was pulled down in 1987, and Brevik centre, with its stop on the Lidingöbanan light railway, stands there now. Next door is Blocket, one of Lidingö's oldest apartment buildings, built in 1914–1915. And in 1905 the owner of the manor offered to pay for a small primary school in the area out of his own pocket.
Hela kommundelen har fått sitt namn från: The whole district is named after the farm a couple of hundred metres away. Flemingsbergs gård, once spelt Flemmingsbergs gård, is a manor and former estate with a history going back to the 15th century. On the other side is the industrial area, where LM Ericsson's central warehouse was in its day quite a sight thanks to its automation.
Helige Savas serbisk-ortodoxa kyrka är h: The Serbian Orthodox Church of Saint Sava is dedicated to Serbia's national saint, who founded the Serbian Orthodox Church in 1219, and it's the cathedral for the church's Scandinavian diocese. Nearby is Skagershuset, a block of flats with a wooden façade that was named Stockholm's Building of the Year in 2014. It's named after Skagersvägen, the street, which in turn takes its name from Lake Skagern on the border between the provinces of Värmland and Västergötland.
Helige kung Stefan Dečanskis kyrka, Göte: Church of the Holy King Stefan Dečanski, Gothenburg
Hellasgården är en frisksportanläggning: Hellasgården is an outdoor sports centre and clubhouse on Lake Källtorpssjön, in the heart of the Nacka Reserve. It's the start and finish of Källtorpssjön runt, the yellow trail – a five-kilometre walk marked with yellow dots and arrows. On the north-western shore of the lake is Stengärdet, old farmland enclosed by a stone wall that's protected as an ancient monument.
Hemgården på Östermalmsgatan blev 1906 S: In 1906, Hemgården on Östermalmsgatan became Sweden's first collective housing block. A shared central kitchen was meant to free up time so that residents, young women in particular, could go out to work. The building went up on the site of the 18th-century Brandel sugar refinery, which had also done duty as a cholera hospital. Nearby was Palmgrenska samskolan, the first school in Scandinavia to teach girls and boys together all the way to the upper secondary leaving exam.
Herrgården Lilla Frösunda från 1700-tale: Lilla Frösunda is an 18th-century manor house whose owners included the gardener Anders Lundström. The Swedish state used the main building as an officers' mess until the late 1980s. When Canon moved to Frösunda in 2001, the company brought in the architects Tengboms, who designed its office on Gustav III:s boulevard to echo Canon's high-tech image.
Herrgården Riddersvik ligger vid Mälaren: Riddersvik manor stands on the shore of Lake Mälaren, beside Lövstafjärden bay, and you can still explore Tempeludden headland and the English Park, also called the Star Park. The garden cottage, probably 18th-century, was home over the years to estate workers and crofters' families, and every year the manor holds a Christmas market. The garden suburb also had its own station on the Spånga–Lövsta railway, which carried passengers from 1889 to 1956.
Herrgården Stensjöhill vid Stensjöns väs: The manor house Stensjöhill, on the western shore of Lake Stensjön, has led quite a varied life. It was built in 1917 for the manager of the margarine factory nearby, became offices in the 1980s and was later taken over by the Hare Krishna movement. After that it became a hotel and conference centre, and at the end of 2012 it was sold to become a residential care home for young people. Closest of all is the Kikås ridge, home to Sweden's largest free-standing insect hotel.
Herrgården och det tidigare säteriet Säb: Säby gård, a manor and former noble estate in the Järvafältet nature reserve, has been a state listed building since 1983. It's now owned by Järfälla Municipality, and the main building houses a Waldorf preschool – so the youngest children here have unusually grand surroundings. South of the farm is the rune slab U 90, a Viking Age inscription carved straight into the bedrock.
Herrgården Ålstens gård står på en grund: The manor house of Ålstens gård, right here, stands on 16th-century foundations, and the massive stone walls in the cellar tell you just how old it is. In 1936 it was bought by Axel Gauffin, director of the Nationalmuseum, who restored the house and lived here until 1957. Below it stretches Ålstensängen, one of the estate's old fields, now an open meadow that runs down to a sandy beach on Lake Mälaren.
Herrängens gård har anor från 1600-talet: Herrängens gård dates back to the 1600s, when it was a croft called Isbergatorpet belonging to the Långbro estate. It stands on the northern shore of Lake Långsjön and has given its name to the whole district of Herrängen. The City Museum has marked it in blue, meaning the buildings are judged to be of exceptional historical value.
Hersby gymnasium: Hersby gymnasium, the upper secondary school
Hersby gymnasium, som tidigare hette Lid: Hersby gymnasium, the upper secondary school once known as Lidingö högre allmänna läroverk, got its first school building in 1914, which was rebuilt and extended until 1957. A stone's throw away are the terraced houses of the Tegen större and Tegen mindre blocks, built as early as 1908–1909 to designs by Jacob Gate and now classed as culturally and historically valuable. Hersby as a whole forms the core of Lidingö villastad, the garden suburb founded in 1906.
Hisingen är stor, cirka 199 kvadratkilom: Hisingen is big – about 199 square kilometres, roughly half the area of Gothenburg municipality – and about a quarter of the city's residents live here. The island is framed by the Göta älv river to the south and east, the Nordre älv river to the north and the Kattegat sea to the west. The area also includes the small settlement of Holm in Tuve parish.
Hisingen, ön vi befinner oss på, är till: Hisingen, the island we're on now, is Sweden's fifth-largest island by area – after Gotland, Öland, Södertörn and Orust – and the second most populous. It's bounded by the Göta älv river to the south and east, the Nordre älv to the north and the Kattegat to the west. At 199 square kilometres, it makes up roughly half of Gothenburg municipality.

Hitta Emotrappan i Nordstan: Find Emotrappan, the Emo Stairs, in Nordstan
Hjalmar Brantingsplatsen är Hisingens st: Hjalmar Brantingsplatsen is Hisingen's main transport hub. Hisingen is Sweden's fourth-largest island, and it was once where both ships and cars were built. Volvo was founded in Gothenburg in 1927, and its head office is still here on Hisingen.
Hjorthagen var ursprungligen ett hägn fö: Hjorthagen – ‘the deer park’ – was originally an enclosure for the king's deer. In the late 19th century it became an industrial suburb, with the Värta gasworks and power station as its landmarks. The headland of Ropsten has a lovely name: ‘the calling stone’, where people shouted across the water for the ferry. A 54-storey, 187-metre skyscraper called Stockholmsfyren was once planned for the end of the Lidingö Bridge, but it never got off the ground.
Hjulsta, den västra delen av Tensta, är: Hjulsta, the western part of Tensta, is a textbook example of separating cars from people – a hallmark of the Million Programme, Sweden's big housing drive of the 1960s and 70s. A ring road runs around the more or less car-free housing area, and footbridges tie it together over sunken streets. The metro station, the end of line 10, was blasted out of the rock beneath Hjulstaskolan school.
Hjällbo centrum byggdes 1969 och fick et: Hjällbo centrum was built in 1969 and given a new look when it was rebuilt in 2001. On the square there's a market hall selling fruit and veg, and the shopping building has an oriental grocery, a gift shop and a pizzeria. There's a library, a pharmacy and a church here too, so most of everyday life fits around a single square.
Hjällbo är en stadsdel på hela 927 hekta: Hjällbo is a district covering a full 927 hectares in north-eastern Gothenburg, and Eriksbo lies within it. A little further on begins Nordöstra Göteborg, North-East Gothenburg, an urban area made up mainly of Hammarkullen and Gunnared, with Gårdsten, Lövgärdet, Rannebergen and Angered centre. It's the largest urban area in Sweden that isn't the main town of its own municipality.
Hornsbergs strandpark: Hornsbergs strandpark, the Hornsberg waterfront park
Hornstull har fått sitt namn efter tulle: Hornstull is named after the toll gate – the 'tull' – that once stood here on the old city boundary. This used to be a working-class neighbourhood; today it's one of the liveliest corners of Södermalm, with restaurants lining Hornstulls strand and views out over the water.

Hornstull is named after the toll gate that once stood here on the old city boundary. This used to be a working-class neighbourhood; today it's one of the liveliest corners of Södermalm, with restaurants lining the Hornstulls strand waterfront and views out over the water. To the south lies Tantolunden park, with its allotments and big lawns.
Hornstulls strand, restauranger vid vatt: Hornstulls strand and its waterside restaurants
Hotell The Weaver reser sig 22 våningar,: Hotel The Weaver rises 22 storeys, with 370 rooms and conference space for 600 people. The name is a nod to Krokslätts fabriker, the Krokslätt mills, where weaving went on from start to finish right into the 1970s. Where the looms once clattered, business travellers now sleep.
Huddinge centrum ligger mitt i en villas: Huddinge centrum sits in the middle of a garden suburb that never happened. In 1902 the owner of Fullersta gård began selling off plots for Huddinge villastad, since selling building land close to Stockholm paid better than farming. Only a few of the old villas are left.
Humlegården och Kungliga biblioteket: Humlegården park and the National Library of Sweden
Hungrig? Kville saluhall öppnade 2013 me: Hungry? Kville saluhall, the food hall, opened in 2013 with meat, fish and seafood counters, a bakery and plenty of restaurants. Further on was the Gnistan cinema. It opened in 1938 with the military farce Kamrater i vapenrocken, and the curtain came down for good in 1968 after Django Shoots First. On Kvilletorget stands Carl Milles' statue Susanna, also known as Girl with a Shell.
Husby, en bit härifrån, är byggt på norr: Husby, a short way from here, is built on the northern part of Järvafältet, which the army used as a training ground right up until 1965. From 1971 to 1980 the district was officially called Husby gård. Here you'll also find Husby Church, designed by Karl Erik Hjalmarson and consecrated in 1976, which the City Museum has given a green heritage listing – and the Husby baths, with an adventure pool and a diving tower.
Husbybadet öppnade kring millennieskifte: Husbybadet opened around the turn of the millennium, tempting swimmers with a water park, a jacuzzi and a sauna. A little further on is Akalla church, which has an unusual story. It was consecrated in 1976, and in 2020 the Church of Sweden sold it to the Catholic Diocese of Stockholm. Today it's the home church of the Syriac Catholic Church.
Husen glesnar och villor tar över. Snart: The buildings thin out and villas take over. Keep watching – the sea is coming up soon.
Huvudgatan Sturegatan hette från början: The main street, Sturegatan, was originally called Storgatan, but in the late 1800s it was renamed after Sten Sture the Elder. Along it you'll find shops and restaurants, Folkets hus, the community hall, and Sundbybergs köksbryggeri, a brewery – and there was once a cinema here too. The Allaktivitetshuset cultural centre opened in 2013.
Huvudsta har fler slott än man kanske tr: Huvudsta has more palaces than you might expect: Karlberg Palace, Huvudsta gård and Huvudsta Old Palace. By Lake Ulvsundasjön there's also the popular Huvudstabadet pool. And 25 metres beneath your feet, in the rock, is the metro station, decorated with Per Holmberg's artwork Hängande trädgårdar, 'Hanging Gardens', from 1985.
Huvudstråket genom Akalla heter Sibelius: Akalla's main pedestrian street, Sibeliusgången, is named after the Finnish composer Jean Sibelius, and it runs for 900 metres. Along the way, Bertil Johnson's fountains from 1976 bubble away. But the name Akalla goes back to the Middle Ages: in Akalla village stands the 17th-century Storgården, in one of the best-preserved village settings around Stockholm, complete with a 4-H farm and a café.
Hägerstens gård är en herrgård vars mang: Hägerstens gård is a manor house whose main building and wings are still standing, but since 1997 it has been a housing cooperative with just five flats. At Hägerstens torg – also known as Axelsbergs centrum – the main building is modernist, its façades clad in dark red ceramic tiles. And at night, the trees on Axelsbergs torg are lit up from below by spotlights.
Häggvikstunneln är den kortaste av Norro: Häggvikstunneln is the shortest of the three road tunnels on the Norrortsleden ring road, at just 289 metres, and there's a park on its roof. A little further on is Klasroskolan, a school built in 1804 that was Sollentuna's only school until 1871. It was put up beside the parish's most famous spring, where travellers used to water their horses – the diarist Malla Silfverstolpe called it “la bonne fontaine”. Today the old school is a museum.
Hällsvik vid Hälleviken var förr en lite: Hällsvik, on the Hälleviken bay, was once a small fishing village where people made their living from fishing and, in time, farming – and some of the original buildings are still here. In the heyday of the shipyards, many yard workers bought themselves summer cottages here. Over the years the plots have been divided up, and the cottages have either been demolished or rebuilt as proper houses.
Hälsa på Bellmansbysten: Say hello to the bust of Bellman
Hälsa på bronskvinnan Väntan: Say hello to Väntan, Waiting, the bronze woman
Hälsö är en liten ö i Göteborgs norra sk: Hälsö is a small island in Gothenburg's northern archipelago, just 1.28 square kilometres, with around 590 permanent residents. On its south side a bridge takes you over to Öckerö, and from there you can carry on to Hönö and catch the ferry to Hisingen and the mainland. The islands hang together like pearls on a string.
Här bjuds på namnförvirring: Skarpnäcks: Here's a name muddle for you: Skarpnäck's old school from 1928 is in Enskededalen, while Skarpnäck school from 1952 is across the road in Kärrtorp. The younger school has been called both Nya skolan, the New School, and Skarpnäcks nya skola before getting its old name back, and since 1992 it has served as an annex to its older neighbour. The Stockholm City Museum has classed both school buildings as culturally valuable.
Här doftar det konspiration. En bit bort: There's a whiff of conspiracy in the air here. Not far off is Huvudsta gamla slott, Huvudsta Old Palace, a wooden house from 1750 where, rumour has it, the murder of Gustav III was plotted. It was originally the main house of Huvudsta Farm but was moved in 1834. Down by the water you may also spot the schooner Constantia, built in Denmark in 1908 and now a sail training ship for young people and adults alike.
Här fanns en gång Vårby gård, även kalla: This is where Vårby gård, also known as Vårby Castle, once stood – an estate the City of Stockholm bought in 1931. The main house burned down on 5 May 1975, and today the grounds are mostly park and allotments. Close by, at Duvberget, the Vårby hoard, a buried silver treasure, was discovered in 1871. In the manor park you'll find Myrstugan, a boatswain's croft from the early 1700s that was moved here in 1986.
Här finns ett av Stockholms mer udda mus: Here you'll find one of Stockholm's quirkier museums: Sveriges VVS-museum, the Swedish Plumbing and Heating Museum. The collection started out in Katrineholm and reopened here in Bromma in 2016. Further off, in Tuvanparken, stood Tuvan, a home for people with nervous disorders, in the 1890s. Three patients died in a fire there in 1940, and the building was pulled down in 1960. Where the nursing home once stood, there's now a park.
Här finns gott om skolbänkar: Nacka gymn: There's no shortage of school desks around here. Nacka gymnasium is one of Sweden's biggest schools, and its neighbour, Eklidens skola, is one of the country's largest secondary schools for 13- to 16-year-olds, with an ice rink and a swimming pool right next door. The name Järla comes from the title jarl, meaning earl. In nearby Vikdalen, Stockholm families built summer villas in the late 19th century and came out by steamboat. Then a car engine factory opened in Augustendal, workers moved in, and the villas became workers' housing.
Här gick en gång Göteborgs gräns. Område: This is where Gothenburg's boundary once ran. Kungssten used to be called Stadsgränsen, 'the City Limit', and when the Oden cinema on Långedragsvägen opened in 1919, it stood just outside the city line. Under the hill runs the Gnistäng tunnel: 712 metres long, one of Sweden's longer road tunnels, carrying about 55,000 vehicles a day.
Här har flyghistoria skrivits. En bit bo: Aviation history was made here. Not far away is Säve Airport, which for a time was known as Göteborg City Airport. It was once Sweden's eighth-busiest airport, popular with budget airlines. After 2015 the airlines moved to Landvetter, and since 2026 the only aircraft flying from here are police and emergency service helicopters. Closer to the stop you'll see the panels of Nya Solevi glittering in the sun – a solar farm that was built in just three months in 2018.
Här i Amhult, några hundra meter bort, l: A few hundred metres from here in Amhult was Torslanda airfield, Gothenburg's airport from 1923 right up until 1977, when Landvetter took over. It was originally called Göteborgs Flyghamn and had a seaplane harbour too. By the time it closed, it was one of the oldest airfields in Europe with scheduled flights.
Här i Högdalens industriområde ligger Hö: Here in the Högdalen industrial area is Högdalsdepån, one of the metro's depots, where the trains rest and get serviced. A little further on is Högdalstoppen, three man-made hills, one of which got a disc golf course in 2005. From the summits in Fagersjö there's a sweeping view over southern Stockholm.
Här i Skälltorp, norra Backa, finns en b: Here in Skälltorp, in northern Backa, there's a slice of Swedish music history. In 1970 the music theatre group Nationalteatern moved into Backa Fritidsgård, the youth centre on Selma Lagerlöfs torg. Close by is the Friedländer cemetery – with just over twenty graves, the smallest in Gothenburg.
Här i Västra Frölunda har gatorna musika: Here in Västra Frölunda the streets have musical names, such as Musikvägen and Positivgatan – Music Road and Barrel Organ Street. The district was built in the 1960s, when Gothenburg was spreading rapidly southwards.
Här i de gamla AGA-fabrikerna var uppfin: Here in the old AGA factories, the inventor Gustaf Dalén worked from 1912 until his death in 1937 – hence the name Dalénum. Next door is Stillerska Filmgymnasiet, a film school for upper secondary students named after the director Mauritz Stiller, who started his career in the 1910s at Svenska Biografteatern's film studio, right here on Lidingö. A little further on, look out for AGA's yellow optics tower, where submarine periscopes were developed.
Här i närheten låg Galgbacken, Stockholm: Close to here was Galgbacken, Gallows Hill – Stockholm's largest and last public execution site. A few stones by Solandergatan still mark the spot, which is now a protected ancient monument. The street is named after the botanist Daniel Solander, one of Carl Linnaeus's students. And on a happier note: in an old cinema just next door, EMI built a recording studio modelled on Abbey Road, and it was there that Anni-Frid Lyngstad recorded her first solo album, before ABBA was formed.
Här i trakten fanns en gång en ort som h: Around here there was once a place called Backen och Hultet. In 1990 it was classed as a small settlement in Kållered parish, but it later merged with both Kållered and Lindome, and no locality by that name exists any more. A little further off is Lake Tulebosjön, eight metres deep.
Här i trakten stod slaget vid Brännkyrka: It was around here, on 27 July 1518, that the Battle of Brännkyrka was fought. In the closing stages of the wars over the Nordic union, Swedish rebels took on the union troops – and the Swedes won. Things were far more peaceful at Enskedemejeriet, one of the dairies of the Mjölkcentralen cooperative, which was in business here from 1943 to 1992. A little further on is Valla torg, named after Valla gård, a farm with medieval roots. Look out for the Vallafontänen fountain by Bertil Johnson.
Här ligger Sahlgrenska universitetssjukh: This is Sahlgrenska University Hospital, one of the biggest hospitals in Northern Europe. It's named after Niclas Sahlgren, another of the wealthy directors of the Swedish East India Company, whose money laid the foundations of the hospital.
Här ligger Skinnarviksberget, den högsta: This is Skinnarviksberget, the highest natural point in central Stockholm. Climb to the top for a sweeping view over Riddarfjärden bay, the City Hall and Kungsholmen. The name comes from the skinners who once worked hides into leather down by the cove.
Här ligger två av Stockholms mest besökt: Two of Stockholm's most visited museums are right here. The palatial building is the Nordic Museum. Behind it is the Vasa Museum, home to the warship Vasa, which sank on its maiden voyage in 1628 and was raised in 1961.
Här ligger Östermalms saluhall från 1888: This is Östermalms saluhall, a market hall from 1888 and one of the most beautiful food halls in Europe. Inside the old brick building, traders sell fish, cheese and all kinds of delicacies.
Här låg Råsunda fotbollsstadion, en gång: This was the site of Råsunda football stadium, once Sweden's national arena, with room for 37,285 spectators. It had a soft opening in April 1937 with AIK against Malmö FF, and in May that year King Gustaf V officially opened it at the match between Sweden and England. A stone's throw away is Charlottenburg, Solna's local heritage centre, with a local history museum and a little park to play in.
Här låg en gång Sveriges största mentals: Sweden's largest psychiatric hospital once stood here. Beckomberga Hospital was in use from 1932 to 1995, and in the mid-20th century it had 2,000 patients, making it one of the biggest in Europe. By the time it closed, there were around 250 beds left. Since the mid-2000s the old hospital buildings have been turned into homes.
Här mäter gatunamnen jord. Marklandsgata: The street names round here are all about measuring land. Marklandsgatan was named in 1959 after 'markland', an old unit for valuing land. At the Marklandsgatan stop, tram line 3 turns round, while lines 1, 2, 7 and 8 carry on towards Frölunda torg and Tynnered. Right beside it runs Dag Hammarskjöldsleden, five kilometres long from Linnéplatsen.
Här passerar Hagsätrastråket, ett promen: This is where Hagsätrastråket passes by – a 12-kilometre walking route that runs all the way from Hagsätra to Stortorget, the main square in Gamla stan, the Old Town, by way of Enskede gård and across the Skansbron bridge to Södermalm. The name Enskede gård comes from the old manor and its large estate, mentioned as far back as the 1390s. Right next door is Enskedeparken, which was given its name in 1979.
Här på västra Södermalm snurrade förr vä: Out here in western Södermalm, the Brinckan windmill once turned its sails. It's recorded from the 1670s and disappeared in 1884, but it lives on in Josabeth Sjöberg's watercolours from the 1850s. The neighbourhood is called Södra stationsområdet, the South Station area, because Stockholm's first railway station stood here, along with a large rail yard, until the city bought the land in 1979 to build homes. Up on the hill is Bergsgruvan park.
Här pågår en liten stavningsstrid. Torge: There's a little spelling feud going on here. The square was named in 1963 after Villa Brunsbo, by the nearby level crossing, which was owned by the Brundin family – so the family insists that spelling it with a double 'n' is simply wrong. The main centre building, designed by Sven Brolid's architecture firm, went up in the 1960s, and today the square is a busy bus hub.
The road here quite literally rests on a landslide. Jordfallsbron takes its name from 'jordfall', an old word for landslide – and around 1150, a landslide sent part of the ground at what is now Källarliden tumbling into the Göta älv river. The eastern end of the bridge and the E45 now stand on top of the debris. The bridge is about 700 metres long and can open, with a 49.5-metre bascule span.
Här tar innerstaden slut och vallgraven: This is where the inner city ends and Vallgraven, the old moat, begins. The winding canal is all that's left of the fortifications that once ringed Gothenburg. On its bank stands Feskekôrka, the city's fish market hall from 1874. It looks just like a church, and Gothenburgers have called it the ‘fish church’ ever since.
Här är en klurig geografifråga: centrala: Here's a tricky geography question for you: central Spånga, with its commuter train station and town centre, is actually in the district of Solhem, while Spånga Church is in the district of Tensta. That's because Spånga isn't an official area – the name lives on from the old parish. In the other direction lies Nälsta, a mix of villas, terraced houses and blocks of flats.
Här är ett ortnamnsmysterium som löser s: Here's a place-name puzzle that solves itself. The historic farm of Råsta and its neighbour Frösunda together gave rise to the name Råsunda – Råsta plus Frösunda. And the neighbouring district of Hallonbergen? It sits on a rocky hill and was probably named after the raspberry thickets that once grew all over it – 'hallon' is Swedish for raspberry.
Här, på Campus Solna, utses varje år mot: It's here at Campus Solna that the Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet chooses the winners of the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine every year. Next door is Biomedicum, one of Europe's largest laboratories, with just over 82,000 square metres spread over eleven floors. Also look out for Aula Medica, designed by Gert Wingårdh and named Building of the Year in 2014.
Här, vid idrottsplatsen Yttern strax syd: Here at the Yttern sports ground, just south-west of the Rollsbo industrial area, Kungälv Arena is taking shape. The plan is a bandy hall for around 2,500 spectators and an ice rink for around 1,500, with room for bandy teams, hockey players and figure skaters alike. The arena will replace the historic bandy ground Skarpe Nord and also ease the pressure on Oasen, the town's old ice rink.
Häradsvägen, som slutar en bit härifrån: Häradsvägen, which ends not far from here at the Stuvsta tunnel, was built in the mid-1920s as a public relief project by the road association of Svartlösa härad – the local administrative district, or “hundred”, which gave the road its name. The forest had to be cleared to make way for it, and villas soon sprang up along it. The tunnel itself is unusual: its northern entrance is built right into a block of flats that straddles the road.
Härifrån kan man vandra riktigt långt, f: From here you can walk a very long way indeed. Björkhagen metro station is the starting point for the first stage of Sörmlandsleden, a looping network of hiking trails that winds for some 1,000 kilometres through the province of Södermanland. Markuskyrkan, St Mark's Church, next door, is built on an old lake bed in the birch grove that gave the district its name.
Härifrån ser du Älvsborgsbron spänna öve: From here you can see the Älvsborg Bridge stretching across the Göta älv river. When it opened in 1966, it was the longest suspension bridge in Sweden. Out at the mouth of the river lies the 17th-century New Älvsborg Fortress, which guarded the city against the Danes for more than a hundred years.
Härifrån är det 10,9 kilometer med pende: From here it's 10.9 kilometres by commuter train to Stockholm Central, and on an ordinary weekday in winter around 5,400 people get on at this station. Next door is Eriksberg, a narrow strip of land between the E4 motorway and the railway, named after a small croft called Eriksberg dating from 1819. A little further on is Silverdal cemetery, laid out in 1914 as the burial ground for the Stockholm garrison.
Härifrån är det cirka 14,5 kilometer in: From here it's about 14.5 kilometres to Stockholm Central Station, and the commuter-train station has four tracks so that freight and long-distance trains can speed straight through. In 1728, at Järfälla Church, Olof Celsius the Elder found a runestone that had probably been lying there as a step. It then went missing, but in 1939 seven fragments turned up, and they're now kept at the Swedish History Museum.
Härifrån är det nära till Fåfängan, ett: From here it's not far to Fåfängan, a little café perched on a cliff with one of the best views in Stockholm, out over the harbour entrance, Djurgården and Gamla stan, the Old Town.

From here it's not far to Fåfängan, a little café up on a clifftop with one of the best views in Stockholm – out over the harbour entrance, Djurgården and Gamla stan, the Old Town. A little to the west, Fjällgatan offers another classic viewpoint, with old houses and cobbled streets.
Härifrån är det nära till Götaplatsen, s: From here it's not far to Götaplatsen, the city's cultural square. That's where you'll find the Gothenburg Museum of Art, which opened in 1923, along with the City Theatre and the Concert Hall. In the middle stands Poseidon, Carl Milles' mighty sea god.
Härifrån är det nära till Rågsveds friom: From here it's not far to the Rågsved open space, also known as Kräppladalen: just over 100 hectares of rift-valley landscape with ridges, plateaus and steep slopes. Part of it became a nature reserve in September 2018. Right in the middle is the Snösätra storage area, which since 2014 has turned into a hub for graffiti and street art – the walls are painted with the property owners' blessing.
Härryda kommun har en kuriös detalj: en: Härryda municipality has a curious quirk: a small part in the west, Helenedal, actually counts as part of Gothenburg's urban area. A little north-east of Mölnlycke is Stora Bråta, just nine kilometres from central Gothenburg – the city's nearest small village. The municipality's main town is Mölnlycke.
Hässelby har fått sitt namn från Hässelb: Hässelby is named after Hässelby Palace, whose lands once covered much of today's Hässelby gård, Hässelby strand and Hässelby villastad. Many of the estate's farms and crofts have lent their names to places around here. And a fun quirk: the palace is in the district of Hässelby gård, but its postal address says Vällingby.
Hässelby slott uppfördes på 1650-talet,: Hässelby Palace was built in the 1650s, possibly to designs by Simon de la Vallée, and it's one of the oldest surviving secular buildings in Stockholm. Notice how its tower-topped wings are angled slightly inwards. Just east of the entrance, the runestone U 79 sits on top of a Viking Age burial mound – although it didn't start out here. It originally stood below Skesta backe, about three kilometres away, and was moved in the 1860s. These days the palace markets itself as Hesselby, using the older spelling.
Hässelby strand bildades som stadsdel 19: Hässelby strand became a district in its own right in 1954. Here on the shore of Lake Mälaren stands Hässelbyverket, a combined heat and power station that has been producing both electricity and district heating since 1959. The City Museum has given its buildings a green rating, meaning they are especially valuable. When the metro arrived on 18 November 1958, the first train left Bagarmossen at 13.28, with flags flying at both ends.
Hässelby trädgårds- och hembygdsmuseum: Hässelby garden and local history museum
Hässelby villastad är Stockholms västlig: Hässelby villastad is Stockholm's westernmost district and, by area, its largest. Nearby is the Åkermyntan shopping centre from 1977, which has the curious honour of featuring in a sketch by the comedy group Killinggänget. Further on, outside the Hässelby garden and local heritage museum, stands a grey granite runestone found at Riddersvik in the early 19th century and moved to the museum in 1988.

Hässelby villastad is Stockholm's westernmost district, and its largest by area. It was once a municipality in its own right, the market town of Hässelby villastad. Not far from here, outside the Hässelby garden and local history museum, stands a grey granite runestone. It was found at Riddersvik in the early 19th century and moved to the museum in 1988. The whole Hässelby area takes its name from Hässelby Palace.
Hässelbygårdsskolan byggdes med det mest: Hässelbygårdsskolan was built with just about everything: a doctor's surgery, two dining halls, a swimming pool and an assembly hall that doubled as the Prisma cinema. The cinema opened in 1960 and was open to the public until 1984. The nearby metro station sits on a viaduct above Hässelby torg, the square.
Hästa klack är ett av Järfällas allra ny: Hästa klack is one of Järfälla's newest nature reserves, protected since 2026, with 14 hectares of conifer forest and open woodland edges. In the other direction is Kyrkbyn, once called Järfälla gård and one of the parish's historic farms. Today its name lives on in a housing area within Barkarby villastad, a garden suburb of real historical value.
Hästarna är stjärnorna i Åby. Strax inti: In Åby, the horses are the stars. Right beside us is Åbytravet, Sweden's second-largest trotting track and home to Åby Travgymnasium, one of the country's oldest trotting schools for upper secondary students, where they can earn a B trainer's licence. Very close to the stop is Åbybadet, the swimming baths that opened in 2023. And the name Mölndal? It comes from the mills that have stood by the rapids of the Mölndalsån river since the Middle Ages.
Hästskosömsfabriken: Hästskosömsfabriken, the old horseshoe nail factory
Hågelby gård har medeltida rötter, men d: Hågelby farm has medieval roots, but most of today's buildings and the park were created in the 1910s at the initiative of the telephone maker Lars Magnus Ericsson and his wife Hilda. Several of the buildings were made of reinforced concrete, a new thing in Sweden back then. A runestone from the mid-11th century stands by the farm, and from here the Aspen nature trail loops just over seven kilometres around the lake.
Håll i dig i rulltrappan! På tunnelbanes: Hold on tight on the escalator! Västra skogen metro station has Sweden's longest escalator: 66 metres long, with a rise of 33 metres. The record won't last, though – an escalator at Nacka station on the blue line is expected to be 82 metres long. Not far from here is Arken, the head office of Posten AB, the Swedish postal service.
Håll utkik efter de rödlysande neonglasö: Look out for the glowing red neon glasses above Ringdahls Optik at Fleminggatan 36. The signs date from the 1950s and 60s, and in 2017 the City Museum entered them in a competition for the city's finest illuminated signs, Lysande skylt. Celsiusgatan, nearby, is named after Anders Celsius – of temperature-scale fame – even though he had no particular link to Kungsholmen.
Hållplatsen har fått namn efter Långetjä: This stop is named after Långetjärnen, a woodland lake close by. It's eight metres deep and lies 93.5 metres above sea level. Nearby you'll also find two tiny ponds, the eastern and western Kroppedammarna. The water from here drains via the Finnebäcken stream towards the Kungsbackaån river.
Hållplatsen har fått namn efter Näsets k: The stop takes its name from Näsets kvarn, one of only two windmills left on Lidingö – back in the 1840s there were seven. Next to it is Kvarnskolan, a school from 1875 that at first took only girls. On Stockholmsvägen stands Näsets krog, an 18th-century roadside inn, and Villa Nynäs, on the site of what was probably Lidingö's first general store.
Hållplatsen har fått namn efter SKF, som: The stop is named after SKF, which was founded in Gothenburg in 1907 and went on to become the world's leading maker of ball bearings. The factory site here in Gamlestaden has been the company's home for more than a hundred years.
Hållplatsen har fått sitt namn efter Bil: The stop is named after Billdals gård, the manor house just around the corner in the Billdals park nature area in southern Gothenburg. A little north-east of Billdal is Stora Svindal, which counted as a small village in its own right until 2015 but has since been swallowed up by the town of Billdal.
Hållplatsen ligger vid Volvos bilfabrik,: This stop is at Torslandaverken, Volvo's car factory. Digging began on 4 November 1957, and King Gustaf VI Adolf opened the plant on 24 April 1964. The first car off the line was a Volvo Amazon, and the sporty P1800 was built here from the very start too. Today Torslanda makes models such as the XC90.
Högdalens centrum planerades med Välling: Högdalen's shopping centre was modelled on the one in Vällingby and completed in 1959. It was also home to the Rondo cinema from 1961 to 1983. Right next door is Högdalshallen, a sports centre from 1971, which closed for four years for a major refurbishment and reopened its swimming pool in June 2022. And at the metro station, the middle track leads into SL's train depot.
Högdalens industriområde har av Stockhol: The City of Stockholm has named the Högdalen industrial area the city's most important site for technical infrastructure. At its heart stands Högdalenverket, which burns rubbish and turns it into electricity and district heating. When it fired up in 1970 it produced only electricity; district heating followed in 1979. A little way off is Gubbängens IP sports ground, once known for car speedway.
Högdalshallen har haft en händelserik hi: Högdalshallen has had quite a turbulent history. The swimming and sports centre was completed in 1971, and from 2012 to 2018 it was run by a private company. After years of mismanagement, the City of Stockholm took it back, and it then closed for four years of major renovation before the pool finally reopened in June 2022.
Höghusen i Granängsringen, en bit härifr: The tower blocks of Granängsringen, a short way from here, went up in 1968–1969. With no fewer than 932 flats, they're a textbook example of housing planning under the Million Programme, Sweden's big push to build a million homes. Bollmora, where they stand, was actually a town in its own right from 1965 to 1974 and is now usually called Tyresö centrum. Further south in the municipality the forest of Storskogen takes over, with patches of genuine old-growth woodland in Tyresta National Park.
Höghusen i kvarteren här omkring hör til: The tower blocks around here belong to Granängsringen, built in just two years, 1968–69, with 932 flats – a textbook example of the Million Programme, Sweden's great housing drive. The area is part of Bollmora, which had 16,566 residents in 2010 and is where Tyresö municipality has its main offices. Bollmora used to be a town in its own right, but today it officially counts as part of the Stockholm urban area.
Höghusen runt omkring utgör Granängsring: The tower blocks all around us make up Granängsringen. It was built in record time, in 1968–69, with 932 flats, and it's a classic example of housing from the Million Programme, Sweden's great housing drive. A short walk away is Tyresö centrum – officially Bollmora – with the council offices, a glass-roofed shopping arcade and Bollmoradalen Church, the parish church for the whole of Tyresö.
Höghuset Hagahuset, ritat av Stig Annerf: The Hagahuset tower block, designed by Stig Annerfelt, went up between 1954 and 1957 as the County Council Building, and until the early 1970s it housed the whole of Stockholm County Council's administration. A short walk into Haga Park brings you to Frösundatoppen, also known as Haga kulle. At around 72 metres above sea level, it's one of the highest man-made hills in the county. And in the Copper Tents, the Haga Park Museum displays a large wooden model of Stora Haga Palace, the grand palace Gustav III had planned.
Höghuset och marmorintarsian på torget: The tower block and the marble inlay in the square
Höjden Stigberget var Stockholms avrättn: For most of the 16th and 17th centuries, the hill of Stigberget was where Stockholm carried out its executions – something the old block name Justitia still hints at. The mood is brighter these days. On Stigbergsgatan you'll find Blockmakarens hus, the Blockmaker's House, a museum flat furnished as it would have been in the early 1900s. Over on Tjärhovsgatan, Kafé 44 has been going since 1984 in the old Swedish bottle-cap factory, and right next door is Cornelisparken, a park dedicated to the much-loved singer-songwriter Cornelis Vreeswijk.
Höjden här, Strömmensberg, har kallats b: This hill, Strömmensberg, has also gone by the names Bagaregårdshöjden, Kristinedalshöjden and the Kristinedal plateau. The name probably comes from Olof Ström, ironworks owner at the Sävenäs estate, cousin of Niclas Sahlgren and one of the largest shareholders in the Swedish East India Company. Back in his day, in the 18th century, there wasn't a single building on the hill. Today the average age here is lower than in the rest of Gothenburg.
Hökarängen var en av de första förortern: Hökarängen was one of the first suburbs to spring up along the new metro after the Second World War. Its car-free centre, designed by David Helldén, became a model for suburbs all over Sweden. Right next to it is Farsta fire station, originally called Enskede fire station. And you can spot the light, arched roof of Gubbängshallen from far across Gubbängsfältet, the Gubbängen fields.
Hökarängen växte fram i rasande takt: 19: Hökarängen grew at breakneck speed: in 1946 just 45 people lived here, and only six years later there were 16,000. Its car-free town centre, designed by David Helldén, became the model for suburbs right across Sweden's new welfare state. Helldén also designed the Tobaksområdet area, with 16 slab blocks – one of them rejoicing in the name Sjöskumspipan 4, the Meerschaum Pipe. And the metro station here was the terminus of the city's very first metro line.
Hökarängens tunnelbanestation har en pla: Hökarängen metro station has earned its place in the history books. It opened on 1 October 1950 as the end of the line on Stockholm's very first metro route, from Slussen, and it stayed the terminus until November 1958. The station was designed by Peter Celsing. Close by, where Lingvägen meets Örbyleden, is Söderledskyrkan, a red-brick church opened in 1960 and protected by law as a listed building since 1990.
Hökmossens gård från 1750-talet var ursp: Hökmossen, a farmhouse from the 1750s, began as a croft belonging to Västberga gård, and since the mid-1990s a cultural association has run activities in the house. Close by runs Älvsjövägen, which invites a curious comparison: its 22,000 vehicles a day match all the daily border traffic between Norway and Sweden on the E6 and E18 combined.
Hönö har fått sitt namn av själva berget: Hönö takes its name from its rocks. The name comes from the Old West Norse word ‘hein’, meaning whetstone, a reference to the island's round, smooth-polished slabs of rock. Hönö has more people than any other island in Öckerö municipality, and since 2018 its built-up area has merged with Öckerö's. Hönö Church is not far away.
Hönö är den folkrikaste ön i Öckerö komm: Hönö is the most populous island in Öckerö municipality, with more than 5,500 year-round residents on just over five and a half square kilometres. In 2018 it merged with neighbouring Öckerö into a single town, now called Hönö-Öckerö. The island takes its name from its round, smooth rock, from an old word for whetstone. Hönö Church is a short way from here.
Hönö är kommunens folkrikaste ö, och nam: Hönö is the municipality's most populous island, and its name is very old. It comes from the Old West Norse word hein, a whetstone, and refers to the round, smoothly polished rocks. Neighbouring Fotö is much smaller, but yew trees grow there – locally called barlind – and from the higher ground you can see Vinga on a clear day.
Hönöleden är Sveriges mest trafikerade f: Counted in motor vehicles, Hönöleden is Sweden's busiest ferry route, carrying just over 2.3 million vehicles in 2009. The ferries cross between Lilla Varholmen, off Hisingen island, and Hönö – 2,500 metres in twelve minutes. The route counts as part of county road 155, so it's free. The fleet includes M/S Ada, M/S Beda, M/S Göta and M/S Marie.
Hösten 2006 brann den gamla stationskure: In autumn 2006 the old shelter at Östberga station burned down, and a glass shelter now stands in its place. The station itself has been here since 1910. A couple of hundred metres away is the Laurin villa at Hildingavägen 26, designed by Karl Güettler in 1910, and at Djursholm cemetery in Altorp is the funeral chapel where services are held around All Saints' Day.
I Backa Folkets hus, byggt 1924 och om-: Backa Folkets hus, a community hall built in 1924 and rebuilt and enlarged in functionalist style in 1939, was once home to the Rex cinema. It opened in September 1940 and closed in June 1958. But the big screen made a comeback in 1992, when Folkets Hus Backa bio opened in the same premises. The building is protected in the municipality's conservation programme and has five rooms seating between 30 and 200 people.
I Backlura, den nordöstligaste delen av: In Backlura, the north-eastern corner of Hässelby villa town near the Järfälla border, every street is named after a flower or plant. A couple of minutes from here stands One Tonne Life, also known as Villa Bright Living – an experimental low-energy family home designed by Wingårdh Architects and built by A-hus.
I Bergsjön har gatorna fått namn efter r: In Bergsjön the streets are named after space and the universe – hence Teleskopgatan, Telescope Street, and Stjärnbildsgatan, Constellation Street. In the 1980s, Stjärnbildsgatan came up with an unusual answer to its empty flats: the top floors of the four-storey blocks were simply removed, leaving terraced houses around generous courtyards. Nearby is Interkulturella folkhögskolan, the first folk high school in the Nordic countries for Roma students, opened by Crown Princess Victoria.
In Bergsjön, outer space is never far away. Teleskopgatan – Telescope Street – was named in 1967 and is one of a whole cluster of streets named after space and the universe. The district is about 8 kilometres from the city centre and had just over 16,000 residents in 2013. Keep an eye on the street signs as we go – you'll spot more heavenly bodies along the way.
I Bromstens industriområde fanns en gång: Bromsten's industrial area was once home to Fascinate, Sweden's oldest surviving large-scale graffiti piece. It was a living slice of street-art history, but in early December 2021 the wall was knocked down, and the painting went with it. The Bromsten district is part of the Järva city district, and the Bällstaån stream runs through it.
I Danderyd startade 2011 tennisakademin: In 2011 the Good to Great tennis academy opened in Danderyd, founded by three former tennis pros: Magnus Norman, Nicklas Kulti and Mikael Tillström. Among its students were the brothers Mikael and Elias Ymer. All around is Enebyberg, a villa community where most of the houses date from the first half of the 20th century.
I Eriksbergshallen, där Eriksbergs Mekan: Eriksbergshallen, once part of the Eriksberg shipyard – Eriksbergs Mekaniska Verkstad – hosted Melodifestivalen, Sweden's Eurovision selection contest, in 1997. The old shipyard buildings have found new roles: next door, the Quality Hotel 11 was formerly known as Blå Hallen, the Blue Hall. And in a converted service building for the floating docks, the restaurant Westra Piren opened in 1990 and earned a Michelin star as early as 1992.
I Fructushuset på Ulvsundavägen tillverk: Pommac, a classic Swedish soft drink, was once made at Fructushuset, the Fructus Building, on Ulvsundavägen. The factory was built in 1939–40, and the long white building is seen as a fine example of modern, functionalist industrial architecture. By the canal leading to Lake Ulvsundasjön stands Mejerivillan, the Dairy Villa, from 1905 – the only building left of the old Ulvsunda farm.
I Gamla Filmstaden i Råsunda producerade: At Gamla Filmstaden, the Old Film City in Råsunda, a large slice of Swedish cinema was made – almost 400 feature films between 1920 and 1973 – and the studios are linked above all with Ingmar Bergman. The last film shot here was En liten julsaga, 'A Little Christmas Story', in 1999. Näckrosen station takes its name from Näckrosdammen, the Water Lily Pond. The name Råsunda was ruled out, since Råsunda Stadium was near a different station.
I Glömstadalen, en bit härifrån, finns G: Down in Glömstadalen is Glömstahällen, a slab of rock with runes carved straight into the bedrock. Glömsta was once a noble estate and is now a residential area around Lake Gömmaren and the Gömmaren nature reserve. Much of the area used to be summer cottages, which have gradually been joined by newly built family homes.
I Hagaparkens sydöstra del ligger Finnst: In the south-east corner of Hagaparken, Haga Park, are Finnstugorna, the Finnish Cottages. The log house Stora Finnstugan was already standing when Gustav III bought Haga in 1771. Back then the spot was called Finntorpet, and the king is said to have enjoyed himself here even as crown prince. Not far away is Stallgrunden, the remains of Gustav III's Great Stables, where digging began in 1789. The stables were meant to mirror Stora Haga slott, the Great Haga Palace, but were never completed.
I Hammarbyverket utvinns värme och kyla: At Hammarbyverket, heating and cooling are drawn from treated wastewater. The plant opened in 1986, and in 2013 it was ranked the largest heat pump plant of its kind in the world. Its neighbour is Fryshuset, the youth centre that sets out to help young people change the world through the things they love. By the quay, from 2017 until December 2024, the Swedish Internet Foundation ran Goto 10, a free meeting place for internet ideas.
I Hanneberg, en bit härifrån, har parken: In Hanneberg, not far from here, the park has two rabbit houses where children and teenagers can keep and look after rabbits of their own. There's also a youth centre with a café and three villas from the early 20th century. At Storgatan 27 is Löftets kyrka, a former church.
I Historiska museets Guldrum glänser for: In the Gold Room of the Swedish History Museum, the distant past really does glitter. The collections hold 52 kilos of gold and more than 200 kilos of silver, including three unique gold collars from the Migration Period and the Timboholm Hoard, the largest gold treasure ever found in one place in Sweden. Since 2020 the museum has shared its building with the Economic Museum, the Royal Coin Cabinet. Next door stood Fredrikshov, which over the years managed to be a royal palace, a prison and an arsenal.
I Härlandaparken ligger resterna av en g: Härlandaparken park holds the remains of an old church. The parish was merged into Nylöse as early as 1528, and what was left became the Härlanda church ruin, beside the new church. Nearby Munkebäckstorget takes its name from the Munkebäcken stream, and the monks – munkar in Swedish – were probably from Nya Lödöse.
I Hässelby villastad står ett experiment: In Hässelby villastad stands an experimental house with the telling name One Tonne Life – a climate-smart, low-energy home designed by Wingårdh Architects. It was one of five finalists for Stockholm Building of the Year in 2011. A little further off, towards Lake Mälaren, is Lövsta, where people have lived for at least 2,000 years.
I Hässelbygårdsskolans aula fanns biogra: The assembly hall at Hässelbygård School was once home to the Prisma cinema, which opened in November 1960 and screened films to the public until December 1984. The school also had its own doctor's surgery and swimming pool. A little further on is Hässelby familjehotell, the 'family hotel', which was the builder Olle Engkvist's largest collective housing block when it opened in 1955. The professional services stopped in 1976, but residents still keep some of the activities going as volunteers.
I Inverness låg bryggeriet Inverness bru: Between 1929 and 1945, Inverness was home to a soft-drinks factory called Inverness brunn, which among other things produced Sweden's very first club soda. The spring is still there on the shore of the Stocksundet strait, but the water isn't safe to drink and tastes salty. Closer to the stop stood Mörby gård, an 18th-century manor farm that gave the area its name. It was listed as a historic building in 1944, but burned down in 1976.
I Kulturum huserar delar av Partille gym: Kulturum houses part of Partille gymnasium, the sixth-form school formerly known as Porthälla gymnasium. A little further away stood Partillebohallen, opened in 1967 as the sports hall for Porthällaskolan, with a handball court, a bowling alley and seating for about 1,800 spectators. It hosted everything from badminton and basketball to table tennis, and IK Sävehof played here up to and including spring 2016.
I Kvarnparken, vid bäcken som rinner frå: In Kvarnparken, the Mill Park, beside the stream that runs from Lake Ekebysjön down to the Edsviken bay, you'll find Norahällen – a rune inscription carved straight into a smooth slab of bedrock. There's also the old 18th-century mill cottage, which once had a water mill and a water-powered sawmill and is now a weaving workshop. And if you fancy a dip, there's Kvarnparksbadet, a swimming spot kept going by dedicated volunteers.
I Lilleby finns Sillviks Havskoloni, som: In Lilleby you'll find Sillviks Havskoloni, a colony of seaside cottages that came about when the Burgården colony in central Gothenburg was cleared to make way for the Valhallabadet swimming baths. It has just over 120 cottages, a shared clubhouse and a beach café, all still in genuine 1950s style. So a swimming pool in town ended up creating a whole cottage village by the sea.
I Lundas arbets- och industriområde finn: There's a surprising amount of green technology in the Lunda business park. Ferroamp, a Swedish greentech company founded by Björn Jernström in 2010, develops and manufactures its products here in Spånga. Its systems optimise electricity use in buildings with solar panels, small-scale wind power, energy storage and charging for vehicle batteries.
I Mölnlycke utbildas bland annat tullspe: Mölnlycke is one of the places where Sweden trains its customs specialists. Yrkeshögskolan i Mölnlycke, a higher vocational college run by Härryda Municipality, opened in 1998 and has about 200 students, who can also train as payroll specialists or in information security. A short way off, right in central Mölnlycke, is the little lake Massetjärnen.
I Nackareservatet, en bit härifrån, står: In the Nacka nature reserve, not far from here, is Brotorp, a tiny croft just eight metres by five. It's now a protected ancient monument and the clubhouse of the orienteering club Skogsluffarnas OK. Right beside it flows the Ältaån stream, which long-distance skaters and canoeists like to call the Brotorp Canal. Closer by stood the croft of Parken, built in 1839 and pulled down in the mid-1950s.
I Nobelparken, ett stenkast härifrån, sk: In Nobelparken, a stone's throw from here, there were plans for a monumental Nobel Palace in memory of Alfred Nobel. The architect Ferdinand Boberg worked on designs for it from 1906 to 1911, but it was never built. All that's left of those grand plans are the names Nobelparken and Nobelgatan, chosen in 1912. Today the street runs through Diplomatstaden, an exclusive neighbourhood of grand villas and embassies.
I Nockeby, en bit härifrån, ligger Villa: In Nockeby, a little way from here on Grönviksvägen, is Villa Markelius, the functionalist house the architect Sven Markelius lived in from 1930 to 1938. Sankta Birgitta kyrka, St Birgitta's Church, was built where the Nockebybanan tram line used to end and was consecrated in 1962. Winding past the villas is Hässelbystråket, a walking trail of about 19 kilometres that runs all the way from Hässelby strand to Gamla stan, the Old Town.
I Nordre älv, en bit härifrån, finns Orm: A short way from here, in the Nordre älv river, is the Ormo barrier, an adjustable dam that can hold back the flow in the Nordre älv when needed and send the water down the Gothenburg branch of the Göta älv instead. It sits between the Nordre älv railway bridge and the Kornhall ferry – a kind of tap that decides how the river splits.
I Restaurang Barnvagnsfabrikens gamla lo: On Sockenvägen, in the old premises of Restaurang Barnvagnsfabriken – 'the pram factory' – the upmarket restaurant Mistral served local seasonal food and, often, biodynamic wines between 2009 and 2012. It had moved here from Gamla stan, the Old Town, where it had held a Michelin star. Right next door is the Mursmäckan block, named after the women who carried mortar to the bricklayers on building sites. Its urban terraced houses were voted Stockholm's Building of the Year in 2012.
I Roslags Näsby finns en runhäll med en: Roslags Näsby has a rune-carved rock that was discovered by a writer. The Kvarntorp rock was found in 1943 by the author Jan Fridegård, who was living in Täby at the time. The inscription is faint and partly worn away, but it includes the word for “stepsons”, which appears in only a handful of runic inscriptions. Roslags Näsby is about a kilometre south of Täby centrum.
I Troxhammar på södra Färingsö ligger Tr: Troxhammar, in the south of Färingsö, is home to Troxhammar Golf Club – but the area has traces far older than any golf ball. A little further on stands a granite runestone from the Viking Age, 2.2 metres tall. The village of Ekeby is mentioned as early as 1342, when land was swapped with the Vårfruberga convent, and in the 1400s the Crown took over a royal farm in Ekeby that had long been abandoned.
I Vinsta industriområde ligger Vällingby: In the Vinsta industrial area you'll find Vällingby fire station, designed by Mårten J. Larsson and opened in January 1965. The firefighters based here are specially trained in cutting through roofs and in high-rise climbing. This area was once also home to Hässelby kvarn, a windmill that belonged to the Hässelby manor estate. It was first recorded in the mid-1600s and had vanished by the 1820s. And when the metro reached Hässelby gård on a temporary basis in 1956, it was only a month before passenger trains on the Spånga–Lövsta railway stopped running.
I berget en bit härifrån gömmer sig Nybo: Hidden in the rock nearby is Nybohovshissen, a funicular-style lift in a rock tunnel nicknamed Klumpen, 'the Lump'. It's 230 metres long, climbs 37 metres, and the ride between Liljeholmen metro station and Nybohovsberget hill takes 2 minutes and 16 seconds. The Nyboda tunnels also pass through Nybodaberget, and the oldest of them became Sweden's very first railway tunnel when the Western Main Line reached Stockholm in 1860.
I byn Bärby skipades rätt under 1800-tal: In the 1800s, the village of Bärby was where justice was done. It was the court site for the Western and Eastern Hising court district, formed in 1824 to cover both the Västra and Östra Hising hundreds. The district lasted until 1888, when it was merged into the Askim, Hising and Sävedal court district. Today Bärby is a quiet little village west of Säve.
I byn Törnby på södra Färingsö, en bit h: In 1541 the village of Törnby on southern Färingsö, not far from here, had two farms owned by the nobility and one tax-paying farm. In 1544 Karin Axelsdotter Tott sold both noble farms to none other than King Gustav Vasa. The village is first mentioned back in 1342 and has now merged with Stenhamra, while neighbouring Söderberga has become part of the Tureholm built-up area.
I den lilla Karptjärnen, en bit härifrån: In Karptjärnen, a little pond not far from here, live both medicinal leeches and horse leeches. They're thought to have been put there back in the days when Stockholm's pharmacies released and collected leeches to treat all sorts of ailments. In spring the pond is teeming with tadpoles. Since the mid-1990s, the area around Tyresö Strand has filled up with detached, semi-detached and terraced houses – but this same part of Tyresö is also home to the 17th-century Tyresö Palace and church.
I det före detta Långbro sjukhuset fanns: For several years, the former Långbro hospital was home to Långbro Folk High School, a college for adult education. Among other things, it housed the Linnea art school, a three-year post-secondary art course for people with intellectual disabilities, which moved to Södra Stockholms folkhögskola in Skärholmen in 2007. The old heart of the hospital grounds is now Långbroparken park.
I det här industriområdet forskade state: The state once carried out aircraft research in this industrial area. The Aeronautical Research Institute was based in the Ulvsunda industrial area, doing research and testing in aeronautics until, at the turn of 2000/2001, it became part of the Swedish Defence Research Agency. A short way from here, the Huvudsta bridge – known locally as the Pripps bridge – crosses over to Solna.
I det här området finns något så ovanlig: This area has something rather unusual: a prison just for women, Anstalten Sagsjön in Lindome. Not far from it is Lindome station, which has had a real rollercoaster history. It opened in 1888, stopped serving passengers in 1970 and closed altogether in 1989 – only to be given a new lease of life by the commuter trains in 1992.
I det informella området Vasalund ligger: Vasalund, an informal neighbourhood rather than an official district, is home to Solna's only municipal sixth-form school and the Vasalundshallen sports hall. Here too is Södra Långgatan, which became 'Lyckliga gatan', the Happy Street, in Anna-Lena Löfgren's hit song – although the stretch in the song was actually in Hagalund. You'll also find Charlottenburg, Solna's heritage farmstead and home to the local history museum.
I en gammal konsumbyggnad i villaområdet: An old Konsum co-op building in the villa area was home to the restaurant Aloë from 2015 to 2025. The restaurateurs Daniel Höglander and Niclas Jönsson won a Michelin star in 2018, and two years later a second one. There was room for just 35 guests, and the name Aloë is Latin for 'of unknown origin'.
I en trädgård vid gamla Råsta gård, en k: In a garden at the old Råsta farm, a short walk from here, stands Råstastenen, a runestone from the days when Råsta belonged to Spånga parish. There used to be a second runestone here as well, but only a fragment of it survives, kept since 1976 at the Sundbyberg museum. Råsta gård sits at the north-western corner of Lake Råstasjön.
I grannskapet öppnade 1907 landets först: In 1907, Sweden's first home for patients with skin tuberculosis opened in this neighbourhood. Patients were treated with Finsen light, an ultraviolet therapy invented by the Danish doctor Niels Ryberg Finsen, who won the Nobel Prize for it in 1903. Right next door stood Vattenborgen, the Water Castle, one of the city's early water reservoirs. It was demolished in 1934, and Stadshagsplan is on the site today.
I hamnbyn Kornhall en bit härifrån gömme: The harbour village of Kornhall, a little way from here, has a name with a hint of grain about it. According to place-name experts, it comes from 'korn', barley, and 'hall', a place where the barley was loaded or unloaded, and it's recorded as early as 1774. The village is best known, though, for its ferry across the Nordre älv river, a crossing with a long history that makes the journey to Gothenburg a good deal shorter.
I huset Ryttaren 15 vid Valhallavägen in: The Ryttaren 15 building on Valhallavägen was the first to have rubbish chutes, built to the architect Sven Wallander's own patent. From the start, it was also run so that tenants gradually bought shares in the property company – a forerunner of Sweden's housing cooperatives and of HSB, which Wallander helped to found in 1923. Next door, Wittstocksgatan commemorates Johan Banér's victory at Wittstock in 1636.
I hörnet av Kronobergsparken finns en ju: Tucked into a corner of Kronoberg Park is a Jewish cemetery that exists because of a quarrel. Some members of the city's Jewish congregation felt that one of its leaders, Aaron Isaac, was far too domineering, so they simply got a cemetery of their own. It was laid out in 1787, the last burial was in 1857, and 209 people lie here. Just a little further away, the Sörman sign used to glow – one of Stockholm's classic neon signs.
I kvarteren runt Skälby gård har folk hå: People have lived around Skälby gård for a very long time. The manor and its former estate go back to the 16th century, and the current main building, from 1802, is surrounded by no fewer than four burial grounds. Nearby is a pair of Viking Age runestones, U 88 and U 89, known as the runestones by Häradsvägen. Back in the 17th century they already stood inside a ring of smaller round stones.
I norra delen av Rissne, inte långt häri: In the northern part of Rissne, not far from here, the whole blue line goes to bed. Every metro train that runs on the blue line is parked overnight in the Rissne depot, on tracks underground. Between 1975 and 1985, the link track there also carried ordinary passengers, because the section via Huvudsta and Rissne wasn't finished yet.
I närheten har skonaren Ingo sin hemmaha: The schooner Ingo has her home port nearby. Built in 1922, this three-master keeps alive the west coast tradition of sailing historic vessels. A short walk away is Kanalhuset, where SVT, Sveriges Radio and Utbildningsradion – Sweden's public television, radio and educational broadcasters – are based. The building was actually put up for the camera maker Hasselblad, which moved out after only a short time. And Jägaregatan was once home to the Lundby Bio cinema.
I närheten ligger Backa Folkets hus, upp: Nearby is Backa Folkets hus, a community hall built in 1924 and rebuilt and extended in the functionalist style by Sven Wedenmark in 1939. The Rex cinema opened here on 13 September 1940 and showed films until 1958. But that wasn't the end of the big screen: in 1992 Folkets Hus Backa bio opened in the same premises.
I närheten ligger Näsbydal, ett bostadso: Nearby is Näsbydal, an egg-shaped housing estate with 900 flats, ranging from studios with a sleeping alcove to seven-room flats on two floors. The residents' association has its own tennis court, basketball court, boules court and barbecue area. Just a couple of hundred metres away is Kvarntorpshällen, a faint and partly worn-away runic inscription on a slab of rock, discovered by the author Jan Fridegård in 1943.
I närheten låg Fjällbohemmet, ett vårdhe: Nearby was Fjällbohemmet, a care home in Utby from 1939 to 1983. It then became sheltered housing for older people, until it was closed down around 1990. But Utby's history goes back much further: the old Utby parish was absorbed into Partille parish as early as 1571, after its church was destroyed in 1566.
I området Kristinedal en bit härifrån ka: In Kristinedal, a short way from here, you can see the 1960s dream of a home of your own. Around a hundred detached, terraced and linked houses were finished in 1964, single-storey and split-level homes in facing brick. It was in small-house areas like this one that the carport made its debut. Neighbouring Sjövalla is older – villas began going up there as early as the 1920s and 1930s.
I området Kummelby låg förr en gård, och: There was once a farm in Kummelby, and on its site the first Kummelby Church was built in 1956–57. It was so small that it could only hold 50 people, which is why it was sometimes called Kummelby's little church. A new church was consecrated just before Christmas 2000. Beside it stands Kummelbystenen, the Kummelby Stone, a runestone from the late 11th century.
I området finns Mariakyrkan i Hammarkull: Round here you'll find Mariakyrkan, St Mary's Church, in Hammarkullen. It used to be called Tomaskyrkan, and – unusually – it's shared by two churches: the Uniting Church in Sweden, Equmeniakyrkan, and Angered parish. In the other direction is Hjällbo centrum, built in 1969, with a fruit and vegetable market hall, a library and a church grouped around the square.
I området ligger Atlantisområdet, en rad: This area includes the Atlantis estate, a little village of terraced houses designed in the early 1950s by the architects Bertil Karlén, Jon Höjer and Sture Ljungqvist.
