The houses drew attention from abroad, and today they carry the City Museum's highest heritage rating. From 1968 to 1983, one of them was home to Lisbeth and Olof Palme – the future prime minister – and their three sons.
I området ligger Glose, där betade stran: The area includes Glose, where grazed shore meadows meet the shallow waters of Ryskärsfjorden. Birds and plants both thrive here, and the fjord and Glose's meadows are part of the Nordre älv estuary, a vast nature reserve. The six-kilometre Glose å stream also flows out into the fjord.
I området ligger Gunnestorps mosse, en b: The area includes Gunnestorps mosse, a mix of lake, fen and bog in Hisingsparken, Hisingen's big park. Reeds, bulrushes and water lilies grow here alongside cranberries, sundews and cotton grass. North of the bog are the ruins of Mosstorpet, now part of the Fruktträdgården adventure playground.
I området ligger Helgered, med drygt 240: The area includes Helgered, with just over 240 households on either side of Björlandavägen. In its north-eastern corner is Klare mosse, a lovely place for a walk, where the Osbäcken stream has its source. Helgered also borders the Hisingsparken and Svarte mosse nature areas, so forest and bog are never far away from here.
I området ligger Hisingsparken, Göteborg: This is the area of Hisingsparken, Gothenburg's largest park at around 320 hectares, though it only became an official park in 1980. Its oldest part is S.A. Hedlunds park, laid out in the late 1800s. Runners can choose from four trails, from the 2.8-kilometre blue route to the green one, a full 11.1 kilometres. In the northern part of the park is Kättilsröd 4H farm.
I området ligger Mölnlycke, centralorten: This area includes Mölnlycke, the main town of Härryda municipality, about ten kilometres south-east of central Gothenburg. The Mölndalsån river runs through the centre on its way from Lake Landvettersjön to Lake Rådasjön. Since 2023 the village of Öjersjö in neighbouring Partille has also counted as part of the same urban area, so Mölnlycke has now spilled over the municipal border.
I området ligger Vidkärr, som under mång: The area takes in Vidkärr, for many years the end of the line for tram number 1, until it was extended to Östra sjukhuset hospital in 1982. The first two houses in Vidkärr's garden suburb were finished on 24 January 1922. Right next door is Sävenäs station, where commuter trains stood idle from December 2024 to August 2026 while work went on along the Western Main Line.
I området ligger den lilla sjön Skåtte m: The area includes Skåtte mosse, a small lake about 55 metres above sea level, whose water drains away through the Glose å stream. Not far away is Kärna bokskog, a beech forest that has been a nature reserve since 2008, where the rare wood fescue grass and several red-listed lichens thrive. Parts of the forest have been made accessible.
I området runt omkring, ett par kilomete: Around here, a couple of kilometres south of central Mölndal, is the residential area of Rävekärr. It's known for its grey, square terraced houses, aptly nicknamed ‘lådhus’ – box houses. South-east of the houses, two lakes glitter: Horsikan and Rävekärrs Långevatten.
I området, vid Agnesbergs industriområde: It was here, by the Agnesberg industrial estate, that the riverbank gave way on 14 April 1993. The Agnesberg landslide covered an area of roughly 80 by 30 metres along the Göta älv river. A few hours after the first slide, an eight-metre-wide section broke away further back, and several smaller slides followed during the day. It was one of many landslides in western Sweden after the war.
I parken vid Jakobsbergs folkhögskola, e: In the park by Jakobsbergs folkhögskola, the folk high school just up the road, are two runestones that originally stood on the land of Vibble gård – the old name for Jakobsberg. They've been in their present spot since 1926. One of them tells us that Gunnvar and Kättilfrid had the stone raised. Nearby also stood Jakobsberg mill, a windmill from the 1840s that burned down no fewer than three times: in 1980, 1997 and 2005.
I postala sammanhang heter stadsdelen Hi: The district's postal name is Hisings Kärra, and it covers 1,438 hectares. A little further away is Larsered, whose name is a bit of a mystery. It clearly refers to someone called Lars, but nobody knows who he was. The ending '-red' means cleared woodland, so perhaps it was Lars who once cleared the land.
I rondellen vid infarten till Lidingö st: In the roundabout at the entrance to Lidingö stands Till en annan värld, To Another World. Carl Milles only ever made it as a bronze sketch just 66 centimetres high, and it wasn't cast at full size until 2008, long after his death. The municipality commissioned it as a symbol of Lidingö's focus on health and wellbeing, and the 240-centimetre version was created by computer-scanning the original. A little further on is Lidingö town hall from the early 1970s, designed by Sten Samuelson.
I skogarna en bit härifrån ligger Natura: Out in the forests not far from here is the Natura 2000 site Maderna-Haketjärn, with small lakes such as Haketjärnen and Långevatten. Haketjärnen is shared between the municipalities of Härryda and Partille and is just over seven metres deep. Lilla Långevatten covers only 0.03 square kilometres, yet it's almost ten metres deep. Partille is also home to Partille SC, the oldest field hockey club in Sweden that's still going.
I skogen en bit härifrån ligger Södra Lu: In the woods not far from here is Södra Lundtjärnen, a small lake with a quirky detail: the coordinates given for it actually point to a nameless lake just south of the real one. In the other direction is the village of Pinntorp, near Tahult, where the road-racing motorcyclist Kent Andersson has lived.
I skogen en kort promenad härifrån låg s: In the woods a short walk from here stood Kappsta, a summer villa also known as Wisingska villan, where Raoul Wallenberg was born. The house burned down in 1931, but its foundations are still there in Kappsta nature reserve, along with a memorial by Gustav and Ulla Kraitz called Attachéväska R.W., Attaché Case R.W. Nearby are Villa Ekbacken, built in 1912–1913 for Gustaf Dalén, and Skärsätra water tower from 1912.
I skogen mellan Fisksätra och Igelboda,: In the woods between Fisksätra and Igelboda, just south of the Saltsjöbanan railway, you can still find the stone foundations of Vinterbrinken, a lineman's cottage where a railway worker lived with his family. The last to live here were the Nordgrens: first Ludvig, his wife Kristina and their five children, and then their son Ragnar, a station hand, with his own family until the end of the 1920s. The name lives on in Vinterbrinksvägen.
I trakten finns gott om natur. En bit hä: There's plenty of nature round here. Not far away is the Älta mosse – Strålsjön reserve, created in 1995 and owned and run by Nacka municipality. In the other direction is Stensö, named after the peninsula that used to be an island in Lake Ältasjön, with a swimming spot at its tip.
I trakten finns gott om runor. Vid Sundb: This area is rich in runes. At Sundby is U 80, a large, elaborately carved rock slab, with an unfinished one, U 81, right beside it. Flysta had a Viking Age runestone too, but despite several searches it has never been found and is probably lost. And in the Bromsten industrial area was Fascinate, Sweden's oldest surviving large-scale graffiti painting – until the wall was torn down in early December 2021.
I trakten flyter Lärjeån, som börjar nor: The Lärjeån river runs through the area, rising north of Gråbo and flowing into the Göta älv at Lärjeholm. On the eastern bank of the Göta älv, by the E45 road and the Bergslagsbanan railway, is Agnesberg, an old coaching inn that belonged to Angered municipality until 1967. The railway station arrived in 1880, and industry soon followed.
I trakten ligger Långsjö gård, som på 16: In this area is Långsjö gård. In the 17th century it was a croft belonging to Långbro farm, and it later gave its name to the whole district of Långsjö. Nearby runs Långsjövägen, which partly follows the old Göta landsväg – the highway travellers once took heading south from Stockholm.
I trähuset i backen har Djurgårdsskolan: Djurgårdsskolan has been in the wooden house on the slope since 1878, making it one of Stockholm's oldest schools. Not far off stand Karl Johans-ekarna, the Karl Johan oaks, where tradition has it the king rested in the 1820s. Slätten, the meadow here, used to attract a colourful crowd, and according to the national librarian Rydqvist, Gustav III himself came here incognito. The poet Bellman is said to have sat beneath an oak, improvising songs on his mandolin.
I vattenvaktarstugan bodde förr en vakt: The water keeper's cottage was once home to a watchman whose job was to keep Stockholm's main water pipeline running smoothly between Norsborg waterworks and Nybohov reservoir. The first pipeline was laid in 1902–1904, and it's still one of the city's most important drinking-water mains. Not far away, in Gömmaren nature reserve, there are also the remains of a farm from the middle Iron Age.
I Årsta har gatorna fått namn efter sven: In Årsta the streets are named after Swedish lakes, like Skagern and Hjälmaren, so a stroll here is almost a geography lesson. Vättersparken used to have a supervised playground, Vättersdälden, which closed in 1992 – but the paddling pool, swings and sandpits are still there. A little further on stands Skagershuset, a block of flats with a wooden façade that was named Stockholm's Building of the Year in 2014.
Idrottsplatsen vid Kyrkvikens inre del h: The sports ground at the head of Kyrkviken bay has everything from athletics to ice hockey. But walk a little further and you'll come to Lidingö's oldest farm, Bo gård, whose history goes all the way back to the late Iron Age. Right next to it are the Trisshusen from 1909 – an early type of terraced housing designed by Jacob Gate.
Igelbäcken rinner förbi alldeles i närhe: The Igelbäcken stream winds past close by on its 10.5-kilometre journey from Lake Säbysjön to Edsviken bay, and its valley is one of Stockholm's ‘green wedges’ of open countryside reaching into the city. A short way off is Akalla village, a name known since the Middle Ages. The oldest house, Storgården, dates from the 17th century, and today the village has a 4H farm, a café and bike hire – in one of the best-preserved village settings in the Stockholm area.
Ikeas andra svenska varuhus, efter det i: IKEA's second store in Sweden, after the original in Älmhult, opened here on 18 June 1965. Its round original section was inspired by the Guggenheim Museum in New York, and after later rebuilding and extensions it became the second-largest IKEA in the world by floor space. One of its very first neighbours was the Esso Motorhotell from 1968 – today the Scandic Kungens Kurva hotel.
Ingemarsgatan har troligen fått sitt nam: Ingemarsgatan is probably named after Ingemar Frodbom, a wine merchant who ran an inn at the Ingemarshof country house in the 1700s. When he died, he left a plot of land to his loyal head waiter, Clas Browall, who in 1731 opened his own inn, Browallshof – today the Clas på Hörnet hotel and restaurant. Incidentally, the surrounding area was nicknamed Siberia, because moving this far out of town felt like being sent into exile.
Ingen säger Köpstadsö. I dagligt tal het: Nobody actually says Köpstadsö. Everyone calls the island Kössö, and it's famous for its wheelbarrows. Just over a square kilometre in size, with 129 year-round residents in 2020, it's part of Gothenburg's southern archipelago. Look out for the wheelbarrows when you step ashore – they're the island's trademark.
Inloppet till Göteborg har länge bevakat: For centuries, this area has guarded the approach to Gothenburg. On Lilla Billingen, a headland a short way off, you can still see an angular fortification from 1741–1742, and in 1789 a square redoubt was added, with batteries facing the river. Gothenburg's saluting station was here too. The neighbouring hill, Stora Billingen, has military chambers blasted into the rock.
Innan Frösunda började bebyggas på 1990-: Before Frösunda started to be built up in the 1990s, the area was given over to the military, home to the Signal Regiment and the Svea Engineer Regiment. In its final years it was known as the Frösunda detachment and housed, among others, the units that served as the royal guard. A little further off is Annelunds gård, where Per Henrik Ling, the father of Swedish gymnastics, lived from 1822 to 1839.
Innan tunnelbanan kom stannade spårvagns: Before the metro came, tram line 19 stopped here, at Enskedefältet. On 9 September 1951 the tram stop gave way to the metro station, and today the trains cross Sockenvägen on a viaduct. Next door is Enskedefältets skola, a school designed by Paul Hedqvist and built in 1933. A little further off was the Enskede ski jump, where in 2016 the district council decided to build a viewpoint.
Inne i Fredhällsberget, alldeles intill,: Right beside us, the Essingeleden motorway roars through the Fredhäll tunnel deep inside Fredhällsberget hill, then carries straight on over the 270-metre Fredhäll bridge across the Mariebergssundet strait. Up above ground it's much calmer. Leafy Rudbecksparken is full of oak trees, and Fredhäll primary school, designed by Paul Hedqvist and opened in 1938, has been given a green listing for its heritage value by the City Museum.
Inne i berget en bit härifrån döljer sig: Hidden away inside the rock not far from here is Aeroseum, an aviation experience centre in an underground cavern. It was once the rock hangar of the Göta Wing, one of only five ever built for the Swedish Air Force. Since 2000, visitors have been able to head down into the bunker and get up close to aviation history.
Inne i berget en bit härifrån gömmer sig: Hidden inside the rock nearby is Vargen, the Wolf, a secret nuclear-proof command centre from the 1970s with room for 200 people. It was built to shelter the leaders of Stockholm and Huddinge in the event of war, but it was eventually decommissioned and turned into a data centre. North of Stockholm it has an almost identical twin called Elefanten, the Elephant. Nearby Lake Lissmasjön has shrunk to a third of its original size after several attempts to drain it.
Insekterna har det lyxigt i Kikås. Vid K: In Kikås, the insects live in luxury. By the lake Kikås Långvatten is Sweden's largest free-standing insect hotel, built to boost biodiversity, especially for wild bees, butterflies and birds. Kikås is the name of the high ridge on the southern shore of Lake Stensjön, and Fågelberg church is not far from here.
Inte långt härifrån ligger Anstalten Sag: Not far from here is Anstalten Sagsjön, a women's prison in Lindome. It takes its name from Sagsjön, a little further on – a tiny, very shallow lake, just 1.5 metres deep, that sits 20 metres above sea level and drains into the Kungsbackaån river basin.
Inte långt härifrån reser sig tre konstg: Not far from here rise three man-made hills, built up from demolition rubble and bulky rubbish. The first, Högdalstoppen, was finished in 1964, and the rock on that spot had previously been the highest point in Högdalen and Fagersjö. Today the summits are an outdoor recreation area with a skatepark and a disc golf course. Högdalstoppen 3 is still growing, topped up with soil dug out during road building.
Interkulturella folkhögskolan: Interkulturella folkhögskolan, the intercultural folk high school
Invalidkyrkogården: Invalidkyrkogården, the old military veterans' cemetery
Ishallen en bit härifrån blev känd i hel: The ice rink a short way from here became famous across Sweden thanks to the TV series HCZ. It has changed its name several times: first Dalénhallen, after the inventor Gustaf Dalén and the nearby AGA factory, then Danske Bank Hallen, and now Childhood Hallen. Lidingö Vikings Hockey Club play here, and figure skaters train here too.
Islandstorget fick sitt namn 1936, men d: Islandstorget, Iceland Square, got its name in 1936 – but not because of exiled Icelanders or fishmongers. The connection is vaguer than that: when the streets and squares of Norra Ängby were being named, the planners drew inspiration from the ancient remains in the area. From the autumn of 1944, trams on the Ängby line, route 11, turned round here. A short walk away is Björklunds hage, the burial ground of Viking Age Ängby.
Jakobs stege är en trappa med 187 granit: Jakobs stege, or Jacob's Ladder, is a flight of 187 granite steps leading down towards Lake Mälaren, named after the biblical patriarch Jacob's dream of a ladder reaching from earth to heaven. Nearby is Bellmanskällan, a spring that local tradition says is the one the poet Carl Michael Bellman sings about in Fredman's Epistle No. 82, “Vila vid denna källa” – Rest by this spring. The water still trickles out, if slowly, and it's safe to drink.
Jakobsbergs Centrum, alldeles intill, är: Right here is Jakobsbergs Centrum, Järfälla's big shopping centre, with around sixty shops as well as homes and offices under the same roof. A couple of minutes away stands Gula villan, the Yellow Villa, the old station building from 1876, and where Vasavägen meets Ynglingavägen is Maria kyrka, St Mary's Church.
Jakobsbergs folkhögskola: Jakobsbergs folkhögskola, the folk high school
Jakobsbergs gård var från början ett tor: Jakobsbergs gård started life in the early 17th century as a croft belonging to the Sätra estate. The manor-like house was added in the 1750s, when the farm had become a summer retreat for well-off Stockholmers, and today the City Museum gives it a blue heritage rating. Down by the water is Mälarhöjdsbadet, a public beach that, despite its name, isn't in Mälarhöjden at all but in Bredäng.
Jakobsbergs kvarn från 1840-talet hade o: Jakobsberg's windmill from the 1840s had no luck with fire: it burned in 1980, 1997 and 2005, and after that third blaze it was never rebuilt. Next to it, in the buildings of the old manor, is Jakobsbergs folkhögskola, a folk high school for adult education. Two runestones in the park were moved here from the lands of Vibble farm, and one of them tells us that Gunnvar and Kättilfrid had the stone raised.
Jakobsbergs sporthall stod klar 1967 och: Jakobsberg sports hall was completed in 1967 and is home to teams including Järfälla Basket. The club was founded in 1973, and its men's team was already playing in the top division, Elitserien, by 1981, with the women's team following a year later. Since a refurbishment in 2009, the main hall holds about 1,100 people. A stone's throw away is Järfällabadet, the swimming centre that opened in 2018.
Jarlabergs vattentorn är 47,5 meter högt: Jarlaberg water tower stands 47.5 metres tall and has been a landmark in south-east Stockholm ever since it was finished in 1987. A little further on, in Augustendal, Johan Victor Svenson bought two old summer houses in 1899, planning to build a car factory. But car technology was moving too fast, so he made paraffin engines instead, sold under the name Avance – and they soon became a hit.
Johannebergs vattentorn från 1924 byggde: The Johanneberg water tower from 1924 was turned into housing in 1995, with just two flats on each floor. The top floor is 134 metres above sea level, and for many years these were the highest homes in Gothenburg – until Karlatornet took the record in 2023. All around is Chalmers, a university of technology founded back in 1829.
Jonsered var ett säteri som från 1830-ta: Jonsered was a noble estate that grew into a mill town under the Gibson family from the 1830s onwards. The brick buildings from its industrial heyday still shape the place, and the Swedish National Heritage Board has designated Jonsered a heritage site of national interest. Nearby is Göta Bio, where the film society Götas Vänner has been running the screenings since 1996.
Jubileumsparken anlades till Göteborgs 4: Jubileumsparken, the Jubilee Park, was created for Gothenburg's 400th anniversary. There's a public sauna and a place to swim in the river, and the park is a testing ground for ideas for the new district due to be built around Frihamnen.
Jubileumsparken i Frihamnen växte fram i: Jubileumsparken, the Jubilee Park in Frihamnen, grew up in the run-up to Gothenburg's 400th anniversary as an experiment in city planning. It's home to Hamnbadet, also known as Pöl Harbour, with saltwater pools and a diving tower, and to Allmänna bastun, the public sauna. The sauna is built from recycled materials, its changing rooms are made of 12,000 glass bottles, and it stands four metres above the water. Plans for 5,000 homes on nearby Bananpiren, the Banana Pier, were dropped in 2020 because the ground was too poor to build on.
Jubileumsparken med bastu och bad: Jubileumsparken park, with sauna and swimming
Jungfruplatsen, några hundra meter bort,: Jungfruplatsen, a few hundred metres away, was named in 1958 after the constellation Virgo – Jungfrun in Swedish – and opened on 6 December 1959. Built by Wallenstam, it was Mölndal's first proper shopping centre. It's also home to Mölndal's first piece of public outdoor art, Bossanova by Bertil Lundgren, unveiled in 1964. All around, the streets of Bifrost have names linked to farming.
Jungfrusund är både bostadsområde och ha: Jungfrusund is both a residential area and a harbour on Vårbyfjärden bay, on the east side of the island of Ekerön. Just offshore are the Jungfruholmarna, two islets that belong to the Göta Sailing Society. The club began leasing them in 1915, bought them in 1936 and built its own clubhouse there in 1955. They lie about six nautical miles from Stockholm out into Lake Mälaren.

Jungfrusund is both a residential area and a harbour on Vårbyfjärden, on the east side of Ekerön. Out in the water are the Jungfruholmarna, two islands belonging to the Göta sailing club. The club leased them in 1915, bought them in 1936 and built a clubhouse in 1955. The Ekerö ferry also crosses the bay here.
Juringe gård var en gång utgård till det: Juringe gård was once an outlying farm belonging to the large Vårby estate. The old main house was pulled down in 2001 and replaced by a lookalike, which is now a preschool. Still standing from the farm's working days are the storehouse, a laundry and dairy shed, and the farmhands' house, Väderluven. The croft of Nytorp was also here, beside the new road of 1673 that replaced the old Götha vägen route.
Järfälla gymnasium har funnits här nära: Järfälla gymnasium, an upper secondary school, has stood here near Jakobsberg centre under various names since 1962, and in 2020 it had just over 1,000 students. Among the schools once based here was SAM-gymnasiet, which offered social sciences with specialisms ranging all the way to football. Close by is the Imam Ali Mosque, considered the largest Shia Muslim congregation in the Nordic countries.
Järfälla är en kommun där det mesta är b: Most of Järfälla is built up, and that has led to some creative ways of saving what nature is left. The Norra Igelbäcken nature reserve, for instance, includes an old airfield – and a metro line is being built underneath it. Otherwise, the municipality is best known for shopping, thanks to the Barkarby retail park.
Järfälla är rikt på runor. I Skylsta fin: Järfälla is rich in runes. At Skylsta there's a Viking Age inscription carved straight into the rock, while a fragment of a runestone that, according to Richard Dybeck, stood on the same hill has vanished without a trace. A little further on, on the Stockholm side, is Backlura, where every street is named after a flower or plant.
Järfällabadet, en bit härifrån, invigdes: Järfällabadet, a short way from here, opened on 14 April 2018. It has a 50-by-25-metre pool, two water slides and pools with floors that can be raised and lowered. It replaced the Jakobsberg swimming baths, which opened on a Monday in August 1971 and had a 48-metre water slide. The old building was originally going to be demolished but will instead be turned into a space for leisure activities.
Järfällas sydligaste kommundel heter Bar: Järfälla's southernmost district, Barkarby-Skälby, had about 12,000 residents in 2011. It's home to Kyrkbyn, the old church village, with the Gästgivargården coaching inn – in recent years known as Wärdshuset Lasse-Maja – and the old courthouse. Closer to the sports ground is the manor of Skälby gård, whose current main building dates from 1802.
Järla gård är en riktigt anrik herrgård:: Järla gård is a manor with deep roots: the first farm called Järla is believed to have been built around the year 900. It appears in Stockholm's court records in 1453, and a map from 1690 shows it on the northern shore of Lake Järlasjön. Industry later grew up all around it, and branch lines once ran from Saltsjö-Järla station to a yeast factory and to De Laval's steam turbine works.
Järnbrottsmotet i närheten är en ovanlig: The nearby Järnbrottsmotet is an unusual type of motorway junction, known as a double trumpet interchange. It was built in the 1990s on the site of the Europa roundabout, a gigantic roundabout with the Söderleden road cutting straight through it at traffic lights. In the wall of Västra Frölunda cemetery next door there are still iron rings where churchgoers once tethered their horses.
Järntorget har fått sitt namn av järnet: Järntorget, Iron Square, is named after the iron that was once weighed and shipped from here. The fountain in the middle dates from 1927 and depicts the world's five continents. This is where the old working-class districts begin. To the south is Haga, with its cafés and landshövdingehus – Gothenburg's typical houses with a stone ground floor and wooden upper storeys – and to the west run the Långgatorna streets, packed with vintage shops and bars.
Järva krog var en vägkrog cirka 3,5 kilo: Järva krog was a roadside inn on the Uppsala road, about 3.5 kilometres north of Norrtull, Stockholm's northern gateway. Its name lives on in the motorway junction. A short walk away is something far older: the Mellanjärva burial ground. With around 175 visible graves, it's one of the largest farm burial grounds in the Stockholm area.
Järvastaden är ett stadsbyggnadsprojekt: Järvastaden is a building project that's taking its time. The first residents moved in in September 2007, and once it's finished it's planned to be home to more than 15,000 people. The ninth and last phase won't happen until after 2030, though, because a high-voltage power line has to be moved first. To the east is the neighbouring residential area of Agnesberg.
Kallhäll ligger intill Mälaren i Järfäll: Kallhäll lies on Lake Mälaren in northern Järfälla, and at its centre is the Folkets hus community centre, with a cinema and a library. A little further away is Stockholm Mejeri, Arla Foods' big dairy, which began production in 1984. Beneath the library is the Bolinder Museum, displaying products from Bolinders Mekaniska Verkstad, the Bolinder engineering works.
Kanske skrevs svensk kungahistoria i när: Swedish royal history may well have been made just near here. Korseberget, a little village on the northern bank of the Nordre älv river close to its mouth, could be the same place as Horsaberg – where King Magnus Ladulås held peace talks with his brother Valdemar on 26 June 1274. A small community with a possibly big place in the history books.
Kanton var en liten hantverksby som Lovi: Kanton was a little craft village that Queen Lovisa Ulrika and King Adolf Fredrik had built beside Kina slott, the Chinese Pavilion. Craftspeople here made ironwork and lace and wove silk ribbons. The queen even tried her hand at silk farming, but the mulberry trees didn't take to the cold and the venture lasted only about ten years. Today the houses are private homes, and they're regarded as a forerunner of the Swedish garden city.
Kapplandsgatan intill känns igen på sina: Kapplandsgatan next door is easy to spot by its red three-storey buildings, and at the southern end of the street is Högsbo Hospital. The nearest square is Axel Dahlströms torg, which stands out with a 16-storey tower block from 1956 and a marble inlay by Endre Nemes on the community centre. Along Marklandsgatan you'll find a pizzeria, a bakery and a grill.
Karl XII står i brons och pekar mot Ryss: Karl XII stands in bronze, pointing towards Russia – a reminder of his wars. Johan Peter Molin's statue was unveiled on 30 November 1868, the 150th anniversary of the king's death. It was cast on Kungsholmen and weighs two and a half tonnes. The mortars around the plinth are war trophies from Riga. The Green Party has put forward a proposal to move the statue.
Keillers park och utsikten från Ramberge: Keillers park and the view from Ramberget hill
Kika in på Malmstens möbelskola: Peek into Malmstens, the furniture-making school
Kikås är den höga åsen vid Stensjöns söd: Kikås is the high ridge on the southern shore of Lake Stensjön, and it's home to Sweden's biggest free-standing insect hotel, where wild bees and butterflies check in. Not far from here is Södra Långevattnet, a long, narrow lake with clear water, surrounded by rocky hills and wooded ridges. It's a popular place for a swim – but if you want to fish, you'll need a licence.
Kista Nod, alldeles intill, kostade 700: Kista Nod, right next door, cost 700 million kronor and was completed in 2014. Stockholm University carries out research there in computer and systems sciences. The area is also home to the Electrum laboratory, with a complete production line for semiconductor chips. And, rather more discreetly, Kista houses Försvarsunderrättelsedomstolen, the Defence Intelligence Court, which decides on permits for signals intelligence.
Kista tunnelbanestation är den enda på b: Kista is the only station on the blue line that's above ground. It sits on a viaduct 1,120 metres long – the longest anywhere on the metro. When the station was being named, the naming committee first wanted to add 'Gård', meaning farm, so that nobody would think of a 'likkista', a coffin. Rising above the shopping centre is Kista torn, the Kista Tower, 120 metres tall.
Kista är fullt av forskning. Rise SICS,: Kista is packed with research. Rise SICS, formerly the Swedish Institute of Computer Science, does non-profit computer science research to help Swedish companies compete. The Electrum Laboratory, part of the KTH Royal Institute of Technology, has a complete production line for semiconductor circuits and carries out research in micro- and nanotechnology.
Kistas tunnelbanestation är den enda på: Kista is the only station on the blue metro line that's above ground. The trains glide in along a 1,120-metre viaduct – the longest bridge on the whole metro network. Near the centre you'll also find the eight-sided Kista Church, and on Kista torg is Kista folkhögskola, Sweden's first folk high school – a kind of adult education college – with a Muslim profile.
Klareberg i Kärra är en plats där bussar: Klareberg in Kärra is where the buses get to catch their breath. Drivers like to take their breaks here, and the big bus stop serves routes to Kungälv, Angered and Gothenburg. But the area is also popular with riders and dog owners, who come here to ride and train their dogs.
Klingska huset, i hörnet av Älvsjövägen: Klingska huset, on the corner of Älvsjövägen and Johan Skyttes väg, is the oldest surviving block of rented flats in Solberga. Built between 1923 and 1925 in a town-style design, it was Älvsjö's first piece of town-centre development. A couple of hundred metres away is Älvkvarnstenen, an ancient cup-marked stone that has been moved twice and has stood next to Lerkrogen since 1994.
Klippan är en av Göteborgs äldsta miljöe: Klippan is one of Gothenburg's oldest neighbourhoods, with old seamen's cottages and the remains of the earlier Älvsborg fortress. Right beside it towers the Älvsborg Bridge, and beneath the bridge is the Röda Sten art centre.
Klippan är fullt av historia. Här låg Ga: Klippan is steeped in history. This was the site of Gamla Älvsborg, a mighty fortress from the 1300s to the 1600s that's now a ruin. The old sugar refinery, Sockerbruket, was home to 24 kvadrat, Sweden's smallest dance stage. And Klippans värdshus, the inn from 1762, was made famous by the ship's chaplain Jacob Wallenberg in his book Min son på galejan, 'My Son on the Galley'. The trams sleep in the Majorna tram depot next door.
Kliv ner i Rinkeby tunnelbanestation och: Step down into Rinkeby metro station and you'll find yourself in a Viking treasure chamber. The artist Nisse Zetterberg took small Viking Age objects dug up in the area and blew them up into huge mosaics on brick-red walls, with gold inlays and runes. The station opened in 1975, when the blue line was launched.
Kliv rakt in i 1950-talet! Ett stenkast: Step straight back into the 1950s! A stone's throw away is Kortedala museum, a completely ordinary two-room flat with a kitchen, kept just as it was when the working-class families first moved in. It's so authentic that it's been used as a set for period films. Citytorget, the square right next to it, was built at the same time, between 1955 and 1957, with tower blocks, rows of shops and a street kiosk.
Klättra upp till stångmärket Valen: Climb up to the Valen pole beacon
Knarrholmen var en present till arbetare: Knarrholmen was a gift to the workers. In 1940 the shipowner Axel Ax:son Johnson donated the island to the shipyard workers at Götaverken, and summer cottages went up here after 1945. In 2014 the trade unions sold the island, with its 33 cottages, restaurant and village shop. Neighbouring Sillfarsholmen was bought by the Aeolus sailing club in 1935 for a single krona.
Kolla in Flatenbanan för radiostyrda bil: Check out Flatenbanan, the track for radio-controlled cars
Kolla utställningen i biblioteket: Check out the exhibition at the library
Kollektivhuset Sockenstugan är ett gemen: Sockenstugan is a cohousing block for people in the second half of life – one of many created in Stockholm after a political decision in 1980. One report called it a real success story. Right next door is Gränsberget park, an old moraine hill shared between the districts of Enskededalen and Kärrtorp.
Kommunalvägen löper genom Huddinges hjär: Kommunalvägen runs right through the heart of Huddinge, with the station, the shopping centre, the church and the municipal offices all along its 1.3 kilometres. There's been news here recently too: Sjödalsgymnasiet, an upper secondary school that opened in 1994, closed in 2026. In its final year it had 185 students, compared with 608 just three years before.
Kommundelen Tibble rymmer både Täby cent: The Tibble district is home to both Täby centrum, the shopping centre, and the church that's been nicknamed “the Cathedral of Roslagen”. The shopping centre has 215 shops, and since 2022 its official name has been Westfield Täby Centrum. Its library keeps two fragments of Viking Age runestones that were found in Lissby in 1930 – though it later turned out that several of the pieces actually belonged to a different stone.
Konsthallen Accelerator har sina utställ: The Accelerator art gallery has its exhibition halls in a former underground lab for accelerator physics, and it opened in 2019 with a work by Tino Sehgal. Its neighbour is Villa Frescati, designed by Louis Jean Desprez in 1791–1792 as a summer retreat for Gustaf Mauritz Armfelt, facing Gustav III's pavilion across the water. And at the Swedish Museum of Natural History is Cosmonova, Sweden's only domed IMAX cinema.
Konstnären Olle Olsson Hagalund bodde he: The artist Olle Olsson Hagalund spent his whole life in the same wooden house, built in 1897 by the master carpenter Carl Jakob Brolin. Today it's a museum, both for his art and for the old shanty town of Hagalund, which was demolished in the 1960s to make way for the Blåkulla tower blocks. Inside you'll find a model of old Hagalund. Nearby stands Hagalund water tower from 1912.
Kontorshusen vid Solna strand står på ga: The office blocks at Solna strand stand on old industrial land – the area used to be called Vretens industriområde. Granite was once quarried nearby: from 1875 the City of Stockholm leased Huvudsta quarry on Lake Ulvsundasjön to make cobblestones, but by the early 1880s the rock was considered worked out. And the metro station here sits in a rock cavern a full 28 metres underground.
Kontorsområdet hette förr Virebergs indu: This office district used to be called Virebergs industriområde, the Vireberg industrial estate. It was planned in the 1950s by Valvet, a Wallenberg-owned property company that had bought the land from Huvudsta gård in 1947. Being close to the railway, with a siding of its own, was a big selling point, but building didn't really get going until the 1960s. Next door is Löfströms gymnasium, an upper secondary school that takes in just over 55 elite athletes a year in football, ice hockey and floorball.
Kornhall är en liten hamnby vid Nordre ä: Kornhall is a little harbour village on the Nordre älv river, with a small shipyard and a marina. From here, the Kornhall ferry – a cable ferry – crosses the river to Brunstorpsnäs on Hisingen. The crossing dates back to 1850, and it got its first motor ferry in 1951, when traffic had grown because the route made the journey to Gothenburg so much shorter.
Korsvägen är porten till Göteborgs evene: Korsvägen is the gateway to Gothenburg's events district. Here you'll find the Liseberg amusement park, opened in 1923, the Universeum science centre and the Museum of World Culture – and Svenska Mässan, the Swedish Exhibition and Congress Centre, is right next door.
Kortedala byggdes på 1950-talet som en m: Kortedala was built in the 1950s as a modern suburb with everything close at hand – homes, a square, schools and green spaces. A lot of the architecture from that era is still here today.
Kortedala byggdes som Göteborgs första f: Kortedala was built in the 1950s as Gothenburg's first suburb, on the city's north-eastern outskirts, where until then there had been little more than crofters' cottages. A few farms hung on right into the 1960s. Not far from here, at the entrance to Bergsjön, the long blocks of flats on Siriusgatan stand in a row along a hilltop, a landmark for the whole area.
Kortedala torg, en bit härifrån, hette f: Kortedala torg, just along from here, was originally called Kortedalstorget. But Göteborgs Spårvägar, the Gothenburg tramways company, pointed out that everyone actually said 'Kortedalatorget', and that the official name was a mouthful. The city council voted 24 to 17, and in 1959 the square got the name it has today. That same year the Forum cinema opened on the square – only to close at the end of 1965.
Kovikshamn ligger vid havet, strax norr: Kovikshamn lies by the sea just north of where the Nordre älv river flows out, and it has not one but two marinas. The northern one, Kovikshamns Norra Småbåtshamn, is privately owned and the bigger of the two. Since 2015 Kovikshamn has officially counted as an urban area, and at the same time the neighbouring villages of Sundhammar and Tofta, along with Brunnefjäll, were merged into it.
Kring Bromma kyrka ligger en liten klung: Around Bromma Church is a small cluster of old rectory buildings with a long history. The red Sockenstugan, the 17th-century parish cottage, was the vicar's home right up until 1850, when the new rectory was finished. On the same plot is a tithe barn, where the priest once collected the Bromma farmers' taxes – paid in produce rather than cash. And up on Kråsberget hill, north of Sockenstugan, stands the church's bell tower.
Kring köpcentrumet i norra Botkyrka finn: The area around this shopping centre in northern Botkyrka has an unusually close-knit cluster of churches. Botkyrka folkhögskola, a folk high school – a kind of adult education college – founded in 1997, is owned by five Christian congregations, three of them Syriac Orthodox, yet it's open to everyone, whatever their faith. Ljusets kyrka, the Church of Light, on Tomtbergavägen, sits right next to the Syriac Orthodox Church of St Peter and St Paul, while Hallundakyrkan is practically wall to wall with the shopping centre.
Krokslätts fabriker är gamla industribyg: Krokslätts fabriker are old industrial buildings where textiles were once made. Today they're home to businesses, restaurants and flats – a good example of old factories getting a new lease of life.
Krokängsparken, en promenadpark på cirka: Krokängsparken, a park for walking of about 7.5 hectares, was laid out as far back as 1902 between Bratteråsberget hill and Pölsebo. A little further on, towards the river, towers the Eriksberg crane, a gantry crane from 1969 that's just over 70 metres tall and almost 110 metres wide. It's a listed structure and a symbol of the shipyard era, when everything about shipbuilding was on a giant scale.
Krontorpet Hökmossen nämns första gången: Hökmossen, a croft owned by the Crown, is first mentioned in 1748 in a document in the Military Archives. Back then it was called Hökmåsen, after a bog north of the farm that has since disappeared. A little way off, in an old co-op building in the villa suburb of Långbro, was the restaurant Aloë, which served luxurious tasting menus from 2015 to 2025 and earned two Michelin stars.
Krossgatan ligger i Vinsta industriområd: Krossgatan runs through the Vinsta industrial area, where Vällingby fire station opened in December 1964. Its firefighters have special training in roof ventilation and climbing at height. Johannelund metro station was built as an 'industrial station' with two side platforms – the only one like it on the Stockholm metro – and until October 1997 it opened only at rush hour. The Vinsta district takes its name from the old village of Vinsta.
Krusboda byggdes under åren 1970–1975 oc: Krusboda was built between 1970 and 1975 and has its own school. Not far away, on Lake Albysjön, is Nyfors, a well-preserved 1940s holiday-cottage area where more and more people now live all year round. Between the branches of the Wättinge stream lies Bullerholmen – ‘Noisy Islet’ – which, despite its name, is now completely uninhabited. North of the cottages begins the Alby nature reserve.
Kulan på kullen är Bällsta radartorn, i: The ball on the hill is the Bällsta radar tower, nicknamed the Golf Ball, standing between Bromma Airport and Solvalla. The Solvalla trotting track opened in 1927, holds 35,000 spectators and hosts the Elitloppet race every year. In Bällsta itself, around 200 cottages were built by their owners with their own hands, using materials and instructions from the city's small-house office.
The ball-bearing giant SKF has deep roots here. Not far away in Gamlestaden was Mariedal's landeri, a small country estate, where SKF had its office from 1910 to 1914. Nearby was also Torpavallen, the old home ground of Qviding FIF, with two gravel pitches and a grass pitch with a stand. Where footballs once rolled, the Torpavallen shopping centre now stands.
Kultur i oväntade lokaler finns en bit h: Culture in unexpected places awaits a short way from here in Fullersta. Fullersta bio is now an art gallery and theatre, housed in former Konsum co-op shops and an old cinema. And since 2009, the manor house Fullersta gård – once the centre of an estate whose lands covered the whole area – has been home to a contemporary art gallery.
Kulturhuset Bergsjön: Kulturhuset Bergsjön, the Bergsjön culture house
Kungens kurva har fått sitt namn från en: Kungens kurva, 'the King's Curve', is named after a real accident. On 28 September 1946, King Gustaf V's chauffeur came off Södertäljevägen near here and ended up stuck in a water-filled ditch – and the name stuck too. IKEA opened its second store here in 1965, and the round building was inspired by the Guggenheim Museum in New York.
Kungliga tennishallen: Kungliga tennishallen, the Royal Tennis Hall
Kungsgatan 65 har levt många liv. Biogra: Kungsgatan 65 has worn many hats. The Palladium cinema opened here in 1918, with the Bal Palais dance restaurant in the basement. Later it became the Heaven nightclub, and from 2003 to 2025 it was Casino Cosmopol. Next door is Oscarsteatern from 1906, a listed theatre named after King Oscar II. The same building is home to Fasching, Scandinavia's largest jazz club since 1977.
Kungsholms folkskola var Sveriges störst: Kungsholms folkskola was Sweden's biggest primary school and one of the largest in the world, with room for 4,000 pupils. Only the northern part survives today, home among other things to Stockholm's arts school. This neighbourhood is full of firsts: Kungsholmen's crèche was the first of its kind in Sweden, and Kvinnohuset, a fourteen-storey cooperative block of flats for women, opened here in 1947.
Kungsladugård är tidigt bostadsbyggande: Kungsladugård is an early chapter in Gothenburg's housing history. The Svärdsliljan block from 1927 was one of HSB's first blocks of landshövdingehus – Gothenburg's typical houses with a stone ground floor and wooden upper floors. The district also has a bronze statue, Ung man, Young Man, made by Astrid Noack in 1948 and set up on the corner of Ståthållaregatan and Fågelfängaregatan in 1968. Kungsladugård Church is just a short walk away.
Kungsladugårdsgatan är bred av en anledn: There's a reason Kungsladugårdsgatan is so wide. In Albert Lilienberg's town plan of 1916, it was drawn at double width to leave room for a future railway between the harbour and the city. The name comes from Älvsborgs Kungsladugård, the royal farm that supplied Älvsborg Castle with horses and grain. Along the street stands the Broström Foundation's building from 1924, listed since 2017.
Kungssten lies close to the mouth of the Göta älv river. From here you can see Älvsborgsbron, the Älvsborg Bridge, which was the longest suspension bridge in Sweden when it opened in 1966. Out in the estuary is the 17th-century New Älvsborg Fortress, built to defend the city against the Danes. Down by the water is Klippan, with old seamen's cottages and the remains of the older Älvsborg Fortress.
Kungsträdgården var från början kungens: Kungsträdgården, the King's Garden, began life as the royal kitchen garden. Today it's one of the city's best-loved parks, and in spring its cherry trees burst into pink and white blossom.
Kvarnholmen var en gång en ö full av mjö: Kvarnholmen, ‘Mill Island’, was once all about flour and bread. The Tre Kronor mill started up in 1897, and there was also a macaroni factory, an oat mill and a crispbread bakery. Today people live in the old silos – when Silo III was turned into flats, for a while nothing but its outer walls was left standing. The old bakery, Bageriet, is now Kvarnholmen's centre, and the oat mill, Havrekvarnen, has been listed since 2016.
Kvarnholmen var från början en ö, men su: Kvarnholmen used to be an island, until the channel separating it was filled in during the 1970s to give the factories a better transport link. This was home to the Tre Kronor flour mill, and its oat mill, Havrekvarnen, built in 1927–28, is now a listed building. Around Tre Kronors väg the company built a model village for its workers, with terraced houses, narrow blocks of flats and its very own Konsum co-op store, open from 1935 to 1977. The Munspelet office building from 1966 – nicknamed “the Harmonica” – is listed for its striking modernist architecture.
Kvarnholmens centrum ligger i Bageriet,: Kvarnholmen's centre is Bageriet, the Bakery – the old crispbread factory, whose earliest drawings date from 1929. Today people live where the crispbread used to be baked. Right next door is Disponentvillan, the manager's villa, built in 1931 for the head of Kvarnen Tre Kronor, the Three Crowns Mill. Makaronifabriken, the macaroni factory, is still here too, and the Lilla Kvarnholmen playground is themed on the island's old industrial buildings.
Kvarteren vid Åkerbyvägen hör till HSB:s: The blocks along Åkerbyvägen are part of HSB's low-rise housing in Tibble, one of the areas built in the 1950s and 60s. A little further away is Täby centrum, with the Filmstaden cinema, opened in 2013, which has five screens and 516 seats. In the other direction is Ensta station on the Roslagsbanan railway, where around 500 people get on on an ordinary winter weekday.
Kvarteret Gamlebo, intill Svedmyra tunne: The Gamlebo block, beside Svedmyra metro station, was originally built as Gamlebo, the City of Stockholm's old people's home, later known as Gammelbyn. Its ten original residential buildings are now owner-occupied flats. Much closer, on the corner of Bandhagsvägen and Tussmötevägen, was the Corso cinema, which opened in 1938 as Tusse-Bio and closed in 1969.
Kvarteret Holmia bildades 1906 av det ny: The Holmia district was founded in 1906 by a newly formed company, AB Lidingö Villastad, and its early 20th-century character is still beautifully preserved, with villas in National Romantic, Art Nouveau and Art Nouveau Baroque styles. Here you'll find Lidingö museum, in the former Villa Fornboda from 1907, with exhibitions on 20th-century Lidingö and a turn-of-the-century salon. It's run by Lidingö's local heritage society – one of the largest in Sweden – which among other things organises Bellman Day.
Kvarteret Rosteriet har fått namn efter: The Rosteriet block – ‘the Roastery’ – is named after a German firm that roasted coffee substitute here from 1913 to 1920. Pharmacia then made medicines on the site, and in the 1950s and 60s AB Atomenergi produced fuel rods here for Swedish research reactors. Up on Liljeholmsberget hill is Brännkyrka's old parish hall from the 1920s, which since 2003 has been home to Nordic Music, an upper secondary school.
Kvastekulla griftegård, en bit härifrån,: Kvastekulla cemetery, not far from here, was designed by the Finnish architects Bengt Lundsten and Per-Mauritz Ålander, who won a Nordic architecture competition. Their idea was to keep the beautiful landscape intact and disturb nature as little as possible. Planning began in 1952, the cemetery opened in 1959, and the chapel followed four years later.
Kvibergs kaserner var militärförläggning: The Kviberg barracks were an army base from 1895 to 1994. Today they're listed buildings with a restaurant, museum and market. They're also home to the Sports Museum, Idrottsmuseet, founded in 1983, which has had two Olympic medals among its exhibits. Just to the north is Prioritet Serneke Arena, the largest multi-sports venue in the Nordic countries, with an indoor ski track 1.2 kilometres long.
Kvibergs marknad håller till i det gamla: Kvibergs marknad, the Kviberg market, is held in the old horse stables of the artillery regiment. Every weekend 10,000–15,000 visitors browse 160 stalls for antiques, curios and odds and ends. A little further away is Prioritet Serneke Arena, the biggest multi-sport venue in the Nordic countries, with a full-size football pitch and a 1.2-kilometre indoor ski track.
Kvibergsnäs landeri: Kvibergsnäs landeri, a historic country estate
Kynäsberget, ett par hundra meter bort,: A couple of hundred metres away is Kynäsberget, a large expanse of forest and rock of national interest for outdoor recreation. Further south, in Lake Trehörningen, lies Storholmen, which was originally an island. In the 1920s it was divided into plots for summer cottages, mostly sold to working people from Stockholm, and the island was linked to the mainland by a footbridge. Today most of it is forest and shoreline that everyone is free to enjoy.
Kyrkan i slutet av Värmlandsgatan bär ku: The church at the end of Värmlandsgatan carries King Oscar II's full name, and the king himself came to visit in 1898 and signed the guestbook. Round the corner runs Nordhemsgatan, with the Briggen food hall. The area is also home to SS Manhem, Gothenburg's biggest chess club, with more than 400 members – one of the top clubs in Sweden.
Kyrkan med de två tornen här bredvid är: The church with the twin towers right beside us is Högalidskyrkan, consecrated in 1923. Keep watching now, because we'll soon be heading up onto Västerbron, the bridge with one of the best views in Stockholm.
Kyrkbytorgets hus byggdes i mitten av 19: The buildings around Kyrkbytorget square went up in the mid-1950s, and the Roxy cinema here showed films from 1956 to 1965. The library opened the same autumn as the cinema, in November 1956, and much of its 1950s interior was kept when it was renovated for its 60th anniversary. Nearby runs the Lundby Tunnel, which at 2,060 metres is one of Sweden's longer road tunnels.
Kyrkeby och Nereby är ett gott exempel p: Kyrkeby and Nereby are a good example of how statisticians keep redrawing the map. Before 2015, there was a small settlement here officially called Nereby and Sjöhed. When the boundaries were redrawn, a larger built-up area was marked out instead and named Kyrkeby and Nereby. A little way off is the church village of Kyrkeby, with Harestad Church.
Källö, officiellt Stora Källö, har fått: Källö, officially Stora Källö, is named after a pothole on the island – a ‘giant's kettle’ worn into the rock. Islanders once made their living from fishing and farming, and the oldest houses date from the 1700s. In 1932 Gothenburg's motorboat club bought land here and built a jetty, a dance floor and a kiosk. Today there are around 30 summer cottages on the island.
Kälvestas radhus och villor har en helt: Kälvesta, with its terraced houses and villas, has a very different neighbour to the north-east: Lunda, a district taken up mostly by a large business and industrial estate just south of Hjulsta and west of Spånga. Two very different worlds, then, at a comfortable distance from each other – a good example of how varied Västerort, Stockholm's western suburbs, can be.
Kärleksstigen vid Isbladskärret: Kärleksstigen, the Lovers' Path, by Isbladskärret
Kärna bokskog ligger nära, ett naturrese: Kärna beech forest is close by: a nature reserve of about 18 hectares, created in 2008 and managed by the West Coast Foundation. The rare wood fescue grass grows among the beeches, along with several red-listed lichens. Parts of the reserve have been made accessible, so the forest isn't just for seasoned hikers.
Kärra kyrka alldeles intill hette faktis: Kärra church, right next to us, was actually known as Kärra chapel right up until 2001. North of the church is a parish hall from 1978. And Kärra was once a place of justice: from 1824 to 1887 the district court for the Askim area held its sessions here.
Kärrdal hör till Östra Sjöberg, en kommu: Kärrdal is part of Östra Sjöberg, a district tucked between Edsviken bay, Lake Rösjön and the Rinkeby forest. Further on, on the eastern shore of Edsviken, is Bergendals herrgård, Bergendal Manor. The site is known from the 1650s, when the croft of Snickartorpet stood here, and the grand manor house was built in 1913 at the initiative of landowner Ragnar Liljenroth. Today it's a hotel and conference venue. Along the same road is Landsnora kvarn, a mill that is Sollentuna's oldest secular building.
Kärringstan är inget officiellt namn, me: Kärringstan – roughly 'Old Wives' Town' – isn't an official name, but this villa area has earned it. The streets are named after famous women, and the blocks have names like Baderskan, Barnjungfrun, Kallskänkan and Tvätterskan: the Bath Attendant, the Nursemaid, the Cold-Kitchen Maid and the Washerwoman. So the Barnmorskan block, the Midwife, fits right in – its terraced houses won Stockholm's Building of the Year award in 2011. Just around the corner is Modellvillan 21, which took the same title in 2017.
Kåhög är ett litet villasamhälle vid Säv: Kåhög is a small village of houses on the Säveån river, with the Western Main Line railway to the south. At the bridge in Kåhög begins the Jonsereds strömmar nature reserve, the Jonsered Rapids, which follows the Säveån valley all the way to Lake Aspen. With a bit of luck you might spot kingfishers and dippers.
Kållered ligger precis vid gränsen till: Kållered lies right on the border with the province of Halland. It used to be farming country, but today western Kållered is dominated by hypermarkets. A short distance away is Kållered station – the first station here opened back in 1891 – and the area also has the Shopping Park Kållered retail park.
Kållered ligger vid gränsen mot Halland: Kållered sits on the border with the province of Halland and was once farming country. Today it has big out-of-town stores such as IKEA, a small hotel and a golf course beside the Torrekulla nature reserve. Not far from here is Kållered Church, the oldest building in Mölndal municipality.
Kållered var en gång lantbruksbygd, men: Kållered was once farming country, but today western Kållered is all about big-box retail. Shopping Park Kållered is right here, and nearby was EkenCenter, a shopping centre from 1990 with about 25 shops. The competition proved too tough, the building was demolished in 2013, and yet another retail building went up in its place.
Kållereds socken hörde till Askims härad: Kållered parish was part of the old Askim district and existed long before any motorways were built through here. Its parish church, Kållered Church, stands on a hill in the village and is in fact the oldest building in the whole of Mölndal municipality. This area was also once home to the EkenCenter shopping centre, which was demolished in 2013.
Kållereds station har haft två liv. Den: Kållered station has had two lives. The first station opened in 1891 but closed in 1972. When commuter trains between Gothenburg and Kungsbacka came back, a new station opened on 17 August 1992, and in the rush hour there are now trains every fifteen minutes in each direction.
Köpcentret Allum har ett namn från forns: The Allum shopping centre has an Old Swedish name: it's the dative form of ‘alla’, all, and means roughly ‘for everyone’. It opened in 2006 and spans the E20 motorway with shops and a walkway. Not far away, Partille herrgård – the manor house locals call Slottet, the Castle – sits on a hill overlooking the Säveån river valley. It has been listed since 1995.
Köpcentret Allum, alldeles intill, har e: The Allum shopping centre, right beside us, has a name with a story. Allum, or allom, is an Old Swedish dative form of 'all', meaning something like 'for everyone'. Work began in September 2004, and it opened in April 2006. A building with shops and a passageway spans the E20 motorway, linking the northern and southern halves.
Köpcentret Stinsen invigdes 1995 av Ingv: The Stinsen shopping centre was opened in 1995 by the TV presenter Ingvar Oldsberg, in a former car showroom where Mercedes-Benz cars used to be sold. One reminder of those days remains: the two big car lifts are still in use, now as goods lifts. The centre was extended in stages and reopened in 2009.
Köpcentret här hette Mörby Centrum ända: The shopping centre here was called Mörby Centrum until May 2026, when it was renamed Danderyds Centrum – though the metro station in the northern part of the building kept the old name. It opened on 29 January 1978. Not far off is Villa Markelius, which the architect Sven Markelius designed in 1945 for himself and his family. And down by Edsviken bay stands Berzelii ek, Berzelius' Oak, today what's known as an oak ruin.
Landshövdingehus i kvarteren runt omkrin: Landshövdingehus – Gothenburg's stone-and-wood tenement houses – in the blocks around
Landstingshuset, där Region Stockholms p: Landstingshuset, where Region Stockholm's politicians meet today, spent more than 150 years as a military hospital, Garnisonssjukhuset, from 1811 to 1969. Next to it stands Graverska huset, built in 1754 as a home for the tanner Jacob Graver. And for food lovers: at Bergsgatan 33, the chef Mathias Dahlgren ran the restaurant Bon Lloc – Catalan for “good place” – which held a Michelin star from 1997 to 2005.
Lasse and Maja have moved to Skogås! Härbreparken, nearby, is a themed play park inspired by Valleby, the fictional little town where the children's detective agency Lasse-Majas detektivbyrå solves its mysteries. The park won Huddinge's architecture award in 2020. In the middle of Skogås centrum, on Yttertorget, stands Mariakyrkan, the parish church of Trångsund-Skogås.
Lemmingvallen heter fotbollsanläggningen: Lemmingvallen, the Lemming Ground, is the football ground a stone's throw away – a name that makes many people think of little mountain rodents. Here in Utby, in eastern Gothenburg, there's a grass pitch and an artificial pitch for eleven-a-side, plus two gravel pitches for seven-a-side. Utby Church is close by too.
Lerkrogen är ett hus som har flyttat. De: Lerkrogen is a house that has moved. The old tavern first stood near Brännkyrka Church, but it was taken down in 1968 to make way for new roads and the Stockholmsmässan exhibition centre. In 1986 it was put back up near Älvsjö station, and today local heritage societies use it. Next to it is the Älvkvarn stone, an ancient cup-mark stone that has also been moved twice.

Lexby var landsbygd ända tills radhusen: Lexby was open countryside right up until the terraced houses arrived in the 1950s, followed by the Vintergäcken estate in the late 1960s. The actor and director Sissela Kyle grew up here and writes about it in her memoir. Partille IF and the rugby club Spartacus both play their home games in Lexby, and a little further away is Partille Arena.
Lidingö centrum, kommunens största centr: Lidingö Centre, the island's biggest shopping area, opened in 1995 and combines shops with owner-occupied flats. Next door is Lidingö Town Hall from the early 1970s, designed by Sten Samuelson and given the blue rating for its high architectural and historical value. The Grand cinema, which opened in autumn 1993, is the only cinema in the whole municipality.
Lidingö har bara tre vattentorn, och ett: Lidingö has just three water towers, and one of them stands a short walk from here, at the end of Tallbergsvägen. Käppala water tower is sometimes called Brevik water tower, even though it's actually in western Käppala. The area also has Villa Brevik from 1920, which for many years hosted HSB's in-house training courses.
Lilla Bommen och Göteborgsoperan: Lilla Bommen and the Gothenburg Opera
Lilla Ursvik har en oväntad industrihist: Lilla Ursvik has a surprising industrial past. In 1906 the brothers Alexander and Patrick Graham founded their lift company, Graham Brothers, here, and from 1929 it made neon signs as well. A new factory went up in 1937. Lifts were still being made here until the late 1970s, by which time the Finnish company Kone had taken over.
Lilla Varholmen är porten till Öckeröarn: Lilla Varholmen is the gateway to the Öckerö islands. It's linked to Hisingen by a bridge, and from here the car ferries head out to the islands of Öckerö municipality on two routes, the Björkö ferry and the Hönö ferry. The Björkö crossing is only about 900 metres long and takes roughly five minutes. The island has its own lighthouses too: the leading lights that guide ships in today date from 1927.
Lilla Ösbysjön är bara 4,1 meter djup oc: A couple of minutes away, in the middle of the villa area, is Lilla Ösbysjön, a small lake only 4.1 metres deep. Close by is Vendevägen station on Roslagsbanan, the Roslagen railway. It opened in 1912 as Parkvägen and didn't change its name until 1956. The waiting shelter was designed by the architect Sigge Cronstedt.
Lilleby vid havet på Hisingen var länge: Lilleby, by the sea on Hisingen, was pure countryside for a long time and belonged to Björlanda parish until it became part of Gothenburg in 1967. As early as 1846, the farmland here was redistributed in a land reform. Today the housing areas are growing fast. The district covers 1,330 hectares and is also home to Sillviks Havskoloni, a seaside holiday colony with its cabins preserved from the 1950s.
Lillängen nämns första gången 1653 och v: Lillängen is first mentioned in 1653, when it was a grazing and hay meadow belonging to the Järla estate. The villa area was planned in 1937, and the first families moved into their new houses that same autumn. The same year, the area got its own stop on the Saltsjöbanan railway, and the functionalist waiting shelter from 1937 – green with white corners – is still standing today.
Lindevägen fick sitt namn 1917, och vill: Lindevägen got its name in 1917, and the villa area along it was first known as Nya Enskede, 'New Enskede', or Palmeska förstaden, 'the Palme suburb'. The name Linde comes from a croft, an inn and a coaching station that stood nearby from 1762. Since 2012 the metro station has been decorated with Maria Miesenberger's Ögonblick i rörelse, 'Moments in Motion', with granite-ceramic walls and aluminium sculptures.
Lindholmen var länge ett av Göteborgs st: For many years Lindholmen was one of Gothenburg's great shipyards. Where ships once took shape, you'll now find Lindholmen Science Park and part of Chalmers University of Technology. From the quay there's a view straight across the river to the city centre.
Lindholmspiren ligger vid den gamla varv: Lindholmspiren is in the old shipyard district of Lindholmen, where ships were built for more than a hundred years. Today it's home to Lindholmen Science Park and part of Chalmers University of Technology, and from the quay you can look straight across the river to the city centre.
Lindome ligger cirka 15 kilometer söder: Lindome lies about 15 kilometres south of Gothenburg, but still counts as part of the Gothenburg urban area. It's the church village of Lindome parish, in the province of Halland, wedged between the E6 motorway and the West Coast Line. A short way off is Lindome station, where commuter trains call and buses have a larger stop.
Lindome socken är stor, hela 81,7 kvadra: Lindome parish is a big one, covering a full 81.7 square kilometres, and it takes in both the town of Hällesåker and Lindome itself, with its parish church. Lindome Church is a short walk from here. The parish used to belong to the province of Halland and the old Fjäre district, but since 1998 it has been part of Västra Götaland County.
Lindome station har varit död och återup: Lindome station has died and come back to life. It opened on 1 September 1888, when the Gothenburg–Halland railway was completed, but passenger trains stopped calling in 1970, and in 1989 the station shut altogether. Then, when commuter trains between Gothenburg and Kungsbacka started up again, it made a comeback on 17 August 1992. In 2012 it was rebuilt to take longer trains.
Lindvreten var ett torp under Vårby gård: Lindvreten was a croft belonging to Vårby gård, and its name probably means 'the patch of land with the lime trees'. Nearby was the croft of Månskär, whose curious name has nothing to do with the moon. It comes from Måns, one of its first tenants, and kärr, the Swedish word for wetland. This is also where you'll find Södra djursjukhuset, an animal hospital that started out in 1967 with two people working from a villa.
Liseberg ligger alldeles i närheten. Där: Liseberg amusement park is just nearby. One of its rides is the Flume Ride, opened in 1973, where log-shaped boats float along a 610-metre water channel with drops of up to 14 metres. Beside the park, the Grand Curiosa Hotel opened in 2023, just in time for Liseberg's 100th birthday. Eklandagatan, by the way, is named after the village of Eklanda – and the ending 'landa' means land by the shore.
Ljudet av speedway har ekat här. Arendal: This place has echoed to the roar of speedway. Arendalsbanan, a 336-metre track, was home to the Kaparna team. The attendance record of 5,940 was set in September 2002, against Rospiggarna, and Tony Rickardsson set the lap record riding for Masarna in 2004. A little further on, in Rödjan, is Rya skog, a nature reserve since 1928 and a last remnant of the mixed oak woodland that once covered much of the west coast.
Ljusets kyrka: Ljusets kyrka, the Church of Light
Loviseberg, en bit härifrån, är till sto: Loviseberg, a little way from here, is mostly a lovely area for getting outdoors, with a ski slope, a beach and walking trails. By Lake Albysjön is the Gömsta äng nature reserve. Set up in 1966, it's both the oldest and the smallest reserve in Huddinge, with meadows, alder woods along the shore and a grove full of wild flowers. Part of the 80-kilometre Huddingeleden trail runs through it.
Lovö skogskyrkogård anlades på 1830-tale: Lovö Woodland Cemetery was laid out in the 1830s, after complaints that the old churchyard at Lovö Church had grown too cramped and sat on marshy ground. It lies on Lovö kyrkallé, inside the Drottningholm Palace World Heritage area. From here you can also join Lovöns fornstig, an 18-kilometre heritage trail across the island of Lovön that links ancient remains, memorials and interesting buildings.
Lovö socken rymmer både Drottningholms s: The parish of Lovö is home to both Drottningholm Palace and the old parish church, Lovö kyrka, a little way from here. Outside the church stand five runestones, and one of them has had quite an adventure. In the 17th century it stood by the door of the church porch, but when the porch was pulled down in 1798, the stone ended up buried. It wasn't found again until 1935, when the church was being restored – all 2.7 metres of it, raised in memory of a woman.
Lovön is full of traces of the Viking Age. About 500 metres south of Edeby farm is a runic inscription carved straight into the bedrock, known as U 52. It's a reminder that people have lived and travelled here for a thousand years – long before the buses started running to Ekerö.
Lovön är ön i Mälaren där Drottningholms: Lovön is the island in Lake Mälaren where Drottningholm Palace stands, linked to the mainland by the Drottningholm and Nockeby bridges. A short walk away is Lovö Church, with no fewer than five runestones outside – among them a little sandstone one barely more than a metre tall. From the church, the Lovö church avenue runs ruler-straight for about 1,800 metres towards the palace grounds.
Lullehovsbron spänner över det drygt 200: Lullehovsbron bridge crosses the Lullehovssundet strait, just over 200 metres wide, between Färingsö and Lindö. Both the bridge and the strait are named after the hamlet of Lullehov at the bridge's eastern end. Today's bridge opened to traffic in 1980. The water is about seven metres deep in the middle of the strait, and at its southern end lies the little island of Kaninholmen, Rabbit Island.
Lundbergs konditori: Lundbergs konditori, a classic café and patisserie
Lundens vattentorn, en åttkantig putsad: Lunden water tower, an eight-sided rendered building about 45 metres tall, was built in 1930 to a design by Eugen Thorburn, the architect who also designed Lundenskolan school. A little further away, on the corner of Sankt Pauligatan and Femkampsgatan, is Kolerakyrkogården, the Cholera Cemetery, with a memorial stone to those who died in the cholera epidemic of 1834. The front of the stone simply reads År 1834 – 'The year 1834'.
Lundenskolan invigdes den 15 maj 1914, o: Lundenskolan school opened on 15 May 1914, and its architect, Eugen Thorburn, went on to design the district's water tower too. Next door is Örgryte New Cemetery from 1890, with almost 3,900 graves. A short way off is Tån cemetery. Its name comes from ‘tun’, the patch of land beside the home fields where livestock were let out to graze.
Luxgatan är en blinkning till AB Lux, se: Luxgatan is a nod to AB Lux, later Electrolux, whose factories stood on the south-eastern part of the island – lux is Latin for light. This was also the site of Nya Chartago, the stronghold of a fraternal society called the Coldinu Order, and the Fridberg inn welcomed guests from the 18th century until the 1850s. Over on the Marieberg side, Gideon Forslund built fast motorboats known as flat-iron racers.
Lägg märke till gatunamnen: Sedelvägen,: Take a look at the street names: Sedelvägen, Riksdalervägen and Sparbanksvägen – Banknote Road, Riksdaler Road and Savings Bank Road – with blocks named Valutan, 'the Currency', and Förskottet, 'the Advance'. In the Förskottet block is Hägerstensåsen's old post office from 1951, designed by Lars-Erik Lallerstedt and blue-listed by the City Museum. You can't post letters here any more, but the mail is still sorted inside. The district sits on a ridge that rises to 67 metres above sea level.
Läkare och sjuksköterskor har gett namn: In Guldheden, the streets are named after doctors and nurses. Doktor Allards gata honours the doctor who started free seaside trips to Askim for Gothenburg's children – known as 'Doktor Allard's bathing children'. In the middle of the square, Fina fisken, 'the Fine Fish', spouts water. Palle Pernevi made this steel sculpture in 1961, welding it together himself, and its five jets are meant to evoke Lyrön in Bohuslän, where it was created.
Längre västerut än så här kommer man int: This is as far west as the metro goes: Norsborg is the westernmost station on the whole network and has been the end of the red line since 1975. A short walk away is the Botkyrka poorhouse. Built in 1798, it took in the poor right up until 1911 and then served as an old people's home and nursing home. Since 1998 it has been full of schoolchildren again, as the independent school Botkyrka friskola holds its lessons here.
Längs Bergsunds strand låg förr varv och: Shipyards and workshops used to line the Bergsund waterfront. Just across the water is Långholmen, which for many years was home to Stockholm's central prison until it closed in 1975. Today the old prison is a hotel and hostel, and the island has a popular swimming spot and lovely walking trails.

Bergsunds strand was once lined with shipyards and workshops. Across the water is Långholmen, for many years home to Stockholm's central prison, which closed in 1975. Today the old prison is a hotel and hostel, and the island has a popular swimming spot.
Längs Delsjövägen låg förr Synvillan, so: Delsjövägen was once home to Synvillan, 'the Optical Illusion' – Gothenburg's tongue-in-cheek nickname for the old Swedish Television and Swedish Radio building. SVT moved out in 2007, and the building was torn down in 2010 to make way for housing. One of the new blocks, Studio 1, built in black-fired Danish brick, won the Kasper Salin Prize, Sweden's top architecture award, in 2016 – and that same year it was also nominated for the Kasper Kalkon, the 'turkey' prize for the ugliest building of the year.
Längs Ekerövägen väster om Träkvista fin: Along Ekerövägen, west of Träkvista, is Fantans hög, an offering cairn with a grim legend attached. Fantan is said to have murdered her husband and been forced to run the gauntlet: if she made it far enough up the Asknäsmalmen ridge to see Ekerö Church, she would go free. She collapsed just short of it and was stoned to death. Legend has it that anyone passing should leave a coin, a stone or a dry twig.
Längs Elfviksvägen finns två villor av a: Along Elfviksvägen are two villas by the architect Ralph Erskine: Villa Molin from 1947, built for the garden designer and editor Ulla Molin, and Villa Gadelius, designed in 1961 for the businessman Knut Saburo Gadelius. A little further on is the Canada block. Its terraced houses, together with those in Gamla Enskede, are thought to be the very first in Sweden, and they've been listed since 1981.
Längs Farstaviken byggde porslinsfabrike: Along Farstaviken bay, the Odelberg family, who owned the porcelain factory, built their dream homes. In 1910 Ferdinand Boberg designed Villa Farsta udde for Maria Bennich, the daughter of factory director Wilhelm Odelberg, and the following year Villa Strandvik for her brother Axel. The director himself lived at Farsta Manor, whose original 1620s building was burned down by the Russians in 1719. On a hill by the harbour lies a late Iron Age burial ground.
Längs Farstavägen ligger kvarteren Kampö: Along Farstavägen are the Kampö and Hartsö blocks, with late-1950s terraced houses designed by the architect Birger Nygell and recognised by the City Museum for their heritage value. A short walk away, Farsta torg opens out before you. Laid out like an Italian piazza, it was inaugurated on 23 October 1960. The square was once lined with department stores – Nordiska Kompaniet, Kvickly and Tempo – and the shopping centre has been voted shopping centre of the year several times.
Längs Lantmäterivägen går en gammal tipp: An old landfill runs along Lantmäterivägen, marking the northern edge of Hummelmoraberget, a hilly part of the Görväln nature reserve where, after the Ice Age, the waves left beach ridges of gravel and stone. In the other direction, in Viksjö centre, is Viksjö Church, consecrated as recently as 2005 by Bishop Caroline Krook.
Längs Långedragsvägen fanns förr bio. Ol: Långedragsvägen was once a street of cinemas. Olympia opened in 1929 and kept going until 1971, and even earlier, from 1919 to 1925, the Oden cinema stood here, just outside what was then the city boundary. The Kungssten area was simply known as Stadsgränsen, the City Boundary. A short way off are the Sjöbergen allotments, where people were already keeping small animals in the 1930s.
Längs Malmvägen står tio höghus med 1 24: Ten tower blocks with 1,247 flats line Malmvägen, which is why locals call the street 'Tian', the Ten. The service building, designed by Åke Arell, drew international attention when it opened in 1972, with preschools, shops and club rooms all gathered on the ground floor. Towering over the square is the fifteen-storey Turebergshuset, home to the municipal offices and, since 2023, the library too.
Längs Margaretavägen står Gamla Enskedes: Along Margaretavägen stand the Gamla Enskede terraced houses, known as the English terraces. Together with the Canada Houses on Lidingö, they're Sweden's very first terraced houses. Enskede Church stands out on a rise in a park in the middle of the villas. And on Enskedevägen is Enskedestationen, a former electricity substation from 1911 that's now offices.
Längs Margaretavägen står några av Sveri: Along Margaretavägen are some of the very first terraced houses in Sweden. The terraces of Gamla Enskede – also known as the English terraces – were, together with the Canada houses on Lidingö, the first in the country. The City Museum has marked all 37 homes, in six rows, blue for their outstanding cultural value. Gamla Enskede is a garden city, and it's also home to Enskede skola, one of Stockholm's largest primary schools, with more than 900 pupils.
Längs Sveavägen här har kulturlivet levt: This stretch of Sveavägen has a rich cultural life. The Golden Circle – Gyllene Cirkeln – a jazz club in the ABF building, kept the music going from 1962 to 1969. And in Kårhuset, the Student Union Building, opened in 1935 with a speech by Prince Eugen, students staged their famous occupation in May 1968. The Grand cinema has been showing films since 1933. And here's a bit of trivia: Rådmansgatan is the only metro station named after a street.
Längs gamla Södertäljevägen, strax norr: Along the old Södertäljevägen road, just north of Långbro Hospital, there used to be an inn called Långpannan. It began life as a croft belonging to the Långbro estate and was pulled down in 1964. The name Långbro itself goes back even further: it comes from a medieval causeway of logs – a 'long bridge' – that carried Göta landsväg, the old highway, across the area.
Längs länsvägen mellan Mölnlycke och Möl: Lilla Kullbäckstorp lies along the county road between Mölnlycke and Mölndal, and just a short way off is Lake Vällsjön, glittering and only four and a half metres deep. On the far side of the lake begins Pixbo, a very hilly residential area built on and around a height called Björnåsen. Pixbo even has its own postal town.
