Längs Ältavägen låg dagsverkstorpet Snör: Along Ältavägen was the croft of Snörom – pronounced ‘snör-om’, but also known as Snurrom – whose tenants paid their rent in labour on the Erstavik estate. North of Lake Sandasjön stood Tuppstugan, a former croft for a soldier-sailor that has gone by names such as Oxberget, Svartbäcken and Solmärke. The 18th-century cottage had unique wall paintings by the artist Olle Nyman, but sadly it burned down over the Whitsun weekend of 2004.
Lärje var en gång den första stationen p: Lärje was once the first station out of Gothenburg on the Västergötland–Gothenburg Railway, about six kilometres from the city station. Just beyond it, the line crossed the tracks of the Bergslagen Railway on a viaduct and then followed the valley of the Lärjeån river. The Alelyckan sports centre is close by, too.
Lärjeholms gård, alldeles i närheten, ha: Lärjeholms gård, the farm close by, has an arched stone bridge over the Lärjeån river just to the east, and this is where the river flows into the Göta älv. Nearby runs the two-kilometre Tideräkningsgatan – roughly “Calendar Street” – one of 54 streets in Kortedala that were all named in 1953 using words taken from the almanac.
Lärjeån har gett namn åt Lärjedalen, som: The Lärjeån river gave its name to Lärjedalen, a district in its own right from 1989 to 2010 that took in Hammarkullen, Hjällbo and Agnesberg. The river rises north of Gråbo and flows into the Göta älv at Lärjeholm, draining an area of 119 square kilometres. Closer to the stop is the Bäckebol Center retail park.
Lärjeån, som slingrar förbi en bit härif: The Lärjeån river, winding past a short way from here, gave the former district of Lärjedalen its name. It rises north of Gråbo and joins the Göta älv river at Lärjeholm, draining an area of 119 square kilometres. Nearby is the Bäckebol Center retail park, with around twenty shops.
Lärkstadens villor har haft spännande gr: The villas of Lärkstaden have had some intriguing neighbours. The one on the corner of Baldersgatan and Valhallavägen was designed by the architect Erik Josephson as his own home. Since then it has been the Danish ambassador's residence and the embassy of both Yugoslavia and Serbia. The villa next door, designed by Torben Grut, has been Libya's embassy since 1978. And a little further along, a villa was built for the theatre and film producer Anders Sandrew.
Långbro gård har anor från senare delen: Långbro gård dates back to the late 1400s and was already a manor estate by the end of the 1500s. It gave its name to the district, and the name in turn comes from a long medieval causeway made of logs – långbro means 'long bridge'. It probably ran where the northernmost stretch of Sjättenovembervägen is today. The main house has been marked in blue by the City Museum for its historical value, and it now contains public rental flats.
Långholmen och fängelsemuseet: Långholmen island and the prison museum
Långsjön är bara tre meter djup men har: Långsjön is only three metres deep, but it has an important job: it marks the boundary between the municipalities of Stockholm and Huddinge – or, to be precise, between the residential areas of Herrängen and Segeltorp. On the lake's northern shore is Långsjö gård, dating back to the 1600s, when it was a croft belonging to the Långbro estate. Segeltorpsvägen was named in 1928 after Segeltorp farm, which was pulled down in 1964.
Långsjön är en liten sjö med badplats oc: Långsjön is a small lake with a swimming spot and a 1.4-kilometre jogging trail around it, and since 2005 the lake and its immediate surroundings have been a nature reserve. It's 5.6 metres deep and sits just over 20 metres above sea level. A little further away, in Storängen, stands Villa Widstrand, built in 1906 for the publisher Wilhelm Widstrand of the publishing house Wahlström och Widstrand.
Långsjövägen, ett par hundra meter bort,: Långsjövägen, a couple of hundred metres away, is no ordinary villa street. From its northern end up to Myrvägen it follows the old Göta landsväg, the historic highway to Götaland, and it forms the boundary between Älvsjö and Långbro and between Älvsjö and Långsjö. Close by is Långsjöhöjden, which is a nature area, a residential area and a street all at once.
Långt innan industriområdena fanns Nylös: Long before the industrial estates came along, there was Nylöse parish, the parish of the old town of Nya Lödöse. It ceased to exist around 1624, but the hospital's congregation carried on and in 1627 became Gothenburg's hospital parish, which lasted right up until 1883. The Marieholm industrial estate, incidentally, takes its name from the Marieholm landeri, one of Gothenburg's old country estates.
Långt innan tunnelbanan fanns här rullad: Trams were rolling past here long before the metro arrived: from 1930 the Örbybanan line ran by, with a stop on this very spot. The metro came in 1951, at first with a temporary station, and the permanent station opened in 1953 as the end of the line. In fact, the metro between Globen and Stureby follows the route of the old tramway.
Lövgärdets kyrka, en kort promenad härif: Lövgärdet Church, a short walk from here, is a church that's no longer a church. It was deconsecrated on 19 June 2016. While it was in use it belonged first to Gunnared parish and, from 2014, to Angered parish. Lövgärdet itself is a neighbourhood within the Gårdsten district of north-eastern Gothenburg.
Malmvägen i Tureberg kallas Tian, efter: Malmvägen in Tureberg is known as Tian, the Ten, after the ten tower blocks Åke Arell designed in 1970. The complex holds 1,247 flats, with preschools, shops, a gym and club rooms on the ground floor. It was part of the Million Programme, Sweden's great housing drive, and drew international attention when it opened in 1972. The nearby street name Bagarby recalls Bagare by, an older name for the Tureberg farm.
Manillaskolan grundades 1809 av Pär Aron: Manillaskolan, a school for deaf and blind children, was founded by Pär Aron Borg in 1809 and stayed here on Södra Djurgården, the southern part of Djurgården island, until 2013. Just east of the school stands the mighty King's Oak, Kungseken. In the villa Nedre Manilla, the Bonnier family keeps its collection of more than 300 portraits, most of them of Swedish authors. The very first, bought in 1905, was Hanna Pauli's portrait of Verner von Heidenstam. Down on the little islet of Manillaholmen stands the sculpture Frihetens port, the Gate of Freedom, from 1994.
Marabou kom hit 1916 som dotterbolag til: Marabou, the chocolate maker, arrived here in 1916 as a subsidiary of the Norwegian firm Freia, in a factory designed by Ivar Tengbom. Production moved to Upplands Väsby in 1976. The old chocolate factory and Marabouparken, the park beside the Bällstaån stream, are now considered of very high cultural and historical value, and the park is known for its art gallery.
Marabouparken började fyllas med skulptu: Sculptures started appearing in Marabouparken as soon as the park was laid out, and by the 1970s there were sixteen works in the collection. Beneath the eastern part of the park is the Marabouparken art gallery, opened in 2010 beside the old cocoa laboratory designed by Artur von Schmalensee. The park is also home these days to Långholmen Folk High School, which used to be based in an old pavilion at Långholmen Central Prison.
Mariakyrkan i Hammarkullen: Mariakyrkan, St Mary's Church, in Hammarkullen
Mariakyrkan vid Skogås Yttertorg ligger: Just a few steps away is Mariakyrkan, St Mary's Church, by Skogås Yttertorg – the parish church of Trångsund-Skogås. Hidden up on the cliff a little way off is Lännafortet, a fort built in 1908–1909 as part of the Southern Front. Together with the Northern Front, nicknamed Korvlinjen, 'the Sausage Line', it was a key part of Stockholm's fixed defences until 1952 – and Lännafortet is one of the forts that has survived in good condition.
Mariebergs kyrkogård intill anlades 1787: Marieberg cemetery next door was laid out in 1787 on Majberget hill – the name was simply prettified from 'Maj' to 'Marie'. Among those buried here are Wilhelm Stenhammar and Johan Fredrik Carpelan. Nearby is Captain Hansson's house from 1850, which was threatened with demolition and moved to Chapmansgatan in 1953. And on Chapmans torg square you'll find the Gothenburg English Studio Theatre, the only English-language theatre in western Sweden.
Mariehällskyrkan har bytt psalmer mot ba: Mariehällskyrkan has swapped hymns for nursery rhymes. Until 2015 it was the church and parish hall of Bromma parish, but then the municipality bought the building and opened a preschool here in 2016. The congregation moved across the street to Kvarterskyrkan. A little further away is Annedal, named after Anna Augusta Wickman-Olsson, who owned a plot beside the Bällstaån stream in the 1880s.
The ground here has a dramatic past. On 29 September 1950, Surte was hit by the Surte landslide, one of the worst natural disasters in Swedish history. Several houses were swept away – yet, miraculously, only one person died. Just up the road is Surte station. It opened in 1879, and after a gap of more than 40 years, passenger trains started stopping here again in 2012.
Marken här tillhörde Klara kloster, till: This land belonged to the Klara convent until 1527, when the Reformation parliament in Västerås ordered the convent to be torn down. In the 1560s it was granted to Torbjörn Klockare, who now has a street named after him. Röda bergen, the area around us, is the largest stretch of Stockholm's inner city built all of a piece to the town planning ideals of the 1920s. And over at Torsplan, the Norra tornen, the Northern Towers, rise to 104 and 120 metres.
Mars 1566 small det rejält i trakten. Un: In March 1566 this area was rocked by an enormous explosion. During the Swedish siege of Bohus Fortress, the Danish-Norwegian defenders blew up their own keep, Röde Torn, the Red Tower – an event remembered as Bohusiska smällen, ‘the Bohus Bang’. Rödbo covers the very northern tip of Hisingen island, between the Göta älv and Nordre älv rivers. It's mostly forest, with open fields running down to the water and a scattering of houses. Rödbo Church is only a couple of hundred metres away.
Masthugget hör till Göteborgs allra älds: Masthugget is some of the oldest land in Gothenburg, part of the city since 1621, and it was declared a suburb as early as 1646. An unplanned settlement grew up around the ship harbours along the river. Nearby is the Sjömannasällskapet building, the Seamen's Society house, from 1901 and 1903. Oscar Fredriksskolan, the school from 1897, is said to be named after Oscar II – who was meant to speak at the opening but never turned up.
Masthuggskyrkan, stadens bästa utsikt: Masthuggskyrkan – the best view in town
Masthuggstorget ligger nedanför Masthugg: Masthuggstorget square sits at the foot of the Masthuggsberget hill. Up on the hill is Masthugget Church from 1914, and around the square are some of the city's oldest landshövdingehus – Gothenburg's typical houses with a stone ground floor and wooden upper storeys.
Med 1 390 elever år 2024 hör gymnasiet h: With 1,390 students in 2024, the upper secondary school here, which opened in 1982, is one of the biggest in Stockholm County. Nearby is the Good to Great tennis academy, founded in 2011 by the former pros Magnus Norman, Nicklas Kulti and Mikael Tillström. Players who have trained there include the brothers Mikael and Elias Ymer.
Med sina 199 kvadratkilometer utgör Hisi: At 199 square kilometres, Hisingen accounts for roughly half of Gothenburg municipality. The island is part of Västra Götaland County and is the fifth largest in Sweden. Water surrounds it on every side: Göta älv, Nordre älv and the Kattegat. About a quarter of the island belongs to the province of Västergötland, the rest to Bohuslän.
Medborgarplatsen är Södermalms stora tor: Medborgarplatsen is Södermalm's big square, with outdoor cafés in summer and an ice rink in winter. From here it's a short hop to Götgatan, the lively main street of Söder.
Mellan Hjulsta och Lunda ligger Hjulsta: Between Hjulsta and Lunda are the Hjulsta allotments, run by an association founded in 1973 and today a fine example of a multicultural growing community. Lunda itself is mostly business parks and industrial estates. The old Kälvesta windmill, by the way, is also known as Lunda kvarn – and it actually stood in Lunda for a while after 1884.
Mellan nybyggda hus och köpcentrum står: In among the new buildings and shopping centres stand four stones from prehistoric times. The Sannegården monument is what's left of a burial ground from the end of the Bronze Age and the beginning of the Iron Age. The largest, a triangular standing stone, is still in its original spot, while the others were moved to make way for gravel digging. The harbour below, Sannegårdshamnen, opened in 1914.
Metalfans, spetsa öronen. En bit härifrå: Metal fans, listen up! A short distance from here is Studio Fredman, which the producer Fredrik Nordström founded in 1990 and still runs. In Flames, At The Gates, Hammerfall, Opeth and Arch Enemy have all recorded albums here, along with visitors from abroad such as Dimmu Borgir and Panic! at the Disco. Closer to the stop is the Motor Industry Technical upper secondary school – where the engines make the noise.
Midsommarkransens tunnelbanestation ligg: Midsommarkransen metro station lies in a rock cavern 17 metres underground, and it opened along with the red line in 1964. Along Främlingsvägen are slender blocks of flats from the 1940s; in 2013 they were joined by six new buildings, which were shortlisted for Stockholm's Building of the Year the following year. A little further on, the Hägerstensviadukten viaduct carries the Essingeleden motorway.
Millesgården var skulptören Carl Milles: Millesgården was the home, studio and garden of the sculptor Carl Milles and his wife Olga, and today it's an art museum and sculpture park. Milles made Skridskoprinsessan, the Skating Princess, in 1949, after watching a girl skating at Rockefeller Plaza in New York. He was so taken with the way she moved that he set out to capture it in bronze. You enter through the art gallery, designed by Johan Celsing.
Minnesstenen Norges tack: The memorial stone Norges tack, ‘Norway's Thanks’
Mitt bland forskningshusen står ett lite: Among the research buildings stands a small timber house, painted Falu red, with a royal past. Falkenerarbostället, the Falconers' Lodge, was built in 1726 to house the royal falconers and originally belonged to Karlberg Palace. It's extremely well preserved and rated as exceptionally valuable in cultural and historical terms – but today it's a private home.
Mitt bland lagerhallar och verkstäder st: Right in among the warehouses and workshops stands an old windmill. Ulvsunda kvarn, also called Bällsta kvarn, sits at the foot of Kvarnberget, Mill Hill, beside Ulvsundavägen, just south of Bromma Airport. Even closer is the Fructus building, the white functionalist factory where the soft drink Pommac was made.
Mitt bland villorna i Smedslätten, på en: Right among the villas of Smedslätten, on an empty plot on Aladdinsvägen, lies Kämpakumlet – a Bronze Age burial ground with round, cairn-like stone settings. It was partly excavated in 1922, while the garden suburb was being built. The district is named after Smedslätten farm. All that's left of it is the early 19th-century main house, now surrounded by terraced homes.
Mitt emot Solna centrum ligger Eric Grat: Opposite Solna centrum is Eric Grate's park, named after the sculptor who spent his last fifteen years in Solna. Three of his bronze sculptures stand here: Oberon, Nike de Sant Andria and Sparvguden, the Sparrow God. The shopping centre itself is one of the largest in the region, with more than 95 shops and 22 restaurants.
Mitt hjärta i världen: Mitt hjärta i världen, 'My Heart in the World'
Mitt i Eklanda, en stadsdel där cirka 3: In Eklanda, where around 3,100 people live in some 700 homes, the forest is never far away. The area borders the Änggårdsbergen nature reserve and Högsbo. Most of it was built after 1993, and the plan is for Eklanda eventually to grow together with the village of Fässberg.
Mitt i Lövgärdet, ett primärområde i sta: In the middle of Lövgärdet, part of the Gårdsten district, stands a church that has retired from its role. Lövgärdet Church was deconsecrated on 19 June 2016, after belonging to Gunnared parish from 1973 and to Angered parish in its final years. The building is still right nearby, but the services have moved elsewhere.
Mitt i Rävekärr står de gråa, kvadratisk: In the middle of Rävekärr stand the grey, square terraced houses nicknamed 'lådhus' – box houses – giving the estate a geometry all of its own. Right next door is Fågelberg Church, part of Stensjön parish. To the south-east are two lakes, Horsikan and Rävekärrs Långevatten – perfect if you'd like to swap boxes for water.
Mitt i Solberga ligger Solbergaskogen, m: In the middle of Solberga is Solbergaskogen, a wood of bare rock and pine trees that the Swedish Forest Agency classed as a key habitat in 2009. It holds ancient remains, among them the Solberga burial ground, and takes its name from Solberga farm, mentioned as early as 1636. A little further away is Apelsinlunden, the Orange Grove – a Million Programme housing estate from 1967 that owes its nickname to its orange-red colour scheme.
Mitt i Volvos värld står Volvohallen, en: In the heart of Volvo country stands Volvohallen, a domed exhibition hall on a square plan, built in 1975 beside what was then the company's head office and designed by Lund & Valentin. Right next to it is Torslandaverken, the Volvo Cars plant. When it opened, it was the largest single-storey factory in the Nordic region.
Mitt i centrum ligger Viksjö kyrka, som: In the middle of the centre is Viksjö church, consecrated by Bishop Caroline Krook on 19 June 2005, the fourth Sunday after Trinity. The name Viksjö itself is far older: it's a corruption of an original Vikhusa, which already appears on an 11th-century runestone.
Mitt i ett industriområde gömmer sig en: Tucked away in the middle of an industrial estate is a true survivor: Rya skog, a remnant of the mixed oak forest that once covered much of Sweden's west coast. Most of it became a nature reserve as early as 1928, and a survey in 2007 found 22 rare and endangered species here. It's a favourite with botanists and birdwatchers, especially in spring.
Mitt i ett svenskt villaområde vid kuste: In the middle of a Swedish residential area on the coast, there's a copy of Kina slott, the Chinese Pavilion at Drottningholm. Skintebo, in Billdal, was farmland for many years, but in the 1970s Skintebodalen was built up with car-free footpaths, terraced houses, two-storey wooden houses and what are known as båtmansgårdar – “boatswain's houses” – an odd cross between a terraced house and a villa.
Mitt i handelsområdet Kungens kurva finn: Right in the middle of the Kungens kurva shopping area there's an oasis – at least in name. The sculpture Oas, 'Oasis', was created in 2009 by the artist and designer Thomas Nordström, working with the landscape architect Torsten Wallin. A little further on is Kolartorp, a croft with plenty of names: it has also been known as Kålartorp, Crone and Ryttartorp nummer två, 'Cavalryman's Croft No. 2'.
Mitt i kvarteret står Coldinuorden 3, et: In the middle of the block is Coldinuorden 3, one of Bredäng's many long slab blocks from the mid-1960s – yet the only one the City Museum has rated blue for its exceptional cultural and historical value. Nearby Slättgårdsskolan school burned down in June 2020, and the owner decided to rebuild it with a fresh look. A new gym opened as early as 2021.
Mitt i rondellen står en 4,5 meter hög k: In the middle of the roundabout stands a 4.5-metre pin, pushed through a cross in the ground. The sculpture, by Ebba Matz, is called Här – ‘Here’. The square's name was controversial: the city property office would have preferred Reutersplatsen, partly because Wavrinsky was so hard to pronounce. On the hill next door, students now live in Guldheden's old northern water tower.
Mitt i skogen mellan sjöarna Flaten och: Deep in the forest between the lakes Flaten and Drevviken is Torpet i Orhem, a culture café that has been going since the 1940s. Artists such as Frida Hyvönen and Joel Alme have played on its little stage, which now lives in a converted shipping container. Right next door is Orhems gård, a farm going back to the 15th century, and down by Lake Drevviken is Gebers, a former convalescent home that in 1997 became one of Sweden's first eco co-housing communities.
Mitt på torget, som hette Adolf Fredriks: In the middle of the square, known as Adolf Fredriks torg until 1959, stands Tors fiske, Thor's Fishing, a fountain by Anders Wissler unveiled in 1903. Also on the square is Hotel Rival, owned by the composer Benny Andersson and named after the old Rival cinema in the same building. This was once the site of Sutherska huset, a private palace from 1774. From 1811 the Philipsen school taught poor children there, until the building was demolished in 1909.
Mittemot Segeltorpsskolan, vid nuvarande: Opposite Segeltorpsskolan, the Segeltorp school, at what is now Kapellvägen 1, there was once a croft called Holmtorp. Its first family of crofters were Jonas Olsson and his wife Kjärstin Eriksdotter, both born in 1710, and in the 1760s the place went by the name of either Holmtorp or Cronan. The croft was pulled down in 1859. Another croft, Segeltorp, survived until 1964, when the terraced houses of Jakobslundsvägen were built on the site.
Moderna museet: Moderna Museet, the Museum of Modern Art
Morgonen den 23 september 2009 använde r: On the morning of 23 September 2009, robbers flew a stolen helicopter in to collect their haul from a cash depot in the Västberga industrial area. It was the first helicopter robbery in Swedish history. The police helicopters never got off the ground – someone had left a fake bomb on their landing pad. The building, Vreten 17, was originally built for Volvo, among others.
Motionsanläggningen Fysiken vid Mossen h: The Fysiken sports centre by Mossen had a stormy start. Its predecessor, Plastiken, opened in 1969 – a tent of coated fabric held up by air pressure from inside – and that very autumn a storm almost brought it to a sorry end. Its replacement, Fysiken, opened in 1983, and for a few years students paid ten kronor extra in their term fees to help fund it.
Mulle Meckparken, ett par minuter härifr: A couple of minutes from here is Mulle Meckparken, created under the direction of the artist Tor Svae and opened in autumn 2008. Two years later it won Solna's urban environment prize. Nearby there's a small mystery, too: a runestone found by a spring in 1900 was last seen in 1908, and only a small fragment of it has turned up since.
Munkebäckstorget fick sitt namn 1947 eft: Munkebäckstorget was named in 1947 after Munkebäcken, an old name for the Härlandabäcken stream. The monks – munkar in Swedish – were probably those of Nya Lödöse. Right beside it stand the ruins of the old Härlanda Church, a reminder of a parish that was merged into Nylöse parish as far back as 1528. Next to the ruin is Härlanda New Church.
Museerna här lockar upp till en miljon b: The museums around here attract up to a million visitors a year. Tekniska museet, the National Museum of Science and Technology, was named Museum of the Year in 2025 and once had Sweden's only 4D cinema, where the seats moved and you were treated to gusts of wind, splashes of water and smells. In the grounds of the Ethnographic Museum is the teahouse Zui-Ki-Tei, the Dwelling of the Promising Light. Zui means both 'promising' and 'Sweden'.
Mycket av marken runt Hammarby sjö fanns: A hundred years ago, much of the land around Hammarby sjö lake simply wasn't there. In 1925 a new canal was blasted through the Danvik cliffs, and the lake dropped by about five metres. The newly exposed shoreline was built up with blasted rock, and an area of car workshops and small industries called Lugnet grew up on it. Today it's the site of Hammarby sjöstad, a new waterfront district built between 1994 and 2020.
Mysterna har ett namn med mystik, men fö: Mysterna sounds mysterious, but the explanation is down to earth: myst means a small bog. The village lies a kilometre west of the Göta älv river, and on its edge is the Svankälla wetland park. Created in 2003–2004, it's rich in birdlife, including marsh harriers, little grebes, lesser spotted woodpeckers, coots and mallards.
Mälarhöjdens skola är stadsdelens störst: Mälarhöjden school is the biggest in the district, with more than 1,100 pupils in 2016, from the reception year up to year nine. A little way off was Mälarbio – also known as Mälarhöjdsbio, Kvistoperan and later Färglådan – where regular film shows started in the spring of 1924 and carried on until January 1959. Today the old cinema building houses a school.
Mälarskogens naturreservat, ett par hund: A couple of hundred metres away is the Mälarskogen nature reserve, protected since 2022, with the Mälarpromenaden walking trail running through it. The trail passes Hallundaröset, the second-largest known Bronze Age burial cairn in Södermanland. The cairn survived when the housing went up in the 1970s, thanks to its spot on a hilltop at the edge of the forest.
Mälarstranden här var förr full av sjökr: This stretch of the Lake Mälaren shore was once lined with lakeside inns. Arboga kök, near Sätra shipyard, was probably built in 1829 and burned down in 1967. In what is now the Sätraskogen nature reserve stood Råstock, an inn that ran from 1665 to 1813 – well into the days of the poet Bellman. Down on the shore, at Sätra varv, sailing ships and barges were repaired between 1878 and 1935, and several of the workers' houses still stand on the hill.
Möbelsnickare på riktigt utbildas en bit: Just up the road, real cabinetmakers learn their craft. At Malmstens, formerly the Carl Malmsten school, about 65 students study furniture design, cabinetmaking and upholstery in purpose-built workshops. The area was also once home to Bodal church, since demolished, and Bodals gård, the old farmhouse of an agricultural estate.
Mölndal betyder kvarndalen, och forsen s: Mölndal means 'mill valley', and the rapids that gave the town its name are just nearby. Mills have stood beside the rapids in Kvarnbyn, the Mill Village, since the 1300s, and until the 1600s most of them belonged to the Crown. The falls run for about 800 metres and drop some 45–48 metres. Later, the water powered local industry. Today Kvarnbyn is protected as a heritage area of national interest, and Mölndal City Museum sits right by the rapids.
Mölndal hade förr två järnvägsstationer,: Mölndal once had two railway stations, a lower one and an upper one. The lower station opened in 1888 on the West Coast Line, and its building was pulled down in 1977. The upper one, on the Borås Line, opened in 1894 in red brick and was demolished in 1983. Not far from here is the steep hill on Kvarnbygatan known as Mölndals kråka, Mölndal's Crow, or simply Kråkan.
Mölndal har fått sitt namn efter kvarnar: Mölndal is named after the mills that have stood by the rapids of the Mölndalsån river since the Middle Ages. Not far from here, at Göteborgsvägen 1, was the Grand cinema, which opened on Boxing Day 1938 and closed in 1966. A little further on is Mölndal travel centre, on a 500-metre bridge over the motorway, used by about 3.5 million passengers a year.
Mölndal är ett ställe för både simtag oc: Mölndal is a place for both swimming strokes and hoofbeats. A few hundred metres from here is Åbybadet, a swimming centre that opened in summer 2023 at a cost of 500 million kronor. In the same area is Åbytravet, Sweden's second-biggest trotting track, run by the Åby Travsällskap association. So you can take your pick: go for a swim yourself, or watch the horses race.
Mölndals sjukhus invigdes 1924 och ersat: Mölndal hospital opened in 1924, replacing a municipal infirmary, and is now part of Sahlgrenska University Hospital. The Möllan cinema in Mölndal's Folkets hus, the community hall, has been showing films since 1959. It has 289 seats and has been modernised and gone digital with the municipality's support.
Mölndals stadsmuseum ligger sedan 2002 h: Since 2002, Mölndal's city museum has stood at the top of the steep hill known as Mölndals kråka, the Mölndal Crow – and there's a café if you need a rest after the climb. Just below, the Mölndal rapids, Mölndalsfallen, rush past; in the 1800s their power drove cotton mills, paper mills and a weaving mill. Nearby Royens gata is named after three Roy brothers who emigrated from Stirling in Scotland.
Mölndalsfallen strax intill har gett sta: The Mölndal rapids, Mölndalsfallen, just next to us, gave the town both its food and its name: there was salmon fishing and there were mills, and Mölndal means something like Mill Valley. The steep hill east of the square goes by the name Mölndals kråka, the Mölndal Crow. The streets round here have their secrets too. Götaforsliden has been called both Glada gatan, Happy Street, and Tysta gatan, Quiet Street – nobody knows why – while Royens gata is named after three Roy brothers from Stirling in Scotland.
Mölnlycke station en bit härifrån har fl: Mölnlycke station, a little way from here, has moved house. It opened in 1894 about 350 metres east of where it is today, and moved to its present spot in 2003. The old station building was demolished in 2013. Today Västtågen regional trains stop here on their way between Gothenburg and Borås, on the Kust till kust line – the Coast-to-Coast line.
Mölnlycke är kyrkbyn i Råda socken, och: Mölnlycke is the church village of Råda parish, and the old Råda rural municipality was run from here. Although it's mostly villas, terraced and linked houses, the town is full of greenery, including the Rådasjön nature reserve and the Finnsjön outdoor recreation area. A handful of properties actually lie in Mölndal municipality.
Mölnlycke, centralort i Härryda kommun,: Mölnlycke, the main town of Härryda municipality, lies about ten kilometres south-east of Gothenburg and is made up mostly of detached, terraced and linked houses. Even so, it's a green place, with the Rådasjön nature reserve and the Finnsjön outdoor recreation area close by. The Mölndalsån river flows through the centre on its way from Landvettersjön lake to Rådasjön, and right in the middle of town is the little lake Massetjärnen.
Mörby centrum byggdes 1961 och glasades: Mörby centrum was built in 1961 and given a glass roof in 1977. In 2026, after ten years of rebuilding, it got a new name too: Danderyds Centrum. The metro ends here – Mörby centrum is the terminus of route 14 on the red line. The new look was designed by Gatun Arkitekter.
Mörby station har legat på Roslagsbanan: Mörby station has been on the Roslagsbanan railway since 1906, and just south of it are the line's workshops, there since 1907 and designed by the architect Sigge Cronstedt. A few hundred metres away is Danderyd hospital, one of the county's emergency hospitals, where around 6,300 babies are born every year. That's a lot of people who took their first breath right here.
Mörby verkstäder: Mörby verkstäder, the old Mörby workshops
Mörbyleden slingrar sig mellan E18 och V: Mörbyleden winds between the E18 and Vendevägen and runs right past the Mörbyskogen housing area. Not far from here is Danderyd Hospital, one of the county's emergency hospitals, taking in around 90,000 emergency patients a year. And in May 2026 the nearby shopping centre changed its name from Mörby Centrum to Danderyds Centrum.
Nacka Forum öppnade den 1 mars 1989 och: Nacka Forum opened on 1 March 1989, replacing a makeshift centre in prefab huts that had served for many years. Right next to it, the leafy villa suburb of Storängen begins, where Villa Wållgren from 1907 has been judged irreplaceable. A stone's throw away is Villa Yngve Larsson, designed by Ragnar Östberg and built in 1907 for the future city commissioner and his wife, Elin, née Bonnier.
Nacka kyrka byggdes 1891 i nygotisk stil: Nacka Church was built in 1891 in the Gothic Revival style and stands in Nacka North Cemetery. Around it lies Birka, one of Nacka's oldest residential areas. The first houses went up in the 1880s for workers at the area's booming industries, such as Atlas Copco in Sickla and de Lavals Ångturbin, the steam turbine company, in Järla. The area has changed its name several times – it has been Järla, Järlaby and Birka-Järla.
Nacka strand hette länge Augustendal. 18: Nacka strand was known for a long time as Augustendal. In 1899 the industrial pioneer J.V. Svenson bought the area, and by 1916 his engine works employed 500 people, making it one of the biggest workplaces in Sweden. After going bankrupt in 1922, the company was taken over by Handelsbanken. Offices and homes followed in the 1980s, and in 1988 the area got its current name, Nacka strand. Down in the marina, since 1995, Carl Milles' sculpture God the Father on the Rainbow has been sending an arc of water out over the Saltsjön bay.
Namnet Beckomberga är gammalt. Det äldst: Beckomberga is an old name. Its earliest recorded form, Bäknaberga, dates from 1319, and it means 'the people who live by the stream'. In the Middle Ages the village was made up of three farms: Södergården, Mellangården and Norrgården – South, Middle and North Farm. In the 1950s the Runda husen, the Round Houses, went up on the corner of Bällstavägen and Spångavägen as homes for the nurses at Beckomberga Hospital.
Namnet Blåsut kommer från en krog vid et: The name Blåsut – roughly 'blow out' – comes from a tavern at a forester's lodge, and in the 19th century it was a common name for windswept spots. The metro station opened in 1950, and in 2008 it was given artwork by Ann Edholm: speed stripes in black and white tiles. A little further on is Framtiden 1, 'the Future', from 1915. In the building next door – fittingly called Nutiden, 'the Present' – was the Enskede Kvarn cinema.
Namnet Bräcke kommer av fornsvenskans br: The name Bräcke comes from the Old Swedish word brækko, meaning a broad slope or hillside. A stone's throw away is Bräcke diakoni, the foundation set up in 1923 as Göteborgs diakonissanstalt to train deaconesses. A short walk off is Bräcke cemetery, laid out during the cholera epidemic of 1834, when the disease reached Sweden through Gothenburg.
Namnet Gårda dyker upp redan 1550 och är: The name Gårda goes back to at least 1550 and is simply a grammatical form of the word gård, meaning farm. A stone's throw away is Hästskosömsfabriken, the old horseshoe-nail factory, whose buildings from around 1890 and 1900 are now protected by the state as a heritage site. And Drakegatan is named after the Drake brickworks, founded by Anders Drake in the mid-1700s.
Namnet Högsätra betyder högre belägen än: Högsätra means 'the higher meadow', and the name comes from an area with three 19th-century villas. The complex was built to provide public services for every age group, with a school, sports facilities, healthcare and a pharmacy. Högsätrahuset, which once housed Lidingö hospital, is due to be demolished to make way for the new Kärnan neighbourhood.
Namnet Jättesten kommer från de stora st: The name Jättesten – “giant stone” – comes from the huge boulders on the hill behind the houses. The next street along has an amusing story behind its name. A C Lindblads gata was named in 1954 after Anders Christensen Lindblad, a newspaper editor and pioneer of the labour movement. The naming committee wanted to call it Lindbladsgatan, but at the city council meeting Hugo Höglund pointed out that everyone used to call Lindblad simply “A C” – and so A C it was.
Namnet Kallebäck betyder bäcken med kitt: Kallebäck means 'the stream with the kettle', and the name first appears in 1496. The district sits on Gothenburg's south-eastern edge, hemmed in by major roads. It's also home to Ostkupan, 'the Cheese Dome' – a 14-storey student block from 1964 with a nickname that's appetising, to say the least. A little further on is a cholera cemetery from the epidemic of 1866, now protected as an ancient monument.
Namnet Kungens kurva kommer från en alld: The name Kungens kurva – 'the King's Bend' – comes from a genuinely royal trip into a ditch. On a Saturday afternoon, 28 September 1946, King Gustaf V's chauffeur ran off Södertäljevägen road and got stuck in a water-filled ditch, and the press was there in no time. Today the area is one of the biggest shopping centres in Scandinavia, and together with Skärholmen centrum it pulls in 30 million visitors a year.
Namnet Kvarnskogen passar bra: en bit bo: The name Kvarnskogen, 'Mill Wood', is well chosen: a little way off, on the north-east shore of the Edsviken inlet, there has been a mill for more than 400 years. The first one was abandoned some time in the late 1500s – nobody knows why – but a new one soon went up on the same spot. The mill and the sawmill beside it were in use until the 1950s and are now a museum.
Namnet Käppala klingar bekant för många: For many people the name Käppala rings a bell for quite another reason: Käppalaverket, the sewage treatment plant that opened in 1969 and is considered one of the most efficient in the world. Not far from here is Käppalaställningen, too – an anti-aircraft position from the Second World War, rededicated in 1994 as a memorial to Stockholm's air defences.
Namnet Marievik har använts sedan 1930-t: The name Marievik has been in use since the 1930s. It's a Swedish version of Maryvik, one of four estates that once stood here. Right next door was Liljeholmen station, which opened to passengers on 1 December 1860 and handled goods until 1998. Up on Liljeholmsberget hill stands the old parish hall from the 1920s. Since 2003 Nordiska Musikgymnasiet, a music school, has filled its halls with music.
Namnet Masmo bär på en gammal rädsla: fö: The name Masmo hints at an old fear. The first part, 'mas', is thought to be a taboo word for wolf – a way of avoiding saying the real name – and the whole name is said to mean something like 'the forest where the wolf has been seen'. Just a stone's throw away, Myrstuguberget clings to the hillside above Albysjön lake. It was completed in 1986 and was the architect Ralph Erskine's first housing area in the Stockholm region. The name comes from Myrstugan, a boatswain's croft that was moved when the houses were built.
Namnet Mysterna kommer av ordet myst, en: The name Mysterna comes from 'myst', a word for a small bog. The village, mostly newly built villas and terraced houses, lies a kilometre or so north of Hisings Kärra and has counted as part of the Gothenburg urban area since 2015. On its outskirts is the Svankälla wetland park, a great spot for birds, where coots and mallards are among the residents.
Namnet Rud är gammalt, belagt redan 1495: The name Rud is old. It's recorded as early as 1495, spelled Rudh or Rwdh, and it means a clearing. A short way from here is Ruddalens IP, a football ground for 3,000 spectators, with artificial turf since 2003. The first match was played on 27 April 1985, when Västra Frölunda IF took on IFK Malmö.
Namnet Skra Bro sägs komma av det skrapa: The name Skra Bro is said to come from the scraping noise of sledge runners on the bare ground during a thaw. The old bridge over the Osbäcken stream is still here right next to us, but these days it's just a footbridge between the park-and-ride and a supermarket. Cars now cross a bigger road bridge north of the roundabout.
Namnet Skvaltan minner om en sjö vars ut: The name Skvaltan recalls a lake whose outflow through Vikdalen once powered several 'skvaltkvarnar', simple horizontal water mills. A little further away in Storängen is Villa Waern, built in 1905 for the merchant Charles Waern to designs by Torben Grut and rated irreplaceable. Close by is Villa Kallstenius, designed for the artist couple Gottfrid Kallstenius and Gerda Roosval-Kallstenius.
Namnet Spånga finns i skrift redan år 13: The name Spånga turns up in writing as early as 1300, as ‘apud Ecclesiam spangar’. It belonged to the old church village and simply means footbridges – narrow plank walkways. The station is on the Mälarbanan line, just over eleven kilometres from Stockholm Central. A little further on is Svandammen, the Swan Pond, a park with a swimming spot that's popular with teenagers and families alike.
Namnet Tegeludden är belagt sedan 1649 o: The name Tegeludden is recorded as early as 1649, for a head forester's house on Royal Djurgården – but nobody knows how it got the name. On the street stands Philipshuset, the Philips Building, built in the early 1960s as Svenska Philips' headquarters and warehouse. Today the Administrative Court sits in the old offices, and TV4 makes television in the warehouse.
Namnet Trolldalen har använts sedan 1700: The name Trolldalen, the Troll Valley, has been in use since the 18th century. It referred to the ravine in the middle of the woods on Henriksdal hill, a rift valley that easily sets the imagination running. Up on the hill is Henriksdalsringen, built between 1964 and 1969 to designs by the brothers Erik and Tore Ahlsén, who liked the result so much they moved in themselves. Nearby, in Finnboda, the Finnboda shipyard was in operation from 1884 to 1991.
Namnet Tulebo kan lura en. Den gamla tät: The name Tulebo can be misleading. The old village of Tulebo lies north-east of Lake Tulebosjön, but newer housing areas on the south-west side of the lake have been given Tulebo names too, such as Tulebo Villastad and Tulebo Park – even though they're actually in the villages of Hultet and Stretered. The Nilento Studio recording studio is also nearby.
Namnet Vantör är riktigt gammalt. Den me: The name Vantör is truly old. It was the name of the medieval parish, but after a fire in the 1400s its church became known as Brännkyrka, the Burnt Church. Today's Vantör church is in Högdalen, a short walk away. Högdalen centre also used to have a cinema, the Rondo, which showed films from January 1961 right up to May 1983.
Namnet Viksjö har en lång historia: det: The name Viksjö goes back a long way. It's a corruption of an original Vikhusa, which appears on a runestone as early as the 11th century. In 1963 a building consortium began developing the land, and today Viksjö is mostly houses from the 1960s, 70s and 80s. Not far off is Hummelmoraberget, a hill where old beach ridges show that the sea once reached all the way up here.
Namnet Viksjö är äldre än gården. Det dy: The name Viksjö is older than the farm. It appears on an 11th-century runestone, making it the oldest place name in Järfälla recorded in writing. The stone says that 'Knut in Vikhusum had the stone raised and the bridge made' in memory of his parents and siblings. The farm itself is recorded from 1734, and the neighbourhood around it was built in the 1970s.
Namnet har sin förklaring: här låg Hande: There's a reason for the name: this is where Handen's old folkpark, or people's park, used to be. What's left today is Haninge kulturpark, where local groups look after the last of the old buildings – among them RoJteatern, in the old Folkets hus community hall. Every June the park comes alive with music, theatre and dance during the Kulturparksfestivalen. A stone's throw away is Handens museum och smedja, a museum and smithy with goats and hens, where schoolchildren go on trips back in time.
Namnet kommer från Stuvsta gårds väderkv: The name comes from the windmill of Stuvsta gård, which once stood on Kvarnberget, the Mill Hill. The mill itself is long gone, but several millstones survive, and the municipality has put one of them on display on Gymnasievägen. One Saturday evening in 1908, a train came off the rails on the bend north of Huddinge station. Nobody was killed, and the accident was immortalised on two postcards.
Namnet kommer från en våg. Här vägdes jä: The name comes from a set of scales. This is where iron shipped out through Gothenburg's harbour was weighed, including iron from the ironworks of Värmland. In the 1780s the city's iron weigh-house was moved to a plot just north of today's Järntorget, 'the Iron Square', which was named after it. The men who carried the iron bars settled in the blocks round about. The weigh-house itself was pulled down long ago.
Nationalmuseum: Nationalmuseum, Sweden's national museum of art
Nationalmuseum står på det som en gång v: Nationalmuseum, Sweden's museum of art and design, stands on what used to be a tiny island of its own, Kyrkholmen. When the city gave the land for the museum in 1846, the head of construction, Johan af Kleen, simply filled in the canal separating it from Blasieholmen – without asking anyone's permission. The museum was finished in 1866 and is the largest art museum in Sweden. Just outside stands Theodor Lundberg's sculpture The Foster Brothers; its twin is in Copenhagen.
Naturhistoriska museet och blåvalen: The Natural History Museum and its blue whale
Naturhistoriska riksmuseet: Naturhistoriska riksmuseet, the Swedish Museum of Natural History
Naturhistoriska riksmuseet och Cosmonova: Naturhistoriska riksmuseet, the Swedish Museum of Natural History, and Cosmonova
Naturhistoriska riksmuseet, Sveriges stö: Naturhistoriska riksmuseet, the Swedish Museum of Natural History, is Sweden's largest museum complex. It was founded in 1819, and its present building, designed by Axel Anderberg, opened in 1916. Next door is Bergianska trädgården, the Bergius Botanic Garden. Its biggest building is the Edvard Anderson greenhouse from 1995, named after the wholesaler who left money in his will for a winter garden of Mediterranean plants. The nearby Ekhagen neighbourhood is one of the few built entirely in the functionalist style.
Naturreservatet Välen ligger några minut: The Välen nature reserve is a few minutes' walk away, at the far end of the Askimsviken inlet. It has a wetland museum, a bird-watching platform, a nature trail and a 'time trail' through history. The reserve was set up in 2014 and covers about 68 hectares, and within it are a Bronze Age cairn and stone setting.
Nedanför Baggeby, ner mot Lilla Värtan,: Below Baggeby, down towards Lilla Värtan, is Lidingsberg, one of the best-preserved 19th-century summer houses on Lidingö. Owned by the Wedberg family, it has the island's largest private plot, about six hectares, and is reached by Lidingsbergsvägen, the shortest named road on Lidingö. The buildings have been listed since 1954.
Nedanför Sankt Pauli kyrka står fontängr: Below Sankt Pauli kyrka, St Paul's Church, is Anders Jönsson's fountain group Elementens kamp, 'the Struggle of the Elements', unveiled on Swedish Flag Day in 1930. It originally stood on Olskrokstorget, but had to move when that square vanished to make way for the approach roads to the Tingstad tunnel. Along Redbergsvägen is Flamman, a 684-seat cinema that showed films from 1935 to 1982 and is now a listed building.
Nedanför Tahultsdrumlinen ligger lilla A: Below the Tahult drumlin – a ridge left by the ice sheet – lies little Agntjärnen, a pond just 6.5 metres deep. The slope down to the water is protected as the Gallhålan nature reserve: a large, unbroken oak wood on hilly ground, where wood vetch, wood violets, wood anemones and liverleaf grow. Out on the pond, look out for mallard, goldeneye, goosander and tufted duck.
Nedanför Torsvik vid Lilla Värtan står T: Down below Torsvik, on the Lilla Värtan strait, stands Torsvik lighthouse. Built in 1950 and taken out of service in 1980, it now marks the finish line for the Lidingö Runt sailing race. Where the old Lidingö bridge came ashore there's a small waiting shelter designed by Ivar Tengbom – so exposed to the wind that it earned the nickname the Temple of the Winds. The Torsvikshöjden housing area from the 1940s is seen as an early example of the planned post-war neighbourhood.
Ner mot Lilla Värtan ligger Kappsta natu: Down towards Lilla Värtan is the Kappsta nature reserve, dotted with the foundations of unusual houses. One of them belonged to Wisingska villan, where Raoul Wallenberg was born; today the memorial Attachéväska R.W., Attaché Case R.W., marks the spot. Nearby stood Villa Nidaros, Trondheim's pavilion at the 1897 Stockholm Exhibition. It was shipped here to serve as a summer house and burned down after being struck by lightning in 1960.
Nere i Klippans kulturreservat ligger An: Down in the Klippan heritage area is Ankarsmedjan, the old anchor forge. Anchors and chains were made here for the ships of the Swedish East India Company, which used Klippan as its outer harbour. The building is said to date from the 1770s. Its grey stone walls were one ell and nine inches thick – around 80 centimetres – and there was a cooper's workshop here too.
Nere vid Lilla Värtan ligger Ekhagens st: Down on Lilla Värtan is Ekhagen beach, also known as Lappis Beach. The student village of Lappkärrsberget – ‘Lappis’ for short – is close by. It's Stockholm's largest, with more than 3,000 student flats built in 1968–1970, and the streets have fitting names such as Professorsslingan, Amanuensvägen and Forskarbacken – Professor's Loop, Assistant's Road and Researcher's Hill.
Nere vid Lilla Värtan ligger Lidingsberg: Down by Lilla Värtan is Lidingsberg, one of the best-preserved 19th-century summer houses on Lidingö. Owned by the Wedberg family, it sits on the island's largest private plot – about six hectares – and is reached by Lidingö's shortest named road, Lidingsbergsvägen. The area is also crossed by Södra Lidingöstråket, a walking trail of about 18 kilometres that runs all the way from Gåshaga jetty to Stortorget, the main square in Gamla stan, the Old Town.

Down by the water of Lilla Värtan is Lidingsberg, one of the best-preserved 19th-century summer residences on Lidingö. It belongs to the Wedberg family and sits on the largest private plot on Lidingö, at about six hectares. The way in is along Lidingö's shortest named road, Lidingsbergsvägen, and the buildings have been listed since 1954.
Nere vid Magelungen står en stor röd trä: Down by Lake Magelungen stands a large red wooden villa from 1916–1917, built as a children's home. Its name, Rödkinda – ‘Red Cheek’ – reflects the hope that the fresh air would give the children rosy cheeks. The villa sits on a hill, with a south-facing slope running down to the lake. The old Farsta gymnasium building is now used by Farsta grundskola, a primary school, and the Adolf Fredrik music classes.
Nils Ericsonsplatsen är uppkallad efter: Nils Ericsonsplatsen is named after Nils Ericson, who built Sweden's first main railway lines – and was the brother of the inventor John Ericsson. Right beneath us, Västlänken, the West Link, a railway tunnel under central Gothenburg, is being built.
Nockeby torg, en kort promenad härifrån,: Nockeby torg, a short walk from here, was laid out in the early 1930s as a long, narrow piazza – a classic garden-suburb square. Tram 12 had already been extended this far in the autumn of 1929. Less romantic, but impressive all the same, is the Bromma sewage treatment plant nearby. Since 1989 its treated water has flowed through a tunnel some twelve kilometres long, under Solna and Stockholm, all the way out to the Saltsjön waters at Kastellholmen.
Norr om Humlegården skapades på 1870-tal: North of Humlegården park, a whole town of villas was laid out in the 1870s, modelled on English and German suburbs. Most of the villas later made way for grand apartment buildings, and Floragatan is now one of the most expensive addresses in Sweden. The Curman Villa, built in 1880–1881, is one of the few survivors – a free take on a Roman country house, with a tall, glass-roofed atrium at its heart. Its neighbour is Villa Sandrew.
Norr om Hågelby gård skulle det en gång: North of Hågelby gård, there were once plans for the biggest amusement attraction in northern Europe. The Lindgren family, who have run Stockholm's Gröna Lund amusement park for generations, were set to lease the land for a family theme park, Familjeparken Hågelby, but the plans were scrapped in 2014. What's still here is the Älvestaån stream, which drops 17 metres on its way from Lake Aspen to Lake Tullingesjön and runs partly hidden in a culvert beneath the Hågelby estate.
Norr om Tumlehed, en bit härifrån, finns: North of Tumlehed, not far from here, is an area of countryside criss-crossed by footpaths and trails, hiding several ancient monuments. Among them are rock paintings of four ships, a deer and four fish. Something to think about next time you're out walking in the woods here on western Hisingen.
Norr om sjön Flaten, inne i Flatens natu: North of Lake Flaten, tucked away in the Flaten nature reserve, is Skarpnäcksgrottan, a cave protected as an ancient monument. The Flaten district borders both Lake Drevviken and Lake Ältasjön, which is only about four and a half metres deep. Test fishing there has turned up perch, bream and ruffe, among others.
Norra Biskopsgårdens kyrka byggdes 1970: Norra Biskopsgården church was built in 1970 as a parish hall, when Lundby parish was at its biggest and needed more room. It has a free-standing bell tower. The Church of Sweden deconsecrated it in 2004, and it's now used by the City Mission and the Finnish parish. Not far away is Jättesten, named after the giant boulders on the hill behind the houses.
Nu har staden blivit kust. Långedrag är: Now the city has turned into coastline. Långedrag is Gothenburg's sailing harbour, and in summer the jetties are packed with boats. From here you can look out over the archipelago – and on a clear day, all the way to Vinga lighthouse, far out where the open sea begins.
Nu kör vi ner mot Göta älv och Stenpiren: Now we're heading down towards the Göta älv river and Stenpiren, the old stone pier. During the 19th and early 20th centuries, more than a million Swedes emigrated in search of a new life in America, and most of them left via Gothenburg – many boarding their ships right here. Today the Älvsnabben ferry crosses the river from this spot, and your tram ticket is valid on it too. Over on the far bank you can see Lindholmen and Eriksberg, once home to the city's great shipyards.
Nu kör vi över den lilla bron ut till Re: We're now crossing the little bridge over to Reimersholme. The island is named after Anders Reimers, who owned it in the 18th century. For many years there was a distillery here, and the name Reimersholms lived on on its bottles. Today the island is a quiet residential area with a waterfront path running all the way round. We'll soon reach the final stop. Thank you for riding with us!
Nu passerar vi Lisebergs södra sida. Här: We're now passing the south side of Liseberg amusement park, where you'll often catch a glimpse of the roller coasters. Lisebergshöjden, the hill behind the park, was once part of the Liseberg estate – the country house that gave the park its name.
Nu är vi i SoFo, området söder om Folkun: We're now in SoFo, short for ‘south of Folkungagatan’. It's full of little shops, cafés and bars, and at its heart is Nytorget, one of Södermalm's best-loved parks. Many of the buildings in the surrounding blocks date from the late 1800s.
Nu är vi på Södermalm. Västerbron, som v: We're now on Södermalm. Västerbron, the Western Bridge we've just crossed, opened in 1935 and is more than six hundred metres long. The twin-towered church right here is Högalidskyrkan, consecrated in 1923.

We're now on Södermalm. Västerbron, the bridge we've just crossed, opened in 1935 and is more than six hundred metres long. The twin-towered church right beside us is Högalidskyrkan, consecrated in 1923. You can see it from far away, and it's a landmark for the whole of western Söder.
Nya Ullevi byggdes till fotbolls-VM 1958: Nya Ullevi was built for the 1958 football World Cup and is still one of Sweden's biggest arenas. It's famous for its concerts too: when Bruce Springsteen played here in 1985, the stands swayed so much that the stadium later had to be reinforced.
Nya Varvet blev örlogshamn kring år 1700: Nya Varvet became a naval base around 1700, and in 1717 and 1719 it came under attack from Danish warships led by Vice Admiral Peter Tordenskjold. Right next to it is Nya Varvet cemetery from 1701, with a memorial to the crew of the submarine HMS Ulven, sunk by a mine in 1943. Nobis, the officers' mess a little way up the hill, is a listed building.
Nälsta är en av nio stadsdelar i Hässelb: Nälsta is one of nine districts in Hässelby-Vällingby, with a mix of villas, terraced houses and blocks of flats. Not far away is Spånga torg, the square by Spånga station, served by both commuter trains and buses. It has a good selection of shops, services and restaurants, so you'll find most things you need, whether you're hungry or have errands to run.
När LM Ericsson flyttade till Telefonpla: When LM Ericsson moved to Telefonplan in the late 1930s, the master builder Olle Engkvist put up about 1,000 flats in LM-staden, building fast and keeping the blocks narrow, just 8 to 10 metres deep. Over in Aspudden, in a small park on Manhemsgatan, is the 1912 fountain sculpture Fontändamm. It was paid for by the building company Manhem, which also got the street named after itself.
När Trädgårn öppnade som kafé 1858 fanns: When Trädgårn opened as a café in 1858, the staff were all men, and the only spirit served was punsch, a Swedish arrack liqueur. The building beside the stop, Exercishuset, was finished in 1867, a gift from the wholesaler Julius Lindström. It was meant for schoolchildren to do gymnastics and riflemen to drill. Heden itself was the army's training ground, and until 2019 it had a bandy rink.
När Tuletorget invigdes 1964 var det Sun: When Tuletorget opened in 1964, it was Sundbyberg's most modern shopping centre, complete with an underground car park, a BP petrol station, Systembolaget – the state-run off-licence – a Tempo department store, a post office and a shoe shop. But the shoppers never came, and by the 1970s the square was emptier by the year. Since 2016 it has been renovated and gained two new tower blocks, Tuletornen. Tulegatan is named after the mythical Thule, because the street once marked Sundbyberg's northern edge.
När området började bebyggas 1921 hette: When building started here in 1921, the area was called Ersta Villastad. The name sparked protests, and in 1926 it was replaced with a made-up one: Stureby. A couple of hundred metres away are the Vivstavarvsvägen terraced houses from the early 1950s, designed by Erik F. Dahl. Their 36 homes are the only ones in Stureby to get the City Museum's blue rating for high cultural value.
När tunnelbanan nådde Farsta den 19 nove: When the metro reached Farsta on 19 November 1958, it started out at a temporary station – right here, at Farstavägen 78 and Pepparvägen 81. Two years later the station moved into the new Farsta centrum, where the square, Farsta torg, was laid out like an Italian piazza, perhaps inspired by the Piazza delle Erbe in Verona. Fruit and flowers are still sold there most days of the week.
När tunnelbanan till Hässelby strand inv: The opening of the metro to Hässelby strand on 18 November 1958 was a real celebration. The first train, decked out with a cluster of six flags front and back, left Bagarmossen at 13.28. The 320 invited guests were served coffee on the way, and at the controls was the tramway's oldest driver, Karl Johan Gustavsson. Today the station is the north-western end of the green line.
När Örby slott hade sålts 1897 och ägorn: When Örby Palace was sold in 1897 and its land carved up into plots, Valdorshem was probably built – the very first villa in the area. It was demolished in the autumn of 2020. Older still is Örby kvarn, a windmill first built in 1672 and replaced by a new one in 1885. All that's left from the mill days is the miller's cottage, which has since been turned into a villa.
Nära Villa Källhagen, en anrik krog med: Near Villa Källhagen, a long-established restaurant with roots in the 18th century, is a large stone carrying a message of thanks. Norway's King Olav V presented it to King Carl XVI Gustaf in 1983 as an official thank-you for Sweden's help to Norway during the Second World War. Among other things, a Norwegian army of 15,000 soldiers was trained on Swedish soil, disguised as 'police troops'. There were also film studios nearby, in use from 1940 to 1960.
Nära stationen finns Leksaks- och samlar: Near the station is the Toy and Collectors' Museum, all about toys and play, which since May 2018 has shared a building with Historiearvsmuseet, the History Heritage Museum. Also known as HAMN, it was Sweden's first and only battlefield museum. And Fisksätra itself, by the way, is Sweden's most densely populated urban area, with 7,724 people per square kilometre.
Närlunda är ett av bostadsområdena i tät: Närlunda is one of the residential areas in the town of Ekerö. A little further on is Tappström, which counted as a separate town right up until 1975. That's also where you'll find Ekerö centrum, designed by the architect Ralph Erskine and completed in 1991, crowned by its trademark dot more than twenty metres up. Erskine's vision of a ‘Mälaren town’ has drawn international attention to the area.
Näsby slott ligger vid Näsbyviken av Sto: Näsby Palace stands on Näsbyviken, a bay of Stora Värtan, and is now a conference venue with a hotel and restaurant. The station next door has a little naming story of its own: it opened in 1937 as Alléparken, but after just four months it was renamed Näsby allé. At times the name has even been written as one word, Näsbyallé.
Näsbydal är format som ett ägg, med 900: Näsbydal is shaped like an egg and has 900 flats, ranging from studios with a sleeping alcove to seven-room flats on two floors. The housing cooperative even has its own football pitch, tennis court and several playgrounds. Right next to it is Kvarntorpshällen, a rock slab with runes on it that the author Jan Fridegård discovered in 1943, carved with the word 'stepsons'.
Näsbypark räknas som ett av Täbys mer ex: Näsbypark is one of Täby's more exclusive neighbourhoods, with villas, flats and terraced houses by the water on Stora Värtan. Further on is Näsby allé station, which opened in 1937 as Alléparken but changed to its current name after just four months. On Näsbyviken bay stands Näsby slott, a palace that's now a conference hotel with a restaurant.
Näsets kyrka ligger bara ett par hundra: Näsets kyrka, Näset Church, is only a couple of hundred metres away. The Näset peninsula has lots of places to swim along its rocky shore, including a nudist beach, and at its highest point, 50 metres above sea level, is an old lookout hut once used by maritime pilots. Åkered, with around 600 homes, was built between 1964 and 1966.
Nästan granne med hållplatsen ligger Blå: Almost next door to the stop is Blå Stjärnan, Sweden's largest animal hospital, which treats dogs, cats and small pets around the clock, every day of the year. Many people know it from the SVT series Djursjukhuset, 'The Animal Hospital'. A little further off, Hotel The Weaver rises 22 storeys high. Its name – Vävaren in Swedish – is a nod to the Krokslätt mills, which ran a complete weaving operation until the 1970s.
Nästan granne med hållplatsen står Kasta: Almost next door to the stop is Kastalakyrkan, the church of the Komarken district. Kungälv lies where the Göta älv river splits and the Nordre älv branches off, about 20 kilometres north of central Gothenburg. The town is also home to Nordiska folkhögskolan, the Nordic Folk High School, and to the west the municipality stretches out into a rugged coastline with an archipelago.
Någonstans här i närheten gömmer sig kan: There may be a runestone hiding somewhere around here. It's said to have stood by the avenue leading from Ulriksdal Palace, where there's now a road interchange, and it was probably built into a road culvert in the second half of the 1800s. People have gone looking for it several times, without any luck. Right next to it is Villa Jacobsdal, which shares its name with an older name for Ulriksdal Palace.
Någonstans i Veddesta stod en gång en vi: Somewhere in Veddesta there once stood a Viking Age runestone, U 93. Olof Celsius the Elder wrote about it in 1728 – and no one has seen hide nor hair of it since. The area takes its name from Veddesta gård, a farm that survived until 1983, and the industrial estate is set to become a mixed neighbourhood with several thousand new homes.
Några hundra meter bort ligger lilla Sto: A few hundred metres away lies little Stockbysjön lake, barely two metres deep at its deepest point, with yellow water lilies on its surface. It drains into Kottlasjön through the Stockbyån stream, which runs through flooded woodland and swamp where beavers, among others, are thriving. The area also has the Skärsätra water tower, a drinking-water reservoir that opened in 1912 and closed in 1959.
Några hundra meter bort står en runsten: A few hundred metres away, beside Kummelby Church, stands the Kummelby stone, a runestone from the late 11th century. The church has a little story of its own. The first one was built on the site of the old Kummelby farm, but it only held 50 people and was nicknamed Kummelby's little church. It was taken out of use in 1999, and just before Christmas 2000 a new church was consecrated.
Några hundra meter härifrån glittrar Söd: A few hundred metres from here sparkles Södra Långevattnet, a long, narrow lake with crystal-clear water that's popular for swimming. It drains north into Stensjön, close to Gunnebo House, which has lent its name to both Stensjön parish and Stensjökyrkan church. On the neighbouring ridge, Kikås, you'll also find Sweden's largest free-standing insect hotel.
Några hundra meter härifrån ligger Safjä: A few hundred metres from here is the Safjället nature reserve, on a rocky plateau near the Gothenburg border. To the south-west, the hill drops steeply down to the Toltorp valley. The reserve was set up in 1991 and covers 88 hectares. Closer to the stop is the Bifrost area, where the street names all have a farming theme.
Några hundra meter härifrån ligger Studi: A few hundred metres from here is Studio Fredman, the recording studio Fredrik Nordström set up in 1990. A long line of Swedish metal bands have recorded here – In Flames, Hammerfall, Opeth, Dark Tranquillity and Soilwork among them – and even Britain's Bring Me the Horizon. Just beyond is Radiotorget, opened in 1954 as Sweden's first satellite-town square.
Några hundra meter härifrån ligger Åbyba: A few hundred metres from here is Åbybadet, Mölndal's swimming centre, which opened on 16 June 2023 and cost 500 million kronor to build. In the same area is Åbytravet, the second-largest trotting track in Sweden. In the other direction lies Eklanda, a district built mostly from 1993 onwards.
Några minuter bort ligger Bandyhallen i: A few minutes away is Bandyhallen in Gubbängen, Stockholm's first indoor bandy arena. It's 25 metres high and opened in the summer of 2020, having originally been planned for Tallkrogen. The area also has the Majroskogen nature reserve, created in 2026 – the largest unbroken stretch of forest in all of Söderort, Stockholm's southern suburbs.
Några minuters promenad bort tar Fagersj: A few minutes' walk away is Fagersjöskogen, a forest of 100 hectares and one of the largest in Söderort, Stockholm's southern suburbs. It's also home to the biggest spruce tree in Stockholm! Nearby is Villa Lindhov, a wooden villa that Harald Lind had built in 1910 and then named after himself. It's one of the few well-preserved houses left from Södertörns villastad, a planned garden suburb.
Oljeraffinaderiet Preemraff Göteborg en: The Preemraff Göteborg oil refinery, not far off, gets most of its crude oil from the North Sea. Giant tankers dock at the crude oil harbour on Hjärtholmen, and the oil is stored in rock caverns right beside it. Tankers also unload further in at Skarvikshamnen harbour, but the water there is too shallow for the very biggest.
Oljeraffinaderiet Preemraff Göteborg kan: The Preemraff Göteborg oil refinery can process around six million tonnes of crude oil a year, most of it from the North Sea. Even ULCC-class supertankers – the biggest in the world, 333 metres long – have docked at the crude oil harbour on Hjärtholmen. The oil is then stored in huge caverns in the rock next to the harbour.
Olof Skötkonungsgatan fick 1925 sitt nam: Olof Skötkonungsgatan got its name in 1925, after King Olof Skötkonung and his supposed link to Örgryte Old Church, just a short walk from here. It's one of the most popular churches in Gothenburg for weddings, and the old churchyard, dating from the 13th century, is the resting place of three bishops, among others. At the entrance stands the statue Genomkämpat, roughly 'Fought Through' – the original is in Berlin.
Olshammarsgatan, en av Hagsätras två huv: Olshammarsgatan, one of Hagsätra's two main streets, runs for about 600 metres from Hagsätra centrum out to Ormkärr, crossing both Huddingevägen and the green metro line on the way. The centre itself went up in a single year and opened in 1960, and the copper sculpture 'The Child with the Hobby Horse' still stands guard there.
Om man bortser från en liten flik av Mäl: Apart from a small corner of Lake Mälaren, Lötsjön is the only lake in Sundbyberg, and since 2018 it has been a nature reserve together with the neighbouring Golfängarna meadows. Beside the lake is Lötsjökapellet, a chapel on the edge of Sundbyberg cemetery. The sports ground nearby is known to locals as Sumpan IP, and its all-weather track isn't full-size – it's just 366 metres.
Området Sandbäck i närheten har långa rö: The nearby area of Sandbäck goes back a long way. As early as the 1550s it was made up of two homesteads – two farms – long before any buses came rolling through. A little further on is Rävekärr, whose grey, square terraced houses are known locally as 'box houses', and south-east of them lies the glittering Lake Horsikan.
Ormkärr kallas den del av Hagsätra som l: Ormkärr is the name for the part of Hagsätra that lies south-west of Huddingevägen. From here it's a short way to Hagsätra torg, the square named in 1962, which surrounds the shopping centre. Its best-known landmark is “Barnet med käpphästen”, The Child with the Hobby Horse, a copper sculpture by Marie Stenqvist. And close by is Hagsätraskogen, 31 hectares of protected woodland.
Ormo naturreservat ligger nära, 25 hekta: Ormo nature reserve is close by: 25 hectares of broadleaf woodland and pasture along the valley of the Ormbäcken stream, between wooded hills and open grazing. It has been protected since 2018. Not far off, on the Nordre älv river, is the Ormo barrier, an adjustable dam that can divert water from Nordre älv into the Gothenburg branch of Göta älv, the Göta River.
Orten Kil i Boo har fått sitt namn efter: The village of Kil in Boo takes its name from Kils gård, a well-preserved manor on Graningevägen. The main building and its wings were given their Empire-style look in the 1820s under Major General Louis Marie de Camps. Not far away is Lake Insjön, almost twelve metres deep, with the old Velamsund estate and a swimming spot at its northern end.
Ortnamnen här har bytt skepnad flera gån: The place names around here have changed several times. Until 2010, Statistics Sweden used the name Bårhult for the houses at Röset and Pusta, on the north shore of Lake Landvettersjön. And Landvetters-Kärret only got the “Landvetter” part of its name to avoid confusion with another Kärret in the same municipality. Today both areas are counted as part of Landvetter.
Ovanför Vårberg reser sig Vårbergstoppen: Rising above Vårberg is Vårbergstoppen, known locally as Tippen, ‘the Tip’ – a man-made hill built up between 1965 and 1982 that reaches 90 metres above sea level. Don't mix it up with its neighbour Vikingaberget: at just over 77 metres, that's Stockholm's highest natural point! Close by is the Kummelholmen art gallery, named after the building's land registry name.
Ovanför gatan reser sig Stadshagsberget,: Above the street rises Stadshagsberget, the highest natural point on Kungsholmen at 52 metres above sea level. From the top you can see Karlberg Palace, home to the Karlberg Military Academy – the oldest military academy in the world still in its original location and building. Across Lake Karlbergssjön, Rörstrand porcelain was once made. The brand dates from 1726 and is the second-oldest porcelain brand in Europe, after Meissen.
Ovanför oss reser sig Ramberget med Keil: Above us rises Ramberget hill and Keillers park. From the top you get one of the best views over Gothenburg and the river. It's a steep but short climb.
Ovanpå Guldhedens vattentorn, med sina v: On top of the Guldheden water tower, with its arches and yellow brick, there was once a café for 40 guests, which opened in 1953. Since 2020 the tower has been a protected site, closed to the public. A little further away stands Hästen, 'the Horse', a two-metre teak horse by Ivar Lindekrantz from 1956, put together using boatbuilding techniques – rather like a barrel.
Paddan, båttur på kanalerna: Paddan boat tour on the canals
Park-Bio i Örby Folkets hus invigdes 192: Park-Bio, the cinema in Örby's Folkets hus community hall, opened in 1928 and showed films until 1968 – and since 2021 the building has been screening films again. Nearby is Park Studios, where Ace of Base, Stina Nordenstam and Dan Hylander were among those who recorded in the 1990s; the band Kent owned it from 2004 to 2016. And Örby Castle? Since the 1970s it has been leased to the Embassy of Vietnam.
Parken här är kärnan i det som en gång v: This park is the heart of what was once Långbro Hospital, a psychiatric hospital built between 1905 and 1910 to designs by Gustaf Wickman, which closed in 1997. Two of its distinctive buildings, Stora Mans and Stora Kvinns – the large men's and women's wards – still stand in the park. And the old chief physician's residence? That's now Långbro värdshus, an inn.
Partille kan verka som en ren förort, me: Partille might look like just another suburb, but a remarkable 60 per cent of the municipality is protected nature. It's small in size but medium-sized in population, and its main town merged with Gothenburg long ago. The municipality has four parts: Partille, Sävedalen, Öjersjö and Jonsered.
Patent- och registreringsverkets hus: The Swedish Patent and Registration Office building
Pendeltågen stannar vid Huddinge centrum: Commuter trains stop at Huddinge centrum, the municipality's heart and main shopping area. Kommunalvägen runs almost parallel to the Western Main Line tracks for about 1.3 kilometres, and along it you'll find both Huddinge Church and the municipal hall. Nearby are traces of Svartlösa domsaga, a former court district. Its courthouse was designed in 1959 by the architect Karl Karlström, yet the district itself lasted just twelve years before it was abolished in the court reform of 1971.
Per Anders Fogelström skildrade det gaml: The author Per Anders Fogelström wrote about Barnängen, the old factory district on Hammarby sjö, in his novel Vävarnas barn – “Children of the Weavers” – and this is also where the Hammarby IF sports club has its roots. Barnängsparken runs down to the waterfront, with lawns and a ferry jetty looking across to Hammarby sjöstad. A little further on is the Toy Museum, with collections ranging from 19th-century dolls to Lego, Barbie and Star Wars.
Peter Celsing ritade Filmhuset åt Svensk: Filmhuset, the Film House, was designed by Peter Celsing for the Swedish Film Institute and opened in 1971. The institute, which among other things hands out the Guldbagge awards, Sweden's national film prizes, is run from here. Just up the hill on Hakberget stands the 1986 sculpture Protest: three blocks of red granite, the middle one shaped like a clenched fist. From 1890 to 1965 this was where the labour movement's May Day marches ended. And right next to it is a military heliport with no special facilities at all.
Pilgrimskapellet är ett träkapell helt u: Pilgrimskapellet, the Pilgrim Chapel, is a wooden chapel with no religious symbols whatsoever, consecrated in 1977 by Bishop Ingmar Ström. The chapel and the cemetery around it were both designed by the landscape architect Per Friberg, and together they form Järfälla's entire burial ground. Graves lie both out in open fields and in the forest, and a 300-metre watercourse with eleven little waterfalls runs down to a large reflecting pool.
Pixbo ligger vid Rådasjön, en sjö som är: Pixbo lies on Rådasjön, a lake 23 metres deep that also supplies drinking water to Mölndal municipality. The Mölndalsån river flows through the lake and, further downstream, changes its name to Gullbergsån. Pixbo itself is built on and around the Björnåsen hill, so there are plenty of slopes to climb.
Pixbo är ett bostadsområde där man får g: Pixbo is a neighbourhood where you get fit for free: it's built on and around the Björnåsen ridge, and it's very hilly. It lies on the south side of Lake Rådasjön and has its own postal town. Little Lake Vällsjön forms its south-eastern edge, and the Vällbäcken stream runs along the east.
Platsen bär namnet Wieselgren, och enlig: The square bears the name Wieselgren, and according to Gothenburg City Museum it honours Peter Wieselgren and his son Sigfrid. Peter became Dean of Gothenburg and is seen as a pioneer of the Swedish temperance movement. His followers promised to give up brännvin, Swedish schnapps – though beer and wine were still allowed. The square lies in Rambergsstaden, at the foot of the Ramberget hill.
Platsen har fått namn efter Frantz Zinck: This area is named after Frantz Zinck, who lived on the farm for just five years in the 17th century and never even officially owned it. Yet his name lives on. The neighbourhood has a place in food history too: Gässlingen, at Brännkyrkagatan 93, won a Michelin star in 1999. And the Samariten children's hospital was extended with money left in the will of the singer Jenny Lind.
Polhemsplatsen fick 1883 sitt namn efter: Polhemsplatsen was named in 1883 after the inventor Christopher Polhem. This is where you'll find the GP building, which the newspaper Göteborgs-Posten moved into in 1935 and which is still the main building of the Stampen media group. A stone's throw away is a statue of Gunnar Gren – one third of the famous Gre-No-Li trio, and one of Gothenburg's most successful footballers of the 20th century.
Precis här intill, vid Stensjön, låg Mus: Right here by Lake Stensjön, Mustad's margarine factory was in business from 1897 to 1960. Not far away is Kristinedal, a small-house area completed in 1964, with about a hundred villas, terraced houses and linked houses. It was built by Skånska Cementgjuteriet to designs from Malmö, following the ideal of the day: single-storey houses with brick façades.
Precis intill doftar det jul året om. Gö: Right next door, it smells of Christmas all year round. Göteborgs pepparkaksbageri, the Gothenburg gingerbread bakery, opened in 1924, and these days it bakes just one thing: gingerbread biscuits with a hint of citrus, made to a secret recipe. The shop on Sankt Sigfridsgatan still has its original 1940 interior, and the bakery has been awarded a diploma by the Swedish Gastronomic Academy for its unbeatable gingerbread.
Precis intill ligger Skändla sörgård, en: Right next door is Skändla sörgård, a typical Hisingen farm from the early 1800s and one of the best-preserved farmsteads in the Gothenburg area.
