The City of Gothenburg bought it in 1966 to save it, and today it's a listed building rented by the Tuve local history society. A little further away rises Skändla rös, a Bronze Age cairn.
Precis intill står Villa Brevik, byggd 1: Right next to us is Villa Brevik, designed by Jacob Gate and built in 1920 for the district judge Franz Stolt. For many years the housing cooperative HSB ran its staff training courses here, and the facade is protected so that it can't be altered. A short way off is Abeniuska villan from 1910, designed by Ferdinand Boberg and Bror Almquist and classed as being of irreplaceable historical value.
Precis vid korsningen mellan Vårby allé: Right where Vårby allé crosses Mogårdsvägen stood Vårby grindstuga, the gatekeeper's cottage – a croft belonging to the Vårby gård estate from 1689. At first it was home to craftsmen, and the last crofters were Johannes Larsson and his wife Eva Charlotta. The cottage was pulled down around 1970. A little further on, a milestone marks the spot where Vårby School stood from 1901 to 1942.
Prins Bertil invigde Skärholmens centrum: Prince Bertil opened Skärholmen Centre on 8 September 1968. It was planned as a regional shopping centre serving 250,000 people across southern Greater Stockholm and is still one of the largest shopping centres in Sweden. It was built during the Million Programme, Sweden's huge housing drive, and is listed in the SOS Brutalism database of brutalist concrete architecture.

Pucken är i centrum här: på Björkängens: Here it's all about the puck. Björkängen sports ground has a football pitch and two ice rinks, and Björkängshallen is the home rink of the ice hockey club Huddinge IK. The second rink used to be called Nickehallen, after one of the club's key figures, Bengt 'Nicke' Nilsson. Further on is Kvarnberget, where Stuvsta gård's windmill once stood.
På 1880-talet skulle här byggas en roman: Back in the 1880s, this was meant to become a romantic villa suburb, Hornsbergs villastad. The project was a complete flop – the company didn't manage to sell a single plot. All that's left of the dream are a few block names and Nelly Sachs park, which used to be called Hornsbergsparken. Instead, the skyline is now dominated by Lindhagsskrapan, a 24-storey, 78-metre tower by Lake Ulvsundasjön. And nearby Hornsbergs hage, a stretch of open meadow, was once where the workers of Kungsholmen used to gather.
På 1930-talet var Långbrodalsvägen centr: In the 1930s, Långbrodalsvägen was the high street of what was then the district of Långbrodal, buzzing with shops and businesses. When the big shopping area at Kungens kurva opened, the crowds moved there instead. Right next door is Linboda, one of the earliest self-build housing areas in Långbro, where the hundred plots were once simply numbered from one to a hundred. Fewer than twenty of the original houses are still standing today.
På Björkängens idrottsplats, en kort pro: At the Björkängen sports ground, a short walk away, the ice hockey team Huddinge IK plays in Björkängshallen. One of the rinks used to be called Nickehallen, after the club's strongman Bengt 'Nicke' Nilsson. In the other direction, the Stuvsta estate's windmill once stood on Kvarnberget, Mill Hill – which is how the Kvarnbergsplan area got its name.
På Byfogdegatan 3 ligger Nostalgicum, et: At Byfogdegatan 3 you'll find Nostalgicum, a museum about the 1950s and 60s that opened in 2009. Its exhibition covers both everyday life and the big events of the era. At home, modern housing was going up, and industry was running at full tilt and needed workers from abroad. Out in the world, the civil rights movement was growing in the USA, the Berlin Wall went up and Hungary rose in revolt.
På Hallunda tunnelbanestation, några min: At Hallunda metro station, a few minutes from here, a neon loop and Plexiglas rods glow in the dark – a 1993 work by the artist Kazuko Tamura. In the other direction, on Sankt Botvids väg, stands Botkyrka's oldest school building, the church school from 1849, still in use as an annexe to Botkyrka Free School. It's part of the old church village that was once the heart of Botkyrka parish.
På Kaggeledstorget en bit härifrån står: On Kaggeledstorget, a little way from here, stands Våren, 'Spring', a bronze by Eric Grate from 1944 showing a naked woman on a granite plinth. It was installed in 1950, bought together with its sister statue Sommaren, 'Summer'. Another copy stands in Museiparken in Alingsås. The square got its name in 1946, probably after the governor Nils Kagg.
På Kikås, den höga åsen vid Stensjöns sö: On Kikås, the high ridge on the southern shore of Lake Stensjön, stands Sweden's biggest free-standing insect hotel. Not far from here is Lake Södra Långevattnet, a full 13.5 metres deep and ringed by wooded ridges. The lake has been stocked with fish, and its water flows on northwards towards Stensjön and the Mölndalsån river.
På Krällingegränd 3 ligger Järvabadet, e: At Krällingegränd 3 is Järvabadet, an outdoor pool that opened on 12 June 2020 and the following year made the shortlist for Stockholm Building of the Year. Right next door is Eggeby gård, a farm where people have lived and worked the land since the Viking Age. The Eggeby Stone, runestone U 69, also stands at the farm, and today Järva Folkets Park runs cultural activities here.
På Måndalshöjden en bit härifrån ligger: Up on Måndalshöjden, not far from here, is Måndalsfortet, a fort begun in 1903. It was part of the Southern Front, which together with the Northern Front – nicknamed the Sausage Line – formed a key part of Stockholm's fixed defences until 1952. It's one of the best preserved of the forts. Closer to the stop is Trollbäckens IP, a sports ground with an ice rink, an athletics track and three football pitches.
På Narvavägen 7, runt hörnet, låg först: Round the corner at Narvavägen 7 there was first the Narva cinema and then a theatre with an unlikely pair of owners: the actor Sture Lagerwall and the businessman Oscar Lindgren, who was also Haiti's consul general. They renamed it Alléteatern and put on light comedies there from 1951 to 1957. And several generations of the von Platen family lived in the building at Strandvägen 45.
På Nyängsvägen 155 bodde makarna Alva oc: Alva and Gunnar Myrdal lived at Nyängsvägen 155, in a villa Sven Markelius designed in 1937 in his trademark functionalist style. The neighbourhood has a more down-to-earth side, too: the Stora Mossen allotments were first laid out during the First World War, so that people could grow their own root vegetables through the hard war years.
På Ringön en bit härifrån ligger Vagnhal: On Ringön, a short way from here, is Vagnhallen Ringön, where Gothenburg's trams go to sleep. The first phase, with covered parking, opened at the turn of May and June 2020. There's room for about 30 trams today, and once the depot is extended it will hold about 70 more. Nearby is Hjalmar Brantingsplatsen, the main public transport hub for south-eastern Hisingen.
På Råsundavägen 45 låg en gång biografen: Råsundavägen 45 was once home to a cinema called the Savoy. In 1974 the auditorium became the Marcus Music recording studio – according to Studio Sound magazine, the first in Sweden with a 24-track tape recorder. Abba recorded most of The Album here in 1977. Today it's called Soundtrade Studios, and artists such as Robyn and Joey Tempest have recorded here over the years.
På Sandhamnsgatan står ett kontorshus fr: On Sandhamnsgatan stands a 1961 office building that was once Preem's headquarters. Between 2009 and 2011 it was turned into flats – and gained a row of terraced houses on its roof. Further on is 79&Park, designed by the Danish firm Bjarke Ingels Group, and Kampementsbadet, a municipal outdoor pool. The pool opened in 1962, and its low entrance building was designed by the city's head gardener, Holger Blom.
På Sundby gård en bit härifrån finns Lit: At Sundby gård, a farm a little way from here, you'll find the Lithographic Museum – the only one of its kind in Sweden, devoted entirely to the art of printing from stone. Just south of the farm, by the southern bay of Lake Orlången, is Sundbyfortet, also known as Örnnästet, the Eagle's Nest. The fort was part of Södra fronten, the Southern Front, a line of defences built around the time of the First World War to protect Stockholm from attack from the south.
På Surbrunnsgatan ligger Norra Brunn, so: On Surbrunnsgatan is Norra Brunn, which opened as an inn in 1903 and is now a stand-up comedy club. Over the 20th century it went by several names, including Zum Alten Brunnen and Old Bowler. On the corner of Birger Jarlsgatan and Odengatan stands Sankt Georgios katedral, St George's Cathedral, built for the Catholic Apostolic Church and now Greek Orthodox. And the inn Clas på Hörnet goes back to the 1700s.
På Teknologgatan en bit härifrån låg Thö: On Teknologgatan, not far from here, was Thörnströms Kök, run by Anne and Håkan Thörnström from 1997. From 2011 until it closed in 2021, it held a star in the Michelin Guide. Underground, the trams climb through the Chalmers tunnel, 1,050 metres long with a gradient of 24 per mille.
På Torshamnsgatan 21–23 ligger Isafjord: At Torshamnsgatan 21–23 is Isafjord 1, the block that houses Ericsson's headquarters. The office complex, designed by Wingårdh Architects, was nominated for Stockholm Building of the Year 2013. A stone's throw away is Kistamässan, the Kista exhibition centre, which opened in September 2008 and was built together with the hotel skyscraper Victoria Tower.
På Tunberget en bit bort står Tunbergsre: On Tunberget hill, not far away, stands the Tunberg reservoir, a water tower completed in 1973 that holds 25,000 cubic metres of drinking water. Closer by is the Häggvik tunnel, opened in 1998 and the shortest of the three tunnels on the Norrortsleden road. It's just 289 metres long, and there's a park on its roof.
På Vasagatan 7 låg krogen Tre Remmare, m: Vasagatan 7 was once home to Tre Remmare, a restaurant with a casino and nightclub on the same premises. It was one of the few places in Stockholm allowed to stay open until five in the morning, and it became notorious for drunkenness and drugs. It lost its licence and closed in 2007, and the Bishops Arms pub has been there since. Across the street stands the World Trade Center, designed by Ralph Erskine.
På en 45 meter hög bergknalle, en kort p: On a rocky knoll 45 metres high, a short walk from here, stood Skärholmen's hillfort, dating from the Migration Period and the Viking Age. It was a strategic spot, close to the ancient shipping route to Helgö and Birka. The rock falls steeply towards Lake Mälaren, and on the gentler inland side you can still see the remains of a wall made of huge boulders piled one on top of another.
På en av Äppelvikens högsta punkter, ett: On one of the highest points in Äppelviken, close by, Västerled Church looks out over villas from the 1920s and 1930s. Stora mossen is part of the Old Bromma garden city, and almost two thirds of its homes are villas. Nearby Bromma Upper Secondary School is a World Heritage school, working with its nearest World Heritage Site, Drottningholm Palace.
På en berghäll i Skylsta, en bit härifrå: On a slab of rock at Skylsta, not far from here, is a Viking Age runic inscription, 1.7 metres long and 0.85 metres wide, with runes six centimetres high. According to Richard Dybeck, there was also a fragment of a runestone on the same hill, but no one has ever found it again. A little runic mystery at the edge of the forest.
På en berghäll vid Drottningholmsvägen f: On a rock slab beside Drottningholmsvägen are two rune carvings from the 11th century. They were found by chance in 1904 by someone out picking berries. For centuries they'd lain under soil and moss, which is why they're still in such good condition. One of them tells us that Sigvid and Sigrev had the stone carved in memory of their father, Sinar.
På en höjd med utsikt över Säveåns dalgå: On a hill above the Säveån river valley stands Partille herrgård, Partille Manor, known locally as ‘the Castle’. It's a short way from here, about 200 metres west of Partille Church, and you get there via Carl Wilhelm Carlbergs Allé. The manor has been a listed building since December 1995.
På en kulle alldeles intill står Burås k: On a hill right next to us stands Burås kvarn, a three-storey windmill built in 1892–1893 by the master builder Emanuel Andréasson. The wind has been hard at work here for a long time – there have been windmills on this spot since the 18th century. Listed since 2004, the mill is a landmark in south-western Kungälv municipality.
På en liten kulle i kvarteret Grimhild s: On a little hill in the Grimhild block stands the Ekeby water tower, designed by Axel Bergman and built in 1908. Its tank was drained in 1965, and since 1995 the tower has been a private home – quite an unusual address. Below it is Lake Ekebysjön, just three metres deep, in the middle of a nature reserve with wooded meadows and black alder swamp forest.
På en numera skogbeväxt kulle, kallad Kv: On a hill now covered in trees, known as Kvarnbacken – Mill Hill – there once stood two windmills with wonderful names: Stora Stampan, the Big Stamp, and Holländskan, the Dutch Lady. Together they were known as the Rinkeby mills, after the village of Rinkeby in Spånga parish, on whose land they stood. Only the western one, Stora Stampan, is still standing today, just a couple of minutes' walk from here.
På en trädbevuxen kulle söder om Ekerövä: On a wooded hill south of Ekerövägen is the Wallenberg family's resting place. Their mausoleum has become a landmark for the whole area. Lindö, incidentally, was once an island of its own, but as the land has risen it has grown and joined up with Lovön. At Tappström, bricks were fired at the Tappsund brickworks right up until 1959.
På ett hustak i Råcksta centrum lyser en: On a rooftop in Råcksta centre glows a neon sign from the 1950s, with RÅCKSTA in green and a jaunty 'Centrum' in yellow. It was restored in 2011 and shines as brightly as ever. The nearby metro depot was originally called Spångahallen, because Vällingby belonged to Spånga municipality, which had joined Stockholm only a few years earlier. And Råcksta cemetery has around 30,000 urn graves.
På höjden alldeles i närheten fanns unde: On the hill just nearby, during Sweden's wartime state of readiness from 1939 to 1945, was the Skanskvarn anti-aircraft battery, complete with firing trenches, gun pits and tank traps. Its job was to protect three bridges – Skansbron, Skanstullsbron and the vital Årstabron railway bridge – and if the defences had given way, the plan was to blow up Årstabron before the enemy could use it. Below the hill is an allotment garden that dates all the way back to 1917, when it was set up as Koloniföreningen Stugan.
På nordöstra Lidingö, norr om Hustegafjä: On north-eastern Lidingö, north of the Hustegafjärden bay, is the little village of Furutorp. Nearby you'll find Långnäs gård, a privately owned farm that grew out of a larger farmstead from the mid-14th century, and the Sjövik housing area, on a strip of shoreline along Kyrkviken bay that was left out of the Långängen-Elfvik nature reserve.
På slottsområdet står en stuga som har v: In the palace grounds stands a cottage that has been to a World's Fair! The Ornäs cottage is a slightly smaller copy of the original in Ornäs in Dalarna. It was shown at the 1867 World's Fair in Paris and has stood here since 1869. The neighbourhood also has villas with funny names, such as Villa Snörin – pronounced 'snör-in'.
På torget står Vesslan, en fontänskulptu: On the square stands Vesslan, the Weasel, a fountain sculpture by Otto Strandman from 1912. A naked young man in bronze has just spotted a weasel, which is hiding in a little cave at the very bottom of the sculpture, and there's a drinking fountain on either side. Round the corner, at Scheelegatan 8, was the restaurant L'Escargot – in 1984 it became one of the first four restaurants in Sweden to win a Michelin star.
På tunnelbanestationen står ett exemplar: In the metro station you'll find a copy of Carl Fredrik Reuterswärd's sculpture The Knotted Gun – the best-known version stands outside the UN headquarters in New York. A couple of hundred metres away is Fittja gård, an old farm whose inn was one of Sweden's biggest coaching inns in the 1600s and 1700s. One of its buildings served as the district courthouse right up until 1916. Today the farm is home to Mångkulturellt centrum, the Multicultural Centre.
Radhus och villor präglar Kälvesta, en s: Kälvesta, a district of terraced houses and villas, sits in the north-western corner of Hässelby-Vällingby, a bit like a border guard. To the north is Skälby in Järfälla municipality, to the west Hässelby Villastad, and to the south-west Vinsta. Vinsta, incidentally, takes its name from an old village and only became a district in 1953.
Radhusbyn Atlantisområdet byggdes 1952–1: The terraced houses of the Atlantis area were built between 1952 and 1955 to designs by Bertil Karlén, Jon Höjer and Sture Ljungqvist, and they attracted attention from abroad. From 1968 to 1983, one of them was home to Lisbeth and Olof Palme – the future prime minister – and their three sons. Today the City Museum has given the houses its highest heritage rating for their exceptional historical value.
Radhusen i kvarteret Tegen: The terraced houses in the Tegen block
Radhusområdet Hersby Åker byggdes 1949–1: The terraced-house area of Hersby Åker was built in 1949–1955 to designs by Holger Blom: thirteen rows of terraced houses with 115 homes in all, a fine example of the architecture of the Swedish folkhem, the post-war 'people's home' welfare state. Nearby, on a small hill, stands the Hersby farm storehouse, a listed building that once belonged to Hersby gård, one of Lidingö's traditional main farms.
Radiotorget i närheten var något helt ny: Radiotorget, nearby, was something completely new when it opened in 1954. It was a “satellite square” – a shopping square outside the city centre, on the American model – the first of its kind in Sweden and one of the first in Europe. It was spruced up in 2019–20 and still has several small shops.
Radiotorget, några hundra meter bort, in: Radiotorget, a few hundred metres away, opened in 1954 as Sweden's first satellite town square – a shopping centre on the American model. Further on is the Högsbo pegmatite quarry, where feldspar, quartz, mica and beryl were mined from 1945 until the late 1950s. Rare minerals such as monazite and bismuthinite have also turned up there.
Rakt fram ligger Gröna Lund, Sveriges äl: Straight ahead is Gröna Lund, Sweden's oldest amusement park.
Rakt fram ligger Skansen Lejonet, en för: Straight ahead is Skansen Lejonet, the Lion Fort – a 17th-century stronghold topped with a gilded lion.
Rakt fram ser du den röd-vita skyskrapan: Straight ahead is the red-and-white skyscraper that Gothenburgers call the Lipstick.
Rakt under Östasiatiska museet finns ett: Right beneath the Museum of Far Eastern Antiquities is a rock shelter, blasted out in the early 1940s for the naval commander and his staff to use in wartime. Today it's home to Stockholm Toy Museum, full of toys and comics. Next to it is Högvakten, the Main Guard building from 1777, and the former Skeppsholmen Church, now the Eric Ericsonhallen concert hall, with a seven-metre tapestry called Havets sång, Song of the Sea.
Rannebergen Centrum byggdes 1974 och har: Rannebergen Centrum was built in 1974 and has its own swimming pool, and across the street the Bohusleden trail and the Vättlefjäll hills are waiting, with lovely lakes for swimming and fishing. Nearby is the start of the Lärjeån valley nature reserve, protected in 2026 and covering more than 1,100 hectares.
Rannebergen ligger högt och nära naturen: Rannebergen sits high up, close to nature. Just a few minutes away is Idtjärnet, a forest lake 109 metres above sea level, and a little further on is Lake Stora Mölnesjön, with a swimming spot and a jetty. The centre itself, with a swimming pool and a pizzeria, was built in 1974, and the Bohusleden trail and the Vättlefjäll hills are right on its doorstep.
Redan innan Stadion fanns idrottade stoc: Stockholmers were playing sport here long before the Olympic Stadium was built. Stockholms idrottspark opened in 1896 as the city's first civilian sports ground. It had a 400-metre concrete track for cycling and running and was demolished in 1910. Along Valhallavägen, in the Villastaden area, stand 1880s houses that carry the City Museum's highest heritage rating.
Redaren Jacob Gustaf Setterwall gjorde s: The shipowner Jacob Gustaf Setterwall did very well for himself, and in 1896 he built a grand villa in Finntorp that is now one of the oldest buildings in Nacka. A little further off, by the bay of Svindersviken, is Svindersvik, a mid-18th-century summer residence designed by Carl Hårleman for the merchant Claes Grill. It's considered one of the best-preserved Rococo estates in Sweden – partly because nobody has ever lived there all year round.
Redaren Jacob Gustaf Setterwall köpte 18: In 1871 the shipowner Jacob Gustaf Setterwall bought the land between the Kyrkviken and Svindersviken bays, and his first summer home was a small wooden villa in Swiss chalet style. Then the shipping line took off and things got grander: in 1896 the lavish Setterwall villa, designed by Johan Laurentz, was completed. On the Nysätra headland a little further on stood the Nackanäs inn, which welcomed guests right up until it burned down in 1960.
Redbergsplatsen hette förr Korsvägen och: Redbergsplatsen square was once called Korsvägen, 'the crossroads', and got its current name in 1883. In 1873 a public water pump was put up here, so that people could enjoy water from Lake Delsjön. Just north of the square, in Redbergslids Folkpark – a 'people's park' for popular entertainment – a pavilion with a stage for performers went up in 1886. And below Sankt Pauli kyrka, St Paul's Church, look out for the bronze fountain group Elementens kamp, the Struggle of the Elements, which was moved here from Olskrokstorget in 1968.
Reenstiernska palatset, även kallat Momm: The Reenstierna Palace, also known as Mommas hus, was built in the 1660s and still looks much as it did then. It's a fine example of the influence Dutch immigrants had on Stockholm's architecture. Right next door stood Södra barnbördshuset, the city's maternity hospital, and Maria Hospital, which opened in 1876. The hospital started out with 125 beds in an old 18th-century factory building, which has since been converted into flats and a nursery school.
Riddarfjärden är Mälarens östligaste fjä: Riddarfjärden is the easternmost bay of Lake Mälaren, and the border between the provinces of Uppland and Södermanland actually runs right through the middle span of Västerbron bridge. On the Kungsholmen shore, Mälarbadet opened in 1906. At the time it was the biggest and most exclusive indoor bathhouse in Scandinavia, with pools beneath large skylights. Street names around here remember the tanners who once worked in the area – Garvar Lundins gränd, for example, is named after the tannery owner Anders Wilhelm Lundin.
Riddarholmen och utsikten över Riddarfjä: Riddarholmen and the view over Riddarfjärden
Rinkeby i Danderyd ska inte förväxlas me: Rinkeby in Danderyd shouldn't be confused with the Rinkeby district in northern Stockholm – this one is an old farm and a housing area. A fragment of a Viking Age runestone, U 132, was once found here, but it vanished without trace in the second half of the 1800s. Nobody knows where it went.
Rinkeby är äldre än många tror. Byn omta: Rinkeby is older than many people think. The village is mentioned as early as 1347, when it was made up of several farms. Modern Rinkeby was built from 1968 onwards as part of the Million Programme, Sweden's huge housing drive of the 1960s and 70s. Rinkebytorget, the square, now has a small shopping centre and Folkets hus, the community centre, and it's a good place to pick up fruit and veg.
Rissne är den enda tunnelbanestationen i: Rissne is the only metro station in Stockholm with its name carved in runes. The name also appears on a runestone in Sigtuna, raised in memory of 'Gunnar's son in Risnö'. In 1640 Rissne gård was bought by Reinhold Goevert Leuhusen, secretary of the Admiralty board. Today the old farm is a restaurant and conference venue.
Ritorp anlades redan på 1600-talet som e: Ritorp goes back to the 1600s, when it was a croft belonging to the village of Nederjärva, just south of the country road to Enköping. Today's farmhouse dates from the 1770s. It's a private home, but Stockholm County Museum calls it irreplaceable. Two thousand years ago this spot was under water: the bay of Fröfjärden linked the Baltic waters of Saltsjön with Lake Mälaren, and the shoreline of Brunnsviken was about ten metres higher than it is today.
Ritorp började som ett torp på 1600-tale: Ritorp started out as a croft in the 17th century, and the current farmhouse from the 1770s is described by Stockholm County Museum as irreplaceable. The buildings around it have charming nicknames: the Tower Villa from 1903, the Majhill house from 1911 and the Horseshoe Stable from 1929, which was moved in 1993. And in the northern part, look out for the houses known as Rödingarna, 'the Red Ones'.
Roslags Näsby är Roslagsbanans stora väg: Roslags Näsby is the main junction on the Roslagsbanan railway, where the line splits towards Kårsta – formerly Rimbo – and towards Österskär. The station has two island platforms, reached by a footbridge over the tracks. Not far away is Kvarntorpshällen, a rock with a runic inscription discovered in 1943 by the writer Jan Fridegård while he was living in Täby. It contains an unusual word: styvsöner, stepsons.
Roslagsbanan nådde Lahäll 1928, när linj: Roslagsbanan, the Roslagen railway, reached Lahäll in 1928 with the opening of the line from Altorp, and in 1937 it was extended to Näsbypark. Further on, by Näsbyviken bay, is Näsby Castle, today a conference hotel with a restaurant. And to the south, in Djursholm, lies the Svalnäs burial ground, with graves from around 500 to 1000 AD – one of the largest and most impressive in Danderyd.
Roslagsbanan nådde hit 1937, när Stockho: The Roslagsbanan railway arrived in 1937, when the Stockholm–Roslagens Järnvägar company extended the line from Lahäll, and this is where that branch ends. Näsbypark is known as one of Täby's more exclusive neighbourhoods, with villas and terraced houses close to the water at Stora Värtan bay. Right next to the station is Näsbypark Church, part of Täby parish.
Rudboda har fått sitt namn efter Rudboda: Rudboda takes its name from Rudboda gård, a farm first mentioned in writing in 1381. The area includes the Lojo block, built in 1970–1973 as part of the Million Programme, Sweden's great housing drive – though the municipality describes it as a smaller-scale, higher-quality version. Out on Bosön there's a student campus from 1998–1999, built to show what the Olympic Village might have looked like had Stockholm won its bid for the 2004 Summer Games. It didn't.

Rudboda is named after Rudboda farm, mentioned in writing as early as 1381. The Lojo block was built between 1970 and 1973 during the Million Programme, Sweden's big housing drive, and the municipality calls it an excellent example of the programme's ideas applied on a smaller scale. On Bosön, student flats were built to show what an Olympic village might look like – ahead of the 2004 Summer Games, which Stockholm never got.
Runhällarna U 80 och U 81: The rune-carved rock slabs U 80 and U 81
Runstenen U 88 i Skälby, en bit härifrån: Runestone U 88 in Skälby, not far from here, has had an eventful life. For at least part of the 19th century it served as a doorstep in Lindal, so people walked over the Vikings' words every day. Then it disappeared for a while, until it was found in 1938 at Skälby Farm, lying on a burial mound. Today it stands beside its companion, U 89.
Runstenen vid slottets infart: The runestone at the palace entrance
Runt 14 000 studenter läser vid Södertör: Around 14,000 students attend Södertörn University, which offers police training and teacher training with an intercultural focus, among other things. Much of the research here is about the Baltic Sea and Eastern Europe, backed by Östersjöstiftelsen, the Foundation for Baltic and East European Studies, which the government set up in 1994. The library is open to everyone, and right next to it is Flemingsberg Park, winner of Huddinge's building award in 2021.
Runt Järfälla kyrka har runstenar kommit: Runestones have a habit of coming and going around Järfälla Church. In 1728 Olof Celsius the Elder found one inside the church, probably used as a step. It then vanished until seven fragments turned up in 1939. Another stone lay outside the porch door and was already described back then as lost and worn – it's still missing today. Next door is Kyrkbyn, the church village, once known as Järfälla gård.
Runt Rådasjön breder ett naturreservat u: A nature reserve surrounds Lake Rådasjön, with pastures, broadleaf woodland and alder swamp forest teeming with wildlife. The area around Mölnlycke is famous for its masses of wood anemones, which turn the ground white in spring. Also by the lake is Råda säteri, a manor with wings and farm buildings, listed since 1969.
Runt hörnet ligger kvarteren Kampö och H: Around the corner are the Kampö and Hartsö blocks, terraced houses from the late 1950s that the City Museum has marked green as especially valuable. A short way off rise the offices of Televerket, the old national telecoms agency – the headquarters of Telia Company until 2016. They were designed by Bengt Hidemark and Gösta Danielson, and the buildings on Mårbackagatan won the Kasper Salin Prize, Sweden's top architecture award.
Rymdtorget byggdes 1970 och är hjärtat i: Rymdtorget, Space Square, was built in 1970 and is the heart of Bergsjön, where the streets are named after space and the universe – Tellusgatan, for instance. On the square is Kulturhuset Bergsjön, the Bergsjön Culture House, with a library, café, studios, an exhibition hall and even a music studio. It offers everything from music and art to crafts and children's events.
Rymdtorget byggdes 1970, och gatunamnen: Rymdtorget, Space Square, was built in 1970, and the streets around it keep up the space theme, with names such as Tellusgatan and Merkuriusgatan. On the square is the Bergsjön Culture House, with a library, a music studio, artists' studios and an exhibition hall, offering a mix of concerts, crafts and activities for children.
Rymdtorget, Kometgatan, Kosmosgatan, Uni: Rymdtorget, Kometgatan, Kosmosgatan, Universumsgatan, Meteorgatan – Space Square, Comet Street, Cosmos Street, Universe Street and Meteor Street. Here in Bergsjön, the street names are straight out of outer space. Just up the road is Rymdtorget, built in 1970, home to Kulturhuset Bergsjön, the local cultural centre. It has a library, café, studios, a music studio and an exhibition hall, with everything from music and art to events for children.
Rådsparken, alldeles i närheten, har båd: Just nearby is Rådsparken, a park with both an animal park and a sports ground, next to Huddinge Church, which has been the parish church since the Middle Ages. A fragment of a runestone is set into the church's outer wall, and just east of the church lay the assembly site of Tomtabergh, mentioned as early as 1433. The church school close by opened in 1914 and was threatened with demolition in the 1950s, but it survived – today the parish choirs rehearse there.
Rågsved är en stadsdel med två ansikten,: Rågsved is a district with two faces, split down the middle by the metro. On one side is the iconic horseshoe-shaped shopping centre; on the other, the buildings climb up a hill. The station opened in 1959 and is about 8.5 kilometres from Slussen.
Rågsved är känt för sin ikoniska hästsko: Rågsved is known for its iconic horseshoe-shaped shopping centre, and the metro station was the end of the line when it opened in 1959. On the platform stands the bronze sculpture Fågel Grön, Green Bird, by the artist Björn Selder. A little further away in Högdalen is Cyklopen, a self-run cultural centre staffed entirely by volunteers. Its first building was destroyed in 2008 in an arson attack thought to be the work of Nazis, but the association simply built a new one.
Råsunda vattentorn, ritat av Sigge Crons: Råsunda water tower, designed by Sigge Cronstedt, opened in 1910 and was taken out of service in the early 1950s. Since 1994 it's been a home – the tower has been converted into flats. On a rocky hill by Näckrosparken, the Water Lily Park, stands Råsunda Church. And on the southern shore of Lake Råstasjön is Råstahällen, Solna's only natural monument, a slab of bedrock where you can see three criss-crossing sets of scratches left by the ice during the last Ice Age.
Röda Korsets Högskola: Röda Korsets Högskola, the Swedish Red Cross University
Röda Sten konsthall: Röda Sten konsthall, the art centre
Röda Sten konsthall under Älvsborgsbron: Röda Sten art centre, beneath the Älvsborg Bridge
Röhsska museet för design och konsthantv: Röhsska museet, the museum of design and craft
Rösjön är en avlång sjö, 7,3 meter djup,: Rösjön is a long, narrow lake, 7.3 metres deep. Most of it belongs to Sollentuna, with a smaller part in Danderyd – while Täby, right next door on the eastern side, doesn't get a single metre of shoreline. A little further on, Landsnoravägen runs for about three kilometres past Edsberg Palace and Landsnora kvarn, a mill that is Sollentuna's oldest secular building.
S:t Eriksgatan, kaféer och butiker: S:t Eriksgatan, for cafés and shops
Salems centrala bebyggelse hette förr Sa: The centre of Salem used to be known as Salemstaden. For a long time the area was crofters' land belonging to the Fågelsta farm. One of the crofts, Bergfana, was built in the late 1840s, and the first to move in were Eric Ode – a former soldier who worked on the estate – and his family. When the railway arrived in 1860, Bergfana became one of Salem's four lineman's cottages, where the people who kept watch over the track lived.
Salems kyrka står på en udde söder om Bo: Salem Church stands on a headland south of Lake Bornsjön, framed by big oaks, limes and birches. The old Södertälje road, Gamla Södertäljevägen, runs past the church, and the whole area is rich in ancient remains. Follow the road east and you'll reach Sankt Botvid's spring, a cold spring at the south-eastern tip of Bornsjön. About fifty metres from it stands the old Söderby runestone.
Saltsjö-Järla station invigdes 1894 unde: Saltsjö-Järla station opened in 1894 under the old-fashioned name Jerla, and branch lines once ran from here to a yeast factory and to De Laval's steam turbine works. Today the old industrial buildings by Lake Järlasjön have been reborn as Järla sjö, with around 700 homes, shops and restaurants, and about 1,200 people working there. In 2004 the area won the Urban Environment Council's award for improving the townscape.
The Saltsjöbanan railway station here opened in 1894. While the new Slussen was being built, Henriksdal served as the line's city-end terminus from 2016 until the end of 2022. Large parts of the line have been closed since 2023, and the stretch to Slussen isn't expected to reopen until 2028 at the earliest. Danvikstull was once home to the Klippan summer theatre, where audiences laughed along with John Elfström and Arthur Fischer.
Saltsjöbanans station invigdes 1894, då: The station on the Saltsjöbanan railway opened in 1894, when the name was spelled Jerla. Branch lines ran from here to a yeast factory and to De Laval's steam turbine works. Here's a fun fact: Anna Book was a pupil at Nacka music school when she sang “ABC” in Melodifestivalen, Sweden's Eurovision selection, in 1986. And from 2030 you'll be able to change to the blue metro line at a new station here.
Sandbäck är ingen ny plats. Redan på 155: Sandbäck is no newcomer. As early as the 1550s – more than four hundred years ago – there were two farmsteads here. Today it's in the south-western part of Östra Mölndal, and a little way off is the Pepparred nature reserve, with old pastures and broadleaf trees, protected since 1925.
Sandås ligger i Askim, och namnet Askim: Sandås is in Askim – and Askim, by the way, is actually pronounced “Ashim”. The parish dates back to the Middle Ages. To the south, Sandås borders Skintebo, a residential area by the coast that was farmland until the 1970s. It has car-free footpaths, båtmansgårdar – a sort of boatswain's cottage – and, more surprisingly, a copy of the Chinese Pavilion at Drottningholm.
Sankt Olofs kyrka, Täby: Sankt Olofs kyrka, St Olaf's Church, Täby
Sankt Olofs kyrka, en kort bit bort, hör: St Olof's Church, a short way off, belongs to Täby parish. Through neighbouring Hägernäs runs the E18 motorway, completed on the Danderyd–Ullna stretch in 1957, cutting straight through the area. A little further north is Rönninge, which has no built-up areas at all – just the Rönninge by-Skavlöten nature reserve and the Skavlöten outdoor recreation area.
Sankt Pauli kyrka: St Paul's Church, Sankt Pauli kyrka
Sankt Paulus av Korsets kyrka alldeles i: Right next door is the Church of Saint Paul of the Cross, Angered's Catholic parish church. A short walk away stands Alexander Calder's steel sculpture The Three Wings, which spent twelve years on Götaplatsen before it was finally allowed to move to Angered in 1979. Since 2013 it has stood on an open lawn in the town park.
Sankt Sigfrids kyrka: Sankt Sigfrids kyrka, St Sigfrid's Church
Sankt Sigfrids kyrka är en riktig flyttf: Sankt Sigfrids kyrka has done some travelling. The red wooden church originally stood in Vasastaden and was moved here in 1904, when it was called Sankt Stefans kapell. Designed to be portable, it looks a lot like the flat-pack timber villas of the period, and it has been a listed building since 1993. Further along Hägerstensvägen is the Aspen cinema – when it opened in 1952, it was the first privately run cinema to open in Stockholm since 1943.
Sankta Birgitta kyrka: Sankta Birgitta kyrka, St Birgitta's Church
Sankta Birgitta kyrka byggdes 1960–1962: Saint Birgitta's Church was built between 1960 and 1962 and consecrated in December 1962. The architect Rolf Bergh designed the church, its bell tower and the parish hall next door. And here in Nockeby, the architect Sven Markelius built his own villa in 1930 – one of the very first houses designed to the new ideals of functionalism.
Sankta Birgitta kyrka i Nockeby står på: Sankta Birgitta kyrka, St Birgitta's Church in Nockeby, stands where the trams used to turn round. This was the old terminus of the number 12, with its turning loop, until work on the church began in November 1960. It was consecrated on 9 December 1962. All around, Nockebyhov is lined with terraced houses from the late 1940s that the City Museum has marked blue for their exceptional cultural and historical value.
Sanna betyder ungefär sandmark. Här i nä: Sanna means something like 'sandy ground'. Close by is Plaskis – or Älvsborgsdammen, to give it its proper name. In summer, families paddle in 20 to 45 centimetres of water, and when the pond is drained, the skateboarders move in. At the edge is the sculpture Boll, 'Ball': a two-metre blue steel sphere that looks like a giant beach ball.
Sannegårdshamnen invigdes i januari 1914: Sannegårdshamnen, the Sannegården harbour, opened in January 1914, though these days the name usually means the residential area around it. Culture has moved into the old industrial buildings: Backa teater, one of Sweden's leading theatres for children and young people, performs in a converted sheet-metal workshop on Lindholmen. And a stone's throw away is Aftonstjärnan, a cinema and theatre that has been a listed building since 1995.
Scheelegatan hette förr Trädgårdsgatan,: Scheelegatan used to be called Trädgårdsgatan, but in 1885 it was renamed after the chemist Carl Wilhelm Scheele. On the corner of Fleminggatan and Pipersgatan is Separatorhuset, built around 1900 as the head office of AB Separator – later Alfa Laval – whose factory once filled the whole large site by Barnhusviken bay. The City Museum has now given the building its blue heritage rating.

Sedan 1946 har Lundbergs konditori legat: Lundbergs konditori has stood on the same corner of Gröndalsvägen since 1946, with the same name and in the same premises, making it a true fika classic – fika being Sweden's beloved coffee-and-cake break. Up on the Sannadal plateau rise the point blocks of Ljuskronan, Ljussaxen and Lyktan, built between 1958 and 1972 and now a familiar part of Gröndal's skyline. The light-themed block names – the Chandelier, the Candle Snuffer and the Lantern – suit the hilltop nicely.
Shopping i gamla flyghangarer! Köpcentre: Shopping in old aircraft hangars! The Bromma Blocks shopping centre is housed in Bromma Airport's hangars, which were the largest in northern Europe in their day. The architect Paul Hedqvist designed them in a chunky, block-like functionalist style – hence the name. And out in Bällstaviken bay is an islet that's actually a shipwreck: an old cargo ship that sank and has slowly been taken over by greenery.
Shoppingen här sker i Bromma flygplats g: The shopping here takes place in Bromma Airport's old hangars, which were once the biggest in northern Europe. In 1972 the first hypermarket moved into one of them, and in September 2010 the converted Hangar 3 opened, with around 80 shops under one roof. The name Bromma Blocks is a nod to the boxy functionalist architecture.
Shoppingsugen? Bäckebol Center rymmer et: Fancy some shopping? Bäckebol Center has around twenty shops spread over 95,000 square metres. The area has changed hands several times, and in 2008 Media Markt – later Power – opened its second Gothenburg store in Coop Bygg's old premises. A short walk away is the Lärjeån river, which gave its name to the whole Lärjedalen valley.
Sickla har länge varit en plats där bruk: Sickla has a long history of industrial workers living close to their jobs. As early as the late 1890s, homes went up in Tallbacken for workers and foremen at AB Diesels Motorer. Then, in 1947–48, the Sickla strand housing area was built for employees of Atlas Diesel – later Atlas Copco – to designs by the architects Erik and Tore Ahlsén. The name Sickla itself roughly means a low-lying spot where water wells up.
Sickla kanal skiljer Södra Hammarbyhamne: The Sickla canal divides Södra Hammarbyhamnen from Nacka. The industrial past is easy to see here: in the 1920s Atlas Diesel, later Atlas Copco, moved its entire operation to Sickla, and the company's head office is still here. The factories kept going until the late 1980s, and in 1994 the area was transformed into the Sickla shopping quarter.
Sieverts Kabelverk grundades av Max Siev: Sieverts Kabelverk, the cable works, was founded by Max Sievert in 1888 and was originally called Trådfabriken, the Wire Factory. For many years it was Sundbyberg's biggest employer. Today the Signalfabriken quarter, with homes, restaurants and hotels, has grown up among the old industrial buildings. Just nearby, Bällsta bro, the Bällsta bridge, crosses Bällstaån stream, which marks the boundary between Sundbyberg and Stockholm.
Sikreno låter italienskt, men namnet har: Sikreno sounds Italian, but the name has nothing to do with its neighbours Frescati and Albano. According to one unconfirmed theory, it's actually an anagram based on the name Erikson! This is also where you'll find the Stocksund Inn, built between 1814 and 1816 by what was once the end of the Stocksund Bridge. The inn closed in 1938, and today the building is divided into homes.
Silverdals griftegård anlades 1914 som g: Silverdal cemetery was laid out in 1914 as the burial ground for the Stockholm garrison, and Sollentuna parish took it over in 1960. A crematorium and a funeral chapel were added later. The area now called Silverdal was once home to two crofts, Rådan and Silverdal, which in time grew into farms.
Sim- och sporthallen invigdes 1973 och a: The swimming and sports centre opened in 1973, and two years later its architects, Gustaf Rosenberg and Olle Stål, won the Kasper Salin Prize, Sweden's top architecture award, for it. Just a couple of hundred metres away is Edsberg Palace from 1760, home to the Rudbeck family for almost 200 years. Up on the stable hill, until 2019, was Edsvik konsthall, an art gallery that put on twelve exhibitions a year.
Sisjöns industriområde ligger runt hörne: The Sisjön industrial area is just around the corner, directly south of the Söderleden road. It grew up as an industrial area in the 1960s but has gradually turned into a shopping area. Frölunda torg is just over two kilometres away, and Mölndal's town centre four.
Sju rader med skivhus på en höjd, det är: Seven rows of slab blocks on a hillside – that's Siriusgatan, a real landmark as you enter Bergsjön. From some of the flats you can see all the way out to the island of Vinga! It's the most populous street in Gothenburg. The façades were originally grey and yellow, but during an eco-minded renovation in 1992, the anthroposophist Fritz Fuchs gave the buildings a new palette of light, soft shades.
Själva Byälvsvägen byggdes runt 1970 och: Byälvsvägen itself dates from around 1970 and is the odd one out in Bagarmossen, otherwise a well-preserved 1950s suburb. The district won international praise for keeping pedestrians and cars strictly apart and for buildings that follow the lie of the land. A little further on, the Nacka nature reserve begins, with forest along the southern shore of Lake Sicklasjön and historic surroundings at Lilla Sickla.
Sjättenovembervägen hette tidigare Torsv: Sjättenovembervägen – Sixth of November Road – used to be called Torsvägen, and most of it follows the old Göta landsväg, the historic highway south. The long log causeway that gave Långbro its name – “long bridge” – back in the 1400s probably lay where the northern end of the street runs today. The district of Älvsjö was formed in 1932, and at the time it also took in what are now Rågsved, Solberga and Hagsätra.
Sjöberg ligger inklämt mellan tre naturo: Sjöberg is squeezed between three green areas: Edsviken, Rösjön and Rinkebyskogen. A little further away is Rösjön, a long, narrow lake 7.3 metres deep and 6.3 metres above sea level. Most of it belongs to Sollentuna and a smaller part to Danderyd – while Täby, right next door, doesn't touch its shores at all.
Sjöfartsmuseet Akvariet: Sjöfartsmuseet Akvariet, the Maritime Museum and Aquarium
Sjön Bergsjön, som gett stadsdelen sitt: Lake Bergsjön, which gave the district its name, is very close by – though it's tiny, to say the least. It covers just 0.0257 square kilometres, roughly two and a half hectares. It does sit high up, though, at 101.7 metres above sea level, and its water drains into the Göta älv river.
Sjön Grötfatet ligger bara några hundra: Lake Grötfatet – 'the porridge bowl' – is only a few hundred metres away, and the name tends to raise a smile. Fisksätra Church beside the square is a little out of the ordinary: it belongs to Nacka parish but is also used regularly by the Catholic parish of Saint Konrad, as part of the Guds hus, or God's House, project.
Sjön Trekanten hette Trehörningen fram t: Lake Trekanten was known as Trehörningen until the mid-19th century. On its north shore lay Nynäs, a ramshackle working-class suburb with a tannery, a coffee roastery, workshops and a bakery famous locally for its Nynäs loaf. Once the houses had fallen into disrepair, they became the backdrop for Bo Widerberg's 1970 film Joe Hill, standing in for the 'Lumberyard' and the 'Saloon'. The last of them were demolished in 1980.
Sjöräddningens station vid Hammarbysluss: The sea rescue station by the Hammarbyslussen lock
Sjötorp var ett torp under Balingsta går: Sjötorp was a croft belonging to Balingsta gård, on the Flemingsbergsviken inlet. Its main building was put up in 1904 by the Ersta Deaconess Society as a home for what were then called “wayward girls”. Since 1998 it has been a private house, set in the middle of the Orlången nature reserve. A couple of hundred metres away is Stensättra gård, an old manor estate in an area that was probably first settled in the Viking Age.
Skalden Carl Michael Bellman tillbringad: The poet Carl Michael Bellman spent the summer of 1773 at Fållan by Lake Magelungen, where his relatives the Zetterman family had their summer home. That's why four lime trees beside the old house foundations are known as Bellmanslindarna, the Bellman Limes. The houses themselves were pulled down around 1840. Closer to the stop is Magelungsfortet, a fort wedged between Nynäsvägen and Gamla Nynäsvägen. It's a remnant of the Southern Front, a ring of defences built to protect Stockholm around the time of the First World War.
Skandiahamnen intill är Sveriges största: Next door is Skandiahamnen, Sweden's largest container port, with 2,200 metres of quays. Huge container ships and car carriers sail from here. A little further away is Arendalsbanan, the old speedway track of the team Kaparna. Its attendance record of 5,940 was set in 2002, and the lap record belongs to none other than Tony Rickardsson, from 2004.
Skansen Kronan, utsikt över staden: Skansen Kronan fort, with views over the city
Skansen öppnade 1891 och är världens äld: Skansen opened in 1891 and is the oldest open-air museum in the world. It has old farmsteads from all over Sweden, Nordic animals and a wide view over Stockholm.
Skanstull har fått sitt namn efter Söder: Skanstull gets its name from Söder skans, a fort between Årstaviken bay and Hammarby sjö lake. It was built in 1645 and later enlarged to plans by Nicodemus Tessin the Elder, and the last traces weren't cleared away until the 1920s. These days the spot is watched over by Folksamhuset, a 27-storey tower that has been called an indispensable part of Stockholm's skyline since it went up in 1960. Down at Hammarbyslussen lock is the Swedish Sea Rescue Society's floating station, opened by Prince Carl Philip in 2019.
Skanstull har fått sitt namn efter en sk: Skanstull is named after a skans, a small fortification, and the toll gate at the city's southern entrance. From here the Skanstullsbron bridge heads south towards Johanneshov, and across the water you can see the big white dome of the Globen area. Götgatan, Södermalm's main street, starts just north of here.

Skanstull is named after a skans, a small fortification, and the tull, or toll gate, at the city's southern entrance. From here the Skanstull bridge heads south, and across the water you can see the big white dome of the Globen area.
Skarpa by nämns för första gången redan: The village of Skarpa is first mentioned as far back as 1318. The Skarpnäck manor was established in 1660 by Maria Sofia De la Gardie of Tyresö Palace, but its golden age came under the German brewer Friedrich Rudolph Neumüller, who built the main house between 1865 and 1867. In 1922 his descendants sold the farm and its land to the City of Stockholm.
Skarpa by nämns första gången redan 1318: The village of Skarpa is first mentioned as far back as 1318, and the Skarpnäck manor estate was created in 1660 by Maria Sofia De la Gardie of Tyresö Palace. The present main house was built in the 1860s by the German brewer Friedrich Rudolph Neumüller, and under his ownership the estate enjoyed its golden age. The district itself was formed in 1963 from Pungpinan and Skarpnäck. Its metro station, opened in 1994, lies in a rock cavern 25 metres underground.
Skarpnäcks tunnelbanestation, en kort pr: Skarpnäck metro station, a short walk away, became the hundredth station on the network when it opened on 15 August 1994. It sits in a rock cavern 25 metres underground, decorated by the artist Richard Nonas with 17 sculptures that look like benches. Even closer is Skarpnäcks folkhögskola, the largest folk high school in Stockholm.
Skarpnäcksfältet var förr ett flygfält,: Skarpnäcksfältet was once an airfield, and for many years it hosted the Skarpnäcksloppet motor race. The last air show took place in August 1980, and during the 1980s a new residential area grew up on the field. Today Australian rules football is played at The Jordo Cricket Ground, where the very first match, between the Södermalm Blues and the Norrtälje Dockers, took place on 6 August 2012.
Skarpäng har fått sitt namn av ett dagsv: Skarpäng takes its name from a day labourer's croft on the Ella farm, built in 1715. In the 1920s land began to be divided into plots for holiday homes, and by 1940 around 550 had been sold. Neighbouring Ella park got its name in the early 1930s, when what was then northern Ella was split up. Today it's a purely residential area of large villas.
Skeppsholmen var länge flottans ö. I dag: For a long time Skeppsholmen was the navy's island. Today it's home to Moderna museet, the Museum of Modern Art, and to the old sailing ship af Chapman, now a youth hostel. From the shore you get one of the best views across to Gamla stan, the Old Town.
Skidbacken Ekebyhovsbacken är hemmabacke: Ekebyhovsbacken is the home slope of Mälaröarnas Alpina Skidklubb, the local alpine ski club, and from the top you get a sweeping view over Ekerö and Lake Mälaren. A little further on, on Gällstaö, grows the Gällstaö oak, which may be between 400 and 500 years old. By volume it's Sweden's second-largest broadleaf tree, beaten only by the Ekebyhov oak.
Skivhusen på Siriusgatan står i sju rade: The slab blocks on Siriusgatan stand in seven rows on a hillside, a landmark as you come into Bergsjön. From some of the flats you can see all the way out to Vinga lighthouse! It's Gothenburg's most populous street, with 3,199 residents in 2021. The facades were originally grey and yellow, but during a renovation in 1992 the anthroposophist Fritz Fuchs was given the job of repainting them in a range of pale shades.
Skog och berg dominerar i den här delen: This part of Huddinge is all forest and rocky hills. Not far from here, Kynäsberget stretches out to the south-west of Lake Magelungen – an area of woods and crags considered of national importance for outdoor recreation, and there are plans to protect its northern part as a nature reserve. In the other direction is Björkängen sports ground, home to the ice hockey team Huddinge IK.
Skog och berg tar över en bit härifrån:: Not far from here, forest and rock take over. Kynäsberget, south-west of Lake Magelungen, is of national importance for outdoor recreation, and its northern part may become a nature reserve. Further off, on the Stockholm border, is the Rågsved open space, also called Kräppladalen – just over 100 hectares of rift-valley landscape, with ridges, steep slopes and clay-filled valleys.
Skogarna här hör till Nackareservatet, e: The forests here are part of Nackareservatet, a large nature reserve and outdoor recreation area shared by Stockholm and Nacka. A little further on is Lake Källtorpssjön, 7.6 metres deep, with the Hellasgården outdoor sports centre on its shore. Test fishing in the lake has turned up perch, white bream, common bream, ruffe and roach.
Skogen här är full av små sjöar. Örtjärn: The forest here is dotted with little lakes. Örtjärnen, a few hundred metres away, is a full ten metres deep despite its small size, and its water drains out through the Finnebäcken stream. A little further away is Västra Kroppedammen, just 0.006 square kilometres – a real dwarf among lakes.
Skogskapellet var det allra första kapel: Skogskapellet, the Woodland Chapel, was the very first chapel at Skogskyrkogården, the Woodland Cemetery. Gunnar Asplund designed it, and it was built in 1919–20. Close by stands the Resurrection Monument, a bronze group of six figures that John Lundqvist worked on from 1928 to 1941. The new crematorium, designed by Johan Celsing, has also won acclaim, picking up the Kasper Salin Prize, Sweden's top architecture award, in 2013.
Skogskyrkogården skapades av Gunnar Aspl: Skogskyrkogården, the Woodland Cemetery, was created by Gunnar Asplund and Sigurd Lewerentz on a pine-covered gravel ridge, and it has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1994. On the roof above the entrance to the Woodland Chapel stands Carl Milles' small gilded Angel of Death – the only time Milles and Asplund worked together. The angel sparked a debate in the city council, as some priests found it offensive and indecent!
Skogås sträcker sig från Mörtvik i norr: Skogås stretches from Mörtvik in the north to Gräsvreten in the south, with Lake Drevviken along its eastern edge. On Mörtviken, a bay of the lake, is Mörtviks gård, a group of buildings that still feels like a farm even though several of the houses have been heavily rebuilt. Closer to the stop is Östra gymnasiet, an upper secondary school that was named one of the buildings of the year in 2005.
Skolan är uppkallad efter Johan Skytte,: The school is named after Johan Skytte, and its main building, begun in 1946, was designed by the architect Paul Hedqvist. Close by is Långbrodal School, whose 2017 extension attracted a lot of attention. And further off was Långbro Hospital, a psychiatric hospital built between 1905 and 1910 and closed in 1997.
Skulpturen Arbetarhustru: The sculpture Arbetarhustru, the Worker's Wife
Skulpturen Fosterbröderna: The sculpture Fosterbröderna, the Foster Brothers
Skuru var från början namnet på en gård,: Skuru was originally the name of a farm, and that farm lives on today as Solsunda. In the 1500s King Gustav Vasa gave it to Danvik's hospital, and in the early 1900s it belonged to Stockholms sjukhem, a nursing home. The area also has Bastusjön, a lake you can swim in, and a little further off is Glasbrukssjön, which is small but a surprising 13 metres deep.

Skuru started out as the name of a farm, and today the area is mostly villas and semi-detached houses surrounded by nature. Not far from here, on the shore of Saltsjön, is Stora Nyckelviken, a manor from the mid-1700s – and as early as the 1600s there was a sailors' inn on the spot. Around the manor lies the Nyckelviken nature conservation area, 171 hectares of hilly, historic farmland.
Skvalta var ursprungligen en sjö, och va: Skvalta was originally a lake, and the water flowing out through Vikdalen powered several 'skvaltkvarnar', small horizontal water mills – which is where the name comes from. A little further on, in the villa suburb of Storängen, are two genuine artists' homes. Villa Bergh was home to the painter Richard Bergh from 1904 to 1919, and next door is Villa Pauli, where the artists Georg and Hanna Pauli lived. Both were designed in 1904 by the architect Albin Brag.
SkyView, gondolen upp på kupolen: SkyView – the gondola ride up the dome
Skälby är ett villaområde i södra delen: Skälby is a residential area of villas in southern Järfälla, part of the Stockholm urban area, and in 2005 it had 6,336 residents. The name comes from Skälby gård, a manor dating back to the 16th century. To the south, across the municipal boundary, begins Kälvesta, a Stockholm neighbourhood of terraced houses and villas.
Skälby, villaområdet runt omkring, har f: Skälby, the residential area all around us, is named after Skälby gård, a manor house not far from here. It's a former noble estate in Järfälla parish dating back to the 1500s, though the current main house was built in 1802. It's also in an unusual spot – right in the middle of four ancient burial grounds.
Skälltorp, området här intill, omfattar: The neighbouring area, Skälltorp, takes in northern Backa with Selma Lagerlöfs torg square, as well as Backadalen, Blå staden, Åketorp and Backatorp. A little further on is Sophie Elkans gata, named in 1992 after the Gothenburg-born writer Sophie Elkan – best remembered as Selma Lagerlöf's close friend. So here, the two friends meet again in the street names.
Skärholmen har en egen liten bergbana. S: Skärholmen has a little funicular of its own. The inclined lift between Skärholmen and Ekholmshöjden is 63 metres long, holds about 30 people and takes around a minute – and there's no driver on board. Also nearby is Skärisbiografen, a non-profit municipal cinema that opened in 2017 and is part of Kulturhuset Stadsteatern, the city's culture house and theatre.
Skärholmen hörde till Huddinge ända fram: Skärholmen was part of Huddinge until 1963, when it was transferred to Stockholm along with Vårberg. Down on the metro platform you can take a little trip to America: in 1990 the artist Ulf Wahlberg painted a spot in New Mexico in a series of 23 pictures, from sunrise to sunset. And close by, a funicular carries passengers up to Ekholmshöjden.
Skärholmens gård, vid Mälaren en bit här: Skärholmens gård, down by Lake Mälaren, started out as a simple croft belonging to Vårby gård. In the mid-18th century it was rebuilt as a summer retreat for wealthy Stockholmers. The City of Stockholm has owned it since 1945, and the City Museum has given it a blue listing, meaning its buildings are judged to be of exceptional cultural and historical value.
Skärsätra gård, alldeles intill, har get: Skärsätra gård, the farm right next to us, gave its name to the whole district, and its old main house is still standing, though it has been altered over the years. The villas round about make for a nice little architecture walk: there's Villa Bergtomta, an Art Nouveau house from 1910; Apelsinvillan, the Orange Villa, by Lake Kottlasjön, listed since 1982; and Villa Smith, which the architect Nils Tesch designed for himself in 1959 but never actually moved into.
Skårsgatan har fått namn efter gården Sk: Skårsgatan is named after the farm of Skår – 'skår' means a notch or ledge in the rock – and the name appears, spelt Shor, in a court letter as early as 1496. Sankt Sigfridsgatan, next to it, is named after the patron saint of Västergötland. And on that street you'll find Göteborgs pepparkaksbageri, the Gothenburg gingerbread bakery, which since 1924 has been baking citrus-scented gingerbread biscuits to a secret recipe.
Sköndal blev en egen stadsdel 1932 och h: Sköndal became a district in its own right in 1932, and there's plenty of architecture to discover. The architect Eskil Sundahl designed Villa Sundahl in 1955 as his own home, and Sköndalsskolan, the school opened in 1953, is the work of none other than Cyrillus Johansson. A little further on, Stora Sköndal Church sits proudly on a rocky outcrop near Lake Drevviken.
Sköndalsbro var en gång ett torp, och hu: Sköndalsbro was once a croft, and its main building probably dates from somewhere between 1700 and 1750, or perhaps later. The blocks around it are like a small open-air museum of architecture. Eskil Sundahl designed Villa Sundahl as his own home, and the architect couple Hanna and Roy Victorson built Villa Victorson. The two houses, from 1955 and 1958, are marked blue by the City Museum, meaning they're of exceptionally high cultural and historical value.
Slussen är platsen där Mälaren möter Sal: Slussen is where Lake Mälaren meets Saltsjön, the inlet of the Baltic, and where Södermalm meets Gamla stan, the Old Town. There have been locks here since the 17th century, and right now the whole area is being rebuilt in one of Stockholm's biggest construction projects. From the quays you can look out over Gamla stan, Skeppsholmen and Djurgården.
Släktforskare, spetsa öronen! Alldeles i: Calling all family historians! Right next door is the home of Genealogiska Föreningen, the Genealogical Society. Founded in 1933, it's a national association and one of Sweden's oldest in the field of family history. A stone's throw away is Jungfrudansen, now a housing area with culturally valuable Million Programme buildings but once a festival ground. The Huvudsta quarry was here too.
Slättens gård är ett före detta torp som: Slättens gård is a former croft that originally belonged to Sätra manor, and it's one of the few buildings left from before the Mälarhöjden villa suburb was built. Today its three houses are managed by AB Stadsholmen. A little further on is Mälarhöjden sports ground, known locally as Myren, which – despite its name – is actually in Fruängen.
Smycketorget i närheten anlades på 1960-: Nearby Smycketorget was built in the 1960s on two levels: shops and a hairdresser upstairs, an Asian restaurant and a pizzeria downstairs. A little further away is Frölunda torg, opened by Olof Palme on 8 September 1966. Seven years in the making, it was then the largest shopping centre under one roof in the Nordic countries.
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ab: We'll soon reach the final stop, Abrahamsberg. Here's a little naming quirk: Abrahamsberg metro station isn't actually in Abrahamsberg at all, but in Riksby. Before the metro, trams on the Ängby line ran past here from 1944, and the station's abstract murals in glazed tiles, made by Rigmor Roxner in 1999, are a nod to the tiled stations of the tram days. Close by is the white-rendered Abrahamsberg Church, consecrated on All Saints' Day 1955. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ak: We'll soon reach the final stop, Akalla. Akalla's main walkway, Sibeliusgången, is named after the Finnish composer Jean Sibelius and runs for 900 metres, with Bertil Johnson's fountains from 1976 bubbling away along the route. Yet the name Akalla goes back to the Middle Ages. In Akalla village stands Storgården, a 17th-century farm in one of the best-preserved village settings around Stockholm, now with a 4-H children's farm and a café. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Al: We'll soon reach the final stop, Alvik. Alvik is an interchange where the Tvärbanan and Nockebybanan light rail lines meet the metro. From here you can head out into Bromma, with its villa neighbourhoods and the shores of Lake Mälaren. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Alviks strand. Alvik's old industrial area once lined the shore of Lake Mälaren; today it's mostly offices and a few restaurants. Nearby is Gamla Tryckeriet, the Old Printworks, an events venue where the TV competition Floor Filler was recorded. The Tvärbanan light rail plunges into the rock through the Alvik tunnel, about 250 metres long, then crosses the Oxhålssundet strait on the 400-metre Alvik bridge, finished in 2000. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Am: We'll soon reach the final stop, Amhult Resecentrum. A few hundred metres from here in Amhult was Torslanda airfield, Gothenburg's airport from 1923 right up until 1977, when Landvetter took over. It was originally called Göteborgs Flyghamn and had a seaplane harbour too. When it closed, it was one of the oldest airfields in Europe with scheduled flights. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen An: We'll soon reach the final stop, Angered Centrum. Angered was built in the 1970s, and today it's one of Gothenburg's most international districts. It's home to the Blå Stället cultural centre, and all around are large stretches of countryside with lakes and forest. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Angereds Storåsväg. Not far from here is Hammarkulletorget, built in 1971, which got new colours and a new shape during a renovation in 1997. You can reach it by tram, getting off at what's been called Gothenburg's only underground station. Closer to this stop is Eriksbo, part of the Hjällbo district. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ap: We'll soon reach the final stop, Aprilgatan. Årstidstorget, the Seasons Square, is better known to many as Norra or Norra centrum, and it's the little hub of northern Kortedala. There's a health centre, a pizzeria, tobacconists and a pâtisserie if you fancy a fika – a Swedish coffee-and-cake break – plus a pub close by. Local clubs and associations have their premises on the square too. It sits on tram line six, by the end of the line. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ar: We'll soon reach the final stop, Arendal Portal. Right next door is the Arken combi terminal at Skandiahamnen, the Skandia Harbour, where semi-trailers are transferred between ships and trains. It replaced the old terminal at Gullbergs vass and Gothenburg Central Station, which had to make way for the Västlänken rail tunnel. Work started in January 2018, and the terminal was officially opened in February 2019. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen As: We'll soon reach the final stop, Askims Svartmosse. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ax: We'll soon reach the final stop, Axel Dahlströms Torg. The square is dominated by a 16-storey tower block completed in 1956, and the community centre is decorated with a marble-inlay mural by the artist Endre Nemes. The same year Högsboskolan, the Högsbo school, opened right next door, built for around 1,000 pupils. The school is gone now, though – it was demolished in 2013. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ba: We'll soon reach the final stop, Backlura. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Bagarmossen. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Bagartorp södra. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Balingsnäs. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Barkarby handelsplats. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Barkarby station övre. Barkarby is a place being transformed. The commuter rail station took on its present form on 10 October 2016, with four tracks and a ticket hall up on the Barkarbybron bridge. Meanwhile, a new metro station is being built underground, and once everything's finished, a new entrance at the north end of the station will become the main way in. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Barkarby station. It's about 14.5 kilometres from here into Stockholm Central, and the commuter train station has four tracks so that freight and long-distance trains can race straight through. In 1728, Olof Celsius the Elder found a runestone in Järfälla church – it had probably been used as a step. It later went missing, but in 1939 seven fragments turned up, and today they're kept at the Swedish History Museum. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Barnängen. Per Anders Fogelström brought the old factory district of Barnängen, on the shore of Hammarby sjö, to life in his novel Vävarnas barn, 'The Weavers' Children' – and this is also where Hammarby IF football club has its roots. Barnängsparken slopes down to the waterfront with lawns and a ferry pier facing Hammarby sjöstad. A little further on is Leksaksmuseet, the Toy Museum, with everything from 19th-century dolls to Lego, Barbie and Star Wars. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Be: We'll soon reach the final stop, Beatrice Lesslies Gata. A few hundred metres from here is Studio Fredman, the recording studio Fredrik Nordström set up in 1990. A long list of Swedish metal bands have recorded here – In Flames, Hammerfall, Opeth, Dark Tranquillity and Soilwork among them – as well as the British band Bring Me the Horizon. Just beyond is Radiotorget, the first square built for a Swedish satellite town, opened in 1954. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Bj: We'll soon reach the final stop, Björknäs centrum. Björknäs is mentioned in writing as early as 1436, and takes its name from Stora Björknäs farm. It sits at the eastern end of the Skuru bridges, where the Skurusundet strait marks the boundary between two historic provinces: Södermanland to the west and Uppland to the east. Bridges have been built here three times – in 1915, 1957 and 2023. When the newest one opened, it took over the name Skurubron, and the older ones became Gamla Skurubron, the Old Skuru Bridge. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Björnbo. Elfviksvägen has two villas by the architect Ralph Erskine: Villa Gadelius, designed in 1961 for the businessman Knut Saburo Gadelius, and Villa Molin from 1947, built for the garden designer and editor Ulla Molin. A little further on is the Kanada block. Its terraced houses, along with those in Gamla Enskede, are thought to be the very first in Sweden, and they have been listed since 1981. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Björnkulla. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Bl: We'll soon reach the final stop, Blackebergs gård. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Blockhusudden. This headland is named after a blockhouse of timber and stone, built in Gustav Vasa's day to guard the approach to Stockholm. Later it became a customs post for incoming boats, and the old customs houses at Stora Sjötullen are now private homes. Out here you'll also find Thielska galleriet, the Thiel Gallery, an art museum on Djurgården. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Bo: We'll soon reach the final stop, Bockkranen. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Borås resecentrum. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Bosön. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Br: We'll soon reach the final stop, Bredäng. Bredäng is seriously hilly: Bredängsskolan, the school, sits 62 metres above sea level, and Bredängshemmet, the care home, a full 67 metres. Bredängsparken, next to the centre, is one of the biggest parks in the district, and drinking alcohol has been banned there because things used to get rowdy. Bredäng Church doesn't have a building of its own – it's in a parish hall at one end of the shopping centre. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Bromma flygplats. The building on Ulvsundavägen went up in 1946 as the head office of the airline ABA and was later used by SAS. It was designed by Paul Hedqvist, the architect behind several of the airport's hangars, too – in their day the biggest in northern Europe. These days the hangars house the Bromma Blocks shopping centre. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Brommaplan. By the metro viaduct stands the sculpture ‘Bird Rock with Three Eggs’, made by Berndt Helleberg in 1969. The viaduct is actually older than the metro: it opened in 1944, when trams ran across it. The art in the station, in sheet metal, glass and photographs, tells the story of Bromma and of aviation. The 16-storey Brommahöjden tower block is a newcomer by comparison – it only arrived in 2008. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Brunnsparken. Brunnsparken is the beating heart of the city's public transport – almost every tram line passes through here. Right next to it is Gustaf Adolfs torg, with a statue of the king who founded Gothenburg in 1621. The city was built by Dutch engineers, and that's why Gothenburg has canals: the Dutch knew how to build on clay. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Brännö Rödsten. Brännö is a car-free island in Gothenburg's southern archipelago. Its summer dances on the jetty are famous all over Gothenburg, and the island has lovely rocks to swim from. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Bu: We'll soon reach the final stop, Burö färjeläge. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ce: We'll soon reach the final stop, Centralen. At Vasagatan 7 was the bar Tre Remmare, with a casino and nightclub under the same roof. It was one of the few places in Stockholm allowed to stay open until five in the morning, and it became notorious for heavy drinking and drug abuse. It lost its licence and closed in 2007, and the Bishops Arms pub has taken over the premises. Across the street stands the World Trade Center, designed by Ralph Erskine. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ci: We'll soon reach the final stop, Cityterminalen. Kungsgatan 65 has had quite a few incarnations. The Palladium cinema opened here in 1918, with the Bal Palais dance restaurant in the basement. Later it became the Heaven nightclub, and from 2003 to 2025 it was Casino Cosmopol. Next door is Oscarsteatern, the Oscar Theatre, from 1906 – named after King Oscar II and now a listed building. The same building houses Fasching, which since 1977 has been Scandinavia's biggest jazz venue. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Da: We'll soon reach the final stop, Dalens sjukhus. Dalen hospital, completed in 1977, is a well-preserved example of the late modernist architecture of its day and an important piece of urban planning history. A little further away, on the Nytorps gärde field, stood the croft of Nytorp, which belonged to the Hammarby estate. It disappeared in the early 1960s to make way for the Nytorpsbadet pool. The residential area of Dalen is made up of 14 blocks, and the Stockholm City Museum has classed the whole of it as culturally valuable. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Danderyds sjukhus. Over in Inverness, the Inverness brunn mineral water works was in business from 1929 to 1945 – among other things, it made Sweden's first soda water. The spring is still there on the shore of Stocksundet, though the water isn't fit to drink and tastes salty. Closer to the stop stood Mörby gård, an 18th-century farm that gave the area its name. It was listed in 1944, but burned down in 1976. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Dj: We'll soon reach the final stop, Djurgårdsbrunn. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Djursholms torg. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Djurstensvägen. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Do: We'll soon reach the final stop, Doktor Sydows Gata. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Dr: We'll soon reach the final stop, Drottningtorget. Drottningtorget sits right in front of the Central Station, which opened in 1858 and is one of the oldest station buildings still in use in Sweden. Much of the largest tram network in the Nordic countries fans out from here. Gothenburg got horse-drawn trams in 1879 and electric ones in 1902 – and while many other Swedish cities scrapped their trams, Gothenburg chose to keep them. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Du: We'll soon reach the final stop, Duvbo. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ek: We'll soon reach the final stop, Ekensberg. Ekensberg is named after the Ekensberg inn, built in the early 18th century and still standing at Gröndalsvägen 184. Between 1926 and 1934, most of what we now call Gröndal went by the name of Ekensberg. The headland sits between Mörtviken bay and the Essingesundet strait. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Ekensbergsvägen. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Ekerö centrum. From Tappström, commuter boat line 89 runs all the way into Stockholm to Stadshuskajen, the City Hall quay, with boats such as M/S Lux. The Tappström strait, which separates the islands of Lovön and Ekerön, also has a guest harbour for visiting leisure boats. A little further away was Tappsund brickworks, founded in the late 19th century and closed in 1959. Thank you for riding with us!
