We'll soon reach the final stop, Älvsjö station. Älvsjö gård has deep roots, with owners known by name from the mid-15th century. One family held the estate for almost two hundred years, right up until 1968. For a long time hardly anyone lived in the area: around 1900 the population was mainly people working on the estate or at the station. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Åk: We'll soon reach the final stop, Åkareplatsen. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Åkerby industriområde. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen År: We'll soon reach the final stop, Årsringsgatan. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Årstaberg. Årstalänken offers an unusual sight. The eastern part of this stretch of motorway has been closed since 2004 – a 'ruin motorway', as it's known – and there are now plans to build housing on it. Årstaberg commuter rail station sees around 8,300 people board on a normal winter weekday, and the Tvärbanan light rail has stopped here since 2000. Along Årstaskogs väg rise the Årstahusen, three residential tower blocks built between 2017 and 2020. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Öc: We'll soon reach the final stop, Öckerö färjeläge. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ös: We'll soon reach the final stop, Österlyckan. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Östervägen. Artillerigården, the Artillery Yard, has served the army's gunners since the 1640s, and today it houses the Army Museum. Hidden beneath it are two Second World War air-raid shelters, which are occasionally opened for guided tours. Just round the corner, at Artillerigatan 14, was the Michelin-starred restaurant Gastrologik, where there was no menu – the chefs decided what you ate. Since 2024 the restaurant ergo has taken over the same premises. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Östhammarsgatan. Thank you for riding with us!
Sockenstugan och Bromma kyrka: Sockenstugan, the old parish hall, and Bromma Church
Sofielundsskolan har ett eget litet kapi: Sofielundsskolan, the school here, has its own small place in local school history: from 1994, the newly founded Sollentuna Fria Gymnasium, an upper secondary school, used it as a temporary base for its academic classes. Right beside it runs Sollentunavägen, which was the main road between Stockholm and Uppsala until the Uppsalavägen highway was expanded in the 1950s. A little further on is Sollentuna Hospital, opened in 1978 and completely renovated between 2015 and 2020.
Solgård är ett villaområde söder om Hudd: Solgård is a villa area south of Huddinge centrum, and the view here is something special. From the highest hills, about 60 metres above sea level, you can see all the way to the Globe arena in Stockholm. If you're driving, there are only two ways in. And in the woods by Solgårdsvägen there's an ancient hillfort, Solgårds fornborg.
Sollentuna station, en kort promenad bor: Sollentuna station, a short walk away, is the busiest commuter train station on the line to Märsta, 13.2 kilometres north of Stockholm Central. Tureberg has been the heart of the municipality since the council offices moved here from Norrviken in the 1940s. Today you'll find Tureberg Church, the shopping centre and the fifteen-storey Turebergshuset, home to the municipal offices and, since 2023, the library too.
Sollentunas centrum har flyttat. Från bö: Sollentuna's centre has moved around. It started out by the church village at Sollentuna Church, then the local administration grew up in Norrviken, and in the 1940s it all moved to Tureberg. Right next door are Turebergskyrkan church and the remand prison, which opened in 2011 and is part of Rättscentrum Sollentuna, the justice centre. And a couple of hundred metres away stood Sollentunamässan, in its day the third-largest exhibition centre in Sweden.
Sollentunas förvaltning låg förr i Norrv: Sollentuna's administration used to be based in Norrviken, but in the 1940s it moved here to Tureberg, which has been the natural heart of the municipality ever since. A little further on is Arena Satelliten, opened in 2009, with sports halls, a music studio, a café and a fully equipped theatre stage. And on Malmvägen stands Tian, 'the Ten' – ten tower blocks from the Million Programme, Sweden's great housing drive.
Sollentunavallen ligger i ett gammalt gr: Sollentunavallen sits in an old gravel pit in the Stockholm esker, a long glacial ridge, and opened for the Swedish Athletics Championships in August 1969. The stands hold about 4,500 people, and in winter the artificial pitch next door becomes a bandy rink for Helenelunds IK. A little further away is Edsbacka krog, the first restaurant in Sweden to win two Michelin stars.
Sollentunavägen var en gång huvudvägen m: Sollentunavägen was once the main road between Stockholm and Uppsala, until Uppsalavägen was widened in the 1950s. Nearby is the fifteen-storey Tureberg Building, Turebergshuset, home to the municipal offices and, since 2023, the library as well. Arena Satelliten, opened in 2009, has sports halls, a media studio and a theatre seating 200.
Solnahallen stod klar 1983, och fasadern: Solnahallen was completed in 1983, and its east and north facades are decorated by the artist Per Olov Ultvedt. AIK plays floorball, handball and basketball here, and in the late 1980s the hall welcomed national teams such as Cuba, Bulgaria and Germany for the Euro Volley volleyball tournament. It's also used for concerts.
Solsunda hette fram till 1922 Skuru gård: Until 1922 Solsunda was known as Skuru gård. In the 16th century King Gustav Vasa gave the farm to Danvik hospital, so that the rent would help cover the hospital's costs. Since the early 20th century the manor house has served as a rest and treatment home. Little Bastusjön lake nearby is home to perch, roach and two kinds of freshwater mussel.
Som en skärgård på land: begravningsplat: Picture an archipelago on dry land: the cemetery here opened in October 2024 and is laid out as a cluster of small islands, each one its own burial section, with a reflecting pool in the middle. Its neighbour is Granholmstoppen, a former rubbish tip that has grown into a hill 49 metres above sea level. It was built up from earth dug out when the blue metro line and the surrounding districts were built – although, according to the lorry drivers who built it, a bit of everything ended up in there.
Spana in Tomtehuset vid Vasagatan: Look out for Tomtehuset, the Gnome House, on Vasagatan
Spana in soffan på möbelhusets tak: Spot the sofa on the furniture store's roof
Sporthallen en kort promenad bort, Botky: The sports hall a short walk away, Botkyrkahallen, combines royal glamour with everyday use. King Carl XVI Gustaf opened it in the summer of 2000, and it's also the sports hall for Brunnaskolan school. Balrog IK's men's team play here in front of up to 1,500 spectators. A short way in the other direction is Slagsta gård, a historic manor and former noble estate.
Spånga IP är en riktig allt-i-ett-anlägg: Spånga IP really has it all: an ice rink, an indoor football hall, a bandy rink, street basketball and athletics tracks. In snowy winters they even lay cross-country ski tracks on the running track. A short way off was Fascinate, Sweden's oldest surviving large-scale graffiti painting – until the wall was demolished in December 2021.
Spånga är ett riktigt gammalt namn. Det: Spånga is a truly old name. It appears in writing as early as 1300, in Latin, as apud Ecclesiam spangar, referring to the old church village. The name is simply the plural of spång, a footbridge. Today Spånga is an informal area that roughly covers the districts of Bromsten, Flysta, Solhem, Lunda and Sundby.
Spårvagnarna under Frölunda torg en bit: When Frölunda torg, just up the road, was built in 1966, the trams beneath it ran into a stop that was completely underground – but in 2008 it was partly opened up to the outside. Next to the square stood Frölunda specialist hospital, opened in 1968 and replaced in early 2024 by the new Högsbo local hospital. Closest to us are Tynnered Church and Smycketorget square.
Spårvagnen kom hit redan hösten 1929, in: The tram reached this spot as early as autumn 1929, before the square even existed. The square itself was laid out in the early 1930s as a long, narrow piazza – a classic garden-city square. The town plan was approved in 1932 and bears the signature of Albert Lilienberg. All around is Nockeby, part of the Bromma garden city.
Spårvägsmuseet i Norra Djurgårdsstaden v: The Tramway Museum in Norra Djurgårdsstaden tells the story of public transport around Stockholm – on water as well as land – from the 1650s right up to today. Next to it is Husarviken bay, whose name has nothing to do with hussars. It comes from Husarnæ, a village mentioned in 1288, so the stress falls on the first syllable. Since 2018 the bay has been spanned by the Husarviken bridge, an opening bridge for pedestrians and cyclists.
Stadsarkivet Liljeholmskajen: Stadsarkivet, the City Archives, at Liljeholmskajen
Stadsdelen Backa, ofta kallad Hisings Ba: The district of Backa, often called Hisings Backa, is no small place: 1,473 hectares stretching from Brunnsbo in the south, through Backa in the middle, to Skälltorp in the north. Backa was once a rural municipality of its own in what was then Gothenburg and Bohus County. Not far from here is Selma Lagerlöfs torg, the local centre of northern Backa.
Stadsdelen Gubbängen har fått sitt namn: Gubbängen gets its name from Gubbängens gård, a croft that later became an independent farm and was pulled down in 1965. Nearby is Gubbängsparken, a landscaped park of almost twelve hectares with a staffed playground. And a little further on, south of Skogskyrkogården, the Woodland Cemetery, is the Southern Jewish Cemetery, in use since 1952.
Stadsdelen Larsboda ligger klämd mellan: The Larsboda neighbourhood is squeezed in between Nynäsvägen and Magelungsvägen, and just east of Filipstadsbacken rises Burmanstorpsberg, 73 metres high. A little further away, on Lake Drevviken, is Hökarängsbadet, with a sandy beach about 60 metres long, a swimming jetty, a big meadow and rocks to sunbathe on. There's also a barbecue area and a café if you feel like staying a while.
Stadsdelen Rud har ett namn som berättar: The name Rud speaks of hard graft: it comes from Old Swedish rýdh, a clearing. The village is recorded as Rudh as early as 1495. Not far from here is Ruddalens IP, a sports ground with room for 3,000 spectators. The first match was played in 1985, when Västra Frölunda IF took on IFK Malmö, and the ground has hosted several seasons of Allsvenskan, Sweden's top football league.
The district of Syrhåla has an honest name. First recorded in 1550, it means ‘swampy place’ or ‘sour ground’ – a nod to the low, damp land between the hills. Syrhåla became a district of its own in 1957, when Arendal was split in two. Arendal itself is now given over entirely to industry and logistics, and it's where Volvo Buses, among others, has its headquarters.
Stadsdelen Torp har fått sitt namn efter: The district of Torp takes its name from two old farms. Lilla Torp was built in 1748 by Bengt Wilhelm Carlberg, and close by is the manor of Stora Torp, which dates back to the 1550s. Back then the estate was known as Torpit, and its tenant farmers answered to Kärra, the estate of Sten Eriksson Leijonhufvud. After his violent death in 1568, the farm passed to his widow, Gref Ebba.
Stadsdelen Vinsta är en ganska ung skape: Vinsta is a fairly young district. The City of Stockholm bought the land from Spånga in 1949, and four years later the district was created and named after the old village of Vinsta. Its 1.67 square kilometres today take in an industrial area that includes Vällingby fire station, designed by the architect Mårten J. Larsson and opened in 1965.
Stadsdelen bildades 1954 och gränsar öve: The district was created in 1954 and looks across the waters of Lake Mälaren to Ekerö municipality. On Strandliden stand 16 slab blocks from the late 1950s, which the City Museum has green-listed for their cultural, historical and artistic value. Right in the middle of the centre, on Maltesholmstorget, is Hässelby Strand Church.
Stadsdelen har fått sitt namn efter ett: The district is named after a small croft belonging to Hammarby gård – and the crofter's cottage is still standing in the southern part of Kärrtorpsparken park. Near the square is the Reflexen cinema, opened in 1961. Today volunteers from a cultural association run it, sharing the building with Teater Reflex. Down in the metro station glows Björn Olsén's artwork Ljuslådor med hemliga tecken, Light Boxes with Secret Signs, unveiled in 1994.
Stadshuset invigdes 1923 och är en av St: Stockholm City Hall was inaugurated in 1923 and is one of the city's great symbols. Every December the Nobel Banquet is held here in the Blue Hall, and from the tower there's a sweeping view over Riddarfjärden bay and Gamla stan, the Old Town.
Stallbacken är ett passande namn, för hä: Stallbacken – “Stable Hill” – is a fitting name, because this is home to Åby Travgymnasium. Opened in autumn 2005, it's an upper secondary school for young people from all over Sweden and the Nordic countries who want a career in harness racing or riding. It's based at Åbytravet, Sweden's second-largest trotting track. A little further on, you can swap the sound of hooves for film soundtracks at Fässbergs Bio, a 400-seat cinema in a converted school hall.
Statarmuseet, Överjärva gård: Statarmuseet, the farm workers' museum, at Överjärva gård
Stationen öppnade 1890 och fick el redan: The station opened in 1890 and was electrified as early as 1895. In the early 1950s it was the busiest railway station in Sweden, handling around 340 trains a day, freight included, with lines heading off in four directions. The villas round about started going up in 1896, when Djursholms AB began selling plots near the station. In the 1970s and 80s the whole Roslagsbanan railway was under threat of closure.
Stationen öppnade 1890 och hette först D: The station opened in 1890. It was called Djursholm at first, then Ösby, and from 1920 Djursholms Ösby. The line was electrified as early as 1895. With trains running in four directions – around 340 a day, freight included – it was once reckoned to be the busiest railway station in Sweden. The villas round about started going up in 1896, when building plots near the station were put on sale.
Stationen öppnade 1937, när Roslagsbanan: The station opened in 1937, when the Roslagsbanan railway was extended to Näsbypark. At first it was called Alléparken, but the name lasted only four months. The trains here run on a single track with just one platform. Down by the bay of Näsbyviken is Näsby Castle, now a conference venue with a hotel and restaurant.
Stationen öppnade 1944 som spårvagnshåll: The station opened in 1944 as a tram stop on the Ängby line, under the name Färjestadsvägen. It became a metro station in 1952, but it wasn't called Ängbyplan until 1962. Not far from here, as far back as the 16th century, stood Karsvik farm, on the shore of Lake Ängbysjön, which has since disappeared. Today the Mälaren Scouts have their base in Karsvik's meadow. And nearby Ängby torg square only got its official name in 2005.
Stationsnamnet är en ledtråd. En kort bi: The station name gives it away. A short distance from here was Täby Galopp, the biggest gallop racecourse in Scandinavia, opened by King Gustaf VI Adolf in 1960 to replace the Ulriksdal racecourse in Solna. The last race day was 18 May 2016, after which the horses moved to Bro Park. Where the track used to be, a new district, Täby Park, is now taking shape, planned for around 20,000 residents.
Statyn Avskedet på polarisen: The statue Avskedet på polarisen, Farewell on the Polar Ice
Statyn mitt på platsen föreställer Karl: The statue in the middle of the square is King Karl IX – Charles IX – on horseback, but to Gothenburgers it's simply Kopparmärra, the Copper Mare. It went up in 1904. This is where Kungsportsavenyn, the city's grand avenue, begins, and on the canal alongside, the flat Paddan sightseeing boats glide by, ducking under the low bridges. A short distance away is Stora Saluhallen, the big market hall, from 1889.
Stenhamra, på västra sidan av Färingsö m: Stenhamra, on the western side of Färingsö island in the middle of Lake Mälaren, is best known for its disused 19th-century quarry and the industrial village that grew up around it. Neighbouring Törnby is far older: it's first mentioned in 1342, in connection with a land swap with Vårfruberga convent, and has since grown together with Stenhamra.
Stenhamra, på västra sidan av Färingsö,: Stenhamra, on the western side of Färingsö, is best known for its disused 19th-century granite quarry and the company town that grew up around it. If you'd like to go even further back in time, look for runestone U 32, which stands in a patch of woodland just under a kilometre from the centre. Ekerö municipality, by the way, is made up of a cluster of islands in Lake Mälaren long known as Mälaröarna, the Mälaren Islands.
Stensö har fått sitt namn efter en halvö: Stensö is named after a peninsula that was once an island in Lake Ältasjön, and the Stensö swimming spot is at its tip. Through the area runs Ältavägen, built in 1934, which winds for just over eight kilometres through open countryside between Älta and Nackanäs. Not far away, in the Flaten nature reserve, people race radio-controlled model cars.
Sticklinge på nordvästra Lidingö är beka: Anyone who has run Lidingöloppet, the famous cross-country race, will know Sticklinge in north-western Lidingö, because the course runs right through it. South of the houses stretches the Sticklinge nature reserve: 108 hectares of forest, coast and grassland, protected since 2021. By Rödstuguviken bay stands Rödstugan, a house with roots in the 17th century that has been home to crofters, ferrymen and the families of farm labourers.
Stjärnbildsgatan, en bit härifrån, fick: Stjärnbildsgatan, a short way from here, had an unusual makeover: its four-storey blocks were rebuilt so drastically that the top floors were removed altogether, leaving terraced houses around generous courtyards. Nearby is Interkulturella folkhögskolan, the Intercultural Folk High School. It started in 2007 as the first folk high school in the Nordic countries for Roma students and was opened by Crown Princess Victoria.
Stjärnhusen i Gröndal byggdes av Olle En: The Star Houses in Gröndal were built by Olle Engkvist to designs by Sven Backström and Leif Reinius, and the architectural historian Fredric Bedoire ranks them among the finest groups of buildings in Stockholm. The area is of national interest and a textbook example of folkhem architecture, from the early days of the Swedish welfare state. And after all that architecture, it's time for fika, the Swedish coffee break: Lundbergs konditori has been on the same corner, under the same name, since 1946.
Stockholms frihamn öppnade som ett provi: Frihamnen, Stockholm's free port, opened in 1919 as a temporary solution, yet it kept growing right up until the 1970s. For much of that time, from 1921 to 1952, seaplanes landed at Lindarängen, where the port stands today. The Ford Building, designed by Uno Åhrén, went up between 1929 and 1931 as an assembly plant for Ford cars; these days it's the home of the stock exchange operator Nasdaq. The huge Magasin 6 warehouse had less luck – it was out of date almost as soon as container shipping took over.
Stockholms stad köpte egendomen Gubbänge: The City of Stockholm bought the Gubbängen estate from the farmer Albin Arvidsson in 1908, but building didn't really get going until the 1940s. The district grew up around two farms, Herrängen and Gubbängen, neither of which survives. The metro arrived on 1 October 1950, when the line from Slussen to Hökarängen opened.
Stockholms största koloniområde ligger a: Stockholm's largest allotment area is right nearby, with no fewer than 554 plots, each with its own little cottage. It was laid out in three stages – in 1936, 1939 and 1941 – to replace several allotment areas in the southern suburbs that were cleared during the 1920s and 30s. Also in the neighbourhood is Pungpinan, an area of small cottages, where building began on Lugna Gatan as early as 1927.
Stockholms ånglokssällskap: Stockholms ånglokssällskap, the Stockholm steam locomotive society
Stockholms ånglokssällskap bevarar och r: Stockholms ånglokssällskap, the Stockholm Steam Locomotive Society, preserves and restores old railway vehicles. It started out in 1974 with an emergency reserve locomotive bought from SJ, the Swedish state railways. The society was first based at Tomteboda and then in the old slaughterhouse district, but when the Globe arena was about to be built it had to move, in 1988, to an industrial siding here in Västberga. Nearby Midsommarkransens skola was an elementary school from 1915 to 1962.
Stockholmsmässan hette Älvsjömässan fram: Stockholmsmässan, the Stockholm exhibition centre, was called Älvsjömässan until 1976. Today it's Sweden's largest venue for trade fairs and conferences, with around seventy fairs a year and just over a million visitors. In spring 2020 its halls were put to a very different use, when the Älvsjö field hospital was set up inside.
Stockholmsvägen är en av Lidingös äldsta: Stockholmsvägen is one of Lidingö's oldest roads – the municipality calls it Lidingö's historic lifeline. Along it stand Kopparhusen, the Copper Houses, three tower blocks from the 1950s and 1960s; the oldest has been marked by the city museum as being of very high cultural and historical value. Further on is Lidingö Arena, an office and retail building from the 1970s by the architect Bo Möller, so striking that it has become a local landmark.
Stocksund är rikt på arkitektvillor. Vil: Stocksund is full of architect-designed villas. Villa Gärdsgården was built in 1904–05 to designs by Ragnar Östberg, for the artist Alf Wallander. Villa Tallom was built in 1904–06 by the architect Lars Israel Wahlman as a home for himself and his family, and it has been listed since 1979.
Stocksundet förbinder Lilla Värtan med E: The Stocksundet strait links Lilla Värtan with the bay of Edsviken and marks the border between Danderyd and Solna. Stocksund station used to sit closer to the harbour, with tracks running down to the water so goods could be loaded onto ships. The harbour also had the power station that supplied electricity to the Djursholm railway, and the Långängsbanan tramway started from the station.
Stora Essingen är en 73 hektar stor ö i: Stora Essingen is a 73-hectare island in Lake Mälaren. Its highest point, Kungsklippan, is 41 metres above sea level, and on the second-highest stands Essinge church, designed by Cyrillus Johansson and consecrated in 1959. The local cinema Orkanen opened nearby in 1938. The two apartment buildings on Badstrandsvägen are called Byggindustrihuset, after AB Byggindustri, the construction company that built them.
Stora Essingens sommarvillor från 1700-t: The 18th-century summer villas on Stora Essingen became year-round homes in the early 20th century, and things really took off when the Essinge bridge opened in 1929. In 1966 came Essingeleden, Sweden's first six-lane motorway, along the island's eastern shore. On 14 October 2005 the floating crane Lodbrok crashed into the bridge, causing massive traffic jams.
Stora Förö är genom landhöjningen numera: Thanks to post-glacial land uplift – the land here is still slowly rising after the Ice Age – Stora Förö is now joined to Lilla Förö by a narrow isthmus. The island has a burial cairn and finds from the Stone Age. When the master carpenter Axel Hellqvist came out here on a boat trip in 1927, there wasn't a single tree, because the island had long been used for grazing sheep and cutting timber.
Stora Kåsjön är Partille kommuns största: Stora Kåsjön is the largest lake in Partille municipality, just over a square kilometre in area and a full 32 metres deep. It sits high up, about 109 metres above sea level, and it's also the municipality's source of drinking water. Around it are more small lakes, such as Haketjärnen in the Maderna-Haketjärn Natura 2000 area.
Stora Saluhallen vid Kungstorget: Stora Saluhallen, the market hall on Kungstorget
Stora Sjötullen: Stora Sjötullen, the old customs house
Stora Ursvik gränsar mot Kymlinge, Lilla: Stora Ursvik borders Kymlinge, Lilla Ursvik, Rissne and Rinkeby. Not far from here, on a hill by the Rissne interchange, stands the Stora Stampan windmill. Its companion, Holländskan, burned down in 1989, but Stora Stampan was restored over the winter of 2019–20 and now has new sails.
Stora delar av grannområdet Ekängen bygg: Much of neighbouring Ekängen was built in the 1940s as a neighbourhood of small family houses, and it's still a quiet residential area just north of Saltsjö-Duvnäs. A little further on you'll find Långsjön, a small forest lake that has been a nature reserve since 2005. There's a swimming spot and a 1.4-kilometre jogging trail all the way round – perfect if you fancy swapping the town centre for a lap of the lake.
Storholmen i sjön Trehörningen var en gå: Storholmen in Lake Trehörningen was once a proper island. In the 1920s it was divided into plots, most of them sold to workers from Stockholm, and a footbridge was built to the mainland. Around twenty little summer cottages sprang up. Today it's mostly forest and shoreline open to all, and the lake is rich in fish and birdlife – the lesser spotted woodpecker among them – and even bats.
Storskogstorget invigdes 1958 och formga: Storskogstorget square opened in 1958. The landscape architect N.H. Orénto designed it very much in the style of the day, with seating, greenery and two ponds. From here you can also get to Näckrosen metro station, the only one on the network with entrances in two different municipalities. A little further on is Filmstaden in Råsunda, the studios where almost 400 Swedish feature films were shot between 1920 and 1973 – a place especially linked with Ingmar Bergman.
Storängens industriområde, alldeles i nä: Building work on the Storängen industrial area, right nearby, began in the early 1950s, just under a kilometre south-east of Huddinge centrum. Now the area is about to change. Under a plan from 2009, it will eventually become a mixed neighbourhood, mostly homes plus businesses that sit comfortably alongside residents. It's also where you'll find Storängshallen, a hall for athletics and gymnastics.
Storängshallen alldeles intill, invigd 2: Right next door is Storängshallen, opened in 2007, a hall mainly for athletics and gymnastics. The area has an amusing history. In 1902 the owner of Fullersta gård launched Huddinge villastad, a scheme for a brand-new garden suburb of villas. Only a handful of the old villas are left, and Huddinge centrum now stands right where the villa town was supposed to be.
Strawberry Arena, som invigdes under nam: Strawberry Arena, which opened as Friends Arena, is Sweden's national stadium, home to the men's football team, and since 2013 it has hosted the final of Melodifestivalen, the contest that picks Sweden's Eurovision entry. For concerts it holds up to 65,000 people. Next door is a 25-storey hotel with round windows designed to look like footballs, and Mall of Scandinavia has an IMAX cinema with the biggest screen in Sweden, almost 22 metres wide.
Strax härifrån ligger Hammarkulletorget,: Just up the road is Hammarkulletorget, a square designed by White Architects and built in 1971. Beneath it lies the only completely underground tram stop in Sweden. It was modelled on the Stockholm metro – because in the 1970s there really were plans for a metro all the way out to Angered. That's why it's sometimes called Gothenburg's only metro station.
Strax intill inträffade Tuveraset, en av: It was right near here that the Tuve landslide struck – one of the worst natural disasters in modern Swedish history. At 4.09 pm on 30 November 1977, the ground in Tuve gave way in a massive landslide that claimed nine lives. It's also known as Raset i Tuve or Tuveskredet.
Strax intill ligger Arken kombiterminal: Right beside us is the Arken combi terminal in Skandia Harbour, where semi-trailers are switched between ships and trains. It replaced the old terminal at Gullbergs vass and Gothenburg Central Station, which had to move to make way for the Västlänken rail tunnel. Work started in January 2018, and the terminal was officially opened in February 2019.
Strax intill ligger Fässbergs kyrkogård,: Right next to it is Fässberg cemetery, with 4,800 graves and a chapel from 1936. A little further on is Fässbergs Bio, a 400-seat cinema run by the municipality in the converted Fässbergssalen assembly hall, which opened in January 2013. The upper secondary school that houses the hall was once one of Sweden's 20 schools with specialist elite programmes.
Strax intill ligger Hult Åsens naturvård: Right beside it is the Hult Åsen nature conservation area, a stretch of high ground with pine, birch and bare rock. Set aside in 1994, it covers ten hectares and is looked after by the City of Gothenburg. A little further away is Askims torg, the square at the heart of Askim, a district facing Askimsfjorden bay.
Strax intill ligger Kvibergsnäs landeri,: Right next door is Kvibergsnäs landeri, a country estate between Kviberg and Gamlestaden. Its present buildings date from the first half of the 19th century. Kvibergsnäs is something of a survivor: it's the only country estate in Gothenburg where both the house and the barns are still standing.
Strax intill ligger Lillhagsparkens sjuk: Right beside us is Lillhagsparken hospital, originally named Lillhagen hospital for the mentally ill. Gothenburgers usually just called it Lillhagen, Hagen or LS. There's no longer any care here – the forensic psychiatric unit moved to Rågården in 2013.
Strax intill ligger Mariakyrkan i Hammar: Right next to us is Mariakyrkan in Hammarkullen, formerly known as Tomaskyrkan, a church shared by the Uniting Church in Sweden and Angered parish. Close by there was also Hammarkullens Folkets Hus Bio, a 200-seat cinema. And a short walk away is Hammarkulletorget – the place to go for Gothenburg's only underground tram stop.
Strax intill ligger Motorbranschens tekn: Right next door is the Motor Industry Technical Upper Secondary School, where the focus is on vehicles and transport. A short way from here is Västra Frölunda Cemetery, with medieval roots; the old Västra Frölunda Church stood here until it was pulled down in the 1860s. Iron rings for tethering horses are still set into the cemetery wall – a kind of car park from days gone by.
Strax intill ligger Nylöse kyrka, som ti: Right next to it is Nylöse Church, which used to be called Gamlestadens kapell. A little further along Gamlestadsvägen is the Gothenburg Hospital Cemetery, which dates back to the late 1500s. Only the odd gravestone is left today, but the site is protected by law as a heritage site, and a Franciscan friary also once stood here.
Strax intill ligger Rudboda gård, ett ti: Close by is Rudboda gård, a former croft that gave its name to the whole district. On Elfviksvägen stands Villa Molin, designed by Ralph Erskine in 1947 for the garden architect Ulla Molin. Not far off is Kyrkviken, once called Koltorpsviken, the narrow inlet of the sea that splits Lidingö into a northern and a southern half.
Strax intill ligger Råda säteri, en herr: Right next door is Råda säteri, a manor on Lake Rådasjön with a main house, wings and old farm buildings, all listed since 1969. The lake is up to 23 metres deep and supplies Mölndal with its drinking water. The Mölndalsån river runs straight through it and changes its name further downstream to Gullbergsån, so the water here flows all the way into Gothenburg.
Strax intill ligger Solvalla, Sveriges n: Right next to us is Solvalla, Sweden's national harness racing stadium and the largest trotting track in the Nordic countries. Every year it hosts Elitloppet, one of the world's biggest trotting races, and the stands hold 35,000 spectators. The track opened on 31 July 1927, and twelve races were held in its first year.
Strax intill ligger Tuve kyrka, en av Gö: Right beside us is Tuve Church, one of the most popular churches for weddings in the Diocese of Gothenburg. Since 2010 it has been part of Tuve-Säve parish. The old parish of Tuve belonged to the province of Västergötland and the Östra Hising hundred, and became part of the City of Gothenburg in 1967. In 2000 the parish had just over 10,000 residents.
Strax intill låg Karlsrofältet, en idrot: Right beside us was Karlsrofältet, a sports ground for almost sixty years. The name goes back to the iron porter Carl Jonsson and appears as Carlsro as early as 1834. A little further on begins the Botanical Garden, which opened in 1923 in time for the Jubilee Exhibition but wasn't considered finished until 1948. Its emblem is a wood anemone, and it has two stars in the Michelin travel guide.
Strax intill reser sig Fässbergs kyrka p: Right nearby, Fässberg Church stands on its hill. From 1922 to 1976 it was called Mölndal Church, because in 1922 the old Fässberg parish became the town of Mölndal. The parish goes back to the Middle Ages, and Gunnebo House lies within it too. A stone's throw away is Fässbergs Bio, a 400-seat cinema in a converted assembly hall.
Strax intill rinner Tappström, sundet me: Right beside us is Tappström, the channel between the islands of Ekerön and Lovön. It's about one and a half kilometres long but only 3.2 metres deep. On the Ekerö side there's a guest harbour for visiting boats, and the bridge here carries Ekerövägen, county road 261, all the way towards Brommaplan. So this is where one island ends and the next begins.
Strax intill studsar basketbollarna i Go: Right next door, basketballs are bouncing in Gothia Arena – home of Högsbo Basket and the only club-owned sports hall in Gothenburg. On match days it holds a thousand people. This whole area was once part of the parish of Västra Frölunda, which had around 13,500 residents in 1944 and became part of the City of Gothenburg the following year.
Strax intill står Akalla värmeverk, ett: Right beside us is Akalla värmeverk, a district heating plant from the mid-1970s. It may not sound thrilling, but the Stockholm City Museum rates two of its buildings as especially valuable to the city's cultural heritage. A little further away, in Akalla centrum, is a church with an unusual story. Consecrated in 1976, it was first shared by the Church of Sweden and EFS, a Lutheran revival movement. In 2020 it was sold to the Catholic diocese and is now the home church of the Syriac Catholic community.
Strax intill står Gibraltar herrgård, fa: Right next to us is Gibraltar herrgård, the old Chalmers family manor that gave Gibraltargatan its name. The wooden main house, in the Empire style, was built in 1847, and since 2024 it has stood in a new spot on Orrspelsgatan, south of the Chalmers University campus. One of the old estate manager's houses served as the Chalmers students' union building from 1948 to 1952.
Strax intill står Nacka kyrka, byggd 189: Right next door is Nacka Church, built in 1891 in Gothic Revival style, which gained a new funeral chapel in 1908–1909. It belongs to the old parish of Nacka, which had just 1,708 inhabitants in 1887 and became the town of Nacka in 1949. Across Kyrkviken bay, the Nysätra headland juts out into the water. The Nackanäs Inn welcomed guests there until it burned down in 1960.
Strax söder om Barkarby ligger Vålberga,: Just south of Barkarby lies Vålberga, a housing area built around 1963, made up mostly of long rows of terraced houses around a sports field. A little further away is Barkarby Villastad, with the neighbourhoods of Tingsbyn and Kyrkbyn – regarded as one of Järfälla's most valuable historic environments.
Strax utanför kusten ligger ön Trälen, o: Just off the coast lies the island of Trälen, which has had its moment as a TV star. In autumn 2006, TV4 aired a reality show called Trälen every weekday, in which wealthy inner-city Stockholmers and some less well-off suburbanites lived together on the island for 40 days. Half a million viewers tuned in for the first episode, but the numbers soon dropped off. The winner was Serhan Sören Erdal.
Strax väster om Danderyds kyrka, en bit: Just west of Danderyd Church, a little way from here, the runestone U 131 stands between the old Klockargården, the parish clerk's house, and the former parish hall. The Danderyd district is bordered by the Edsviken inlet to the south and west, and just over 11,000 people live here, most of them west of the E18.
Strax öster om Filipstadsbacken reser si: Just east of Filipstadsbacken rises Burmanstorpsberg, a 73-metre hill named after Burmanstorp. Around 1900, the land towards Lake Magelungen was meant to become Södertörns villastad, a garden suburb with almost 600 plots for well-to-do Stockholmers. But the plots were slow to sell, mostly because transport links were poor, and in 1912 the City of Stockholm bought out the whole company.
Strosa förbi Engelska radhusen i kvarter: Stroll past Engelska radhusen, the English terraces, in the Drivbänken block
Strosa i Ekerö centrum och leta upp den: Wander round Ekerö centrum and find the giant 'dot'
Strosa i Järla sjö bland gamla industrih: Wander around Järla sjö among old industrial buildings
Studenthuset Fyrtalet heter så för att m: The student residence Fyrtalet – 'the Foursome' – got its name because four identical buildings were planned, though only one was ever built. It was designed by the architect Léonie Geisendorf. On Furusundsgatan stands YK-huset, built in 1939 as a collective housing block for the Professional Women's Club, complete with a nursery, restaurant and gym. And Värtan's station building from 1882 has a blue rating – the highest level of protection the City Museum awards.
Studentområdet Kungshamra har ett kungli: The Kungshamra student village has a royal name for good reason: the land was a gift from King Gustaf VI Adolf. The buildings went up between 1965 and 1967, and today there are 1,383 student homes here. A short walk away, in a patch of woodland, is Invalidkyrkogården, the Invalids' Cemetery – a burial ground opened in 1824, where the last burial took place in 1905.
Stureby började byggas 1921 och hette då: Building started in Stureby in 1921, when it was called Ersta Villastad, but after protests it was renamed in 1926 – and Stureby is a made-up name. Nearby is the Vivstavarvsvägen terrace, 36 terraced houses from the early 1950s designed by Erik F. Dahl, and the only housing in Stureby marked blue by the City Museum. And Sockenvägen, which links up the northern part of Brännkyrka parish, is no less than 5,450 metres long.
Stureplan är Östermalms livliga mötespla: Stureplan is Östermalm's buzzing meeting place. In the middle of the square stands Svampen, the Mushroom, a concrete rain shelter from the 1930s that has become the classic place to meet up.
Stuvsta gårds kvarn, Kvarnberget: The Stuvsta gård windmill on Kvarnberget
Stuvsta och Snättringe var fram till 201: Until 2018, Stuvsta and Snättringe were a single municipal district of just over 16,000 people, before being split in two. Not far from here, Stuvsta gård's windmill once stood on Kvarnberget, Mill Hill, and several of its millstones survive. The municipality has placed one of them on Gymnasievägen, where Huddingegymnasiet, the sixth-form school, occupies a building listed among the municipality's most valuable.
Stuvsta sträcker sig hela vägen från Hag: Stuvsta stretches all the way from Hagsätra in the north down to Tomtberga and Hörningsnäs farm in the south, and east to Lake Trehörningen. Not far from here, the Stuvstaleden road runs through the Kungsklippan rock in the Stuvsta tunnel, opened in 1994. Its northern entrance is built into a block of flats that straddles the approach road.
Styrsö är en av de största öarna i södra: Styrsö is one of the largest islands in the southern archipelago. People live here all year round, and the island has sheltered swimming coves, meadows and old fishing villages.
Subtopia, en kort promenad bort, hette t: A short walk away is Subtopia, formerly known as Kulturhuset Rotemannen. Today it's a production hub for the arts, with studios, workshops and rehearsal spaces, and it has been a long-standing supporter of the circus world. Further on is Fittja farm, whose inn was one of the largest coaching inns in Sweden in the 17th and 18th centuries. Since 1987 the farm has been home to the Multicultural Centre.
Sundbyberg är Sveriges till ytan minsta: Sundbyberg is the smallest municipality in Sweden by area, at just 8.79 square kilometres. On Esplanaden you'll find the library, Det Nya Museet – the New Museum – and a bust of the town's founder, Anders Petter Löfström. Right next door is the Bristol cinema, which opened on New Year's Eve 1939 and now doubles as an arts venue.
Sundbyberg är en av Stockholms äldsta fö: Sundbyberg is one of Stockholm's oldest suburbs. It became a market town, a köping, in 1888, and was granted town status in 1927. The railway station is older still: it opened in 1876 on the Stockholm–Västerås–Bergslagen railway. And 26 metres beneath your feet, deep in the rock, is the metro station, decorated with sculptures of building façades and the human senses.
Sundbybergs stadsmuseum berättar histori: Sundbyberg City Museum tells the story of Sweden's first suburb from the 1860s onwards. Its collection includes burnt bones from a Viking Age grave, excavated on the spot where the Sieverts cable works later stood. You can also see parts of the runestone U 78, which went missing in the 18th century. Two pieces were found in Ursvik, spent many years in the porch of Solna Church, and finally came to the museum in 1976.
Sundbybergs viktigaste landmärke, det nu: Sundbyberg's best-known landmark is its water tower, no longer in use. It was designed by Ivar Tengbom and completed in 1912 as a symbol of a growing, modern Sundbyberg. Around it lies Tornparken, the Tower Park, whose dance floor was a popular meeting place in the 1940s and 50s, and in the 1970s its community sing-alongs drew big crowds. The Bristol cinema on Sturegatan opened back on New Year's Eve 1939.
Svandammen i Solhem är både park och bad: Svandammen, the Swan Pond, in Solhem is both a park and a swimming spot, and it's become a favourite hangout for teenagers and families alike. No wonder, really, since buses leave from there in almost every direction: to Brommaplan, Backlura, Vällingby, Hallonbergen, Solna centrum and Spånga station. A swim and a bus ride, all in one.
Svandammen är både park och badplats, oc: Svandammen, the Swan Pond, is both a park and a place to swim, and a favourite meeting spot for teenagers and families in Solhem. The name Spånga is really old: it was first written down as early as 1300, and means roughly 'spångar' – simple plank bridges over boggy ground. Spånga parish once took in both Hässelby Castle and Akalla.
Svartedalen byggdes mest under 1950- och: Svartedalen was mostly built in the 1950s and 60s, and between 1965 and 1967 the city's own housing company put up 358 flats here. A little way off is Jättesten, named after the boulders on the hill, and A C Lindblads gata, a street named after the newspaperman who became the first Gothenburger to sit in parliament for the Social Democrats.
Svedmyra låter oskyldigt, men namnet kom: Svedmyra sounds harmless enough, but the name comes from a croft called Svinmyran – ‘the pig bog’. Known since the 14th century, the croft belonged to Östberga farm. The district is ringed by woods and parkland, and the City of Stockholm classes the Svedmyra woods as a core area of high ecological value. In the metro station, the artist Torgny Larsson has created a 40-metre glass screen decorated with the leaves of broadleaf trees.
Svedmyra tunnelbanestation ligger, trots: Svedmyra metro station, despite its name, isn't in Svedmyra but in Stureby. A stone's throw away is Svedmyrabadet from 1969, where the water is kept at a toasty 32 to 34 degrees for warm-water exercise. A little further off was the Enskede ski jump, which opened in 1924 and hosted jumping competitions right up until 1990.
Sveriges första klinik för cancerbehandl: Sweden's first cancer clinic, Radiumhemmet, was founded in 1910 in a flat on Kungsholmen, and since 1938 it has been part of the hospital here in Solna. A little further on stood Norrbacka inn, one of Stockholm's well-known roadside inns on the road to Uppsala, until it burned down in 1882. There were also plans for a lookout tower in Hagaparken, but work on it never even began.
Sveriges volymmässigt största levande lö: A short walk from here grows Sweden's largest living deciduous tree by volume: the Ekebyhov Oak. It may be around 500 years old and was declared a natural monument in 1956. Beside it is Ekebyhov Palace, a Carolean-style manor house built in the late 17th century for Carl Gustav Wrangel. It may well be the largest surviving wooden palace in Sweden.
Synskadades museum: Synskadades museum, the museum of visual impairment
Syrhåla, stadsdelen en bit härifrån, har: Syrhåla, the district just along from here, has a name that's hardly a selling point. It's recorded in 1550 as Siöralla and means a swampy spot or sour ground, after the low, damp land between the hills east and south-east of the old village. The district was created in 1957, when Arendal was split in two.
Säby kyrka, församlingskyrkan för hela S: Säby Church, the parish church for all of Salem municipality, is just a few steps away. A couple of hundred metres from here stood Charlottenlund, also called Lottalund, a little cottage for a farm labourer and his family. In the autumn of 1853 the labourer Lars Björkman moved in with his wife Christina Charlotta, and he put in his days of labour at Fågelsta farm. The family stayed until Björkman died in 1887.
Sätra gård hör till Stockholms äldsta gå: Sätra gård is one of the oldest farms in Stockholm, known since the 1300s. It gave its name to the whole district, and its two surviving buildings probably date from the 1700s. On the district's highest point, Sätra berg, 71 metres above sea level, stands the water tower – a landmark since 1969 that you can see all the way from Ekerö.
Sätra radiolänktorn, även kallat Sätra t: Sätra radio link tower, also known as Sätra telelänktorn, stands on Backvindeln, close to where Mälarhöjden meets Bredäng. Painted in the pale 'Stockholm white', it has become a familiar landmark, though it isn't open to the public. A little further on is Bredängshallen, a swimming pool and sports hall from the mid-1960s that the City Museum has marked in green for its heritage value.
Sätras högsta punkt är Sätra berg, 71 me: Sätra's highest point is Sätra berg, 71 metres above sea level, crowned by a water tower since 1969. The district is named after Sätra gård, one of Stockholm's oldest farms, known as far back as the 1300s. A little further on you'll find the Church of Saint Maroun, formerly Sätra church, and the Smistabron bridge for pedestrians and cyclists, which has spanned the motorway since 2008.
Säve har vuxit rejält. År 1913 bodde 1 5: Säve has grown a great deal. In 1913 Säve parish had 1,598 inhabitants; by 2000 there were almost 12,000. The parish belonged to Västra Hising hundred, an old district of Bohuslän, and became part of the City of Gothenburg in 1967. The parish church, Säve Church, is a short walk away, and since 2010 it has been part of Tuve-Säve parish.
Sävedalen betyder helt enkelt Säveåns da: Sävedalen simply means the valley of the Säveån river. It's an inner suburb of Gothenburg in Partille municipality. Right here, from 1985 to 2013, was Partille Bokhandel, a bookshop that sold mostly Swedish titles but also books in French – a little corner of Paris in the middle of Sävedalen.
Så sent som på 1940-talet bestod området: As late as the 1940s, the area around Blackeberg was mostly woods and rocky hills. Then, in the early 1950s, the district was built to a town plan drawn up under Sven Markelius. Bio Kaskad, the cinema on Blackebergsplan, opened in 1957, closed in the late 1990s and was brought back to life in 2018. And Råcksta träsk, the little pond nearby, was dredged in the early 1970s when it was starting to silt up.
Sågen är själva mittpunkten i Vendelsö,: Sågen is the very heart of Vendelsö, a residential area made up mostly of blocks of flats from the 1950s to the 1970s, with a grocery shop and a restaurant in the centre. Vendelsö lies on both sides of the Gudöbroleden road, between Lake Drevviken and Tyresta National Park to the east. Winding through it is the Vendelsån stream, which gathers water from three lakes on its way to Drevviken.
Söder om Lundby nya kyrka står Sannegård: South of Lundby nya kyrka, Lundby New Church, is Sannegårdsmonumentet, what remains of a burial ground from the transition between the Bronze and Iron Ages. Four standing stones are lined up in a row. The biggest, a triangular stone, is still in its original spot, while the other three were moved because of gravel digging. The church's own name, incidentally, has been used for two different church buildings.
Söder om Rågsved tar Rågsveds friområde: South of Rågsved begins the Rågsved open space, also called Kräppladalen: just over 100 hectares of wild country with some dramatic terrain – heights, cliffs and valleys in an ancient fissure-valley landscape. Part of it became a nature reserve in 2018. In the other direction is Högdalen skatepark, Stockholm's largest, built at the initiative of a local group called Stockholm Sub Surfers.
Söderhöjden, en bit härifrån, byggdes 19: Söderhöjden, a short way from here, was built in 1967 as part of the Million Programme, Sweden's great housing drive, and it's where you'll find Jakobsberg's bowling alley. The square was renovated and reopened on 31 August 2013. In the middle stands a spherical artwork that glows in different colours depending on the season.
To the south, Årstaviken bay sparkles.
Sörred har ett namn som inte smickrar. D: Sörred's name isn't exactly flattering. It's recorded in 1388 as Surfua rudi, and the first part is thought to come from the nickname Surv, meaning a lazy, careless sort of man – a slacker or a good-for-nothing. The second part comes from the Old Swedish word ryd, a clearing. Still, the slacker's clearing ended up as a place of hard work: this is where construction of Volvo's Torslanda plant began in 1960–61.
Ta en fika eller middag på Trädgårn: Stop for fika – a coffee break – or dinner at Trädgårn
Ta en paus i Trekantsparken vid sjön Tre: Take a break in Trekantsparken, by the little lake Trekanten
Ta en paus vid dammen: Take a break by the pond
Ta med kikaren! En bit bort ligger Svank: Bring your binoculars! A short way off is Svankälla wetland park, home to marsh harriers, little grebes and lesser spotted woodpeckers. A little further west is Ligårds mosse, a bog so hemmed in by marshland that it's hard to reach. Among the reeds and water lilies, crucian carp and grass carp weighing several kilos are said to lurk.
Tallkrogen har fått sitt namn efter ett: Tallkrogen takes its name from an inn, Stora Tallkrogen. It's one of Stockholm's garden suburbs, and one of its streets, Victor Balcks väg, is named after the father of Swedish sport. The area also had a croft called Svedmyra, known in earlier times as Svinmyra, Pig Bog. It was pulled down in the 1930s but lent its name to the neighbouring district.
Talludden kallas också Neptuns udde. I o: Talludden is also known as Neptune's Point. Here you'll find Käppalaställningen, a Second World War anti-aircraft battery with gun pits and weapon emplacements. It was restored and reopened in 1994 as a listed memorial to Stockholm's air defence, the only one of its kind in Sweden. A little further away is Käppalaverket, a sewage treatment plant from 1969 that's regarded as one of the most efficient in the world.
Tallumpaviljongen, med sina pyramidforma: The Tallum Pavilion, with its pyramid-shaped roofs, was designed by Gunnar Asplund in 1922. Its name comes from ‘Tallum’, the motto Asplund and Sigurd Lewerentz used when they entered the 1915 competition to design Skogskyrkogården, the Woodland Cemetery. The building was probably only meant to be temporary, but it stayed and served as a utility building until 1981. Skogskyrkogården has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1994.
Tappström är ett smalt sund mellan Ekerö: Tappström is a narrow strait between the islands of Ekerön and Lovön – about 1.5 kilometres long and only just over three metres deep. On its shore, Ralph Erskine designed Ekerö centrum, completed in 1991, with a 'dot' more than twenty metres high as its landmark. Erskine lived on Lovön himself and said he enjoyed coming here to do his shopping. From here, commuter boat 89 runs all the way into Stadshuskajen, the City Hall quay.
Teaterälskare, spetsa öronen! Angereds t: Theatre lovers, listen up! Angereds teater, in the Blå Stället arts centre, stages brand-new plays for children, teenagers and adults, and runs its own drama school too. The arts centre is on Angereds torg, the square that was called Triörtorget until 1977. Closer to the stop is Gunnared cemetery.
Tekniska museet: Tekniska museet, the National Museum of Science and Technology
Telefonpionjären Lars Magnus Ericsson äg: The telephone pioneer Lars Magnus Ericsson owned Alby gård, the manor by Lake Albysjön a little way from here, from 1895 to 1913, and it was in his time that the house got its distinctive look. A later owner, Alfred Ekström, founded the laundry firm AB Fittja Familietvätt and pioneered new methods of industrial washing. Also in the neighbourhood is Fittja gård, where the Svartlösa district court used to sit.
Telefonplan domineras av LM Ericssons ga: Telefonplan is dominated by LM Ericsson's old factory and head office, built between 1938 and 1940 to designs by Ture Wennerholm. The architectural historian Fredric Bedoire has called it perhaps the most beautiful of all Stockholm's functionalist industrial complexes. Today it's home to, among others, Konstfack, the University of Arts, Crafts and Design, and the interactive light installation Colour by Numbers glows above Telefonplan.
Televerkets förvaltningsbyggnader: The old Televerket offices, once home to Sweden's telecoms authority
Televerkets förvaltningsbyggnader, en ko: A short walk away are the former offices of Televerket, the old Swedish telecoms authority, which served as Telia Company's headquarters until 2016. The complex was built in stages between 1962 and 1972 to designs by Bengt Hidemark and Gösta Danielson, and the buildings on Mårbackagatan won the prestigious Kasper Salin Prize for architecture. If you'd like to dig deeper into the area's past, Farsta hembygdsförening, the local history society, covers Farsta's story from prehistoric times to the present day.
Tensta byggdes mellan 1966 och 1972 som: Tensta was built between 1966 and 1972 as part of the Million Programme, Sweden's great housing drive, but today it's the culture that draws people in. Tensta konsthall, a few minutes away, shows contemporary art, and Tenstakyrkan church has a thriving music scene rooted in gospel, where many different Christian traditions share one congregation.
Tensta gymnasium och Tekniska i Tensta: Tensta gymnasium and Tekniska i Tensta, upper secondary schools
Tensta vattentorn tronar på Tenstas högs: Tensta water tower stands proudly on the highest point in Tensta and can be seen from far across the open land of Järvafältet. It was built in 1969 and the Stockholm City Museum has marked it in green as particularly valuable. Underneath the tower is the Tensta tunnel, where the E18 motorway runs through two separate 300-metre concrete tubes, built between 2010 and 2014.
Tenstakyrkan, alldeles intill, är en fri: Right next door is Tenstakyrkan, a free church known for its rich musical life with strong gospel roots. Close by is Tensta konsthall, a centre for contemporary art. And down in the metro, the artist Helga Henschen decorated the station on the theme A Rose for the Immigrants, using texts and poems among other things.
Till Hökmossen hörde förr backstugan Mic: Hökmossen once included the cottage of Mickelsberg, which gave Mickelsbergsvägen its name. A little further away is Hägerstensbadet, known locally as Personnebadet after Personnevägen – an outdoor pool that opened on 21 June 1961. The water is heated by solar panels, and swimming is free.
Till en annan värld: The sculpture Till en annan värld – “To Another World”
Till höger ligger Gröna Lund, Sveriges ä: On the right is Gröna Lund, Sweden's oldest amusement park.
On your right is Kungliga slottet, Stockholm Palace.
Till höger ligger Skansen Lejonet, en fö: On your right is Skansen Lejonet, the Lion Fort, a 17th-century stronghold crowned with a gilded lion.
On the right is the Liseberg amusement park.
Till höger reser sig Avicii Arena, den s: Rising on your right is Avicii Arena, the big white dome formerly known as Globen, the Globe.
Till höger reser sig Nya Ullevi, arenan: On your right is Nya Ullevi, the stadium built for the 1958 football World Cup.
Till höger ser du Vasamuseets tak, med m: On your right you can see the roof of the Vasa Museum, with masts that show just how tall the ship Vasa is.
Till höger ser du den röd-vita skyskrapa: On your right is the red-and-white tower that Gothenburgers call Läppstiftet – the Lipstick.
Till höger syns Kaknästornet, ett av Sto: On the right you can see Kaknästornet, the Kaknäs Tower, one of the tallest towers in Stockholm.
Till höger syns Riddarholmskyrkan med si: On your right is Riddarholmen Church, with its slender cast-iron spire. Many of Sweden's kings are buried there.
Till höger syns Stadshuset med sitt torn: On your right is Stadshuset, Stockholm City Hall, with its tower topped by the three golden crowns.
Till höger syns Älvsborgsbron, invigd 19: On the right is Älvsborgsbron, the Älvsborg Bridge, opened in 1966.
Till höger, på andra sidan vattnet, ligg: Across the water on the right is the island of Långholmen.
Till höger, uppe på berget, ser du Masth: On your right, up on the hill, is Masthuggskyrkan, the Masthugget Church, from 1914.
Till höger, uppe på berget, syns Skansen: On your right, up on the hill, is Skansen Kronan, the Crown Fort, built in the 17th century.
Till höger, vid kanalen, ligger Feskekôr: On your right, by the canal, is Feskekôrka, the city's fish market hall from 1874. It looks just like a church – which is why Gothenburgers call it 'the fish church'.
Till vänster ligger Gröna Lund, Sveriges: On your left is Gröna Lund, Sweden's oldest amusement park.
On your left is the Royal Palace.
Till vänster ligger Skansen Lejonet, en: On your left is Skansen Lejonet, a 17th-century fortress with a gilded lion on top.
Till vänster ligger nöjesparken Liseberg: On your left is Liseberg amusement park.
Till vänster på berget ser du Masthuggsk: On the hill to your left is Masthuggskyrkan, the Masthugget church. To your right you can catch a glimpse of the harbour and the Göta älv river.
Till vänster reser sig Avicii Arena, den: On your left rises Avicii Arena, the big white dome once known as the Globe, Globen.
Till vänster reser sig Nya Ullevi, arena: On the left is Nya Ullevi, the stadium built for the 1958 football World Cup.
Till vänster ser du Vasamuseets tak, med: On your left you can see the roof of the Vasa Museum, with masts that show just how tall the ship Vasa was.
Till vänster ser du den röd-vita skyskra: On your left is the red-and-white skyscraper that Gothenburgers call Läppstiftet – 'the Lipstick'.
Till vänster syns Kaknästornet, ett av S: On your left is Kaknästornet, the Kaknäs Tower, one of the tallest towers in Stockholm.
Till vänster syns Riddarholmskyrkan med: On the left is Riddarholmskyrkan, the Riddarholmen Church, with its slender cast-iron spire. Many of Sweden's kings are buried there.
Till vänster syns Stadshuset med sitt to: On your left is Stockholm City Hall, its tower topped by three golden crowns.
Till vänster, uppe på berget, ser du Mas: On your left, up on the hill, is Masthuggskyrkan, the Masthugget church, built in 1914.
Till vänster, uppe på berget, syns Skans: Up on the hill to your left you can see Skansen Kronan, the Crown Fort, a 17th-century stronghold.
Till vänster, vid kanalen, ligger Feskek: On your left, by the canal, is Feskekôrka, the city's fish market hall from 1874. It looks just like a church, and Gothenburgers have called it 'the fish church' ever since.
On the left, by the canal, is Feskekôrka, the city's fish market hall, built in 1874. It looks just like a church, which is why Gothenburgers call it the “fish church”.
Tingstadsvassen bär ett riktigt gammalt: Tingstadsvassen has a truly ancient name. Tingstad is recorded as early as 1388 and comes from a village where the ting, the local assembly, used to meet. The city was tight-fisted at first: in 1874 it turned down the chance to buy the reed beds for ten öre a square foot. Two years later it changed its mind – and paid 300,000 kronor. Today most of the district is taken up by the island of Ringön.
Titta in i Childhoodhallen, känd från HC: Peek into Childhoodhallen, known from HCZ
Titta på Trisshusen, tidiga radhus från: Look out for the Trisshusen, early terraced houses from 1909
Titta på gamla Lundbybadet på Herkulesga: See the old Lundbybadet baths on Herkulesgatan
Titta på perrongen. Där sitter en kvinna: Take a look at the platform. A bronze woman in a pointed hat is sitting there waiting – and she has been since 2001. The sculpture is called Väntan, 'Waiting', and it's by Britt Ignell. Perhaps she's waiting for someone to step off the tram. In the meantime, she's watched the multi-storey car park opposite get a new top floor of homes.
Titta upp mot en fyra meter hög granitpe: Look up at the four-metre granite column outside Karolinska Institutet. Up on top, running, is a bronze sculpture by Eric Grate called The Entomological Abduction – a woman and a man carrying off a third figure who has no arms or legs. The woman being carried wears a hat or perhaps a crown, and the man carrying her has insect-like antennae sprouting from his jaw.
Titta upp på ÅF-huset, 65 meter högt: Look up at ÅF-huset, 65 metres tall
Titteridamm, en bit härifrån, har fått s: Titteridamm, just up the road, owes its name to a legend. On Saturday evenings, so the story goes, the girls would go down to the pond to check their reflections in the shiny water and make themselves pretty for the dance. They 'tittade' – peeked – into the pond, and that's where the name comes from! Close by is Sankt Paulus av Korsets kyrka, the Church of St Paul of the Cross, a Catholic parish church.
Tolered hette ursprungligen Toleröd och: Tolered was originally called Toleröd, and it's mostly detached and terraced houses. Not far from here is Torpet Klara, a day labourer's croft with five buildings. It was so well hidden at the end of a road through a modern villa area that for many years the post office had no address for it. It has been a listed building since 2006.
Torget Hagaplan ligger delvis ovanpå mot: Hagaplan, a square that opened in 2023, sits partly on top of the motorway tunnels of Norra länken, the Northern Link. In the middle of its southern part stands the round office building Forskaren, 'the Researcher', and some sixty trees are planned here, among them giant sequoias and tulip trees. Since September 2023 the square has also been home to Inflyttarna, 'The Newcomers', an artwork by Johanna Karlin.
Torget byggdes 1971 och är uppkallat eft: The square was built in 1971 and named after the author and Nobel laureate Selma Lagerlöf. It's about four kilometres north of central Gothenburg and serves as the local centre for northern Backa. It's home to two schools, Svenska Balettskolan – the Swedish Ballet School – and Skälltorpsskolan, and the square also once had Bäckebol's church hall, part of Backa parish.
Torget en kort promenad härifrån hette t: The square a short walk from here used to be called Dragonplan, and its octagonal building has become Rissne's landmark. Beneath the square, in a rock cavern 25 to 40 metres down, is the metro station. Along its walls runs a lettered timeline of historical events from 3000 BC up to 1985, an artwork by Madeleine Dranger and Rolf H Reimers.
Torget fick sitt namn 1886 efter Landala: The square was named in 1886 after Landala chapel, and fish was being sold here as early as the 1880s. Landala was one of Gothenburg's first three working-class suburbs outside the Vallgraven moat. On Landala torg it's honoured by the sculpture Arbetarhustru, the Worker's Wife, inscribed: ‘With a firm hand, strong from work, soft with love, you held the home together.’ The school next door opened in 1892 as Landalaskolan.
Torget fick sitt namn 1924 efter den hög: The square was named in 1924 after the high ground it sits on, and the name then spread to the whole district, Höglandet – “the Highlands”. From 1926 to 1929, Höglandstorget was the end of the line for tram route 12. On the square is the Höglandsbiografen cinema, opened in 1936, and a small park a little way off is named after the artist Einar Forseth, who lived in a villa nearby from 1925 to 1981.
Torget fick sitt namn 1946, troligen eft: The square was named in 1946, probably after the governor Nils Kagg. Here stands Våren, 'Spring', a bronze statue by Eric Grate of a naked woman on a granite plinth, put up in 1950 – there's an identical one in Alingsås. The old Torpavallen ground, where Qviding FIF used to play on gravel, is now a retail park.
Torget har fått namn efter en by i Ostpr: This square is named after a village in East Prussia, famous for a battle in the Seven Years' War. Down at Klippan you'll find old inns linked to the ship's chaplain Jacob Wallenberg and his book Min son på galejan, 'My Son on the Galley'. And in Kustens hus next door, emigrants liked to have one last beer before the boat left for America.
Torget hette Torsnästorget fram till sep: Until September 2010 the square was called Torsnästorget. It was then renamed after Jan Stenbeck, in recognition of his importance to Sweden's telecoms industry. Next door is Kista Science Tower, at 123.9 metres the second-tallest office building in the Nordic countries. And the Filmstaden Kista cinema was opened on 27 November 2002 by the actors Josephine Bornebusch and Fares Fares.
Torget sticker ut med ett 16 våningar hö: The square is dominated by a 16-storey tower block completed in 1956, and the community centre is decorated with a marble-inlay mural by the artist Endre Nemes. That same year, Högsboskolan opened right next door, built for about 1,000 pupils. The school is gone now, though – it was demolished in 2013.
Torget vid stationen är uppkallat efter: The square by the station is named after the crime writer Stieg Trenter, who was born at Magelungsvägen 453. His parents ran a grocery by the railway station, then called Södertörns villastad, and young Stieg sometimes lent a hand – his crime novel Träff i helfigur is set in these very surroundings. The planned villa town itself never took off: the plots were slow to sell, mostly because transport links were so poor.
Torget är uppkallat efter polarforskaren: The square is named after the polar explorer and meteorologist Finn Malmgren, and the statue here, Avskedet på polarisen, Farewell on the Polar Ice, is dedicated to him. The oaks and pines around the square were left standing when it was built in the 1930s. And here's an unexpected former neighbour: Willy Brandt, later Chancellor of West Germany, lived at Finn Malmgrens väg 23 while in exile from Nazi Germany in the 1940s. A park nearby is named after him today.
Torpet Bussenhus intill Spånga kyrka var: Bussenhus, the croft next to Spånga Church, was a soldier's croft with an unusual sideline: in the 1740s the cavalryman who lived here was allowed to run a tavern. It crops up now and then in the records of the Sollentuna district court, after assorted brawls. Inside the church are fragments of Viking Age runestones, and one of them is built into the church's outer wall.
Torpet Månskär hade ett egendomligt namn: The croft of Månskär had an odd name, and despite appearances it has nothing to do with ‘månskära’, the crescent moon. The first part comes from Måns, one of its first tenants, and the second from ‘kärr’, meaning marsh. The croft grew up along the new route of Södertäljevägen road, finished in 1673. Right next door is Filmstaden Heron City, Sweden's largest cinema, with eighteen screens and more than four thousand seats.
Torpet Spikborn hade ett märkligt namn,: The croft of Spikborn had an odd name, probably from spikborr, a gimlet. It was most likely built in the 1650s as part of the Vårby estate, and the last of it was demolished in February 1977. Segeltorpsskolan, the Segeltorp school, has a dramatic past too: its first building from 1917 burned down in 1971, and a brand-new main building opened in 2010.
Torrekullagården, en kort promenad bort,: Torrekullagården, a short walk away, has worn many hats. The City of Mölndal has owned the farm since 1973 and has used it for a job-training scheme and as a camp centre. There have been plans for a hotel, the adult education association Studiefrämjandet wanted to take it over, and from 2015 to 2019 it was home to young refugees who had arrived without their families.
Torsby finns inte bara i Värmland. Det h: Värmland isn't the only place with a Torsby. This is Torsby parish in Bohuslän, which has been part of Kungälv municipality since 1971, and its parish church, Torsby Church, is a short walk from here. The parish reaches out to the North Sea coast just north of the mouth of the Nordre älv river, and takes in the small town of Kärna and several villages, such as Kovikshamn and Brunnefjäll.
Torslanda hörde länge till Bohuslän och: For a long time Torslanda was part of the province of Bohuslän and the Västra Hising district; it wasn't until 1967 that the parish became part of the City of Gothenburg. Today Torslanda is a large district on western Hisingen, made up of a string of smaller villages such as Amhult, Hjuvik, Lilleby, Nolered and Tumlehed. Not far from here is Torslanda Church, one of the most popular wedding churches in the diocese.
Torslanda på västra Hisingen är känt för: Torslanda, on western Hisingen, is known for its beaches and countryside – but above all for Volvo Cars' Torslanda Works. Before Landvetter Airport opened in 1977, Gothenburg's main airport was here in Torslanda too. Homes are mostly detached and terraced houses, and the shopping areas are called Torslanda Torg and Amhult.
Torslanda är en stor stadsdel på västra: Torslanda is a large district on western Hisingen, covering 4,425 hectares and taking in smaller places such as Amhult, Hjuvik, Hällsvik and Tumlehed. A short walk away is Torslanda church, one of the most popular churches for weddings in the Diocese of Gothenburg. And before Landvetter was built in 1977, Gothenburg's main airport was right here in Torslanda.
Torslanda är kyrkbyn i den gamla Torslan: Torslanda is the church village of the old Torslanda parish, which became part of the City of Gothenburg in 1967. It's known for its many beaches and its countryside, but above all for Volvo's car plant, Torslandaverken. Sport runs deep here, too: Torslanda IK was founded on 18 January 1944, and it's one of the local clubs along with Torslanda HK.
Torslandaverken, ursprungligen Volvo Tor: Torslandaverken, originally Volvo's Torslanda plant, was the largest single-storey factory in the Nordic countries when it opened. Building began in 1960–61 in the district of Sörred, whose name has an amusing origin. The first part, Sör-, is thought to come from the nickname Surv – a careless fellow, a slacker, a good-for-nothing – while the ending -red comes from the Old Swedish 'ryd', meaning cleared land.
Torsviks skola har vuxit fram i etapper,: Torsviks skola has grown bit by bit, with buildings dating from 1906 all the way to 2021, and today it has around 850 pupils from preschool to year 9. On Stockholmsvägen, look out for Lidingö Arena, an office and shopping block from 1974–1978 designed by Bo Möller, which has become a local landmark. Just west of Lidingö centrum is Ansgarskyrkan, the Ansgar Church, built in 1996 by Lidingö Missionsförsamling, a free church congregation.
Trakten här var kanske Stockholms mest k: This may well have been the most windmill-packed corner of Stockholm. Two of the mills were called Lilla and Stora Tissan, and nearby were others with names like Stora Adam and Lilla Eva. One of the Tissans was moved to Rolsta gård in Märsta in 1887. Next door was the Åhlinska school, a girls' school that Karin Åhlin founded in 1847 when she was just 17 – she started with 14 pupils and her sisters as teachers.
Tranebergs gård: Tranebergs gård, the old Traneberg farm
Tre villor vid Gasverksvägen, Ingenjörsv: The three villas on Gasverksvägen, known as Ingenjörsvillorna, were built as homes for the engineers at the Värtagasverket gasworks. The gasworks buildings were designed by Ferdinand Boberg, and the plant supplied Stockholm with town gas right up until January 2011. This was also meant to be the site of Gasklockan, a residential tower of around 170 metres and some 50 floors, designed by Herzog & de Meuron. In the end, though, it was never built.
Trollbäcken är ett lånat namn. Trakten h: Trollbäcken is a borrowed name. The area used to be called Kumla, after the manor on Lake Drevviken that goes back to the Middle Ages, but in 1947 the residential areas were renamed Trollbäcken to avoid confusion with Kumla in the province of Närke. A couple of hundred metres away is Trollbäcken Church, beside county road 260. The manor itself is still called Kumla herrgård, and since 2013 it has been a restaurant and conference centre.
Trots att Göteborg känns nära är marken: Gothenburg may feel close, but this land is actually part of Halland. Lindome parish belonged to Fjäre hundred, an old district of Halland, and only became part of Mölndal municipality in 1971. Lindome church, the parish's old church, is a short walk away, and the church village of Lindome has now merged with the Gothenburg urban area.
Trots namnet ligger Älvsjöbadet inte all: Despite its name, Älvsjöbadet isn't in Älvsjö at all, but in Hagsätra. The outdoor pool was built in 1937–1938 to designs by the architects Helge Zimdal and Nils Ahrbom. A short way off is Teknik och Servicegymnasiet, founded in 1963 as a workshop school to train staff for Stockholm's tramway workshops.
Trähästen Havre och betong: Havre the wooden horse, and concrete
Träkvista är en idrottsglad del av Ekerö: Träkvista is the sporty corner of Ekerö, with Ekerövallen, Träkvistavallen and Vikingahallen. It's mostly villas, linked houses and terraced houses, and there are several schools. Until 1990 Träkvista was the heart of the town, but then the centre moved when Ekerö centrum, designed by Ralph Erskine, opened.
Tulegatan har fått sitt namn efter det m: Tulegatan is named after the mythical land of Thule, because the street once marked the northern edge of built-up Sundbyberg. Tram line 15 ran along here from 1928 to 1959, and north of the street lies Tulemarken, with its functionalist villas from the 1930s. A short way off rises the town's best-known landmark, the water tower designed by Ivar Tengbom and completed in 1912.
Tullinge gymnasium startade i oktober år: Tullinge upper secondary school opened in October 2000. It's laid out like a small campus, with six buildings side by side and about 730 students. Former pupils include the athlete Michel Tornéus. And the school has an unusual tradition: every year it gets a visit from a Nobel laureate.
Tumba gymnasium: Tumba gymnasium, the upper secondary school
Tumba gymnasium öppnade 1974, och de röd: Tumba gymnasium opened in 1974, and at the time its red sheet-metal facades were seen as daring and modern. It was Botkyrka's first upper secondary school, and one of the first in the country built for both academic and vocational courses under one roof. In 1978 it became one of the first schools in Sweden to get its own computer – with no fewer than 16 users hooked up to it.
Tumba kyrka ligger alldeles intill. Den: Tumba Church is right beside us. It was consecrated in 1973 and, after a renovation, reconsecrated on Palm Sunday 2023. A little further away is the Lill-Tumba farm, which the paper mill bought in 1900 purely to stop anyone else using the land. And the mill has a history that's rolling in money, quite literally: Tumba bruksmuseum, the mill museum, tells the story of papermaking and banknote printing, and in 2008 it was nominated for the European Museum of the Year Award.
Tunnelbanan svävar fram här: Bredängs st: The metro takes to the air here: Bredäng station, opened in 1965, sits on a 180-metre viaduct over Bredängs allé. In the ticket hall you'll find Pusselbitar, 'Puzzle Pieces', sculptures with wooden reliefs that the artist Lena Kriström created together with Bredäng residents in 1982. The district is hilly and has a kilometre and a half of shoreline on Lake Mälaren.
Tunnelbanestationen strax intill är smyc: The metro station right beside us is decorated with Plexiglas rods and a loop of neon – an artwork by Kazuko Tamura from 1993. Just a couple of hundred metres away is Botkyrka's oldest school building, the church school from 1849, still in use by Botkyrka friskola. And in Hallunda's Folkets hus community hall, local residents run a cultural meeting place for northern Botkyrka themselves.
Tureberg är Sollentunas administrativa o: Tureberg is the administrative and commercial heart of Sollentuna, and the centre is just a short walk away. Around the square stand Turebergshuset, the town hall, the Arena Satelliten sports hall and the Sollentuna centrum shopping centre. Closer by, in Töjnan, is Töjnaskolan, a school that takes children all the way from the reception year to year nine.
Tuve kyrka en bit härifrån är en av Göte: Tuve church, not far from here, is one of the most popular churches for weddings in the Diocese of Gothenburg. Past it winds Tuve kyrkväg, once the official highway from Säve into central Gothenburg. The southern stretch, between Tången and the church, vanished completely in the Tuve landslide of 1977, because it ran straight through the area that slid away.
Tuve ligger mitt på Hisingen, precis på: Tuve lies in the middle of Hisingen, right where the built-up city gives way to countryside. Not far from here is Gunnestorps mosse, a patchwork of lake, fen and bog where reeds, bulrushes and water lilies grow alongside cranberries, sundew and cotton grass. Around the bog are wet meadows that were once used for grazing.
Tuve ligger mitt på Hisingen, på gränsen: Tuve lies in the middle of Hisingen, right where the built-up city to the south meets the countryside to the north. The district covers 1,720 hectares. Right next to it is the Tångedal housing area, with terraced houses and L-shaped houses first lived in in 1968–1969, and a little further on is Tuve torg square.
Tuve torg, alldeles intill, stod klart 1: Tuve torg, right next door, was completed in 1971 and was originally called Norums torg. It wasn't renamed Tuve torg until 1998, and in 2007 it got a proper facelift.
